I had the trio of shrimp tacos and our table shared some guacamole, carne asada tostadas, and steak fries. Everything was really good, and the pacing of the food was great as well. I definitely prefer the hole in the wall Mexican joint most of the time, but the upscale Mexican restaurant has it's place and this one is a good one.

Back in the day I used to stroll through Bed Bath and Beyond and I usually walked out with something that I found that struck my fancy whether I needed it or not. I went today for the first time in a few years.

All I could think about it how this place has changed from years ago. Let me first start off by saying that the reason I was there was to return a defective drink dispenser that upon the first use leaked mojitos all over my counter! As others have said the aisles are very narrow and not for the claustrophobic. The shelves are stocked with cheap, Made in China crap that doesn't seem of any quality whatsoever as evidenced by the drink dispenser. 

For a Sunday afternoon, they didn't have but 2 lines open and the people were snaked all throughout the front of the store. It was fine since I didn't wind up buying anything anyway.

Situé dans le village, le Club Sandwich vous accueil 24h sur 24. 
Si après une sortie déchainé sur les plancher de danse vous avez un crave de hot-dog ou une frites, cette place vous attends avec son espace très grand à l'intérieur et une terasse instalé durant l'été. Les prix sont abordable et la bouffe est OK. J'ai pour mon dire: quand tu es sur la brosse pis que tu as faim, pas mal n'importe quoi va te satisfaire. 

J'y ai manger le Hot-dog spéciale qui comprend une portion de frite et un Hot-Dog au fromage et Bacon. (hummm Bacon)

Nouvelle Administration, donc si jamais vous y êtes déjà aller et que vous trouviez sa moyen, essayer de nouveau quelques petite chose on changé..... Dont les lumières de la façade qui on été remplacé!

So glad I didn't spend $27 on shrimp and grits. Funny exchange on that. When I mentioned the high price, it was explained as being a function of the grits from NC. Yeah- me too, from NC and grits are poor people food! The shrimp and sausage should be the money in the dish. So, I went salad and flatbread. Got out more cheaply but this place confirms my Market Square theory: you eat there to sit there -in the square- and not to actually eat a high quality meal.

We visited in September, and I was glad we had booked a table as this small and cost restaurant was busy on a Friday night. 

I had Samlon to start which was lovely and cheap at 5.95 I think. 

Main was Maple Glazed Duck Breast with Wild Mushroom Samosa, Grilled Pak Choi, Sweet Potato Fondant & Chartreuse Sauce (£13.50) My partner had one of the Fish dishes which was absolutely delish! A big juicy portion of Hake with a huge stack of chips - they boy was in heaven!
Dessert was Chocolate Pave with Caramelised Banana, Toasted Pine Nuts & Peanut Butter Ice Cream (£5.50). I was intrigued by the peanut butter ice cream and worried it wouldn't quite work but, oh my, it really did. The saltiness and the sweetness go together really well and this was a stand-out component of a really great pud!

There's a good choice of wines on offer we had a fantastic Sancerre and they also have one of my favourite dessert wines Tokaji that was gorgeous. 

All in all this is a great little gem of a restaurant with all the taste and technique of high quality dining without any of the pomposity or any suggestion of over-pricing. I'll definitely be visiting again...

Went with my parents and kids. We got a large baked ziti, large spaghetti w/extra meat sauce and added meatballs, garden salad and garlic bread. Took a while to get our drinks, with no straws. Asked for straws. Got our salad. Server said garlic bread is coming right up. Finished salad and drink. Then a few minutes later came the straws. Asked for refills. Finally garlic bread came. 10 mins later after eating some garlic bread, refills came. Good thing I had my straw. Then came the meal. Not too bad. I seem to have a problem in this town asking for extra things and not getting it, or getting the very minimum one can possibly receive. The extra meat sauce came in a dipping sauce cup(about three tablespoons full). Seriously? Then it came time for dessert. Was going to get some ice cream, but two of my kids are allergic to milk, so I asked if they had sherbet. A simple yes or no would have sufficed. Instead I got huffed at and had a dessert menu shoved in my hand and was told \"this is what we have.\" So I dropped the menu, said forget dessert and asked for the check. RUDE! They got two stars for their portion sizes, but that's about it. Their food isn't anything to write home about, or get a good review. Prob won't be back.

I went here from work to eat lunch. As you walk inside you can see all the tanks with lobster and crab and different kinds of fish on the menu. I wanted to get chow me in instead of rice and they wouldn't su substitute even for an additional fee I had to order an entire order of noodles if I wanted them. They waiter was rude and seemed to steer clear of us the whole time. The food was only decent. For their outrageous prices for such mediocre food, I'll probably not return.

Do NOT go here!! Beware!!!

I decided to have my car towed there in distress after my front brakes locked on me while I was driving. I had no choice being that it was almost the weekend & the closest repair shop to my house. 
It was late afternoon (couple hours before they closed) & I talked to the guy, who was really nice & assured me he'll check what up with my car. I know a little about cars but was really nervous knowing how mechanic shops work with girls knowing they'd try to rip me off but he seemed to ease that worry.
I had to leave my car overnight & the very first thing I did in the morning I called in to check on my car since I hadn't heard from anyone the night before. He told me he had really bad news that I needed to flush my brake fluid, replace ALL 4 rotors, break pads, hose, calipers &master cylinder!!! A $2,100 repair job?!??! Freaked out I called a mechanically inclined friend of mine told him the deal & he was even surprised & told me that couldn't be true & suggested I got a second opinion. I thought why not & another friend recommended I take it to Master Transmission Automotive (Alllll the way in boulder city). Since he was certain I have them take a look at it I towed my car all the way across the city. The following Monday I got a call from Master saying all I needed was a brake fluid flush & that cost me only $120!!! 

The moral of this review is that Tirewors will try to rip you off especially if you're a girl!!! 

It's been a few months now & my car runs great, not having to replace all that crap tireworks told me I needed. What a place of BS!!

Rolled up at this hotel like many others for the price alone. Got a rate of $37 from hotels.com Got in late at 2am and they said they only has 2 rooms left..... Do they overbook? Room was both fine and quiet, the only drawback was the shower only bathroom. \n\nOddest thing of all was the people staying at this place. I guess it is to be expected..... Can't really beat the price and the location is not far from The strip. I was quiet, cheap, clean and had a casino..... Not a bad place at all and clearly the best price in town.

I gave it one star because its only saving grace is that the kitchen is open late...and it serves Pepsi.

I ordered (so typical of me) their supersomethinggooey chimichanga. You may as well have brought me a pile of flaming poo. It looked so unappetizing when it was plunked down in front of me. You know when you were a kid and you were forced to eat something you hated and you did all you could to prolong the agony? Well, there were no potted plants within range for me to dump my food in and the napkins were so flimsy I couldn't spit my bites out gracefully. Instead, I pushed away the food and claimed, "I savored every bite and now I'm full. I'll take it home." My friend loves that place. Why? I can't understand it, either. I dumped the leftovers off in the trash at the Taco Bell I ended up at.

Service was crap, food was crap, parking was crap. It's located around the corner from my husband's old office...but hell, if the die hard alkies of my husband's office wouldn't go there, that's saying something. Geez, it's stumbling or in their case, tumbling, distance from work. Even happy hour couldn't persuade the guys to go. Yes, it's that bad. You know it's bad when the alcoholics say no.

Thank god it's all you can drink Pepsi or I wouldn't know what to do with myself. *rolls eyes* I know what I'd do - I'd go to Jack in the Box across the street and bring it over because JITB is better than whatever Dos Gringos could ever try to feed me.

PS -- What's up with those park benches for tables?

By far the worst experience with southwest! They keep giving wrong information. The only reason I'm still flying southwest is because their airline tickets don't put a hole in your pocket and the bags are free. First my flight is delayed to 8:25, then they said 9pm. It then goes back to 8:30..... Giving us hope that we'll leave earlier. Then they change it again to 8;45. They finally board us and as soon as everyone is seated and suppose to take off soon, they say they got a message indicating that we will not be taking off to 9:30. What's next? Keeps going back and forth: they should seriously get their facts straight before announcing inconsistent information. Now we're stuck in the plane waiting when we could at least be walking around in the airport. Irritated!!
Horrible service...food being thrown in the kitchen. Order was wrong. No pepper. Bad attitudes from employees. Fails on all counts. Avoid if you can.

Had a blast here on Friday night! The door staff was great, music was fun, crowd was awesome. But the drinks...well, that was another story. I'm kind of a two-drink max type of girl. No tolerance for alcohol really, and after four margaritas I wasn't even feeling it. Stiff pricing on weak drinks. No matter though, I will come again. I just won't be spending my money at the bar!

Update: I had hoped to speak to corporate about my horrible first visit, and even sent them two messages via their messaging service on their website. Sadly, they have never responded to me nor have they even tried to contact me and find out what happened, unlike other restaurants. So pretty much, this place sucks in both customer service and quality. Take your money somewhere else, and don't bother coming to this place. Go somewhere else where they treat customers like people.

I really wanted to like this place. I gave it a try about once every couple months, but every time they would disappoint me. On Sunday mornings with perhaps two other people in here, the waiter and bar tender spend more time watching whatever game is on TV than checking to see if you want to order a drink or food. When you do finally order, expect to wait until half time or the end of the game before you get what you asked for.\n\nI also gave their \"Wall\" challenge a go as well, and made it a point to stop by after work three days in a row. Unfortunately, each day they couldn't find my card and I had to start over, by the third day I gave up and just never went back.

The check-in counter at the LAS airport is not as pretty as the ones back in other airports, it looks like a typical check-in station like any other ones in the airport. Their signature red wasn't found anywhere so they kinda blended in into the background. Our luggage was 3 lbs overweight and they had to make us take out a few items before we can check it in, no flexibility whatsoever. (side note: my sister had once traveled with a luggage that was at the exact size of an on-board luggage, but Virgin still made her check it in to make that $25). I personally think $25/luggage is a little steep because if they were offering any sort of other luxury then I would think its worth it. However, compare to the other airlines, they had to charge you $2 for earphone, no complimentary snack, and no legroom.\n\nThen when we arrived to SFO, they announce our baggage claim was at gate 4, when later we found out all our luggage was actually coming out of carousel 3. Oops much? Virgin at Las Vegas wasn't the best, I would imagine other airlines might be a better choice.
One if the hot spots downtown! There happy hour is pretty decent there burgers are amazing! I love the tangier burger which consists of hummus, sun dried tomatoes and feta cheese!!! Heaven!!

The tragically shabby and nondescript Vegas strip malls make LA's look like Manhattan commercial blocks, but there's one that houses Omelet House--and dang, they serve some of the best \"homemade\" corned beef hash I've ever had. The unique chips and delish pumpkin bread sides along with the perfect over easy eggs help make everything stick to your ribs. Coffee was ok--reminded me of that brand you find in bad motels--\"Chock full o' nuts\"?. Definitely check this place out!

I ate lunch here with my family on Saturday. It is mediocre at best. The atmosphere is..... \"pubby\"- obviously which was fine..... but the food was blaaahh..... I ordered the roast beef sliders which were dry and boring. I ate 2 of the 3..... and that was only because I doused them in mustard. The fries and the pickles were good, but I expect a little more from T.E. No one in my group claimed their meal was excellent..... If you're in the new mall you're better off @ Wolfgang or Social house for lunch..

The last time I stopped in At HoT was with clients for a lunch. Absolute DISASTER. We got our lunchtime libations and ordered. And waited. And waited. And waited. No drink refills. And it was late May so we could have used them. 

Finally, our waiter comes over with a light appetizer plate and apologizes that our order wasn't placed properly. Some lame excuse and then..... he said he paid for the appetizer out of his own pocket since he didn't want the manager to ream him. 

By the time we got our food, it was an hour-and-a-half from when we walked in. Not good in my book. Needless to say, I haven't been back. At least my clients had a good sense of humor and said I pulled a good Trick on them.

Got the assorted pastry basket. Fantastic. The berry fruit salad, also good. This place is solid on baked goods.\n\nTip: they don't take reservations, but you CAN call and get an idea on the current wait before trekking out there.

Very nice restaurant. I was trying to stay away from buffets and this place was conveniently located across the street from our hotel. The host and waitress, not so nice, but the food made up for it. I had to change the time of the reservation time once because we were running late and I guess she didn't like that. The waitress took our order and forgot about us for a while. \nThe food was really good, it had a really good taste. It comes in really big portions so you can share or just take the rest home. \nPrices are reasonable.

I can't believe this place has such good reviews. I went here for my bachelorette party and had to deal with the most scumbag of a waiter and the most incompetent manager ever. If I could give this place no stars I would.

I told the waiter that it was my bachelorette party and asked if he had any suggestions. He said he didn't. Even though we found out later that they had a tasting menu. This would be nice to offer a bachelorette party. We asked him what was on the boat and he couldn't really tell us and said he would check with the chef. He came back about 10minutes later and told us he couldn't understand what the sushi chefs were saying because they didn't speak English very well. Are you kidding me??? You should NOT be working in a Japanese restaurant if you cannot communicate with the sushi chefs. Telling a bunch of Asians that your chef cannot speak English is bordering on being racist. Why don't you try a little harder next time since this IS your job.

He was barely present through out our whole meal and I was so upset that I called the manager over. The manager was useless. He did not see what the waiter did wrong (maybe he was racist as well) and did not offer to do anything extra for us. 

When the bill came, I tried to paid it with my credit card. The scumbag waiter came back and told me that my card was declined. How embarrassed did he make me feel. I found out later when I called my credit card that it was NEVER declined. What a scumbag. He was doing it out of spite.

This is the worse restaurant I have ever dined at. The food doesn't even matter because the service was so horrible. If Shibuya was in NYC, it would not stand a chance because New Yorkers will not put up with this type of subpar service at a fine dining establishment. There are tons of restaurants in Vegas and this one is not worth your aggrevation.

This place is ok. I have been there 3 times. We went there for dinner the first time (husband, my mom, my baby, and I), and then my husband and I returned there for lunch on 2 other occasions for lunch with our baby.

When we came for dinner, we had to wait to get a table even out on the patio because the place is small. Not a big deal. We sat at the bar with our baby in his carrier on the floor while we waited and looked over the menu. The bartender was really nice. She was personable, told us about how business was going since they just opened within the last few months, etc.

When we got to our table, the waiter took our order and brought us our food, but he had no personality. He tried to run out Visa gift card when it came time to pay, but he told us it wasn't working and we'd have to pay via another method. That was okay with us until the next day when we tried to use the gift card elsewhere and we were told that the funds were already exhausted. WHAT!?!?!? That sucked. 

The food had been pretty good which is why we gave them a couple of additional chances. That and the fact that it's only a couple of miles from our home so it's convenient. Again, the food was really great, but both times our server didn't really seem to care that we were there. Kind of gave us an unwelcome feeling. Hmmm..... oh well. We haven't been back since. I'd say this place is just average. No more; no less.

I should have known better than to expect a 5-star hotel for a 1-star price. I looked at the pictures online and it never mentioned that the entire hotel and streets surrounding it were under major construction. The parking ramp was hard to find and the check-in desk seemed like it was a mile away from the parking ramp entrance. Our room was clean enough and housekeeping was quick to bring up the extra towels I requested. 

However, the tub was terrible. It took about 15-20 minutes to drain after I was done with my shower, which meant I had to re-wash my feet and legs. Nasty. 

Also, the walkway to the Strip is under construction and that entire area smelled like urine. Really gross!

I'd definitely spend a little more next time and avoid the slow-draining tub and urine scented walkway.

I haven't been to the restaurant, so this review is primarily about the meat market. I have been to this place for meat numerous times, and I can't say that I have ever walked out of there happy. My first time there an extremely over zealous man helped me. I went in for some rib eyes and the whole time the guy was trying to get me to buy more food than I wanted, and getting me to put their rub on the meat I was buying. I politely refused, and he gave me a dirty look. It wasn't a horrible experience and the meat was good. The last time I went there, and what turned out to be the last time that I will go there (for meat). I was stocking up on my weeks meat, and had a decent size order. I did order two rib eyes that were for the next day. When I opened the wrapping the next day, I found one rib eye, and one NY strip. That was definitely the end for me. Either the guy gave me wrong cut on purpose for whatever reason, or he made a stupid mistake. Either way I'm done with that place. 

As for the bakery. I have only had their donuts, and they are really good. If they have them made. I went in there on Monday, and there weren't really any donuts to choose from. I had to go somewhere else. 

Pretty much I can't see myself ever going back to either store.

On the advice of a friend I tried out Spice 9. It being the first visit, we just went for the lunch buffet to try out a selection of items. We could smell spices from the parking lot, in a good way. The buffet provided a great quick lunch with lots of choices. There were several tasty chutneys, including tamarind and a more unusual coconut. The buffet selection included the Mughal staples: rice, naan, tandoori chicken, butter chicken, and vegetable curries, but there were also more homey Indian dishes like a yellow dal with green peppers, lamb curry, sambar and rasam, an eggplant dish, and dry curries (just veg and spice without a heavy sauce). The spicing seemed very authentic, and the level of heat was definitely higher than in the average Charlotte Indian restaurant. It isn't \"take your face off\" hot -- if you're one of those people that think every meal is a chili pepper eating contest you might be disappointed. The spice blends come out nicely and aren't dominated by the heat, and dishes that are supposed to taste different from each other and use different spice blends, actually do taste different. I lived for a few months in India when I was younger, so I'm pretty picky about Indian restaurants. This is one I'll go back to. \n\nThe restaurant is located right across the road from Concord Mills just south of Lowe's. The interior is nicely decorated and definitely has an upscale vibe, not like the usual strip-mall place. Note: disappointingly, the name of the restaurant is not a Vonnegut reference, although that does not affect the deliciousness of the food.

This chipotles is very sloppy and has major issues with customer service. The short female manger is a bitch and doesn't have a clue on what customer service is..... I have never seen so much turn over in an establishment. Watch the grill guy when he make rice..... he puts his bare hands in it..... gross.

COUNT YOUR CHANGE! These girls repeatedly shorted us - and not just by a couple bucks. Handed her a $100 for a Jack and Coke and got back two $5's and three $1's. As soon as I'd complain they'd make it right but this happened to me 3 times and my brother yet another time. Basic thievery.

Never going to any Hooters again. 1) Flat Ass everywhere. Eat some of the wings and do some squats. 2) They increased the price of the endless wings for the new year yet the wings got smaller. The manager said that it is because they are being charged more. They might want to think about changing suppliers then. 3) To charge for every ranch dressing is asinine. We asked for one ranch each and she brought us a ranch every time we got our next plate of six tiny wings. Never did our server Ashlea tell us we were going to have to pay for each ranch that we did not even ask for. At least the beer was good and at a decent price. I think we will stick to Zipps!

If you are a FIRST TIMER or not familiar with Vegas then READ THIS. STAY HERE.

The casino is dated, not extraordinary, boring, small and not a destination for any visitor. Huh? Why stay here? For the same reasons for the 3 most important thing for real estate. Location, location and location.

Mid strip is really the only place to stay. All the casinos are closer to each other making walking easier here than any other place on the strip. Plus there are some nice casinos that are literally next door. Venetian can be access through the back of the Harrah's. Plus Palazzo is next to it. Mirage, just cross the street. Caesar and Treasure Island a little further walk, but again, cross the street and turn left or right of the Mirage. Next door, Casino Royale and the Quad, which is next door to the Flamingo. Go down the block and there is Bally, Paris and Bellagio. You really don't need a car here. The best shows are also nearby here too. Great restaurants all within walking distance. Two of the greatest casino shopping centers are also a skip and hop away, the Ceasar's Forum and the Grand Canal Shoppes. And a block away is the very large Fashion Show Mall which is across the street from the Wynn. You are right dab in the middle of the best place to stay in Vegas, mid-strip.

Another bonus is that it's one of the few casino where the monorail stops at. Most other monorail stops are not near the casinos at all. This one is just above the lobby with easy access. Parking here is terrible, but I always get a spot. Valet can be slow and at times is snail slow. Access by car all will eventually come to the back where it can be messy and crowded. Bus stops are better here than any other casino.

Yes, you can stay in a nice place (most of the ones I just named above) and they are nicer. But they will cost you more, much more. In Vegas, you need a room to sleep and only stay in as less as you can. The rooms here are nice. They have been renovated and are more than adequate. You will be pleased with them. Don't pay more for a nicer casino; instead use the savings by staying here to go to nice restaurants, shows or gamble.

As far as the casino, yup, my initial description is still is accurate. Boring. But, on the strip, getting a $5 Crap able is impossible. $10 Pai Gow more than impossible. You get them here. Plus the dealers are nice. Slots are not it's strength. The Total Rewards program is good and I can get comp rooms too.

I'm not kidding, I stayed in many of the elite casinos, and I loved them, but for the value and the location, this is the place to stay. Don't get intimidated by the humongous amount of information or opinions of others. This is the place to stay for the reasons I gave above. Do it.
Slow service! Crunchy pancakes? What happened mimis? Used to be good. They also recently changed their menu, with my favorite sandwich gone! Never again.

So I will upgrade my review of the store just because the store itself is kinda cool and fun to browse through. I still havent broke down and bought an iPhone or iPad, but maybe, just maybe sometime soon. Although I'm still waiting for the big announcement of the iPlug 5g cerebral cortex implant with internal cornea heads up display. Come on Steve, get on it, I really hate having to use my hands when I talk or text.

I have eaten here regularly, taken family and friends, and every time I've been satisfied. Sometimes their busy, sometimes it's quiet. The food is usually very good and fresh and the price is very good for the amount and selection of food they offer. Service is usually good, sometimes you can get someone new but most of the time they are very attentive and nice.

My biggest problem has always been with some of the customers, there is always a jerk who wants something for nothing. Or a lack of discipline parent with a screaming child. Not always, but you know who I'm talking about, reminds me of some of the reviewers here. 

I'll still go back.

Currently staying here and I literally can't even. Our room was comped, but I definitely won't be back, nor do I recommend this hotel to anyone.

It's still under construction so there's that. The parking structure is super sketchy. It's not well lit and it's confusing as heck to get in to. I'm from Long Beach, and our structures are nicer than this. What the heck.
We had our room comp email and brought it to the front desk lady who told us that we had to book the room online and then come back. Basically she was saying she cannot even do her job which is to book rooms.
I don't get cell service in here except for maybe in 5 minute pockets.
For the room:
The room is small, there isn't a coffee maker, the bathroom door doesn't close all the way, the channel selection sucks, and our view is of the sketch parking structure. We didn't pay for anything and I feel jipped.

Go anywhere else. There are a million places to go on the strip

We only went in because of the groupon deal for two dinners and a bottle of champaigne. I had never been to this buffet, and I was pleased to see no line. Most of the workers were rude and straight faced. A lady came up to us and asked of we needed anything, and walked away before we had time to answer. The food was bland, and had been sitting there a while (crab legs smelled extra fishy, turkey breast was extra dry and hard). On a positive note, the roasted carrots with raisins and almonds, and the flan were excellent and they had a good selection of cupcakes and dinner rolls. The cleanliness of the place was acceptable, and they had a restroom conveniently located so I could wash my hands from the crab leg juice. There is absolutely no cellphone signal (buffet located at ground level) and the hotel charges you $13.99 to use their wifi per 24hr period. Very unlilely for me to return.

Mammoth Transportation helped make our Vegas wedding extra special. We rented "Tiny" to transport our wedding group of about 25 people to the chapel, locations around the strip for photos and then to nightclubs for us to celebrate. 

"Tiny" was definitely not tiny by any means; our group was very comfortable in the spacious limo. It was clean and had a great sound system. We were able to bring our own alcohol, and cups and ice were provided. 

Our driver, Scott, did an excellent job. He was friendly, personable and professional. He went above and beyond what was required of him. He even helped hook us up with a deal for bottle service at one of the clubs. 

I highly recommend using Mammoth.

Stopped in here for lunch today, joined by Mike C. & Jackie C.

I had a regular Gyro, which comes with a Greek Salad. It was good, and the service was ok. There were some negatives, though:

* They opened 15 minutes late, & even that was with having go to ask the snarky gal working in the take-out room when they were going to open the dining room.:-(

* The restaurant itself has a bar & the whole room was kind of dark, boozy smelling & run down..... wobbly tables, etc. Not my style.:-|

We were the only customers during our lunch visit.

Classic Gyro & Side Salad: $7.99

I've been in Pittsburgh for almost two years and this weekend was my first time visiting station square. I was a little surprised by it all. The image in my head was that it would be bustling with people like other similar venues -- Boston's Faneuil Hall and Seattle's public market on a much smaller scale. When I opened the doors to go in, I was surprised at how dead it was. A few shops here and there but no people. I went late afternoon on a Saturday and the weather was gorgeous. My coworkers tell me that station square is more of a summer venue; that there are a lot more activities happening then. Some of the highlights are the location and the variety of restaurants.

I came in to Bud & Vine just looking to view the flower collection but I got so much more than expected! I made a friendship with the shop owner, Christina, and found a nice place to spend time! She was so sweet and helped me pick out a beautifully crafted bouquet! I can't say enough good things about this flower boutique! Flowers are so beautiful and can make anyone's day! Make sure to stop by Bud & Vine for a great experience.

What a dump. Fuddruckers is better. 
Burger sucked, fries sucked, onion rings were good.

The service sucked. Waitress messed up a few of the orders, and then told us that "she didn't care because the restaurant owes her three thousand dollars." Like I give a sh!t, or want to hear her sob story. Needless to say she didn't get any tip from our party of 6's $100 bill.

You can't just smack the name BLT on a TGI Friday's quality burger and expect me to think that I am eating a quality piece of meat.

I was much happier at In-N-Out fast food the next day. The friendly cashier even said "thank you".

I absolutely love this place. The service is professional, attentive, and friendly. The food is always prepared exceptionally. The drinks are strong but not overpowering the taste of the flavors. If you go, PLEASE GET THE MUSSELS-- I'm from Seattle and these are some of the best I have had (as well as the oysters). Can be a little spendy-- but hey you have to pay some money sometimes for good food. \n\nSimply I do not know why this place is getting some bad reviews. You HAVE to go.

I want to like this restaurant and I keep going back bc I keep thinking its going to get better and it just never does.

The atmosphere is fun and the outdoor seating is great. The atmosphere is the only reason to go here.

Well, their beer list is pretty good too. That's why they get 2 stars. Also, they do have a lot of vegetarian and vegan options so if you've got a veg friend and they want some mediocre food, take them here.

Do not get hte cilantro lime dressing unless you want to have wretched breath all night.

I've always had good service here. I know a lot of people say they've had some problems but the service has always been great. Considering the amount of really beligerent drunks this place gets, they staff is always nice!

Good but not great. 

The outside seating is lovely and will definitely come back for light appetizers and cocktails.

WARNING: They use those baby-martini glasses and still charge whack prices for them. Those baby martini glasses just make me mad.

Oh, and the things others said about the wait staff...not true from my experience. Nice, not obtrusive, and attentive.

Hidden bowling alley that is much larger than it looks on the outside, though still smallish. They have 16 lanes. Been here on the weekday for the special and most of the lanes were still free. 

During the summer, they have SPECIALS where you can bowl as many games as you want for about 2 and half hours including getting shoe rentals for only $10 (Tue - Thurs 6 to 8:30 PM or 9 to 11:30 PM). They still have this outside summer though it is reduced to two days per week. Check their website for up to date information about when their specials are. Otherwise, games are $3.50 each and $2 for shoe rentals. 

They have a computerized scoring system like pretty much all the bowling alleys now.

5 stars for being a super star when it comes to pure perfection with every single presentation of various desserts. It was amazing to see the chocolate fountain flowing with white, milk and dark chocolate at the Bellagio as its display but found the sculpted dragon made out of chocolate molding with pulled sugar even more amazing! I see why people are attracted to this place. Talk about great eye candy! 

My friend ordered the raspberry tart and the rose tea macaron. The raspberry tart was basically a crust filled with pastry cream and a tier of raspberries. That was not something we felt was worth almost $7. Nothing special. The rose tea macaron was definitely something out of the ordinary but again didn't retrieve enough of our interest to try it in the near future. It's basically rose tea infused into cream to give it that distinctive taste. 

I went back the next day to the one inside the Aria hotel and got the fruit tart. Although it was enough to satisfy my sweet tooth, I wasn't feeling much excitement with the pastry cream nor the crust. For paying so much for a little pastry, I had high expectations that this would be the best tart I've ever tasted. Sadly, it just "looked" great. 

I would probably end up going back to vegas to try their other treats. Who knows? I might end up with a favorite!

Set up a VinVillage event at this place, sight unseen, which I hosted last night. After the glowing descriptions on their website, some of the reviews here, and knowing they are located at CityNorth, I expected much better! 

Walking in, I did not get the feeling of "upscale" restaurant. Sports on 2 TVs blaring out over the bar and into the open dining room did nothing for the atmosphere. They had a long table pulled together for our group in the center of the room, but I grabbed a seat at the bar since I was the first to arrive. Took a few minutes, but the bartender eventually gave me a wine list/menu, answered my questions, and proceeded to get my drink. They had a good selection of wines, and some you don't normally find on wine lists at every other place in town.

A few others came in and we moved to the table, no problem transferring tabs. Seemed to take a long time between everyone (about 15 of us, though we initially expected 20) receiving their drinks and the time the first apps came out. Granted, they were complimentary (the deal I worked out for my group), and they were quite yummy - especially the spicy tuna on tempura eggplant - so once we started eating, we forgot about the wait. The pate was very rich and served with soft slices of raisin bread. Some were immediately addicted to the bacon-wrapped dates.

Everyone ordered a burger of one type or another, some opting for the pre-selected toppings, other customizing and adding sweet potato fries. We confirmed that everyone was on separate checks. My burger came out not quite as rare as I would have liked, but what do you expect when the patty is only 1/2" thick? I am not a big beef fan, anyway. Sauces were good, especially the pungent garlic parm, as were the fries.

But then, we waited for the checks...and waited...and waited. Seems the staff didn't begin trying to sort out who had what until at least HALF AN HOUR AFTER everyone had finished eating and plates had been cleared! And none clearly knew how to use the POS system. Those who had cash eventually tired of waiting and just left it on the table. Those of us with credit cards were not so lucky...and several bills had to be re-rung, as they did not include the right items. 

I had wanted to go back to try the salted caramel milkshake, but it will be a long time before I return.

This rating makes me sad. I like the dane downtown and the one in Fitchburg but..... I don't know, something just falls apart here. From the lackluster service, the just-ok food and the fact that it's always so..... dead. Oh! And the fact that I've had to tell a bartender how to make a hot toddy not once..... but TWICE. Seriously?! And why is the food always better at the other locations?? I mean..... don't they use the same recipes??\n\nOne bright spot (that's actually at ALL the great danes)- the David Bacco chocolate flights. Ahhh the tripepper.....!!!

They advertise sale prices but you have to pay $25 membership to get the price! Went in to buy a portable camp fire, retailing at 134.99, they jacked it up to $138 with savings, and $185 without the membership. Even called before hand and they said they had two in stock and they were $130. What a joke! They also charged more than retail on the other items I was there to buy as well. Shame on you CAMPING WORLD! I went to SPORTSMAN WAREHOUSE instead and found what we were looking for.

One of the BEST places I've eaten at since moving to AZ!! Smells good walking in, so many good choices on the menu..... We got the bacon board, turkey leg, brisket sandwich and salmon entree, omg they were all so mouth watering good! Excellent flavors, paired with garnishes that I would have never tried and so glad I did! Bacon that melts in your mouth! Anyone who goes must start with a bacon board! Oh and our drinks were stiff and good size:)..... Good service and ambiance. Will be back for sure!

I've been to Macayo's once before a couple years ago, and it used to be a lot better. I went on a saturday night at around 8 o'clock, and there was no one there, kind of odd. We all had margaritas, which were pretty good. The food was over-priced for what you got, since it was pretty mediocre. I ordered the same thing I did last time I came and I remember it being way better before, I think they changed the recipe, bad decision. Overall, I probably would not come back here again, unless they lowered their prices.

Dan, as I mentioned to you at that time, my condolences to you and your family. By the time I got a hold of you, it was bouncing back and forth via phone calls with your shop. After not getting anywhere, they suggested contacting you. When I did, you had told me of your family emergency, and I gave it a month's time before following up. After that point, I tried to contact you but there was no response from you. I tried other avenues of getting it resolved via your shop but they said I would have to wait as you were the go-to person. Another month went by and I pretty much gave up (when I wrote the first review). I pretty much left it until my fiancee asked me the status of it months later, at the end of 2009. At that point, I decided to initiate a BBB complaint to at least get my money back. I just received the refund a couple months ago, basically a year later. Never during this duration was a phone call made to me with any apologies.

This used to be my bad relationship. For many years, I came to this place. My sister and I had a favorite Pho spot that had closed down and so on our mission to find a new Pho spot we settled at this place. 

I was a weekly regular, that is how much I used to love this place. In the beginning this place was kind to me. It knew exactly what I wanted and always exceeded my expectations. If I was having a bad day, I could come in and be greeted by the servers who were always so welcoming to me and would serve me up a big bowl of delishness.

You know how you hit that 7 year itch in a relationship? I guess that is what you say happened to me. The service went down. The quality of the food went down. They had a couple of bad health inspections and to me, it just never was the same.

So I slowly stopped going. However, just like that bad relationship that you keep coming back to, "because just maybe it'll change and go back to how it used to be", I kept going back. And some days, I would be like "Yes!" this is why I love this place. Yet, more often than not it was like slow torture. The broth would get worse and worse, the meat would be tough and chewy. The last of the last was when I went and it tasted like there was soy sauce in my bowl of Pho. Definitely not okay. Just more often than not, it would be bland and flavorless. How fun is that?

I should give this place a 3 star based on the fact that I was a die hard fanatic for years but considering that I have visited this place in the last couple of months and it's still poor quality, I just can't. 

I remember when I first signed up with yelp and saw all the poor reviews, I didn't get it. I had thought to myself these people do not know what they are talking about. Kinda like, when you have that bad relationship and everyone else keeps telling you need to leave but you just can't, not until you are ready. 

Well, that chapter is closed and this relationship is no more. Onto better Pho!

(I orginally put this review under the wrong location. MY BAD! It has now been corrected to the rightful owner.)
sampled: Hidden Gem in Scottsdale Airpark: Lunch'N Go Delivers Excellence Tucked away in the commercial buildings of Scottsdale's airpark district, Lunch'N Go is a delightful discovery that rewards those who venture off the beaten path. This family-owned deli, operated by a warm Polish family, offers an impressively extensive menu featuring virtually any sandwich or salad imaginable. The standout'Nutty Honey' salad exemplifies their commitment to quality: generous portions of crisp, fresh greens crowned with a uniquely textured chicken salad sweetened with honey and cashews, complemented by fresh tomatoes and cucumber. Customization options like avocado additions and their delicious honey mustard dressing enhance the experience. The sandwich selection appears equally impressive, accompanied by numerous side options. Pricing remains reasonable, making it an excellent value proposition. Their robust delivery service particularly benefits area workers, though the quality justifies a special trip even for those outside the immediate vicinity. The genuine hospitality of the ownership creates a welcoming atmosphere that transforms a simple lunch stop into a memorable experience. For those seeking authentic, quality fare served with heartfelt warmth, Lunch'N Go represents everything a neighborhood deli should be—though you'll need insider knowledge to find this well-kept secret.

Solid Monroe Street Option with Good Beer Selection Jacs offers a reliable dining experience on Monroe Street, suitable for both dinner and brunch visits. The menu features standard fare including sandwiches, salads, and entrees like steak frites. Standout items include the frites and pesto sandwich, though quality varies across dishes. The beer selection impresses, with flight options available for sampling. The interior provides a pleasant atmosphere, though it doesn't quite match nearby Brasserie V's ambiance. Overall, Jacs serves as a dependable neighborhood spot for casual dining with friends.

Another Great Event! This fantastic community gathering showcased nonprofits across all three theater floors, perfectly paired with delicious tastings. Highlights included engaging science demonstrations from Carnegie Science Center and a fun glove-wearing candy unwrapping competition hosted by Big Brothers/Sisters. The diverse range of organizations offered volunteer opportunities for every interest. The culinary offerings impressed equally, with standout shrimp tacos from Luke Wholey's proving irresistible and divine cupcakes from Glutenny Bakery stealing the show. This stellar combination of meaningful community engagement and tasty treats created an unforgettable experience demonstrating countless ways to give back.

A Hidden Strip Mall Gem That Defies Expectations Tucked away in an unassuming Las Vegas strip mall, Yonaka proves that exceptional dining experiences can be found in the most unexpected places. This modern Japanese restaurant delivers authentic cuisine that rivals Hawaii's best, all at remarkably reasonable prices during happy hour. The standout dishes are truly memorable. The Brussels sprouts are an absolute must-order—so exceptional they deserve effusive praise. The avocado nigiri offers a revelation even for avocado skeptics, with its creamy texture creating an explosion of flavor that transforms this simple ingredient into something extraordinary. The restaurant's modern, clean aesthetic makes it equally suitable for romantic first dates or casual gatherings with friends. Service is attentive and excellent, enhancing the overall dining experience without being intrusive. Perhaps most impressive is the value proposition. During happy hour, diners can leave completely satisfied for approximately $20 per person—a refreshing change from typical Vegas Strip pricing. This makes Yonaka perfect for those seeking to "eat like a local" without breaking the bank. Located just minutes from the Strip, Yonaka offers both convenience and authenticity. For anyone visiting Las Vegas who craves quality Japanese cuisine at accessible prices, this hidden gem deserves immediate attention. Don't let the strip mall location fool you—Yonaka delivers an unforgettable culinary experience.

Mixed Review from a Vegetarian Perspective While acknowledging this establishment's controversial reputation, this non-meat-eating reviewer offers a surprisingly positive take. Though unable to comment on the apparently pricey kabobs, they've found the vegetarian sandwich options quite satisfactory and more reasonably priced. A notable highlight is the pizza available through an affiliated operation sharing the same address and phone number. The reviewer enthusiastically praises the pizza quality as "killer" and commends the impressively fast delivery service, which maintains reliability even during snowy conditions. For vegetarians seeking alternatives to the main kabob offerings, this spot provides decent options worth considering, particularly their pizza selection.

Mixed Experience: Great Food, Slow Service This restaurant delivers delicious Korean BBQ and beautifully presented sushi that keeps customers coming back. The food quality is undeniably excellent, though prices have increased noticeably over time. However, service issues significantly impact the dining experience. Wait times for dishes are lengthy, and getting staff attention requires persistent waving and assertiveness. The friendly staff can't quite compensate for the slow service pace. **The verdict:** Peak hours (lunch and dinner) should be avoided to enjoy a better experience. While the exceptional food merits return visits, strategic timing is essential for a satisfying meal without frustrating delays. Perfect for patient diners who prioritize food quality over efficiency.

Service Shines, But Menu Changes Disappoint at Elements My experience at Elements left me conflicted between awarding three or four stars. While the service was absolutely exceptional—truly five-star quality and among the best in Las Vegas—I ultimately judge restaurants primarily on their food. The calamari was outstanding and an absolute must-order item. However, our excitement quickly turned to disappointment when we discovered the menu had changed significantly from what we'd seen on Yelp. My husband specifically came for the duck, which is no longer available. He settled for the bone-in ribeye instead, which was merely good—not impressive for a city with so many excellent steakhouses. Similarly, I'd planned to order the Pappardelle Bolognese, only to find it discontinued. The spaghetti bolognese I ordered instead was decent but couldn't shake our disappointment. The staff did provide a complimentary berry cheesecake, which was delicious and exemplified their impeccable service. Unfortunately, outstanding service cannot completely compensate for menu disappointments when visiting a restaurant primarily for its food.

Overpriced Disappointment Despite Eye-Catching Exterior This hotel's impressive facade is misleading. While we secured a last-minute booking at $140, the room quality resembled a mediocre roadside motel. The lack of WiFi is unacceptable for this price point. Additionally, the party atmosphere may not suit all guests. Though not entirely objectionable, the value proposition is poor—reconsider unless rates significantly decrease.

Authentic Dim Sum Experience at the RIO Located inside the RIO hotel and casino, this traditional dim sum restaurant offers a limited but worthwhile dining window from noon to 3pm. The dim sum quality is good, though slightly sweeter than typical preparations. Service follows authentic dim sum style—efficient rather than hovering—where a simple raised hand promptly summons staff. However, be aware that once items sell out, they won't be replenished, so arriving early is essential. If you're seeking an genuine dim sum experience with competent service and don't mind the time constraints, this spot delivers solid Cantonese cuisine in a Vegas setting.

A Longtime Customer's Disappointment at Raffaele's Pizza As a devoted patron since fifth grade, now 48 years old, I've witnessed Raffaele's Pizza's unfortunate decline over my 38-year relationship with this establishment. What once stood as the pinnacle of meatball subs and Sicilian pizza has gradually compromised its quality. The deterioration began approximately five years ago when management replaced their signature Italian sausage with generic, round processed alternatives, transforming what was once exceptional into merely ordinary. My most recent Sicilian pizza on April 11, 2011, confirmed my worst suspicions—something fundamental has changed. Whether they've altered the sauce recipe or downgraded to cheaper cheese, the distinctive taste that kept me loyal for decades has vanished. With new ownership comes inevitable changes, but these modifications threaten to alienate faithful customers like myself. Raffaele's trajectory from "the best" to "just okay" echoes the sad fate of beloved establishments like Mr. Morts and Gemco. Unless they return to their original recipes, I'll reluctantly seek alternatives, mourning yet another culinary institution's demise. *—Sammy D.*

Double Dutch Café: Two Strikes and You're Out After giving Double Dutch not one but two chances to impress, I'm sad to report that this café simply doesn't deliver on the basics of good service and food quality. While I'm usually willing to chalk up a poor experience to an off day, my return visit confirmed that the issues here run deeper than mere bad luck. ## First Impressions: A Test of Patience My initial visit started promisingly enough with a friendly waitress taking our orders. However, what followed was an interminable wait that tested even the most patient of diners. Thankfully, my companion and I are natural chatterers, but even we found ourselves wondering if our food had been forgotten. When my hamburger finally arrived, it was disappointingly dry, requiring liberal amounts of ketchup to make it palatable. We left with full stomachs but decided to give the place another chance. ## Strike Two: When Bad Becomes Worse My second visit with my mum proved even more frustrating. With limited time before class, we hoped for quick service. Instead, we encountered a series of baffling mishaps. Initially refused window seating because we were "only two," we watched as a couple who arrived after us was immediately seated at those same tables without question. The inconsistency was puzzling and unwelcoming. The service continued to deteriorate. Our server, though sweet-natured, struggled significantly with communication, making ordering unnecessarily difficult. The wait for food was again excessive, especially problematic given my time constraints. When our meals finally arrived, the chips were barely warm, suggesting they'd been sitting out for some time. Adding insult to injury, the table beside us—who'd arrived ten minutes after us—received their order first, which staff initially tried to give to us. My egg and bacon bagel was decent, though hunger likely influenced my judgment. I practically inhaled it to avoid being late for class. The final straw came when settling the bill: after another lengthy wait, we discovered we'd been charged for someone else's order—a more expensive one at that. ## The Verdict Double Dutch occupies prime real estate with lovely indoor and outdoor seating, but atmosphere alone doesn't cut it. With numerous cafés competing for customers in this area, they need to seriously address their service inconsistencies, food quality, and billing accuracy. Until substantial improvements are made, I won't be returning for a third attempt.

Overpriced Pretension Masquerading as Art This establishment epitomizes everything wrong with trendy dining. The atmosphere reeks of self-importance, with pseudo-intellectual posturing replacing genuine hospitality. Simply renaming appetizers as "tapas" doesn't justify exorbitant prices for minuscule portions. The pretentious vibe is so overwhelming that leaving before ordering seemed the only sensible option. Unless you enjoy paying premium prices to discuss political philosophy while nibbling microscopic portions in an insufferably smug environment, avoid this place entirely. For those seeking actual sustenance without the theatrical pretense, countless better options exist. This restaurant prioritizes style over substance, leaving diners hungry both literally and figuratively. **Rating: ★☆☆☆☆**

A Worthy Splurge for Selective Shopping Yes, this is one of those fancy, pricey healthy/natural/organic/vegan grocery shops, so you know what you're buying into before entering. But there are compelling reasons to venture inside. The natural cosmetics section offers an impressive selection, with some brands priced comparably to conventional options like Olay. They stock everything from lotions and eye creams to makeup, making the switch to more natural beauty products surprisingly accessible. Newman's Own products, particularly their popcorn, are standout favorites. The bulk section provides excellent value on grains, nuts, dried fruit, and legumes—perfect for stocking a healthy pantry. The meat counter warrants further investigation for grass-fed options. For occasional meat-eaters concerned about antibiotic resistance and sustainable farming, quality matters more than quantity. The beer selection has also garnered considerable praise from other shoppers. While not an everyday grocery destination, this store fills important niches for health-conscious consumers seeking natural cosmetics, quality packaged goods, and potentially better meat options. It's worth adding to your rotation for selective purchases.

Not Worth the Premium Price While the ambiance and service shine, this restaurant falls short where it matters most. The kitchen's inventory issues, microscopic portions, mediocre food quality, and excessive prices make it impossible to recommend. Skip this one.

A Tale of Two Experiences: Pow Wow Excellence Meets Casino Reality This establishment offers strikingly contrasting experiences depending on whether you're attending their cultural events or visiting the casino itself. My visit primarily centered around the three-day pow wow and buffet, with only a brief foray into the gaming floor. ## The Pow Wow: A Cultural Gem The annual pow wow is absolutely worth attending and comes highly recommended for next year. This free event showcases authentic American Indian culture at its finest. The food court area features wonderful homemade treats, including traditional fry bread that shouldn't be missed. Throughout the evening, dancers perform in stunning costumes that clearly represent hundreds of hours of meticulous craftsmanship and cultural pride. The atmosphere radiates warmth and hospitality—everyone was exceptionally friendly and welcoming. Beyond the performances, visitors can browse authentic American Indian arts and crafts, grab some Kona Ice, or indulge in what might be the best kettle corn available anywhere. Prices remain refreshingly reasonable throughout the event, making it accessible entertainment for everyone. ## The Casino: Room for Improvement Unfortunately, the casino experience doesn't match the pow wow's excellence. The facility suffers from significant connectivity issues, offering neither WiFi nor reliable cell service until you're approximately 200 feet outside the building—a puzzling limitation in today's connected world. Despite numerous "Thank you for not smoking" signs, the casino remains uncomfortably smoky, though admittedly not reaching Las Vegas's Circus Circus levels. Navigation proves challenging due to poor organization, making even finding the buffet an unnecessarily difficult task. ## The Buffet: Surprisingly Satisfactory The all-you-can-eat buffet, priced at $15.99 (cheaper on select weekdays), exceeds expectations despite the uninspiring, blocky seating arrangement. The crab legs, while not premium quality, offer decent value. Everything else impresses: fresh, green salads; attentive staff maintaining cleanliness; fresh seafood without fishy odors; and respectable desserts. **Final Verdict:** Visit for the pow wow and buffet, but for serious gambling, consider traveling further to Talking Stick Resort.
Average Thai Spot with Promising Larb Worth Trying Again

Exceptional Fine Dining Experience at Europea While our original plan to visit Toque fell through due to their Sunday closure, we were recommended Europea as one of Montreal's finest restaurants – and it absolutely delivered on that promise. We opted for the five-course tasting menu, which exceeded expectations with numerous complimentary "surprises" from the kitchen between courses. The standout dishes included an exquisite lobster bisque cappuccino, delicate crab ceviche, and melt-in-your-mouth beef cheeks. The restaurant boasts a sophisticated, chic atmosphere that perfectly complements the exceptional cuisine. The attentive and knowledgeable wait staff enhanced our already wonderful experience. Remarkably, the entire meal would have cost double at a comparable American establishment, making it an outstanding value for such high-quality fine dining.

Solid Sandwich Shop with a Standout Turkey Original This establishment excels at sandwiches, particularly their turkey original, which surpasses competitors like Subway and Paradise Bakery. While service isn't lightning-fast, the quality justifies the wait. However, stick to their specialty—the pizza disappoints with temperature issues. For satisfying sammies, this spot delivers consistently.

Japonais Las Vegas: A Disappointing Experience at Overpriced Prices When convenience meets curiosity, sometimes the results fall short of expectations. Located downstairs from my hotel, Japonais seemed like an easy choice for dinner, especially considering there's a location in Chicago I'd been meaning to try. Unfortunately, this Las Vegas outpost left much to be desired. ## Limited Menu, Lackluster Selection For a restaurant boasting a full sushi bar with dedicated chefs, the sushi menu was surprisingly pathetic. The selection was remarkably limited, lacking the variety and creativity you'd expect from an upscale sushi establishment. While I could have potentially requested off-menu items, the offerings presented seemed more appropriate for a generic Japanese restaurant or steakhouse rather than a specialized sushi venue. The pricing structure was particularly shocking. Compared to other Las Vegas sushi destinations like Little Buddha at Palms and Sushi Roku at Caesar's, the sashimi and nigiri were extremely overpriced. Both alternatives delivered experiences that were exponentially better—I'd recommend either over Japonais without hesitation. ## Service Issues in an Empty Restaurant The service quality was mediocre at best. While staff members were friendly enough, the pace was frustratingly slow. Most telling was our initial greeting: the host spotted us waiting but chose to finish his casual conversation with the bartender before seating us. This set the tone for the evening. Despite the restaurant being virtually empty with approximately ten servers on duty, my wine and water glasses sat neglected for at least ten minutes. By Vegas standards, where attentive service is typically the norm, this performance was subpar. ## The Silver Lining The meal wasn't entirely without merit. The tuna sashimi, soft shell crab roll, and tempura roll were genuinely tasty. The soft shell crab roll particularly impressed, generously topped with crab and complemented by excellent sauce. However, these bright spots couldn't salvage the overall experience. Japonais proved overrated and overpriced, leaving me questioning whether the Chicago location merits a visit.

An Absolutely Appalling Shopping Experience - Never Again My fiancée and I previously had a decent experience purchasing a mattress from this store, which is why we decided to return. However, our recent visit was nothing short of nightmarish and has ensured we'll never set foot in this establishment again. We came in looking for an affordable mattress for our guest bedroom—a simple, straightforward purchase. Instead, we were immediately descended upon by a salesperson named Todd, who embodied every negative stereotype of pushy salespeople. After enduring what felt like an endless stream of high-pressure sales tactics and meaningless rambling, we politely excused ourselves to consider our options. What happened next was utterly unacceptable and frankly disturbing. As we made our way toward the exit, Todd actually **yelled across the store** at us, then proceeded to **chase us out to our car**. We ignored his desperate attempts to stop us and hurried to our vehicle, genuinely concerned he might knock on our windows to continue his aggressive pitch. This behavior is completely inappropriate and unprofessional. No customer should ever feel harassed or pursued when choosing to leave a store. The pushiness we experienced on previous visits was already borderline acceptable, but this incident crossed every line imaginable. **Bottom line:** Stay away from this store unless you enjoy being aggressively pursued by overzealous salespeople. We certainly won't be returning.

A Disappointing Dining Experience Despite Promising Atmosphere While this establishment boasts a visually appealing Hard Rock Cafe-style ambiance and friendly waitstaff, the overall experience falls significantly short of expectations. The restaurant's attempts at creating a fun atmosphere quickly become grating, particularly with the repetitive "Big Unit" bell ceremony that disrupts service every time someone orders their signature dish. ## Food Quality Concerns The primary letdown centers on the food quality. The BBQ sampler was particularly underwhelming, with meats tasting suspiciously like reheated, boil-in-the-bag fare. The sauce proved excessively sweet, and most disappointingly, none of the meats exhibited any genuine smoky flavor or appearance one would expect from authentic barbecue. The nachos fared no better, arriving with soggy tortillas that couldn't support their toppings. Everything slid off upon lifting, leaving diners with wet chips and separated ingredients. Even when eaten with utensils, the toppings lacked satisfying flavor. ## Limited Redeeming Qualities The only edible items were the french fries, though even these were the battered variety, which won't appeal to everyone. The pleasant demeanor of the waitstaff, despite their unusual uniform requirements, couldn't compensate for the subpar cuisine. ## Final Verdict This restaurant fails to deliver on its promise of quality barbecue. With better options available elsewhere, it's difficult to recommend this establishment to others seeking an authentic dining experience.

Disappointing Decline at Once-Great Buffet This buffet has unfortunately fallen from grace. While it uniquely offers tiny slipper lobsters, they're improperly cooked and often taste off. The remaining selections are merely standard buffet fare—nothing special. The sushi looked questionable enough to skip entirely. Sadly, I'd now choose almost any other buffet over this former favorite. A real letdown.

Professional A/C Installation with Excellent Service After contacting multiple air conditioning companies, we selected this one for our new A/C installation, and the experience was thoroughly pleasant from start to finish. **Installation Details:** We chose a mid-range Carrier unit for our nearly 1,800 square foot central Arizona home, with the total cost around $7,000. This price included both the outdoor ground unit and replacement of the heater coil in the attic. The unit came with a solid warranty, providing peace of mind for our investment. **Service Quality:** What stood out most was their professional approach—no high-pressure sales tactics whatsoever. The installation team arrived punctually as scheduled and completed the work efficiently. We were up and running quickly with minimal disruption. **Performance:** The new, more efficient unit has delivered excellent results. Our home stays comfortably cool during Arizona's harsh summers, and we've noticed lower electricity bills compared to our old system. The unit gets seasonal rest during winter months when we rely solely on heating. **Overall Impression:** This company demonstrated professionalism throughout the entire process. Their straightforward approach, timely service, and quality installation make them a contractor we would confidently use again for future HVAC needs.

Smooth Banking Transition with Exceptional Service Kristen provided outstanding assistance during my checking account opening, thoroughly explaining the fee-free structure. Her helpfulness made switching from Bank of America effortless and created a genuinely great banking experience.

**A Delightful Neighborhood Gem Worth the Drive** Buzzberry is a charming neighborhood cafe that truly does it all. Their impressive menu spans coffees, teas, all-fruit smoothies, breakfast, lunch, and nightly dinner specials, plus beer and wine. The tropical escape smoothie was absolutely scrumptious! With convenient 24-hour service and drive-thru options, they've thought of everything—even all-natural dog treats. The service is fast and friendly, and free Wi-Fi connects easily, making it an ideal spot for studying, meetings, or casual hangouts. While the extensive offerings seem almost impossible to manage, they pull it off beautifully. Though I've only tried their smoothie so far, I'm eager to return and explore their vast menu. My only complaint? I wish it was closer to home!

A Grand Romantic Gesture, Expertly Executed Three years ago, I experienced what can only be described as the most elaborate flower delivery of my life. After moving to Edinburgh following a breakup, my ex-boyfriend orchestrated an incredibly creative campaign to win me back through Interflora. What started as a confusing delivery – an empty vase with a single red rose and a card reading simply "it's a" – transformed into a two-week daily ritual. Each day brought another rose and another word, slowly revealing the complete message: "it's a new year, so let's try a new start? meet me at the witchery, sunday 9pm." **The Service Was Impeccable** Throughout this fortnight-long delivery sequence, Interflora demonstrated exceptional professionalism and customer service. The staff clearly understood they were part of something special, as they were sending flowers daily to the same recipient. Rather than treating it as routine business, they genuinely seemed to enjoy being part of the unfolding story alongside me. Every delivery arrived punctually, every rose was perfect, and their friendly demeanor made each pickup something to look forward to. **The Aftermath** I did meet him at the Witchery for what was indeed a lovely meal. However, some betrayals can't be forgiven with roses – no matter how romantically they're delivered. While our relationship didn't rekindle, Interflora's flawless execution of this elaborate gesture earned my permanent respect and loyalty. For grand romantic gestures requiring impeccable timing and professionalism, they're simply brilliant.

**Authentic French Crêpes Worth the Visit** After spending nine weeks in France across three trips, I can confidently say this restaurant serves the most authentic crêpes I've found in the United States. This hidden gem exceeded all expectations. The savory crêpes are generously sized—perfect for sharing or satisfying a hearty appetite. The coffee is exceptional, and the staff welcomes creative requests. The owner's warmth matches the sweetness of the dessert crêpes. Whether you're a crêpe connoisseur or first-timer, this place delivers an authentic French experience. Highly recommended for anyone seeking genuine French cuisine stateside!

Airport Club Disappointment: A Half-Star Experience This airport lounge barely deserves recognition, earning a meager half-star solely for providing basic amenities: walls, a roof, and restrooms. The cramped space offers minimal room for travelers to work comfortably. Most disturbingly, the front desk staff exhibits extraordinary coldness and unhelpfulness—less welcoming than ice cubes. Adding insult to injury, outside food is prohibited while guests are expected to consume questionable day-old soup and communal olive bar offerings. The contradictory policies and unwelcoming atmosphere make this lounge intolerable. **Bottom line:** Skip this frigid, cramped establishment entirely. The main terminal provides a far more pleasant experience.

Disappointing Service and Poor Management I gave this restaurant a second chance after an average first visit, but unfortunately had a worse experience. The front desk confirmed we could dine from 2-5 PM using the bar menu, which seemed fine. However, upon arrival, despite numerous empty tables, staff refused to seat our party anywhere but the full bar. The manager wouldn't honor the front desk's offer, leaving us no choice but to leave. This inflexible approach and lack of communication between staff demonstrates poor business practices and customer service.

A Diamond in the Rough: Cafe Monna's Untapped Brunch Potential Nestled in Pittsburgh's Bloomfield corridor, Cafe Monna operates quietly beneath the city's brunch radar, yet possesses all the ingredients for breakfast greatness—they just need some fine-tuning. The restaurant deserves immediate praise for its physical space. The quaint interior provides intimate dining, while sidewalk seating offers pleasant people-watching. However, the pièce de résistance is undoubtedly the magnificent outdoor porch, perfectly capitalizing on Pittsburgh's precious sunny days. In a city where good weather is fleeting, such thoughtful outdoor spaces elevate the entire dining experience. Cafe Monna cultivates a distinctly hipsterish atmosphere—a characteristic that works in their favor. The succinct menu demonstrates focused intention rather than overwhelming choice, complemented by generously large coffee mugs. Their prix fixe offerings are remarkably reasonable, making quality brunch accessible without breaking the bank. However, the menu could benefit from additional heartier options. Potatoes, the hallmark of any respectable brunch establishment, deserve more prominent representation among the meat-and-potatoes crowd. The culinary execution reveals room for improvement. The Elvis Crepe, featuring bacon, bananas, and peanut butter, suffered from imbalance—drowning in excessive peanut butter that overwhelmed rather than complemented. A crepe's beauty lies in delicate harmony; the peanut butter should whisper, not shout. Meanwhile, the French toast with fig preserve and brie showed considerably more promise, though transforming the preserve into a fig syrup could elevate it further. Cafe Monna stands tantalizingly close to becoming a neighborhood staple. The foundation is solid: excellent ambiance, reasonable pricing, and good bones in their menu. With minor culinary refinements—better ingredient balance and expanded savory options—this under-the-radar spot could easily transform into a repeat destination. The potential is clearly visible; they simply need to reach for it. **Rating: 3.5/5 stars**

**Mediocre Experience with Disappointing Wait Times** Visited during evening hours, so unable to comment on the view. Food quality was average—standard club fare without standout dishes. The chicken pot pie was the highlight, served in a deceptively large shallow bowl and well-prepared. However, the excessively long wait time for our meals significantly detracted from the overall experience, making the visit hardly worthwhile despite some decent options.

Disappointing Thai Cuisine Despite Good Service This restaurant delivers possibly the worst Thai food experience, despite excellent service from staff with limited English. The cuisine leans more Chinese than authentic Thai, with consistently disappointing dishes. The pork ribs contain excessive fat, while the broccoli chicken tastes suspiciously microwaved—crunchy vegetables paired with flavorless meat. Eggrolls have an unpleasant plastic-like taste, and the rice is unacceptably soggy. The only redeeming qualities are the Thai Tea and Thai Iced Coffee, which are worth returning for exclusively. Overall, the tasteless food overshadows the attentive service.

Budget Vegas: The Quad Delivers Basic Comfort Despite Construction Chaos The Quad Resort offers an eye-opening lesson in getting exactly what you pay for. As my friend aptly described our room's location: "Make a left at the first hole in the wall, then pass the two pee stains, straight down to the third dirty door to your right." This colorful description unfortunately captures the property's aesthetic challenges. ## Construction Complications The resort currently undergoes extensive construction, making navigation frustrating—especially after a few drinks, though that admittedly added some comedic value. While the completion timeline remains uncertain, the transformation promises to be impressive once finished. ## Check-In Nightmares Despite arriving second in line, we endured a 30-minute wait while three staff members stood idle nearby. Our heavy bags made this particularly aggravating. Three days later, departing guests faced even longer lines with visibly irritated expressions. The property's decision to staff only two check-in agents simultaneously seems inadequate for guest volume. ## The Bottom Line For budget-conscious Vegas visitors unconcerned with aesthetics, the Quad serves its purpose adequately. The rooms, while requiring creative directions to locate, feature genuinely comfortable beds—a crucial amenity that shouldn't be overlooked. **Recommendation:** Choose the Quad if you prioritize savings over ambiance and can tolerate construction inconveniences and slow check-in processes. The comfortable sleeping arrangements provide some redemption for the property's operational shortcomings.

Mixed Experience with Sears: Great Price, Frustrating Process While Sears' general pricing tends to be higher than competing department stores, we discovered an exceptional deal on wall-style air conditioner installation that ultimately proved worthwhile, despite significant challenges. The installation journey required approximately 10 phone calls, with representatives frequently transferring us between departments without resolution. Communication breakdowns were common throughout the process. We paid $50 for an initial measurement visit for our existing wall opening, which seemed reasonable. The most confusing aspect involved purchasing our AC unit from another retailer, as Sears had suggested. This created substantial confusion among their staff, with one representative questioning how Sears would be compensated for installing equipment purchased elsewhere—apparently not understanding their own installation fee structure. Despite these frustrations, persistence eventually paid off. Once we navigated through the communication obstacles and helped their team understand our requirements, the installation was completed successfully. The final cost was thousands of dollars less than competitor quotes, representing significant savings. **Bottom line:** Sears offered unbeatable installation pricing, but expect to invest considerable time and patience managing their customer service process. The financial savings may justify the aggravation for budget-conscious consumers.

**Disappointing Second Visit - Won't Return** My second salon experience was extremely disappointing. The staff member was pushy and rude, prompting me to leave without receiving any service. I have no plans to return anytime soon.

From Five Stars to One: A Doughboy's Disappointment My relationship with Doughboy's started wonderfully. Their pizza genuinely impressed me—the crust, while heavier than traditional styles, perfectly complements their generous toppings. Their 12-inch two-topping pizza for eight dollars provides two solid meals, and the ground sausage they pile on is absolutely delicious. Their wings also deserve praise. However, one disastrous experience completely destroyed my loyalty. After ordering through their website—a method I'd successfully used for months—I waited an hour and a half with no delivery. When I called to inquire, I was met with shocking attitude from the staff member who insisted I'd used the website incorrectly.
