On a positive note, having a Starbucks conveniently located right by the room elevators was a welcome amenity. The customer service deserves special recognition. When questioning what appeared to be an extra charge after checkout, the front desk staff handled the situation excellently. They were extremely polite, responded quickly, and patiently walked through the billing details, demonstrating professional and courteous service.

Sushi Roll Paradise Perfect for Girls Night Looking for a pre-club dining spot? This sushi haven delivers! My girlfriends and I indulged in a fantastic sushi roll feast with perfectly balanced rice ratios. The fresh nigiri impressed, but the star of the evening was undoubtedly the yellowtail collar – absolutely delicious! The combination of quality food and lively atmosphere makes this an ideal girls night out destination. We'll definitely return before our next club adventure.

**Prime Canal-Side Dining with Standout Guacamole** This restaurant's unbeatable Grand Canal location offers front-row seats to gondolas and singing gondoliers. The surprisingly excellent guacamole steals the show with its bold cilantro flavor—definitely worth ordering despite the chip refill charges. While the chicken enchiladas were decent but unremarkable, the attentive service and reasonable prices make this spot worthwhile. Come for the scenic ambiance and stay for the guac. The combination of location and value makes it a solid choice for a casual meal with a view.

A Solid Upscale Casual Choice at Crystals Visited on a Tuesday evening and found this to be an excellent upscale casual dining option. The atmosphere strikes the right balance, with a patio area overlooking Crystals mall that's perfect for people-watching. The booths are comfortable, though they're unusually deep—eating feels a bit like dining on a couch, which is somewhat quirky. The food truly delivers. Both the veal scallopini and chicken piccata were excellent, with generous portions that justify the price point. Friends have also endorsed their brunch service. Pricing is reasonable considering the prime Crystals/CityCenter location. As a bonus, locals enjoy 20% off or complimentary dessert through September's end. Overall, this is a reliable choice for quality food in a pleasant setting. Definitely worth a return visit.

Mediocre Montreal Chinese: Consistently Underwhelming Another disappointing Chinese dining experience in Montreal. We skipped the city's top-rated Vietnamese restaurant to eat here—a decision we regretted. The food was utterly average: neither offensive nor impressive, just forgettable. While we didn't get food poisoning, that's hardly a ringing endorsement. Montreal's Chinese cuisine continues to underwhelm.

A Hidden Gem for Late-Night Study Sessions Finding Tasty Asian on Yelp proved challenging, but this casual eatery became our go-to spot after abandoning a disappointing Panda Express clone called Chop Chop. While the restaurant serves Chinese, Japanese, and Thai cuisine, we focused on Chinese dishes during our study break. The honey walnut shrimp surprised me with its heavily fried preparation, despite the waitress's misleading description. However, the hot and sour soup delivered satisfying flavors, and my friend's kung pao combination (chicken/shrimp/beef) packed enough heat to clear sinuses effectively. The atmosphere feels somewhat dingy, with most patrons opting for takeout rather than dining in. Despite the lackluster ambiance, Tasty Asian's proximity to our rental house and delivery service make it incredibly convenient for late-night study sessions. The diverse menu spanning three Asian cuisines offers plenty of exploration opportunities—I'm particularly interested in trying their curry next time. While not a destination restaurant, Tasty Asian serves its purpose well as a reliable, nearby option for hungry students needing fuel during marathon study sessions.

Fuzzy's: A Revitalized West Valley Gem Fuzzy's has undergone an exciting transformation, attracting a younger crowd and introducing entertainment like DJ nights and karaoke. The venue now boasts a cool vibe that was previously missing. The food impresses for budget-friendly bar fare—the Chef salad with balsamic vinaigrette is exceptional, and locals rave about their burgers being the West Valley's finest. While service can occasionally be sparse, the staff consistently makes genuine efforts and maintains friendly attitudes. This neighborhood spot successfully balances affordability, atmosphere, and quality eats, making it worth visiting for casual dining and entertainment.

Mixed Experience at Jay Cutler-Recommended Spot While the location proves convenient, situated next to LVAC and a tanning salon, this establishment falls short of expectations set by Jay Cutler's endorsement. The food quality is merely adequate—good but not exceptional—which wouldn't be concerning if complemented by better service. Unfortunately, customer service significantly detracts from the experience. Male staff members demonstrate courtesy and professionalism, but a female employee's rudeness and apparent unhappiness creates an uncomfortable atmosphere. The cleanliness standards are equally disappointing, with dirty tables requiring self-cleaning before seating. For patrons willing to pay premium prices expecting premium service, this location disappoints. The stark contrast between staff attitudes and poor maintenance suggests management issues. Unless improvements are made, Jay Cutler's recommendation seems misplaced for this underwhelming establishment.

A Delightful Sunday Lunch at Maggiano's: Exceptional Food, Service, and Value Our party of four recently enjoyed a wonderful Sunday lunch at Maggiano's that exceeded all expectations. From the moment we arrived, the experience was seamless—we were seated immediately and attended by an exceptionally efficient waitress. The menu variety impressed us, with our group ordering lasagna, meatballs and spaghetti, and tortellini. Every dish arrived fresh, hot, and absolutely delicious, with generous portions that left us satisfied. The warm bread was promptly replenished throughout our meal. What truly set this experience apart was the pleasant ambiance—background music played at a comfortable volume that actually allowed conversation, a rare find these days. We concluded with excellent tiramisu for dessert. The cherry on top? Maggiano's generous take-home policy allowed us to select equal portions of different menu items, providing eight additional meals! This amazing value, combined with outstanding food and service, guarantees our frequent return.

Disappointing Lunch Experience: Time is Money As a business traveler seeking a quick lunch during my work trip, this establishment proved to be a significant letdown. What should have been a simple meal consumed my entire hour-long break, with a staggering 45-minute wait from payment to receiving food. The restaurant's business model appears fundamentally flawed for its location in a busy shopping center. The operational inefficiencies suggest management hasn't adequately prepared for the volume of time-conscious customers they attract. This isn't sustainable in today's competitive market. The food itself? Merely "OK." For basic sandwiches and salads – essentially romaine lettuce plates – the wait time is completely unjustifiable. To add insult to injury, I left with a stomach ache. While I appreciate this cuisine style and would prefer supporting this establishment during my visits, the time investment simply isn't worthwhile. Until they streamline their operations, I cannot recommend this location to fellow business travelers or anyone with time constraints.

A Hidden Gem with Room for Improvement: A First-Timer's Perspective Finding this establishment proved to be an adventure in itself—without GPS technology, I might still be wandering the streets like a modern-day Don Quixote. Once discovered, the upstairs bar revealed itself as an oddly shaped space that nonetheless exudes the comfortable atmosphere of a neighborhood regular haunt. It's the sort of place that attracts what we might call "dipsomaniacs in need of social interaction"—though aren't we all guilty of that from time to time? **The Beer Selection** The beer offerings present an interesting paradox. While the available selections show promise and intrigue, the diversity feels somewhat limited. More disappointingly, two beers I specifically wanted to sample were unavailable—a significant gap when your entire menu contains only twelve options. The establishment would benefit greatly from expanding their list to provide more variety and ensure better availability. **Service Experience** Behind the bar works a blonde bartender who maintains constant motion throughout her shift. However, the service style requires patrons to actively seek attention rather than receiving proactive check-ins. She appeared notably unfazed by the peanut gallery's attempts at humor—whether compliments, jokes, or reactions to the occasional dropped glass. One can sympathize with working under constant observation; it must feel like being displayed in an aquarium, minus the humidity. Additionally, her beer knowledge didn't suggest expertise at the level of a true brew enthusiast. **Final Thoughts** Despite these shortcomings, the experience proved enjoyable—time passed remarkably quickly. The promise of rotating selections and increasingly interesting beer offerings provides reason for optimism about future visits. However, the atmosphere doesn't particularly encourage spontaneous conversation with strangers, making it less ideal for solo visitors seeking social connection. For those already acquainted with regulars, though, it offers a comfortable drinking spot worth revisiting. **Rating: 3/5 stars**

**Great Value for Family Dessert Outings** This frozen yogurt spot is a family favorite, offering excellent value at around $10 for four people. The tart flavors provide a nice alternative to sweeter options, and fresh fruit toppings are a highlight. Everyone can customize their treat exactly how they want it. The only downside is the crowds, but the price and quality make it worthwhile.

A Filipino Buffet Worth Frequenting This Filipino buffet stands out from the competition for excellent reasons. While most establishments serve overly greasy, unappetizing food heavy on meat dishes, Nanay Gloria offers something different. The restaurant provides impressive variety, featuring seafood and vegetable options that many Filipino buffets lack—making it our family's top choice, with Kusina ni Loraine as a close second. The only drawback is limited seating capacity. Arriving during peak hours often means no available tables, which can be frustrating for eager diners seeking this quality dining experience.

Budget Stay with Major Safety and Quality Concerns This Wild Wild West property offers rock-bottom pricing at $22 per night, but numerous issues make it questionable value even at that rate. **Safety Concerns:** The location next to a truck stop creates significant security issues, particularly for female travelers. The reviewer notes suspicious activity around the property and explicitly warns women against staying here unless absolutely necessary. **Accommodations:** Rooms suffer from persistent musty, smoky odors that permeate the space. A cockroach sighting was reported, though the reviewer notes only seeing one instance of pest problems. **Amenities:** The casino floor is minimal, featuring just a few video gaming machines, a roulette wheel, and a craps table. The on-site Denny's restaurant experiences severe understaffing, resulting in extremely slow service. **Bottom Line:** This property serves its purpose as an emergency crash pad for budget-conscious male travelers who simply need somewhere to sleep. However, the safety concerns, questionable cleanliness, and uncomfortable atmosphere make it unsuitable for most visitors. Unless you're on an extremely tight budget with no other options, consider spending slightly more for a safer, cleaner alternative.

Disappointing Value at Premium Prices While the Aria provides a pleasant atmosphere and attentive service, the restaurant's pricing structure is utterly disconnected from the quality delivered. The $50 carne asada arrived shockingly underseasoned, tasting of little more than salt, with beans reminiscent of fast-food chains swimming in excess water. At $17, even the margaritas fail to justify their cost. The fundamental issue isn't merely that this isn't authentic Mexican cuisine—it's that dramatically superior food exists at a fraction of the price from local taco trucks. When a street vendor can outperform a luxury hotel restaurant at one-sixth the cost, something is fundamentally wrong. The service staff performed admirably, and the Aria itself remains a quality hotel, but the restaurant represents poor value that's impossible to recommend, regardless of who's paying.

Disappointing Stay Despite Some Bright Spots While the bellhop and check-in clerk provided excellent service, and the lobby and bar areas were attractive, this hotel falls short of expectations for its price point. The exterior is underwhelming, and the $13 daily parking fee near the dumpster is excessive. The rooms are disappointingly small with tiny beds and extremely firm mattresses. Bathroom space is also cramped. Adding insult to injury, WiFi is only complimentary in the lobby—rooms require an additional charge. The $12 breakfast buffet doesn't justify the cost, offering quality comparable to budget chains like Holiday Inn Express. At over $100 per night, this hotel doesn't deliver adequate value. Consider nearby alternatives for better accommodation.

A Punk Rock Paradise in Vegas: Double Down Saloon Lives Up to the Hype After reading about Double Down Saloon (DDS), I knew I had to experience it during my March Vegas trip. The promise of bacon martinis, Ass Juice, and a punk rock jukebox had me intrigued from the start. My excitement skyrocketed the moment I stepped out of the cab to hear the Disasters' "Warning! Warning!" blasting from the venue. Roger Miret is my hero, and this was the perfect welcome. The night exceeded all expectations with unforgettable moments: I debated Wolfgang Puck's sell-out status with a stranger at the bar, only to have his friends flash me twenty minutes later. I experienced the transcendent combination of Schlitz beer and a Slim Jim – honestly the best meal ever in that moment. My chair literally broke into pieces when I sat down, adding to the authentic dive bar charm. The jukebox offered five plays for just a dollar, and I spent my 4am hours getting wonderfully drunk on cheap drinks while the Dead Boys provided the soundtrack. **The Bottom Line**: If you're into upscale clubs like Pure, XS, or Tryst, stay away – you won't appreciate DDS. But for everyone else seeking an authentic, unpretentious punk rock experience in Vegas, Double Down Saloon is absolutely essential. This place delivers exactly what it promises and then some.

A Disappointing Dining Experience from Start to Finish My visit to this restaurant last Friday evening was unfortunately memorable for all the wrong reasons. Despite the establishment being barely 10% full, I was immediately questioned about not having reservations – a puzzling greeting when roughly 20 tables sat empty throughout the entire night. ## Ambiance Issues The patio, while promising in concept, suffered from a critical flaw: virtually no lighting. Multiple diners, myself included, struggled to read menus in the darkness. By evening's end, our table and those around us resorted to using cell phone flashlights just to see what we were ordering. Hardly the romantic atmosphere one hopes for during dinner. ## Beverage Disappointments The sangria was shockingly watered down, resembling white grape juice more than a proper cocktail, garnished with a single canned peach slice. Even the complimentary water had an unpleasant mildew smell, accompanied by dried-out lemon slices I avoided entirely. ## Appetizer Disaster My fiancé's Fiaggi Misti ($15) was perhaps the most disappointing course. This supposedly artisanal meat and cheese board featured what appeared to be Oscar Meyer-quality garlic bologna, fatty "soppressata," and minuscule portions of dried-out cheese. Most egregiously, store-bought breadsticks arrived still in their commercial packaging, wrappers intact, casually placed atop the arrangement alongside three lonely kalamata olives. ## Main Course Letdown I ordered the Toscana pizza well-done – a simple request that went unfulfilled. The pizza arrived undercooked with what tasted like discount supermarket ingredients: terrible mozzarella, soggy whole mushrooms, and bland sausage completely lacking the expected fennel flavor. The sauce resembled paste rather than anything fresh or flavorful. ## Service Failures With only two servers managing the entire restaurant, service predictably suffered. After requesting our check multiple times, we waited over 35 minutes before finally settling up. This experience has guaranteed we'll never return.

Hidden Gem: Authentic South American Cuisine Worth the Wait Tucked away in an unassuming strip mall lies this delightful South American restaurant that challenges preconceptions about suburban dining. What initially appeared to be a standard Mexican eatery revealed itself as a culinary journey through Peru, Ecuador, and Colombia. The arepas, tamales, and Peruvian carne asada all impressed with their authentic flavors. While service moves at a leisurely pace—courtesy of an unhurried older waiter—this relaxed atmosphere actually enhances the experience. The restaurant fills quickly despite its location, testament to its quality. For those adjusting to life outside major metropolitan areas, this spot proves exceptional food can thrive anywhere.

Exceptional Sushi Experience for a First-Timer This restaurant proved to be the perfect introduction to sushi. The outstanding service exceeded expectations, with attentive staff ensuring a flawless dining experience. Based on glowing reviews, this establishment delivers on its reputation. Highly recommended for both newcomers and sushi enthusiasts alike. A definite repeat visit destination.

Overall 3.5 Stars: A Mixed Sushi Experience While Yama excels in certain areas, it's not the top choice for traditional sushi—Sushi Coma takes that crown. However, Yama's rolls are notably delicious. The standout is their sweet shrimp: large, pristine, with perfectly fried heads. The uni impressed with its fresh, creamy texture, while the gyoza delivered satisfying crispiness and flavor. The major drawback? Extremely long wait times. Arrive early to avoid disappointment. **Bottom line:** Worth visiting for specialty items, but manage expectations and timing. Happy Sushiing!!

A Rich Experience at Au Pied De Cochon Food Truck Stumbling upon the Camion Au Pied De Cochon at Dorchester Square, I decided to sample their offerings: fried pork rinds with ranch flavoring and the infamous foie gras poutine. The pork rinds initially impressed me, reminiscent of sour cream and onion chips from my childhood. However, the novelty wore off quickly as the excessive saltiness became overwhelming. The foie gras poutine proved even more challenging. While I understand richness defines this establishment's identity, the dish was simply too heavy for my palate—I could barely manage four bites before admitting defeat. The silver lining? Both dishes cost under $8.50, making this an affordable culinary experiment. **Final Verdict:** This food truck caters specifically to those craving indulgent, heavy, and salty fare. If you prefer lighter, less adventurous cuisine, you'll want to skip this one. However, for adventurous eaters seeking authentic Québécois decadence on a budget, it's worth trying.

Totes Trend Balls - You don't have to be beautiful to drink here, but it helps..... This cocktail bar delivers city centre style without the pretentious attitude that often accompanies it. It's a genuine gem that deserves more frequent visits, prompting a personal vow to become a regular. The back bar is nothing short of spectacular, featuring an extensive cocktail list that showcases serious mixology skills. The Aged Juniper stands out as a must-try for adventurous drinkers. What sets this place apart is the knowledgeable yet approachable staff—they know their craft without being pretentious about it. The casual atmosphere extends to complimentary Oreos being offered to guests. Comfort is prioritized with oversized Moët & Chandon pillows scattered throughout, creating perfect lounging spots. The food menu complements the relaxed vibe, with nachos that may well be the town's finest—certainly the top hangover cure destination. The burgers also impress. The spacious outdoor area captures sunshine throughout the day, while sliding windows create an airy, open ambiance. Trendy yet unobtrusive music matches the service style perfectly—attentive without being intrusive. This establishment successfully combines quality cocktails, comfortable surroundings, and unpretentious service into one highly recommendable package.

A Hometown Gem with Heart Rocket Burger has become my regular haunt, drawing me back several times monthly—though I'd go more if I could. What keeps me returning isn't just the quality food, but the exceptional people behind the counter. The owners and staff create a welcoming atmosphere that transforms a simple meal into a genuine visit with friends. I strategically time my visits during off-peak hours, allowing unhurried conversations with the team. Their warmth and friendliness are unmatched anywhere. Whether you're seeking a satisfying meal or authentic human connection, Rocket Burger delivers both. Stop by, say hello, and experience this special combination of good food and even better people yourself.

Exceptional Salon Worth Traveling For This modern, glamorous salon boasts incredibly talented and friendly stylists who consistently deliver outstanding results. The reviewer has been a loyal client since June 2011, even traveling to Vegas specifically for appointments. Their stylist Brandon receives particular praise for his brilliant work, demonstrating the salon's ability to build lasting client relationships through exceptional service.

Finally Found My Perfect Brown: Deana Made the Impossible Possible After four unsuccessful attempts at going brunette, I had resigned myself to being blonde forever. Each previous experience left me with hair that was too dark, made me look washed out, or simply wasn't flattering. But boredom got the best of me, and I decided to give brown one last chance. Finding Deana on Yelp was a game-changer. She possesses all the qualities you want in a hair professional. First, she actually listens—asking thoughtful questions about my likes, dislikes, and previous disappointments. Second, her technical knowledge combined with an artistic eye proves she paid attention in beauty school. Third, her honesty ensures realistic expectations. Finally, her pricing is completely reasonable for the exceptional quality of work. The results exceeded my wildest expectations. For the first time ever, I'm not just satisfied with brown hair—I'm genuinely in love with it. Deana accomplished what I thought was impossible: making me feel confident and beautiful as a brunette. I'll absolutely be returning to Deana. She's truly exceptional!

**Mixed Feelings About Long-Awaited Playground Reopening** After nearly a year's delay, the newly renovated playground has finally opened its doors. While parents appreciate the cleaner appearance and improved safety features following completion of all renovations, the layout presents challenges for supervision. The design includes numerous hiding spots and blind spots, making it difficult to monitor multiple children simultaneously, which can trigger anxiety for caregivers. Despite these concerns about overcrowding and visibility issues, families continue to visit periodically. On a positive note, the facility hosts Saturday morning Ultimate Disc pickup games, offering additional recreational opportunities for the community beyond the playground itself.

Exceptional Auto Electronics Installation Experience I discovered this outstanding shop through a modest Craigslist posting and couldn't be happier with my decision. After speaking with Chase, the owner, I felt confident entrusting my brand-new Jeep (under 200 miles) for a DVD receiver installation. Chase's expertise in automotive electronics is truly impressive. His shop maintains impeccable cleanliness and organization, reflecting his meticulous attention to detail. With over 10 years of experience, his craftsmanship speaks for itself. This owner-operated business exemplifies what small businesses should aspire to be. Beyond electronics installation, they offer vinyl wrap services and have convenient partnerships with the neighboring tint shop. The pricing is competitive for both parts and labor, and Chase completed my entire installation—including sourcing the head unit—within three hours. The lifetime installation warranty provides exceptional peace of mind. The combination of superior workmanship, fair pricing, and outstanding customer service makes this shop my go-to recommendation. I've already referred several friends and will definitely return for future automotive electronic needs.

**Mixed Experience at This Rio Rib Joint** While the atmosphere delivers with TVs throughout and an impressive OCC Chopper display outside, the food falls short of expectations. Despite advertising from a famous cook, the baby back ribs were surprisingly dry—disappointing for a restaurant specializing in ribs. The service proved mediocre, neither particularly bad nor notably good. The venue works well for watching games with friends, but the ribs themselves don't live up to the hype. Worth returning if suggested by others, but not a destination worth seeking out specifically. The cool motorcycle outside remains the highlight of the experience.

An Unforgettable Anniversary Stay My husband and I celebrated our ten-year anniversary at this remarkable hotel, and it exceeded all expectations. After mentioning our special occasion in advance, the staff went above and beyond—surprising us with complimentary cupcakes and upgrading us to a room with spectacular city views. While compact, our room was immaculately clean and comfortable. The service throughout our stay was exceptional, with staff attentively addressing every concern. The hotel concierge deserves special recognition for being incredibly sweet and helpful with all our event planning needs. The highlight was undoubtedly the phenomenal breakfast buffet. The selection was incredible, featuring made-to-order crepes and fresh omelets that were absolutely to die for. Combined with the hotel's unbeatable location, this property offers everything you could want. We couldn't recommend this hotel more highly for couples seeking a memorable, special occasion getaway.

**Intimate Thai Gem Worth Revisiting** This cozy Thai restaurant delivers an exceptional dining experience with attentive yet unobtrusive service. The fresh, flavorful cuisine shines through excellent tapas selections and delicious curry dishes, complemented by an impressive wine list. The intimate atmosphere creates a welcoming environment perfect for newcomers to Thai cuisine. An excellent first impression that guarantees a return visit for anyone seeking quality Thai food.

Disappointing Service Overshadows Annual Tradition For years, my family and I have made visiting this Town Square Coffee Bean & Tea Leaf location part of our annual Las Vegas tradition. The walk from our Strip resort to this café has always been a pleasant combination of exercise and relaxation. Unfortunately, recent experiences have convinced me to find alternatives. While rising prices are concerning—$5.50 for a large hot Chai Tea Latte that arrived only lukewarm is hard to justify—the primary issue is the consistently poor service from one particular male barista who has worked there for several years. His condescending attitude and lack of customer service skills have become intolerable. During my most recent visit, I noticed signage encouraging customers to request samples of the new Pumpkin Latte. With only two customers ahead of us and none behind, it seemed like an appropriate time to ask. However, after receiving our original orders, the samples never materialized. When I politely inquired, the barista curtly responded that he was "moving as fast as he could" and needed to serve other patrons first—despite new customers having just arrived after our request. This interaction reminded me of equally unpleasant encounters during previous visits. His consistently dismissive demeanor and inefficient pace suggest someone unsuited for customer-facing roles. If sample offerings cannot be honored during slow periods, perhaps management should reconsider promotional signage altogether. It's disappointing that one employee's poor attitude can undermine what should be an enjoyable experience. Combined with increasingly high prices and lukewarm beverages, this location has lost a loyal customer. Management should seriously evaluate whether this barista's presence is worth the customers he's driving away. **Rating: ★☆☆☆☆**

A Wedding Disappointment: Lackluster Service at Applause Salon When planning my destination wedding, I carefully scheduled all beauty appointments six days before the ceremony. Excited to try my first shellac manicure and pedicure, I purchased a Groupon for Applause Salon, hoping for long-lasting results during my special week abroad. ## Groupon Mix-Up and Initial Concerns Upon arrival, staff informed me of a Groupon misprint—the deal only included a shellac manicure, not the pedicure I specifically wanted. After explaining this was for my wedding, they graciously honored the original offer, which I appreciated. ## Disappointingly Basic Service Unfortunately, the actual service fell far short of expectations. The manicure was essentially just polish application—my extremely dry skin received no moisturizer whatsoever. There was no hand or foot massage, which I understood to be standard for such services. The experience was as bare-bones as possible. ## Poor Results That Didn't Last While the shellac polish technically didn't chip, it began peeling from the top as my nails grew, separating noticeably from the cuticles. The pedicure fared even worse. Within days, the polish—which had been applied too close to the cuticles—started peeling faster than my fingernails. ## Final Verdict For a wedding where every detail matters, the results were far from the picture-perfect look I'd envisioned. The combination of minimal service, lack of basic moisturizing care, and polish that didn't maintain its appearance makes it unlikely I'll return to Applause for nail services in the future.

Hygiene Concerns Overshadow Otherwise Solid Experience As a regular Ra patron, I've always appreciated their consistency and vibrant atmosphere. This particular location started promisingly enough, though table cleanliness left something to be desired—smearing food around isn't exactly proper sanitation. The food quality remained excellent, meeting Ra's usual standards. However, what dropped my rating to two stars was a serious hygiene violation that I couldn't overlook. Upon leaving, I witnessed a sushi chef working completely bare-handed—preparing sushi, cutting vegetables, and handling ginger without gloves. Most disturbing was that management, staff, and waitresses either didn't notice or simply didn't care enough to intervene. While I remain a Ra enthusiast and will continue visiting their other locations, this particular establishment has lost my business until they address their food safety practices.

A Disastrous Dining Experience: Discrimination and Disrespect Last night's visit to this restaurant was, without exaggeration, the worst dining experience I've had in a decade. What should have been an enjoyable evening with friends turned into a nightmare of poor service, unprofessionalism, and what appeared to be discriminatory treatment. The problems began almost immediately with our first waitress, whose demeanor noticeably shifted once she realized we were a table of gay patrons. While I can't prove causation, the correlation between this realization and the subsequent decline in service quality was impossible to ignore. She actually left our table mid-drink order to attend to another table's request—an astonishing breach of basic service etiquette that we didn't even call her out on. The service deteriorated from there. Our appetizers took 30 minutes to arrive, and my beer was completely forgotten. When I politely inquired about my missing drink after waiting 15 minutes—a perfectly reasonable question—and when we mentioned wanting to wait for our final party member before ordering entrees, this was apparently considered "rude" behavior. What happened next was truly shocking. A new waitress appeared at our table, confused about why she'd been reassigned to us. Then a manager arrived and actually informed us that our original waitress had been removed because she claimed we were being rude! This revelation from management was not only unprofessional but completely inaccurate. We had been nothing but patient despite the abysmal service. We decided to cut our losses, finishing only our beers and appetizer before leaving. Apparently, there was an even more disturbing interaction with a second manager as we departed, though I'll leave those details to the others in my party who witnessed it firsthand. Bottom line: avoid this establishment entirely. The area offers numerous superior restaurants with better food, better service, and staff who treat all customers with equal respect and professionalism.

Mixed Experience at Busy Dog Park This dog park offers a tale of two experiences. During off-peak hours, it's a great facility for canine socialization. However, the 5-8 PM rush hour transforms it into chaos, with overcrowding and irresponsible owners leading to frequent dog and owner conflicts. The excessive drama ultimately drove this reviewer away. For a calmer alternative, they recommend Tempe's parks at Curry/College and S Mitchell/10th instead.

A Shadow of Paradise: When Fast Casual Becomes Barely Casual The transformation from Paradise Bakery to its current iteration represents more than just a rebranding—it's a cautionary tale of how cutting corners destroys customer experience. This establishment, once a beloved neighborhood gathering spot, has devolved into something barely distinguishing itself from a gas station convenience counter. ## The Basics Have Failed The fundamentals of restaurant operation are simply absent. No ice in the drink station. Dirty tables throughout the dining area. Unavailable highchairs for families. These aren't minor oversights—they're indicators of systemic neglect. When the basics fail, everything else crumbles. ## Food Quality in Freefall The menu offerings suggest a complete abandonment of culinary standards. Macaroni prepared from envelopes, pre-cut salad components resembling infomercial demonstrations, and chicken that appears to have been mishandled—all served without apparent pride or care. The staff themselves seem defeated, moving through their shifts with visible disengagement that reflects management's apparent indifference. ## Layout Logistics Nightmare The spatial design defies common sense. The main entrance forces patrons to navigate awkwardly around occupied tables in an already cramped dining room. The ordering queue lacks organization, creating bottlenecks and confusion. The drink station is positioned where customers must push through crowds, creating frustration at every turn. ## The Paradise That Was The original Paradise location near Grimaldi's and Cyprus Grill offered quality food in a comfortable, welcoming environment. That establishment understood what fast-casual should mean: efficiency without sacrificing quality, speed without abandoning hospitality. ## The Verdict This location represents everything wrong with cost-cutting corporate transformations. When businesses prioritize margins over experience, they create spaces customers actively resent. The comparison to a QuikTrip isn't hyperbole—it's generous. At least gas stations don't promise what they cannot deliver. **Rating: ★☆☆☆☆**

Disappointing Vegetarian Buffet Experience This restaurant falls short for vegetarian diners. The limited vegetarian curry options lacked flavor, while the white rice was undercooked and naan served cold. Both appetizers and desserts proved equally disappointing. Though the establishment seems geared toward non-vegetarian customers, a buffet format should offer quality options for all dietary preferences. Unfortunately, this venue fails to meet basic expectations for vegetarian cuisine.

Unacceptable Response to Customer Concern I discovered a large bug in my iced coffee and reported it to management. Instead of apologizing, the manager essentially accused me of lying, insisting it couldn't have come from their store. While they offered a replacement drink, their dismissive attitude and refusal to take responsibility was appalling. Their indifference to losing a loyal customer speaks volumes about their priorities. I'll be taking my business to Starbucks across the street from now on. Sometimes paying a bit more is worth it for proper customer service and quality control.

Decent Food Overshadowed by Smoke-Filled Environment This establishment offers surprisingly good bar food and attentive service, but the oppressive smoking atmosphere makes it nearly unbearable. The so-called non-smoking section is ineffective, as smoke continuously drifts over from the overlooking bar area, creating a thick fog throughout the dining room. It's alarming how many families frequent this restaurant despite the heavy secondhand smoke exposure. While the quality of food and service are commendable, the health concerns associated with constant smoke inhalation cannot be ignored. Patrons leave smelling like stale cigarettes, which is unacceptable for a dining experience. **Update:** Though now smoke-free, the restaurant still fails to merit a return visit, suggesting other lingering issues remain.

**Budget-Friendly Post-Strip Dining with In-House Brews** This no-frills establishment offers an unbeatable $5.99 steak and eggs special—perfect for refueling after a night on the strip or at the tables. While this deal isn't prominently displayed on the menu, servers will happily accommodate your order when requested. The atmosphere is casual and straightforward, so don't expect fine dining service. However, at prices comparable to fast food, it's an incredible value for money. The real bonus is their in-house brewed beers, available for just a couple dollars each—ideal for washing down your hearty, greasy meal. This spot delivers exactly what it promises: satisfying carnivore fare and decent craft brews without breaking the bank. It's the perfect combination for late-night cravings.

**A Delightful Dining Experience in Las Vegas** This restaurant delivers on all fronts with exceptional service and delicious food. The chicken parmesan sliders are so impressive they inspire culinary dreams. Beer enthusiasts will appreciate the extensive selection and tasting flight options. While the tempting desserts went untasted due to generous portions, the overall experience exceeded expectations. Best of all, it's refreshingly affordable by Las Vegas standards.

Rude Service Turned Dining Experience into Disaster Reviews often complain about long wait times at this establishment, but my wife and I didn't even get the chance to wait for food. Our experience ended before we could order. After being seated at the only well-lit available table, we were ready to place our order when our waitress, Mayra, abruptly informed us we were at the "wrong table." She demanded we move to accommodate a party of three who had just arrived—without a single "please," "excuse me," or "sorry." Had she shown basic courtesy, we would have cooperated. However, the threesome she prioritized turned out to be picking up takeout, not dining in. When I expressed our preference to leave instead, Mayra curtly stated this was a "community restaurant," implying our reaction was somehow unreasonable. We stood to go, and someone informed Mayra the other party was indeed there for takeout. This should have prompted an apology and perhaps a complimentary drink, but she offered nothing. The lack of professionalism and basic customer service was astounding. We left hungry and disappointed, never to return.

Solid Halal Spot with Generous Portions I've visited twice now, and both experiences were consistently good. The chicken shawarma plate impressed with its generous size, freshness, and overall taste, though I wished for slightly bolder seasoning. Pricing is fair and reasonable. The poutine was decent, nothing extraordinary but satisfactory. A significant advantage is that everything on the menu is halal. My wife, a Concordia alumna, has particular affection for this establishment. The combination of quality food, fair prices, and halal options makes this a reliable choice. Will definitely return for future visits.

Quick and Affordable Windshield Repair at Techna After getting a brand new windshield replacement in California, disaster struck on the drive home when a rock chipped the fresh window. Following frustrating phone tag with various repair shops, we visited Techna for an in-person quote. The result was impressive: just $22 and fifteen minutes later, the chip was virtually invisible. Techna delivered exactly what every customer wants: excellent service combined with fast turnaround time. When you need windshield repair without the hassle or high cost, this is clearly the place to go. Their efficiency and affordability make them stand out from the competition.
Fresh and Healthy Choice Usually get the oriental chicken salad with fried chicken but decided to go with grilled chicken. Just as good if not better. Healthier too. Friendly service as well.

Delightful Japanese Lunch Experience I recently enjoyed lunch here with a co-worker, where we both ordered bento boxes and iced teas. The food arrived promptly and was absolutely delicious, while the service struck the perfect balance of being friendly yet unobtrusive. At approximately $25 for two before gratuity, the value was excellent. The restaurant's transformation is impressive – the décor is simple and elegant, creating a welcoming atmosphere. This part of the Valley desperately needs more Asian dining options, and I'm hopeful this establishment will thrive. I'm already planning my return visit to try their ramen bowls. A promising addition to the neighborhood!

Exceptional Dining Experience - Even Better the Second Time Around This restaurant continues to impress with divine cocktails, excellent cuisine, and outstanding service. Highly recommended for a memorable meal.

Comfortable Suburban Stop with Minor Fitness Room Issues We chose this La Quinta for our return trip from New Mexico, and it provided a pleasant break from the road. After two weeks in the secluded high desert, the suburban Las Vegas setting was quite a transition, though our dog appreciated the well-maintained lawn areas surrounding the property and nearby strip malls. The hotel delivered on the essentials: friendly staff, clean accommodations, and generally well-maintained facilities. However, the fitness center had some drawbacks. The gym equipment showed wear, with the elliptical being particularly unstable to the point of being unsafe. The exercise room's proximity to the pool also created an uncomfortably humid environment. Despite these minor fitness facility shortcomings, the hotel met our needs for a convenient, pet-friendly stopover. We'd consider staying here again on future trips.

A Disappointing Experience That Doesn't Live Up to the Hype After seeing numerous appealing photos from other Yelpers, I had high expectations for this establishment. Unfortunately, my visit was a letdown in nearly every aspect. ## The Food Falls Short I ordered the Mushroom Swiss burger, which turned out to be genuinely the worst burger I've encountered. The presentation was unappetizing—a grease-soaked bottom bun literally swimming in excess oil. While everything appeared freshly made, freshness alone couldn't compensate for the lack of flavor and poor execution. The sides were equally disappointing. The sweet potato tots arrived mushy rather than crispy, and the onion rings were completely bland. Even the chef-recommended sauces failed to enhance the meal in any meaningful way. The overall impression was of mediocre bar food that hadn't been thoughtfully prepared. ## Service Issues Compound the Problem Our server seemed disinterested from the start. She allowed our food to sit in the kitchen for five minutes while socializing at the bar, then barely acknowledged us afterward. We received attention only twice during our entire meal, while the neighboring table's server checked on them approximately eight times. The disparity in service quality was striking and frustrating. ## Final Verdict With countless burger restaurants along Scottsdale Road, I'm genuinely puzzled by this establishment's popularity. If you're seeking quality food and attentive service, I'd recommend exploring other options. This place simply doesn't deliver on its apparent reputation.

Disappointing Dealership Experience Despite Quality Vehicles While Toyota vehicles remain excellent, this particular dealership consistently fails customers with unprofessional service. Multiple visits revealed rude salespeople who lack basic courtesy. Management demonstrates poor judgment in promotional decisions and handles customer feedback terribly—hanging up on polite complaints is inexcusable. The combination of consistently poor salesmanship, questionable marketing choices, and dismissive customer service makes this location impossible to recommend. Toyota buyers deserve better treatment and should consider alternative dealerships for their purchases.

Disappointing Stay Marred by Poor Service and Staff Attitude This budget-friendly Las Vegas hotel proved that low prices can come at a significant cost to guest experience. While expectations were appropriately modest given the rate, the pervasive negativity among staff members was impossible to ignore. The front desk experience set a troubling tone, with employees speaking hurriedly and providing inadequate directions that resulted in confusion finding the room. The Adventure Dome staff appeared equally disengaged, displaying visible annoyance when guests attempted to purchase activities like rock climbing and bungee jumping for children. Additional disappointments included overpriced food that failed to deliver value, a non-functioning in-room coffee maker, and overall cleanliness issues throughout the facility. The overwhelming sense that employees despised their positions created an uncomfortable atmosphere that overshadowed any savings. While budget accommodations naturally involve compromises, basic courtesy and functional amenities should remain standard. This one-night stay was memorable for all the wrong reasons, making a return visit entirely unappealing.

A Warm, Family-Style Breakfast Experience at Lo-Lo's Lo-Lo's charm lies in its exceptional staff and welcoming atmosphere. During our visit, we practically enlisted help from every team member, and their accessibility created a genuine down-home family feel that made the experience special. The mason jar presentation, particularly for the nostalgic kool-aid, added delightful character to the dining experience. As a vegetarian, I found the menu somewhat limited, but the staff's willingness to accommodate was outstanding. Their suggestion to add pecans to my waffle transformed it into something extraordinary. My companions raved about their chicken and waffles, though the grits didn't impress everyone. The true star, however, was the banana pudding—an absolute standout that everyone agreed was perfectly executed. Lo-Lo's succeeds through attentive service and comfort food done right, making it worth visiting despite some menu limitations.

Disappointing Experience with Poor Communication I'm extremely disappointed with this office's lack of communication and customer service. We waited 45 minutes for my daughter's appointment without any notification about delays. The medical assistant was unhelpful, simply stating we were "next" rather than providing realistic wait times. We ultimately left due to another commitment. Any patient waiting over 10 minutes deserves to be informed about delays so they can make informed decisions about rescheduling. This basic courtesy was completely absent. Customer service should be a priority in healthcare. We're now searching for a new provider who values patients' time.

Not Worth the Wait: A Disappointing Stop on the Way to XS My experience at Tryst was purely obligatory - a required hour-long layover before gaining entry to XS nightclub. Unfortunately, those sixty minutes felt longer than necessary. The venue itself is disappointingly small and shows its age. The layout is poorly designed, creating congestion at every turn. The dance floor was impossibly packed, making it nearly unusable. The patio, which could have provided relief from the crowded interior, was equally underwhelming - frankly, a joke. While spending an hour here allowed our group of six to eventually access XS (which proved vastly superior), Tryst on its own merits offers little appeal. The cramped quarters and outdated atmosphere make it difficult to recommend unless, like us, you're using it as a stepping stone to better venues. Consider it a necessary inconvenience rather than a destination.

THE WORST EXPERIENCE EVER! Our nightmare with United Airlines began the moment we landed in Phoenix from our vacation in Cabo San Lucas. What should have been a straightforward 7:50pm departure to San Francisco turned into an hours-long ordeal of constantly changing gate times - first 11pm, then 11:15pm, 11:30pm, and eventually midnight. The lack of clear communication was frustrating enough, but the customer service we encountered made everything exponentially worse. When we finally found someone at the desk, hoping to explore alternatives since we lived an hour south of SFO and had work the next morning, we were met with shocking rudeness. The agent dismissed our concerns about not getting home until 3am or later, rolled her eyes, and offered absolutely no assistance when we inquired about reasonable solutions like switching flights, flying into San Jose, or staying overnight to catch the 6am flight. Ironically, this same unhelpful agent somehow managed to get us onto a US Airways flight departing just 30 minutes later - though in a different terminal with tickets we weren't even checked in for. While we appreciated escaping the delay, the entire experience left us bewildered and frustrated. The combination of poor communication, constant delays, and exceptionally rude customer service has ensured we'll never fly United again. When you're exhausted from travel, basic courtesy and problem-solving assistance shouldn't be too much to expect.

Disappointing Decline at Once-Promising Establishment After a year and a half of patronage, this restaurant has unfortunately taken a turn for the worse. The food quality hovers at merely average while prices remain slightly elevated compared to other local, independent breakfast and lunch spots in the area. Consistency issues plague the kitchen, with dishes regularly arriving overcooked and dry across both breakfast and lunch services. The dining area's cleanliness leaves much to be desired, creating an uninviting atmosphere. Most concerning was my recent visit where, despite being greeted and told to "sit anywhere" in a mostly empty restaurant, I waited 20 minutes without any server acknowledging my presence. This level of inattentiveness is simply unacceptable. With superior dining options available just a few miles away in Queen Creek, I cannot recommend this establishment and won't be returning. **Rating: ★☆☆☆☆**

Authentic Irish Flavors in a Cozy Contemporary Setting Dublin O'Neil's delivers genuine Irish pub fare with notable gastro-pub touches, despite its compact space and occasional service challenges. The standout dish is their extraordinary lamb shepherd's pie—truly exceptional. The cream-based seafood chowder and homemade soda bread are equally impressive. Strong menu choices include curried sweet potato chips with sour cream, perfectly battered fish and chips, and solid burgers. Fresh Guinness on tap complements the authentic experience. The Irish contemporary décor and traditional music create an appealing atmosphere for genre enthusiasts. However, be aware: the small space gets loud when crowded, and service can lag during peak times. Visit during off-hours for optimal comfort. While lacking traditional pub coziness, Dublin O'Neil's compensates with quality food that makes it worth seeking out. **Website:** http://dublinoneils.com/

Mixed Experience at Tequila Bar While this establishment boasts an extensive tequila selection, the offerings lean heavily toward margarita-friendly options rather than sipping tequilas. Service proved uneven, with our bartender showing noticeably more attention to other patrons. The nachos failed to impress, falling short of expectations. However, the salsa stood out as a highlight, delivering excellent flavor that partially redeemed the visit. Overall, a decent but unremarkable experience that leaves room for improvement.

A Heavenly First Indian Food Experience at Mount Everest India's Cuisine After reading glowing Yelp reviews, I decided to take the plunge into Indian cuisine for the very first time at Mount Everest India's Cuisine. Wanting to make it a memorable experience, I brought two friends along to share the adventure. ## Excellent Service from the Start From the moment we walked in, we were impressed by the quick and prompt service. The staff was incredibly kind and attentive, helping us navigate the menu and accommodating our needs without hesitation—a huge plus for first-timers like us. ## A Feast for the Senses We decided to order a variety of dishes to share: prawn curry, chicken biryani, garlic naan, and an extra spicy chicken biryani. When the food arrived, the aromatic smells were absolutely intoxicating! **The garlic naan** was an absolute standout—buttery, perfectly seasoned, and literally melting in my mouth. It was so incredible that I ordered a second round without hesitation. **The prawn curry** delivered just the right level of spice with deep, rich flavors. The portion was generous enough for all three of us to enjoy. **The chicken biryani** featured tender chicken pieces nestled in fragrant, flavorful rice—definitely going on my repeat order list! ## Final Verdict My inaugural Indian restaurant experience exceeded all expectations. Mount Everest India's Cuisine has earned a loyal customer, and I'm already planning my return visit to explore more of their menu!

Mixed Feelings at I-Bar: Great Drinks, Questionable Entertainment The I-Bar offers a peculiar nightlife experience with lingerie-clad dancers performing on elevated platforms to'90s throwback music—literally above patrons' cocktails. While the atmosphere may feel overly provocative for some, the drinks are genuinely impressive. The "Delightful Kiss" cocktail lived up to its name, and the bartender's choice proved adventurously strong. Despite the awkward entertainment setup, the quality cocktails make this spot worth revisiting. The reviewer humorously suggests equal-opportunity eye candy, though admits that might require a Chippendale's ticket instead.

A Theater Where Rudeness Reigns Supreme This establishment represents a perfect storm of poor customer service and management indifference. The staff's rudeness is matched only by inconsiderate patrons, creating an atmosphere resembling "a social experiment" in human behavior at its worst. Operational failures abound: broken ticket machines force customers into chaotic lines where basic queue etiquette is abandoned. Management's cavalier attitude—opening new windows only to serve newcomers while laughing at original waiters—demonstrates stunning disrespect. The reviewer aptly notes this behavior "would not be tolerated at a Regal movie Theater," highlighting how far below industry standards this venue falls. Unless studying terrible service interests you, avoid entirely.

A Step Above Most Fast Food Chains When dietary restrictions force you to skip the cheese curds and frozen custard at this Wisconsin-born chain, you learn to appreciate what remains. Despite having to avoid dairy, this reviewer finds value in Culver's straightforward burger offerings. The burgers themselves deliver on quality, tasting authentically beef-forward without the fillers common to typical fast food establishments. The buns, while containing butter (which fortunately doesn't trigger the reviewer's dairy sensitivity), fall into a middle ground—superior to standard fast food fare but not quite reaching the heights of premium burger joints like Fez or Grind. The reviewer notes the restaurant's overt Christian identity, though considers it a minor issue easily circumvented via the drive-thru. The focus remains on the food rather than the atmosphere. While Smashburger ranks as an equally appealing alternative, convenience often dictates the choice. When a coworker volunteers for the pickup duty and prefers Culver's, the decision becomes easy. The verdict? For those seeking fast food with noticeably better ingredients and preparation, Culver's delivers a satisfying experience. Even with menu limitations due to dietary concerns, the quality justifies the visit, making it a reliable option when quick, decent food is the priority. **Rating: Recommended for quality-conscious fast food seekers**

A Dissenting Voice: Why Dos Reales Doesn't Live Up to the Hype While Dos Reales enjoys popularity for its convenience, affordability, and friendly service, this reviewer finds the food disappointing. The meat quality is questionable, supposedly spicy sauces lack any real heat, and refried beans dominate nearly every dish. The menu suffers from redundancy, with tacos, burritos, and tamales tasting remarkably similar. Regular entrees outperform the specials, though even the carne asada tacos fall short of authentic expectations. The restaurant's pink and orange sponge-painted walls exemplify its underwhelming ambiance. Despite Dos Reales' devoted following and its advantages of proximity to campus and reasonable prices, this diner recommends exploring alternatives like El Charro or Los Amigos for a more satisfying Mexican dining experience. Sometimes popular doesn't mean best. **Rating: ★★☆☆☆**

**LOUD!** Girasole's defining characteristic? The deafening noise level that requires shouting across the table. This small, cramped space delivers quick, attentive service and slightly above-average food—I had the greens and beans with Cappa Santa—but nothing memorable enough to justify the cacophony. The cuisine simply doesn't warrant enduring such discomfort. My recommendation? Stick to takeout if you're curious, but dining in feels more like an endurance test than an enjoyable meal.

**Mixed Feelings About This Drive-In Classic** While the nostalgic drive-in concept appeals in theory, the practical experience often falls short. The food isn't particularly car-friendly, which detracts from the overall enjoyment—though that's hardly Bar-B-Q King's fault. On the positive side, the car hops provide helpful and friendly service, and the food itself is genuinely delicious. The dipped chicken features a unique sauce that bridges buffalo and BBQ styles. It's definitely worth visiting, but locals might want to consider takeout instead of the full drive-in experience to better enjoy the quality food without the hassle.

Excellent Service Despite Understaffing We visited during the Bears vs Panthers game weekend and found the scheduling questionable—only one waitress on a packed Saturday afternoon with Chicago visitors everywhere. However, our server Olivia was absolutely amazing, expertly handling our party of 20 with food and drinks. The food was good and the atmosphere super fun. We returned that evening and enjoyed a great live band. Despite management's scheduling oversight, Olivia's exceptional service made our experience memorable. Highly recommend asking for her!

**A Drunken Disappointment That Fails the Ultimate Test** When food tastes terrible at 3 AM while intoxicated, you know there's a serious problem. This establishment serves what can only be described as inedible fare – featuring squeeze cheese masquerading as Swiss. After one bite, the hot dog went straight into the garbage. The pictures speak volumes. Other reviewers are being far too generous about this truly nasty experience.

Consistently Poor Management and Service This Toys-R-Us location exemplifies everything wrong with retail mismanagement. Multiple visits revealed persistent problems: chronically understaffed checkout lines, inadequately trained employees, and dismissive attitudes during returns. Management appears absent when issues arise, leaving customers frustrated and unsupported. The store's declining standards make it clear why competitors like Walmart and Target are winning customers. This is unquestionably the worst Toys-R-Us location encountered. Save yourself the aggravation and shop elsewhere—this store has earned its zero-star reputation through consistently terrible experiences.

A Disappointing Buffet Experience at Planet Hollywood Our visit to the buffet at Planet Hollywood was unfortunately marred by numerous issues that left us thoroughly disappointed. Despite seeing mixed reviews, we decided to give it a try, only to encounter problems from the moment we arrived. The experience began poorly with a frustrating 45-minute wait, even though empty tables were clearly visible throughout the dining area. The delay seemed to stem from inadequate coordination between the cleaning staff and front-of-house personnel, who couldn't get tables turned over efficiently enough to accommodate waiting guests. Once seated, service continued to be problematic. Our waiter was conspicuously absent, while we observed other sections receiving attentive care, including hot towels with lemon—amenities apparently reserved for other diners. This inconsistency in service was disappointing and made us feel undervalued as customers. The food quality fell significantly short of expectations. The Chinese station was particularly underwhelming, appearing to lack authentic consultation or preparation. The seafood selection, which featured the standard Vegas buffet offerings of shrimp and snow crab legs, was disappointing in both quality and quantity. The crab legs were notably thin with minimal meat content, hardly justifying their inclusion. Throughout the dining area, cleanliness was a significant concern. Food spills remained uncleaned around various stations, and we encountered pasta that had congealed into an unappetizing clump, impossible to serve properly with the provided tongs. At $70 including tip, the experience felt like poor value. We left early with upset stomachs—not from overindulgence, but from frustration and the subpar food quality. We won't be returning to this establishment.

A Dream Destination for Interior Design Enthusiasts Slate Interiors has earned its place as one of my top five destinations for browsing home décor, and for good reason. This treasure trove offers an impressive array of art, furniture, and accessories that inspire endless decorating possibilities—whether you're envisioning a serene beach retreat, cozy mountain cabin, or sleek contemporary space. **The Merchandise** The selection here is truly exceptional. From unique tables and lamps to chairs, chandeliers, and distinctive home accessories, there's always something special waiting to be discovered. The mid-century pieces deserve particular mention—they're fantastic finds, though they disappear quickly. With constantly rotating inventory, each visit feels like a fresh shopping adventure. Fair warning: if something catches your eye, purchase it immediately. I've learned this lesson the hard way after losing several coveted items by deciding to "think about it." The local art collection is particularly noteworthy, with wonderful pieces overflowing throughout the space. Interestingly, these tend to linger longer than furniture items. Most booths feature well-curated, beautifully arranged inventory, though a few could benefit from refreshing. **Pricing and Service Considerations** While most items are reasonably priced, the pricing structure occasionally seems inconsistent. The staff generally maintains a friendly demeanor, but I encountered disappointing customer service when a pricing error occurred. After purchasing what I believed was a set, I received a call explaining the tag was incorrect—the price was per item, not for the pair. When offered the choice to pay more or return the items within 24 hours, I found this resolution unreasonable given their mistake and my cross-town location. Despite this hiccup, Slate Interiors remains a beloved shopping destination worth visiting.

Delightful Cupcakes with Friendly Service I sampled their cupcakes and was thoroughly impressed. The strawberry cake with strawberry icing and lemon combination were both delicious—perfectly balanced sweetness that wasn't overwhelming, though I wouldn't have complained either way. The staff was exceptionally friendly, engaging in pleasant conversation while helping me choose flavors. I'm eager to return and explore their other offerings. Regarding the $8 price for three cupcakes that surprised my friend—as a New Yorker, I found it reasonable. Back home, that might only get you two! The quality justifies the cost.

Consistently Excellent Farmhouse Experience A loyal customer who has followed this restaurant through multiple locations raves about their consistently delicious food. They've never encountered a disappointing meal, highlighting both breakfast and lunch as standouts—with breakfast being particularly exceptional. Despite the small space occasionally requiring a wait, the reliable service and quality cuisine make it worthwhile every time.

Stunning Ambiance Can't Salvage Disappointing Holiday Buffet Experience The Wicked Spoon presents a frustrating paradox: breathtaking interiors housing mediocre food at premium prices. During my Christmas visit, the experience began poorly with a staggering three-hour wait starting at 3pm—a warning for anyone expecting convenient holiday dining. ## The Good Credit where it's due: the venue itself is spectacular. The clean, fresh aesthetic matches the upscale pricing, and the buffet's sheer size is impressive, though attempting to sample everything proves futile (we tried and failed). The standout items included perfectly roasted vegetables, delicious premade salads, and exceptional shrimp cocktail featuring impressively large, juicy specimens. The smoked salmon delivered quality, albeit predictably. Desserts provided redemption with gorgeously plated offerings—cheesecakes, mini cakes, soft serve, chocolate-covered strawberries, fruit tarts, and coveted giant macarons. Snagging a chocolate macaron briefly elevated my spirits, though they disappointingly ran out during my second visit. ## The Mediocre to Bad Unfortunately, premium pricing didn't translate to premium execution. The beef wellington and poke salads were merely acceptable. Sausage and stuffing (slightly dry) met basic expectations. The sushi proved particularly disappointing—while rolls were adequate, the nigiri appeared sloppily assembled, falling short of the "fancy" standard they're attempting. The real failures? Christmas goose arrived unacceptably dry. Both snow and king crab legs—buffet highlights anywhere else—were oversalted and tough from overcooking. Most egregiously, the flan was inedible after one bite, shocking given it's typically my favorite dessert. ## The Verdict Perhaps Christmas operations stressed their kitchen beyond capacity, but shouldn't holiday service exceed normal standards rather than fall short? The premium holiday pricing (increased throughout the Christmas-New Year's week) makes these failures particularly inexcusable. Unless you're specifically drawn to the ambiance and willing to gamble on food quality, numerous better-value options exist elsewhere. **Rating: 2/5 stars**
Authentic Mexican Cuisine - A New Favorite Spot Excellent service and delicious authentic food make this outstanding Mexican restaurant worth visiting repeatedly.

POOL DRINKERS BEWARE!!!! - A Cautionary Tale I learned my lesson the hard way at the Paris Pool. Despite previous disappointing experiences, I returned only to encounter abysmal service from an inattentive waitress who was consistently absent when needed. The situation deteriorated when I requested my change after paying cash. She claimed it was "customary" for servers to automatically keep all change as a tip - an audacious assumption given her poor service quality. The experience reached a disturbing low when I overheard her boasting to a coworker about spitting in my drink after I asked for my money back. This went beyond poor service into completely unacceptable and potentially health-hazarding territory. Such behavior is not only unprofessional but also grounds for serious health code violations. Pool-goers should be extremely cautious about food and beverage service at this establishment.

Mixed Experience at Hard Rock Hotel: Service Inconsistencies and Location Challenges My six-day stay at the Hard Rock Hotel revealed significant inconsistencies in service quality and amenities. While bellhops and housekeeping staff were excellent, other aspects fell short of expectations. **Accommodation Issues:** The casino tower beds were particularly disappointing, and even newer towers suffered from subpar bedding. Room service proved unreliable, botching my breakfast order two out of three mornings. A crucial tip: request rooms away from the bowling alley suite—the noise level is unbearable. Additionally, internet connectivity was frustratingly poor throughout my stay. **Dining Options:** Restaurant experiences varied considerably. While Restaurant 35 delivered decent quality, Nobu disappointed with overpriced, underwhelming dishes. Culinary Dropout, though a welcome addition, suffered from inconsistent service matching the hotel's overall pattern. **Final Thoughts:** Despite friends enjoying the HRH and Paradise Tower rooms' updated aesthetics, I found myself missing the Cosmopolitan multiple times daily. The hotel's remote location compounds these issues, making it inconvenient for exploring Las Vegas. I have no plans to return.

**A Solid Family Dining Experience Worth Repeating** This restaurant delivered a pleasant first visit with excellent, attentive service from their friendly waitstaff. The family-friendly atmosphere was enhanced by a kids-eat-free promotion, making it budget-conscious. The Caesar salad impressed, while the Hawaiian pizza proved satisfying, if not exceptional. The combination of good service, welcoming environment, and decent food quality creates an overall positive experience that earns return visits. A reliable choice for family dining outings.

Mixed Experience at Big Fat Greek While the service shines and the flaming feta presentation impresses, the food falls short of Phoenix's better Greek offerings. Portions are generous, but the gyro tends to be dry, beer selection is mediocre, and pita bread is merely acceptable. The standout? Lemon potatoes—absolutely delicious and worth ordering in large quantities. **Rating: 2/5** The combination of attentive service and those exceptional lemon potatoes saves this from a lower score, despite underwhelming main dishes.

An Unwelcoming Experience at Fleur: A Missed Opportunity Our eagerly anticipated dinner at Fleur turned into a disappointing ordeal before we even sat down. Despite arriving merely four minutes early for our confirmed reservation—booked specifically to accommodate pre-show plans—we encountered inexplicably poor hospitality that left us feeling genuinely unwelcome. The host, fully aware of our reservation, presented us with an unreasonable ultimatum: either squeeze into the crowded happy hour bar area and order small plates, or leave the premises and return in exactly four minutes. This rigid response seemed particularly absurd given the restaurant was already open and operating. Rather than tolerate such inhospitable treatment, we chose to dine elsewhere and enjoyed a lovely meal without any reservation drama. While we'd looked forward to experiencing Fleur's cuisine, this unfortunate encounter has effectively removed it from our future dining considerations. In a city brimming with welcoming alternatives, there's simply no reason to return where guests are treated so dismissively.

Disappointing Breakfast Experience: All Hype, No Flavor With high expectations for their signature chicken and waffles, this restaurant unfortunately failed to deliver. While presentation was impressive with towering plates arriving promptly, the execution fell flat. The chicken, though moist, suffered from completely bland breading lacking basic salt and pepper seasoning. The waffle had an unappetizing chewy texture, and the fried leeks scattered across the plate resembled "bushcut grass," serving no culinary purpose. The corned beef hash concealed literally blackened potatoes underneath, while the eggs arrived disappointingly cold and tasteless. For $45, this breakfast was an expensive letdown. The potential exists here—with proper seasoning and cooking techniques, this could be a different story. However, the current reality is all presentation with no substance. Save your money and look elsewhere for quality breakfast. Until they address these fundamental cooking issues, this establishment remains style over substance.

Disappointing Experience at a High-Profile Steakhouse After eagerly anticipating this visit for a month, my experience at Tom Colichio's establishment fell short of expectations. As a devoted Top Chef fan, I had high hopes that weren't met. The evening started promisingly with excellent rolls and wine while we waited for our entrees. However, the main course proved disappointing. I ordered a filet medium-well, while my companions chose other cuts. Upon returning from the restroom—absent only 8 minutes—I found my steak lukewarm. Initially attributing this to my brief absence, I learned my friend's medium-rare steak was similarly cool, indicating a kitchen issue rather than timing. The side dishes were mixed: potatoes were delicious, but asparagus merely adequate. Given the premium pricing and celebrity chef reputation, this performance was unacceptable. For superior steak at better value, I recommend the Las Vegas Hilton steakhouse instead. I won't be returning. **Rating: ★★☆☆☆**

Authentic Italian Gelato with a Personal Touch The Lombardo family brings genuine passion to their gelato craft, operating three spotless kiosks throughout Valley malls. Their attention to detail shines through, from the authentically bilingual Italian-English signage to the consistently warm service that greets every customer. With approximately 18 rotating flavors, the selection reflects both traditional Italian roots and creative regional flair. Recent offerings showcased seasonal favorites like mango and tangerine alongside adventurous Southwestern-inspired choices including horchata and prickly pear. Classic gelato enthusiasts needn't worry—beloved standards like vanilla bean, chocolate, coffee, and sweet cream remain available. The daily-changing menu keeps each visit fresh and exciting, as the Lombardos personally decide what to prepare. West valley residents are particularly fortunate, with two convenient locations nearby. This family-run operation successfully combines Old World authenticity with accessible mall convenience.

Decent Thai with a Spicy Kick, But Expect Long Waits Le Thai's popularity comes with a price—literally in time spent waiting. A 45-minute lunch wait speaks to their following, though it may test your patience. The menu offers straightforward Thai cuisine without creative twists, which works fine for traditionalists seeking familiar flavors. A crucial warning: their curries run significantly spicier than typical Thai restaurants. What's usually a level 3-4 elsewhere translates to a blazing level 1 here, thanks to their particularly hot curry base. While all curry varieties deliver good flavor, the heat level catches unsuspecting diners off-guard. The restaurant falls short when compared to Pin Kaow, which offers more generous portions and that satisfying "comfort food" quality Le Thai lacks. If you're willing to wait and can handle serious spice, it's decent—but perhaps not worth the hype.

A Promising Coffee Experience with Vintage Charm This cozy café offers a delightful atmosphere that's worth visiting for ambiance alone. The mokaccino was satisfying, though not extraordinary. The interior design steals the show with its creative use of antique sewing machine tables and overall vintage aesthetic that creates a warm, nostalgic environment. While the beverage was enjoyable, a full culinary experience remains untested. The inviting atmosphere and unique décor suggest there's much more to discover. Based on the coffee quality and exceptional ambiance alone, this establishment earns a solid four-star rating, with potential for more once the full menu is explored.

Great Deal with Quality Food and Service We visited this restaurant using a Groupon for their prix fixe three-course meal, which proved to be an excellent value with numerous menu options. Despite not feeling well, I opted for safer choices—chicken entrée and quesadilla appetizer—both of which were quite tasty. The chicken came with a unique papa-style side dish that perfectly bridged chips and French fries, absolutely delicious! My husband enjoyed fresh and flavorful ceviche and steak, both served in generous portions. Our server deserves special mention for his politeness and entertaining banter throughout our meal, never making us feel like "just Groupon customers." The overall experience exceeded expectations, combining quality food, ample servings, and attentive service. We definitely recommend this establishment.

Disappointing Experience with Poor Service Extremely unsatisfactory visit marked by unfriendly staff, subpar food quality, and uncomfortable dining conditions. The lack of air conditioning during summer was unacceptable. Would not recommend or return to this establishment.

Not Worth a Special Trip While the Marché Bonsecours building itself is architecturally beautiful and benefits from its prime Old Montreal location, the actual market falls short of expectations. The vendors primarily sell artisan goods that feel more like browsing through items you'll never actually use than discovering genuine treasures. Unless you're specifically interested in artisan crafts, this isn't worth visiting as a standalone destination.
