Her responsiveness to lengthy emails—often replying late at night—and her ability to answer every question thoroughly demonstrated genuine commitment to her clients' vision. As hospitality industry professionals themselves, the couple recognized the rarity of such exceptional service. ## Flawless Execution The entire staff proved to be attentive listeners, gracious hosts, and accommodating to every request. On the wedding day, every detail exceeded expectations: outstanding food, seamless beverage service, energetic entertainment, delicious cake, and perfect ambiance. Most impressively, if any issues arose, the couple remained blissfully unaware—allowing them to fully enjoy their celebration. ## Lasting Impressions The ultimate testament to TPC Summerlin's excellence? Guests continue declaring it the best wedding they've ever attended. For couples seeking a stress-free, perfectly executed wedding day, this venue and team deliver an experience worth celebrating long after the last dance.

Outstanding Valentine's Day Experience My wife and I celebrated Valentine's Day here and were thoroughly impressed. The restaurant excels in every aspect—stunning landscape design, beautiful interior and exterior, and nearly flawless service. The food quality was excellent, complemented by meticulous attention to detail that creates a uniquely elegant yet comfortable atmosphere. Whether you're local or visiting the area, I highly recommend this establishment. It's an experience well worth your time and will exceed expectations!

Authentic Spanish Gem in Edinburgh This recently opened tapas restaurant on Brougham Street delivers an exceptional dining experience. Located in a cozy space opposite Realfoods, it serves homely, authentic Spanish tapas with genuine passion and warmth. The food is delicious, the service impeccable, and the atmosphere welcoming. Our dinner party hasn't stopped raving about it since. Currently Edinburgh's finest tapas destination – an absolute must-visit for food lovers seeking authentic Spanish cuisine.

Best Value Pizza in Pittsburgh Don't let the shabby interior and old wooden booths fool you—this Oakland gem serves incredible $5 large pizzas that defy expectations. Whether it's a late-night craving, lunch break, or quick dinner, this place delivers exceptional value without sacrificing quality. Unlike typical cheap pizza joints, their pies are high-quality and incredibly tasty, not greasy or unhealthy. The somewhat drab setting becomes irrelevant when you're enjoying what's arguably Pittsburgh's best pizza value. Five stars earned purely on merit: delicious, affordable pizza that consistently satisfies any time of day.

Mixed Experience at Vegas Buffet: Breakfast Trumps Lunch As a buffet enthusiast who values variety over volume, this reviewer found their lunch experience at this Vegas establishment somewhat disappointing compared to previous visits. **The Good:** The shrimp cocktail, stir fry station, noodles, hot entrees, and cold salads all delivered satisfactory quality. **The Bad:** The dessert selection proved lackluster, notably lacking any ice cream options and featuring only uninspiring pastries. The snow crab also had an off-putting taste. While the $20 price point offers reasonable value considering the extensive options available, the reviewer believes superior buffets exist nearby. Their recommendation? Stick with the breakfast buffet at this location, which apparently offers significantly better quality. For indecisive diners seeking the ultimate Vegas buffet experience, this might not be your top choice for lunch.

Disappointing Visit to Celebrity Chef's Establishment I ordered the turkey, avocado, bacon and mayo sandwich, which was supposed to include onions but arrived without them—an omission that would have significantly improved the dish. While my husband and I appreciate quality food and understand premium pricing, this experience fell short of expectations. At $24 for one sandwich, a lukewarm bottled soda, Kettle Chips, and a banana, the value proposition seemed questionable. The food was certainly better than Subway, but that's a low bar for a celebrity chef-owned restaurant. Unfortunately, it didn't deliver the elevated experience one would anticipate given the pedigree. The overall impression was merely "okay"—not terrible, but unremarkable enough that I'm unlikely to return for another visit.

Exceptional Dining Experience at Twin Creeks Twin Creeks delivered an outstanding evening from start to finish. Our server Joey provided impeccable service, demonstrating genuine enthusiasm when recommending wines that proved to be excellent choices. Every course impressed, beginning with exceptional bread service and continuing through expertly prepared appetizers—the scallops and Kobe beef carpaccio were both delicious. The bone-in rib-eye was cooked to perfection, while the filet mignon equally satisfied. Don't miss the truffled potatoes; they're essential ordering. The generous portion sizes, including massive steak fries, added great value. Twin Creeks combines quality cuisine with attentive service for a truly memorable dining experience worth repeating.

Mixed Experience: Great Food, Unprofessional Atmosphere While the food quality was excellent, the overall experience fell short due to disappointing service and unprofessional behavior. Most concerning was observing a chef drinking beer with patrons outside, then continuing inside while giving staff directions. Watching him invite customers for shots at the bar was particularly off-putting. The lack of professionalism significantly detracted from an otherwise promising meal.

A Trusted Veterinary Partner for Two Years and Counting When I welcomed my Puggle puppy Bailey into my home, I was navigating the exciting yet overwhelming world of new pet ownership. The pet store provided a list of local veterinarians and offered to cover any necessary treatments if I visited within a week or two. Family Vetcare was the only option in Ahwatukee, and I'm grateful that convenience led me to what has become our trusted veterinary home for the past two years. ## First Impressions Matter From our very first visit, the welcoming atmosphere stood out immediately. The staff treated both Bailey and me with genuine warmth and professionalism. What really caught my attention were the photographs throughout the office—pictures of pets with their owners. I soon realized these weren't just any clients; they were photos of the staff members with their own beloved animals. This personal touch demonstrated that the people caring for my puppy truly understood the pet owner experience firsthand. ## Navigating Early Health Challenges That initial appointment revealed my adorable new puppy had kennel cough and intestinal worms—concerning news for any new pet parent. Fortunately, the pet store's coverage included all necessary medications. However, Bailey's persistent cough required daily nebulization treatments for an entire week. The convenience of dropping her off on my way to work and picking her up on my way home made this intensive treatment schedule manageable. Throughout this challenging period, the staff consistently showed genuine enthusiasm when seeing Bailey, and their sincere care provided reassurance during a stressful time. ## Consistent Quality Care Over two years of regular visits, Family Vetcare has maintained the same high standards of friendliness, helpfulness, and compassionate care. Their consistency has made veterinary visits stress-free for both Bailey and me. I even utilized their boarding services once, shortly after her treatments concluded. Being a new pet owner without time to research alternatives, I appreciated that Bailey would stay somewhere familiar with staff she already knew. While the boarding experience was perfectly fine, I eventually discovered that my energetic Beagle-Pug mix thrives better with the more active environment provided by Malinda's doggy daycare. ## A Grateful Pet Owner I remain thankful that the pet store directed me to Family Vetcare. They've been instrumental in Bailey's health and well-being throughout her early years. Their genuine love for animals, professional expertise, and consistent quality care have made them our veterinary home. As a final note: regardless of where Bailey came from, every dog deserves a safe, loving home. I'm proud to have given her that, and Family Vetcare has been an essential partner in keeping her healthy and happy.

A Solid Choice with Mall-Adjacent Compromises Social House delivers a respectable upscale dining experience in Las Vegas, though its location proves to be its biggest drawback. Nestled within a mall, the restaurant's ambiance suffers from constant views of shoppers, gamblers, and the bustling tourist crowds. The culinary offerings are genuinely impressive. Fresh ingredients and skillful preparation characterize every dish, earning a solid four-star rating on food quality alone. While nothing was particularly groundbreaking, the kitchen consistently delivers well-executed plates. Service meets expectations without exceeding them—competent and professional, though unremarkable. The interior attempts to create a cozy, upscale Asian atmosphere, which partially succeeds. Unfortunately, the open veranda design exposes diners to the mall's sterile environment, creating an uncomfortable juxtaposition. Sitting near this boundary between refined restaurant and commercial retail space significantly diminishes the overall experience. In Las Vegas's competitive culinary landscape, Social House represents an above-average option rather than a destination restaurant. It's perfectly acceptable if circumstances bring you here, but the city offers superior alternatives worth exploring for those with flexibility in their dining plans.

Hidden Gem: Secret Seafood Congee Shines This restaurant's off-menu seafood congee is absolutely stellar, featuring fresh fish, octopus, scallop, and shrimp in perfect harmony. However, skip everything else on the menu—the congee is the only dish worth ordering to avoid disappointment.

Delicious Return to Zink - Worth the Wait! After years away from Zink since its uptown location, I'm thrilled I finally returned. Our party of 13 received excellent lunch service, and every dish impressed. From flatbreads to sandwiches, everything satisfied. My roasted chicken was exceptional, and the mac & cheese side dish was fantastic—absolutely worth ordering again! The consistently delicious food across our diverse orders and attentive service for our large group made this a memorable experience. I'm already planning my next visits!

Zero Stars: A Quarter-Century Vegas Resident's Worst Dining Experience After living in Las Vegas for over 25 years, I've experienced countless restaurants, but this establishment delivered the most disappointing service I've encountered. Our fried rice arrived over 30 minutes after our entrees, despite repeated inquiries to our elusive waiter who only offered empty promises of "it's coming." Adding insult to injury, we watched other patrons—who arrived after us—receive their rice dishes promptly. The disparity in service was so pronounced that I couldn't help but wonder if racial bias played a role, as we felt virtually ignored throughout the evening. The food quality matched the service level. While appetizers were passable, my braised chicken was disgracefully sweet and syrupy—resembling candied slop more than a proper entrée. **Verdict: Will never return.**

Intimate Entertainment Venue with Excellent Service The Shimmer Cabaret at the LV Hilton offers a charming, intimate setting for live entertainment. This small theater creates a welcoming atmosphere that enhances any performance experience. **Seating and Layout** The venue features an eclectic mix of standalone chairs and seats with small bistro-style tables. Thanks to the compact size, virtually every seat provides an excellent view of the stage, ensuring no guest misses the action. **Service Quality** Cocktail servers continuously circulate throughout the space, making drink orders convenient and wait times minimal. This attentive service adds to the overall comfort of the experience. **Versatility** The venue demonstrates impressive flexibility, quickly converting between different show formats. The efficient stage crew can transform the setup from comedy performances to live band configurations seamlessly. **Final Verdict** While the quality of your visit ultimately depends on the scheduled performer, the Shimmer Cabaret itself provides an excellent foundation for an enjoyable evening with its intimate atmosphere, attentive service, and quality sightlines throughout the space.

Perfect Movie Theater for Parents This theater excels with cleanliness and comfort, but the real game-changer is their childcare service. For just $6 per child, parents can enjoy adult films worry-free while kids are supervised. It's a brilliant concept that transforms the moviegoing experience for families. The reviewer jokes that adding wine service would make it absolutely perfect for parents seeking a relaxing night out.

A Mexican Food Haven in Las Vegas This establishment has earned its place as the ultimate destination for authentic Mexican cuisine in Las Vegas. Having sampled every item on the menu, I can confidently say the quality is consistently exceptional across the board. The star attraction is undoubtedly the adobada tacos, which are absolutely heavenly and perfectly portioned. What sets this place apart is their innovative customization option – any menu item can be transformed into loaded fries, carne asada style. The adventurous menu doesn't disappoint, with standout items including the adobada tacos topped with pineapple, flavorful buche tacos, and surprisingly delicious tripe tacos. This is my go-to spot for impressing visiting friends, and I find myself returning time and again. Simply put, you can't go wrong here.

Clean and Convenient Airport with Good Amenities While unable to access the monorail as a Hawaiian Airlines passenger, this airport impresses with its cleanliness and easy navigation. Friendly staff enhance the experience, and there's ample entertainment via slot machines during wait times. The dining options are plentiful, including the essential Starbucks. Despite the monorail limitation, it's a great airport overall with convenient facilities.
Flavorful Wing Sampler Delights the Whole Family Queen City delivers a winning wing sampler with perfectly balanced sauces and bold flavors that satisfied both adults and children alike.

Budget Strip Hotel Falls Short on Amenities and Quality This no-frills establishment offers rock-bottom prices but delivers a correspondingly lackluster experience. The property lacks basic amenities like a fitness center or complimentary breakfast. Rooms are cramped, and the overall atmosphere feels dated and questionable. While conveniently located mid-strip, it only suits extremely budget-conscious travelers willing to overlook quality and comfort for savings.

A Disappointing Return: Tropicana's Remodel Falls Short After a lackluster experience at the old Tropicana years ago, I decided to give this property another chance based on reports of an extensive remodel and upgraded four-star rating. Unfortunately, what I encountered was essentially lipstick on a pig—or as I'd describe it, a velvet hat on a pig. **The Good** The improvements begin and end at the front entrance. The valet staff was genuinely friendly and welcoming, and the newly redesigned lobby is undeniably beautiful and chic. It sets expectations high for what's to come—expectations that are quickly dashed. **The Bad** Service quality plummeted immediately at check-in. The front desk clerk was disengaged and uncommunicative, responding to questions about the remodel with terse, single-sentence answers. More frustrating was learning about the $26 daily resort fee despite both the pool and fitness center being closed. What exactly was this fee covering? Elevator access? **The Room Reality** The guest room revealed the true nature of this "remodel." Windows are covered with a perforated film that prevents photography—likely concealing outdated windows behind decorative shutters that are difficult to operate. The bathroom features bargain-bin tile from Home Depot that's already chipping, surrounding an old bathtub and shower enclosure. New wallpaper and towel holders can't disguise the aging infrastructure. **Final Verdict** This multi-million-dollar remodel feels superficial at best. The supposed four-star rating is baffling—I'd generously rate this property 2.5 to 3 stars maximum. The Tropicana created an attractive facade while neglecting meaningful improvements to guest experience, service quality, and room conditions. Save your money and book elsewhere; there are far better values on the Strip.

A Disappointing Decline: Mandalay Bay Falls Short of Former Glory Mandalay Bay, once my favorite Las Vegas destination, has sadly deteriorated beyond recognition. A recent weekend visit with friends revealed shockingly filthy accommodations—hair-strewn sheets and visibly aged furnishings desperately crying out for renovation. The checkout experience proved equally frustrating. Despite 5-6 staff members handling registrations and several others inexplicably idle in the background, we endured a grueling 20-minute wait. Each guest transaction consumed approximately 10 minutes, creating unnecessary bottlenecks. While express checkout exists, billing discrepancies forced me into the interminable queue. The buffet experience epitomized the hotel's overall decline. The dinner service was absolutely nasty, featuring warm snow crab that should have been chilled—a basic food safety concern. This culinary catastrophe perfectly symbolizes Mandalay Bay's fallen standards. What was once a premier destination has become a shadow of its former self, plagued by poor maintenance, inefficient service, and substandard dining. I cannot recommend this property until significant improvements are made. **Rating: ★☆☆☆☆**

A Disappointing Decline After 15+ Years of Loyalty As a devoted patron of Richardson's for over 15 years, writing this review pains me deeply. Something has fundamentally changed at this establishment, and not for the better. Our recent visit was marked by numerous disappointments. Our server pressured us three times within the first ten minutes to order entrées, despite having already ordered appetizers and being content with wine and conversation. The timing was completely off—salads arrived after our main courses. My tilapia was drowning in a watery, flavorless sauce that bore no resemblance to the quality I'd come to expect. The wine service was particularly troubling. After breaking the cork, rather than opening a fresh bottle, our server pushed the crumbled cork into the wine, capped it with a different cork, and suggested we take it home. Nearly $300 for four people to endure this experience feels like a betrayal of years of loyalty. Unless multiple trusted sources confirm significant improvements, I'm afraid our patronage has ended.

Mixed Experience at HRH Towers: Excellent Service, Room Issues After switching rooms twice, we finally found satisfaction at HRH Towers. **Avoid smoking rooms** - they're in poor condition. However, the staff truly shines here. Front desk and tower personnel are awesome and genuinely care about guests. Pro tip: treat them respectfully and you'll receive excellent service. We tipped housekeeping daily, and our third room was immaculate. The spa is outstanding and a definite highlight. Despite initial room problems, we love it here. **Major downside:** WiFi is terrible and needs improvement for modern travelers' connectivity needs.

**Solid Thai-Chinese Spot with Great Value** This restaurant offers excellent Thai and Chinese cuisine at reasonable prices with generous portions. The flavors rival Thai BBQ, with some dishes even surpassing it in taste. While the food quality is impressive overall, there's a noticeable tendency to use excessive oil in preparation—though this is a common issue at many restaurants. Despite this minor flaw, it's a reliable choice for satisfying, well-priced Asian fare.

A Coffee Snob's Haven with a Time Trade-Off This establishment has become my go-to spot for exceptional coffee. As someone with high standards for espresso drinks, I'm consistently impressed by their technical execution. Their cappuccinos feature perfectly foamed milk—a detail that separates amateur baristas from true professionals. The quality never disappoints, and I've never experienced any concerning aspects of the atmosphere. However, I'm withholding that fifth star due to frustratingly long wait times. While I appreciate craftsmanship, the time required to receive an 8-ounce beverage feels excessive. Having worked in coffee service in a quality-focused environment abroad, I know excellent coffee doesn't necessarily require such extended preparation periods. Given their substantial customer volume, investing in additional equipment or staff would significantly improve the experience. The coffee itself deserves five stars, but the inefficient service process prevents me from giving an unreserved recommendation. If you have time to spare, you'll be rewarded with outstanding coffee.

Disappointing Service Overshadows Decent Food This restaurant visit was marked by inexplicably poor service despite adequate staffing. While three servers chatted idly in the back, one overwhelmed server and busser scrambled to handle all customers. A simple draft beer took over 10 minutes and required a reminder. The burgers were merely adequate—good but not memorable. Water refills never materialized. With numerous superior dining options nearby, there's no compelling reason to return. The glacial pace and inattentive service made this experience frustrating and forgettable.

A Restaurant Week Experience Gone Wrong Our restaurant week visit was unfortunately a letdown from start to finish. While the wine selection and stuffed mushrooms were enjoyable bright spots, the main courses fell dramatically short. The steak arrived dry and completely flavorless, while the taco platter disappointed with only one of three tacos having any discernible taste. We left most of our food untouched. The service matched the food quality—substandard throughout. The hostess barely acknowledged our arrival, setting a concerning tone. Our waitress seemed perpetually confused and disengaged. When inquiring about gluten-free options, she appeared clueless and left us waiting fifteen minutes while searching for answers. Most troublingly, she walked away mid-conversation while I was asking another question, appearing dazed and inattentive. When declining a to-go box for our largely uneaten meal, explaining the food "isn't very good," our server seemed genuinely shocked—perhaps the most authentic reaction we received all evening.

A Sushi Experience Gone Wrong: Why This Restaurant Lost a Customer Forever When a restaurant fails on multiple fronts simultaneously, it creates an experience so memorably bad that customers vow never to return. This establishment managed to disappoint on every conceivable level across two separate visits. ## First Impressions Matter The initial lunch visit should have been the warning sign. When your sushi chef cannot properly construct a basic sushi roll—arguably the fundamental skill of the position—something is seriously wrong. Loose, falling-apart rolls demonstrate either inadequate training or complete lack of care. Either scenario is unacceptable. ## Service That Defies Logic The second dinner visit revealed systemic problems. Waiting fifteen minutes for an order form while watching later arrivals receive immediate service suggests either incompetence or deliberate neglect. Neither explanation inspires confidence. The timeline speaks volumes: over an hour for three rolls at an all-you-can-eat establishment defeats the entire concept. ## Cleanliness Concerns Perhaps most alarming were the hygiene issues. Massive dust accumulation visible on televisions naturally raises questions about areas customers cannot see. If public-facing surfaces receive such neglect, what conditions exist in the kitchen? The visibly filthy prep area confirmed these fears weren't unfounded. ## Professionalism Abandoned Staff tensions playing out before customers represents complete professional failure. Customers paying $53 for minimal food deserve attentive, courteous service at minimum. Instead, they received indifference from the chef and attitude from the waitress. ## The Bottom Line This review reflects justified outrage. Between incompetent food preparation, glacial service, concerning cleanliness standards, and unprofessional staff behavior, this restaurant accumulated failures that individually would disappoint but collectively become inexcusable. The dramatic declaration about not allowing even a dog to eat there, while hyperbolic, effectively communicates total loss of trust in this establishment's ability to provide safe, quality dining.

A Novel Dining Concept That Falls Short on Execution Heart Attack Grill offers a unique atmosphere with its medical theme and parody posters, creating an amusing dinner environment, though it feels somewhat sterile. The gimmicky hospital gown requirement, while entertaining in concept, proves problematic in practice—inconsistent service leaves some guests receiving assistance while others fend for themselves. The food delivers mixed results. The single burger earns praise for quality, but the disappointingly lukewarm fries detract from the experience. Service lacks polish, with a scattered waitress and staff constantly using iPads, creating an impression of disorganization despite potential efficiency benefits. While the novelty factor initially attracts curious diners exploring Fremont, the execution doesn't warrant repeat visits. The combination of inconsistent service, average food quality, and gimmicks that feel more chaotic than charming makes this a one-time experience rather than a dining destination. **Overall: 3.5/5 stars**

A Tale of Two Visits: From Promising to Disappointing Sometimes a restaurant experience can vary so drastically between visits that it feels like you've entered two completely different establishments. Unfortunately, this French-inspired restaurant in Pittsburgh exemplifies this phenomenon perfectly, transforming from a promising destination into a disappointing experience that left us questioning whether we'd return. ## The Promising First Visit Our initial encounter in late 2011 set high expectations. We were greeted by a charming server with an authentic French accent whose enthusiasm was contagious. He spent a good five minutes walking us through the specials with genuine passion for the cuisine. As vegetarians, we appreciated how accommodating the staff was, preparing an excellent custom pasta dish since vegetarian options were limited on the menu. The French onion soup, also made vegetarian upon request, was absolutely delicious. The bread service particularly impressed us – crusty, warm, and accompanied by an exceptional salty butter that elevated the simple pleasure of bread to something memorable. The quality of the food justified the steep prices, which we'd offset with a Groupon. Everything from the service to the food quality suggested this was a restaurant worth returning to, so when another Groupon became available, we didn't hesitate to purchase it. ## The Disappointing Return Our second visit last week painted an entirely different picture. The atmosphere had deteriorated noticeably – holes in the ceiling went unrepaired, and without air conditioning on an 80-degree day, the dining room felt uncomfortable and stuffy. These physical shortcomings might have been forgivable if the service had maintained its previous standard, but unfortunately, it had declined dramatically. Our server this time seemed better suited for a busy diner than a restaurant charging $20 per pasta dish. Her curt "know what you want yet?" replaced the warm, engaging service we'd experienced before. When we requested a vegetarian pasta option, her doubtful response – "well...the chef is very busy, I'll have to check" – stood in stark contrast to the enthusiastic accommodation we'd received previously. The kitchen eventually prepared another excellent vegetable pasta with noticeably fresh produce, and our appetizer of caramelized onion, brie, and goat cheese tarts was genuinely delicious. However, the service failures continued mounting: forgotten bread that required flagging down another server, and being told they were out of both desserts we wanted to try. We weren't alone in our disappointment – we overheard other patrons complaining about their service that evening. ## The Bottom Line Having worked in the service industry myself, I understand that off nights happen. However, when a restaurant positions itself as an upscale dining destination with premium pricing, the service, atmosphere, and attention to detail must match those aspirations. The contrast between the warm, professional service of our first visit and the indifferent, forgetful service of our second was jarring. Pittsburgh offers many excellent restaurants where $20 will buy you not only great food but also attentive service in a well-maintained space. Skip the Groupon for this place and explore those alternatives instead. You'll likely enjoy better value and definitely receive better treatment. **Rating: 2/5 stars**

A Dealership That Earned My Trust Through Exceptional Service After sustaining a serious back injury, I faced the heartbreaking decision to trade my beloved 2013 Scion tC for a more accessible vehicle. What could have been a stressful experience became remarkably smooth thanks to this outstanding dealership. My journey began with online research, where I submitted an inquiry about a used vehicle. Jose responded promptly and professionally via email, and we efficiently coordinated an appointment over the course of a day. His helpfulness, reassuring demeanor, and genuine approach made all the difference during this difficult transition. The dealership's cleanliness and inviting atmosphere immediately put me at ease. Jose's honest and professional service throughout the process was exceptional. Having previously earned my trust through their service department, they've now proven themselves equally reliable in sales. This experience exceeded my expectations so thoroughly that I'm enthusiastically recommending them to family and friends. When you need a dealership that combines professionalism with genuine care, look no further.

Declining Quality and Poor Customer Service This nail salon has severely deteriorated from previously acceptable to completely unacceptable. The treatment of an 11-year-old customer was particularly troubling—the technician was dismissive and rude when she expressed discomfort during her service. The resulting gel manicure was poorly executed, with a lumpy application that began chipping within just three days. For the premium prices charged, customers deserve professional service and quality results. With numerous superior alternatives available nearby, there's no reason to patronize this establishment. The combination of declining workmanship, poor customer relations, and overpricing makes this salon impossible to recommend.

A Thrift Store Worth the Journey: Red White & Blue Exceeds All Expectations For thrift store enthusiasts, finding that perfect shop can feel like discovering hidden treasure. Red White & Blue isn't just another secondhand store—it's a destination worth traveling for, even if that means a 31⁄2-hour drive. ## Unbeatable Pricing and Payment Details The store's most remarkable feature is its permanent 50% discount on everything. However, shoppers should come prepared with cash, as credit cards aren't accepted. ## Quality and Organization Unlike typical thrift stores with musty odors and questionable merchandise, Red White & Blue maintains impressively high standards. The clothing smells fresh and clean, with most pieces in flawless condition. Items showing wear are priced accordingly, ensuring fair value. The inventory is thoughtfully organized by color and type, though not by size. The selection spans multiple style categories: casual wear, professional business attire, and trendy teen fashion. Plus-sized shoppers will appreciate the dedicated section carefully separated for easier browsing. ## Designer Labels at Fraction of Retail Brand-name treasures abound throughout the store. Shoppers can find Banana Republic, Ralph Lauren, Chico's, Jones New York, Ann Taylor, American Eagle, and H&M. Vintage enthusiasts will delight in authentic 80s pieces featuring bold colors and dramatic shoulder pads. ## Exceptional Value The true testament to this store's value? Walking away with two statement blazers from Ann Taylor Loft and Banana Republic for just $7 total. This thrift store genuinely transforms the shopping experience, making traditional retail feel obsolete.

Delightful Italian Neighborhood Gem with Minor Quirks This local Italian restaurant checks all the boxes: convenient location, casual atmosphere, full bar, and diverse menu options. The standout lasagna features incredible spicy red sauce and generous portions that left us eager to return for pizza. Both the antipasto and dinner salads impressed, while the ravioli, though delicious, came in modest lunch-sized portions. The attentive staff provided excellent service throughout our visit. A few considerations: bread isn't automatically served (just ask), and lunch prices run slightly high. Despite these minor points, this neighborhood haunt delivers authentic Italian fare in a welcoming setting that's perfect for casual dining near home.

A Steak Lover's Paradise with One Caveat SW Steakhouse delivers what may be the ultimate charred steak experience in Las Vegas. For those who appreciate a perfectly seared exterior, their Bone-in Rib Eye stands as the undisputed champion of the menu—so much so that you needn't venture beyond it. However, this focused excellence comes with a warning. The restaurant's inconsistency across menu items cost it a star in my evaluation. A second visit featuring the Chili-rubbed Porterhouse proved disappointing, revealing that not everything achieves the same spectacular standards. Beyond the signature rib eye, the Lobster Bouillabaisse deserves mention as another reliable choice, though availability may vary. The wine list ranges dramatically from accessible $50 bottles to extravagant $20,000 selections for high rollers. While the markup is notable, the experience of that perfectly charred rib eye makes the visit worthwhile. **Bottom line:** Stick with the Bone-in Rib Eye, and you'll understand why SW maintains its reputation.

A Pleasant Greek Discovery: Pita Kitchen Delivers Fresh, Flavorful Food During a family visit last Saturday, I spontaneously decided to try Pita Kitchen instead of following my mom into the neighboring burrito shop. After spotting their menu from the parking lot, I was intrigued enough to order a gyro combo with a greek salad substituted for fries. **Outstanding Service** The service exceeded expectations. When I mentioned my step-dad was watching the baby in the truck, the staff member graciously brought my food outside. The entire order was ready in roughly 10 minutes—impressive for made-to-order food. **Authentic Preparation** While ordering, I noticed they use a traditional gyro loaf and slice the meat fresh for each order, which speaks to their commitment to authenticity. **The Food** The greek salad was definitely the highlight. Fresh and tasty, it came with dressing on the side, allowing perfect portion control. The gyro itself was a mixed experience. The meat was nicely flavored, moist, and clearly well-seasoned. However, it was somewhat greasy, and surprisingly lacked the typical lettuce and tomato toppings. **Family Approval** I shared samples with my mom and step-dad, neither of whom had tried Greek or Mediterranean cuisine before. Both were enthusiastic about the flavors. My step-dad praised the meat's moisture and taste, while my mom was so impressed she's already planning to order from Pita Kitchen next time! Despite minor issues with the gyro's presentation, Pita Kitchen's authentic preparation, excellent service, and flavorful food make it worth visiting.

Great Casual Spot for Burger Lovers This restaurant offers an impressive array of burger options with endless customization possibilities. The Rossini burger, featuring Kobe beef, foie gras, and truffles with added lobster, proved surprisingly delicious despite sounding over-the-top. The slider option provides an excellent opportunity to sample multiple burger varieties, with the Buffalo being a standout favorite. The fry sampler is ideal for sharing, allowing diners to select three different sides. However, the accompanying sauces are underwhelming and not worth the extra expense—better to save those dollars for one of their shakes instead. Beer enthusiasts will appreciate the flights, offering a selection of six different varieties to sample. Overall, this casual establishment delivers quality burgers with plenty of variety, making it perfect for both adventurous eaters and traditionalists alike.

LA Fitness Falls Short: A Former Urban Active Member's Disappointing Experience As someone who transitioned from Urban Active to LA Fitness, I had high hopes that were unfortunately crushed. This location has serious cleanliness issues that are simply unacceptable for any fitness facility. Despite the building not being particularly old, it consistently looks dingy and unkempt—a far cry from what gym-goers deserve. The equipment situation is equally frustrating. On any given day, you'll find at least six of the thirty spin bikes in the cycling studio broken and unusable. This 20% failure rate suggests poor maintenance and a lack of concern for member experience. The class offerings took a significant hit after the LA Fitness takeover. While Urban Active provided diverse, quality fitness classes, LA Fitness has dramatically reduced variety—except for Zumba, which dominates the schedule. Unfortunately, even the Zumba classes lack intensity, failing to provide an adequate workout. The sole bright spot is Larry's Monday step class, which genuinely delivers results. However, one excellent instructor isn't enough to justify the $50 monthly membership fee. This gym receives two stars solely because of Larry's exceptional teaching—otherwise, it would merit only one star.

Disappointing Visit with Slow Service and Bland Food My boyfriend and I gave this restaurant a try but left underwhelmed. Despite the dining room being nearly empty, service was surprisingly slow. I ordered the Red Beans and Rice Bowl, which arrived cold with flavorless Cajun sausage lacking any seasoning. While my boyfriend's meal was acceptable, the overall experience wasn't compelling enough to warrant a return visit. Unfortunately, we won't be back.

A Disappointing Dining Experience: When TV Hype Doesn't Match Reality This restaurant visit proved to be a masterclass in culinary disappointment from start to finish. The signature fried pickles arrived drowning in oil, featuring what appeared to be bargain-basement quality ingredients. The presentation alone was off-putting, with grease pooling around each piece. The "Tommy Boy" burger fared no better. Despite its creative name, this chili cheese burger with slaw was assembled from seemingly pre-packaged components. The burger patty itself was dry and overcooked, topped with what tasted suspiciously like canned chili, grocery store coleslaw, and processed cheese product rather than real cheese. The chicken wings represented the low point of the meal. Even an eight-year-old could detect something was seriously wrong, diplomatically noting they tasted "weird." After one bite, concerns about food safety became paramount, prompting removal from the bill. The restaurant's custom ketchup raised additional red flags about cost-cutting measures throughout the kitchen. The silver lining? Exceptionally friendly staff who handled complaints professionally and offered compensation. However, service alone couldn't salvage the experience. As one young diner concluded, even television endorsements couldn't make this establishment worth a return visit. Sometimes reputation and reality simply don't align.

Disappointing Food Overshadows Good Vibes I really wanted to like this place. The prices are great, location is perfect near campus, and it's a fun spot for drinks. Unfortunately, the food was a major letdown. I ordered the student special with tacos, sweet potato fries, and black beans – everything lacked flavor. The tacos were very inauthentic, overdressed with sauces and sour cream that couldn't mask the bland protein. Even the fries and beans were disappointing. I added an extra star because it works well as a late-night watering hole for cervezas, but come for drinks, not dinner.

Home Depot!! The Wal-Mart of hardware store! Home Depot lives up to its reputation as a one-stop hardware destination with comprehensive inventory at competitive prices. While service quality can be inconsistent—particularly with paint department mishaps—the store's vast selection and reasonable pricing keep customers returning, even for impulse purchases they don't immediately need.

A Disappointing Culinary Disaster at B&B This restaurant represents everything that can go wrong with fine dining. From start to finish, our experience was utterly disastrous and stands as the worst meal I've encountered in Las Vegas—possibly anywhere. The service was abysmal, with staff displaying complete indifference to our concerns. When we discovered bones in the rabbit confit, management dismissively responded with "that happens sometimes," showing zero accountability or care for guest satisfaction. Their haughty attitude made a bad situation worse. The food quality was equally disappointing. Both pasta dishes had a distinctly gummy, off-putting texture suggesting either incompetent preparation or previously frozen ingredients—something immediately apparent to anyone familiar with fresh pasta preparation. After spending over $70, we left hungry and headed to Spago for actual sustenance. In a city brimming with exceptional restaurants, wasting time and money at B&B was utterly inexcusable.

Just OK: Not Worth the Drive After hearing my husband's enthusiastic recommendations, I finally visited Johnny Mac's with high expectations. Our party of ten ordered pizza, hot wings, fries, and homemade garlic bread. While the shoestring fries were good and the wings smelled authentically hot (though I didn't try them), the pizza was merely average—nothing special enough to warrant a return visit. The service was decent for our large group, and the automatic gratuity inclusion was reasonable. However, living in the Aliante area, I can't justify making the trek across town for this experience. Everything was simply mediocre—not bad, but certainly not memorable. There are plenty of comparable options closer to home that would satisfy just as well without the extra travel time.

A Birthday Dinner Turned Nightmare This restaurant deserves absolutely zero stars. What should have been a celebratory birthday dinner for eight people turned into a health crisis when five of us developed severe food poisoning. I ordered a lamb dish—supposedly their Greek specialty—which I violently expelled by 2am. The following 30 hours were spent bedridden and completely debilitated. This wasn't an isolated incident. After sharing my horrific experience, multiple friends revealed they'd suffered similar fates at this specific location. It's deeply concerning that this establishment continues operating despite apparently making customers sick repeatedly. Food poisoning is no joke, and this was hands-down the worst meal I've had all year. Save yourself the misery and avoid this place entirely.

Exceptional Dining Experience with Generous Portions This establishment delivers outstanding cuisine across their entire menu. Multiple visits revealed consistently excellent quality, from their health-conscious options to the heavenly chicken and waffles. The generous portion sizes provide excellent value, though diners should expect crowds and self-seating arrangements. Despite minor logistical considerations, the exceptional food quality makes any wait worthwhile. Highly recommended for anyone seeking delicious meals with abundant servings.

Challenging Layout and Traffic Issues at This GetGo Location This GetGo station suffers from poor configuration and heavy traffic complications. Located on busy Route 51, the facility experiences constant congestion as numerous drivers attempt quick fuel stops simultaneously. Accessing pumps proves frustratingly difficult due to the awkward layout and high volume of vehicles. The exit situation is equally problematic. Rather than risk merging directly onto Route 51, using the traffic light provides a safer alternative. The dangerous traffic conditions make leaving the station a nerve-wracking experience that requires careful planning to avoid potential accidents.

Dangerous Conditions Overshadow Dining Experience This taco establishment presents serious safety and cleanliness concerns that cannot be overlooked. The dining room floor was dangerously greasy, posing a genuine slip hazard that nearly caused injury. More troubling than the hazardous conditions was management's complete indifference—both server and manager ignored repeated requests to address the problem. Such visible neglect raises legitimate questions about kitchen sanitation standards and overall operational oversight.

A Promising Addition to Vegas Entertainment This venue offers an intriguing combination of activities that caught my attention. While laser tag isn't typically my thing, the reasonable pricing and 3D element make it tempting enough to try. The sizeable arcade and party-friendly facilities add to its appeal. The real draw for me is the miniature golf course – a welcome find for Vegas's hot weather. During my visit, the course was festively decorated for Christmas, which was a nice touch. The main drawback is the location, as it's quite far across town from me. I'm planning to return after their grand opening to see what additional features they'll introduce. Overall, it seems like a decent entertainment option worth checking out.

Mixed Experience: Exceptional Food, Disappointing Seating The culinary experience was truly remarkable, with the steak ranking among my top five ever. Both the food quality and service exceeded expectations. However, despite holding a reservation for over a month, our bachelor party was seated in the worst possible location—cornered by the bathrooms in an otherwise empty restaurant. This puzzling decision significantly diminished what should have been a memorable celebration. While the cuisine is undeniably outstanding, the inexplicable seating arrangement has deterred a return visit.

Disappointing Car Wash Experience: Long Wait, Poor Results This car wash falls drastically short of expectations. Despite paying $20, customers endure hour-long waits only to receive subpar cleaning results. The service quality simply doesn't justify the cost or time investment.

Disappointing Service Experience This establishment severely underperformed during my recent visit. After being seated, I waited an unacceptable 20 minutes without service—no order taken, not even a beverage offered. Only my concern for my 3-year-old's disappointment prevented me from leaving. This experience was particularly frustrating given previous positive visits with good service. Unfortunately, this poor service warranted no gratuity and has cost them a returning customer at this location.

L'Esprit du thé: Une destination incontournable pour les amateurs Cette boutique offre un choix très intéressant de thé venant des quatre coins du monde. Vous trouverez des thés blancs, des thés verts, des thés jaunes, des thés fleuris et d'autres catégories encore. Si vous cherchez des thés rares, L'Esprit du thé est l'endroit idéal pour faire ses achats. En bref, une excellente boutique de thé comme on les aime.

Mixed Experience: Good Intentions Fall Short of Premium Expectations While the waitstaff demonstrated genuine sincerity and good intentions, fundamental service execution missed the mark. The restaurant sources phenomenal cuts of meat, but poor preparation techniques undermined quality—likely cooking meat straight from refrigeration resulted in overcooked exteriors and undercooked centers. Side dishes were disappointingly bland and overcooked. Given the premium pricing, perfect execution should be standard, yet the overall experience proved mediocre at best. The disconnect between excellent raw ingredients and poor kitchen fundamentals makes this difficult to recommend until significant improvements are made.

Disappointing Experience Falls Short of Expectations Despite the attractive patio setting, this establishment fails to deliver on multiple fronts. After sampling various menu items, everything proved mediocre at best—lacking inspiration and poorly portioned for the premium prices charged. The service compounded our disappointment, with our server seeming better suited for a different profession entirely. Interestingly, the airport location of their sister restaurant, Barrio Cafe, provided a vastly superior dining experience with flavorful food, suggesting significant quality control issues. The Scottsdale location simply doesn't measure up, leaving us unable to recommend it.

Restaurant Experience Falls Short on Service While the sushi quality was acceptable, this Monday lunch visit was marred by severely inadequate service. Despite being one of few à la carte customers among all-you-can-eat diners, basic requests required constant follow-up—water, wasabi, and ginger all needed prompting. Multiple dishes required returning to the kitchen due to missing ingredients or order errors. What should have been a relaxing dining experience became frustratingly high-maintenance. The food may be decent, but the inattentive service warrants serious concern and prevents this from being a recommendable establishment. **Rating: Service deserves zero points**

A Friendship Lost: When Artisan Hotel Forgot Its Hospitality Roots Some relationships run their course, and my six-year connection with Artisan Hotel has reached an unfortunate ending. What began as a promising friendship—built on shared values, relaxed vibes, and unpretentious style—has deteriorated into disappointment and broken trust. The hotel's transformation from boutique accommodation to club-event venue marks the fundamental shift in our relationship. While I previously supported integrating nightlife elements during the family-run era, the current ownership has prioritized partying over hospitality. This isn't about evolution; it's about abandoning core identity. **The Breaking Points** Minor inconveniences I could overlook: non-functioning TV remotes, absent coffee service at 8 AM because club operations haven't concluded, or special events spilling between floors where my recommended guests are staying. The permanently closed restaurant during my stay and increased taxi costs from the industrial location aren't deal-breakers either. **The Real Betrayal** What destroyed this relationship is something deeper—broken commitments and communication failures despite flashy websites and abundant door staff. Lost reservations for cabana parties, dismissive bar staff who understandably view their positions as nightclub gigs rather than hotel service, and an overall disregard for guest experience reveal Artisan's transformed priorities. The hotel industry demands balance. Artisan could successfully merge boutique hospitality with nightlife culture, but instead chose to abandon one for the other. Management forgot that hotel guests require different treatment than club patrons. **The Verdict** At 2.0 stars, this friendship seems irreparable. I'm writing this review from Aria at City Center—a stark reminder of what proper hospitality looks like. Artisan and I won't reconnect on social media or in person anytime soon. Some relationships simply run their course when values no longer align. For travelers seeking true hospitality, look elsewhere. Artisan has chosen its path.

Family-Friendly Atmosphere Overwhelms Otherwise Excellent Dining Experience While this establishment delivers exceptional food and service, the dining environment presents significant challenges that may deter certain guests. Our Friday evening visit revealed a restaurant that excels in culinary execution but struggles with atmosphere management. ## The Positives The service staff deserves genuine praise. Young, energetic, and remarkably attentive, our servers demonstrated professionalism throughout the evening. The food quality matched the service excellence, with every dish meeting high culinary standards. These elements alone would warrant a strong recommendation under different circumstances. ## The Critical Issues Unfortunately, the overwhelming presence of families with small children created an atmosphere comparable to a fast-food establishment rather than a proper restaurant. The noise level proved nearly unbearable, with children screaming and running freely throughout the dining area. Most concerning was the apparent lack of parental supervision or intervention. A particularly disturbing incident involved witnessing children at a nearby table tampering with salt and pepper shakers—placing their mouths on them and inserting their hands inside. When we alerted staff after the family departed, the server's dismissive response raised serious sanitary concerns. The likelihood that those condiments remained for subsequent diners left us questioning what other hygiene issues might exist unnoticed. ## The Recommendation Despite feeling sympathy for management and staff who perform admirably within their control, the dining room environment significantly compromises the overall experience. Strongly consider ordering takeout or requesting seating in the 21-and-over lounge area. The restaurant's culinary offerings deserve enjoyment without the chaos that dominated our 6:00 PM Friday visit. The food and service earn high marks; the atmosphere, unfortunately, does not.

A Comedy Club Experience That Was No Laughing Matter What started as an exciting opportunity to visit a new comedy club with complimentary tickets quickly devolved into one of the most disappointing entertainment experiences imaginable. From uncomfortable conditions to subpar food and restrictive policies, this venue managed to fail on nearly every level. ## Arctic Conditions and Unwelcoming Atmosphere The evening began promisingly enough, with guests allowed to wait in the adjacent bar rather than standing in outdoor heat. However, once inside the comedy club, the atmosphere became unbearable—literally. The air conditioning was set to such frigid temperatures that concentrating on anything besides shivering became impossible. When politely requesting a temperature adjustment, staff flatly refused, demonstrating a concerning lack of concern for customer comfort. ## Disappointing Culinary Offerings Given that this establishment is associated with chef Aaron May, who operates several well-regarded restaurants, expectations for the food were reasonably high. Unfortunately, the reality fell drastically short. The cheese curds arrived essentially hollow—resembling empty mozzarella stick shells with virtually no cheese inside. The sliders were severely overcooked to the point of being burnt, accompanied by stale, rock-hard buns. Adding insult to injury, both dishes were served cold, suggesting serious kitchen management issues. ## Lackluster Entertainment The comedy lineup proved equally disappointing. Neither the opening acts nor the headliner managed to generate even modest laughter from the audience. For someone who regularly attends and genuinely enjoys comedy shows, this was particularly disheartening and unusual. ## Restrictive and Customer-Unfriendly Policies The most frustrating aspects involved the club's policies. The two-drink minimum (not a two-item minimum as initially understood) felt excessive, especially when combined with the rule prohibiting check delivery until the show's conclusion. This essentially holds patrons hostage, preventing them from leaving even when having an miserable experience. The automatic 20% gratuity added for just two people felt presumptuous, particularly given the poor service quality throughout the evening. ## Final Verdict This establishment fails to deliver on virtually every promise: comfort, food quality, entertainment value, and customer service. Until significant improvements are made, comedy fans should seek their laughs elsewhere.

**Overpriced with Excessive Hidden Fees** While the quality of their products is decent, the numerous hidden charges make this business unreasonable. They charge $7 simply for not purchasing their shirt, calling it a "setup fee" despite everything being computerized. The breakdown is shocking: approximately $2 for actual work and $14 in various fees. The final cost doesn't justify the service received. There are better alternatives available that offer transparent pricing without nickel-and-diming customers at every turn.

A Hidden Treasure Worth Discovering This unassuming spot might not catch your eye from the street, but it's become an absolute obsession for those in the know. Located conveniently near my workplace, it's transformed into a daily craving for my colleagues and me. The spicy miso ramen is exceptional – perfectly balanced heat that keeps you coming back. The broth here is notably thicker than competitors like Manta, with a more robust, complex flavor profile. What sets this place apart is the variety: multiple noodle thickness options and an impressive selection of appetizers and sides. The agedashi tofu and honey chicken are standout starters that shouldn't be missed. As a bonus, their loyalty program rewards every five bowls with a complimentary appetizer. It's these thoughtful touches that make this hidden gem truly shine.

Hotel Stay Marred by Noise Issues and Poor Problem Resolution This hotel experience proved deeply disappointing from start to finish. Despite booking well in advance—over a month ahead—we were placed in an unbearably noisy room that made sleep impossible. The room quality itself was merely adequate, nothing special. What truly soured this stay was management's inadequate response. When we complained about the noise disturbance, staff offered to relocate us to an inferior room—downgrading from our suite to a standard double queen—without any price adjustment or compensation for the difference. This lack of customer service and unwillingness to make things right is unacceptable. I cannot recommend this property and will definitely seek alternative accommodations in the future.

Mixed Experience at Crowded Vegas Venue Visited with a large group when DJ AM performed. The atmosphere was extremely packed, with table service running approximately $375. While the music was just average and the crowd size was overwhelming, the venue featured attractive décor. Overall managed to have an enjoyable evening despite the challenges. Haven't returned to Vegas since.

Unprofessional Management Ruins Customer Experience This AT&T location suffers from severely poor management under Anibal Culk. The manager displays shocking unprofessionalism, speaking condescendingly to customers and treating them disrespectfully. His hostile attitude has clearly influenced the entire staff negatively. The complete absence of basic customer service skills creates a demeaning environment where patrons feel belittled and disrespected. This represents the worst AT&T service experience encountered, demonstrating how poor leadership directly impacts team behavior and customer satisfaction. Management desperately needs improvement.

Serviceable but Soulless: The Kirkland of Vegas Hotels Harrah's is the Kirkland Signature of Las Vegas accommodations—functional and reasonably priced, but utterly lacking personality. Like Costco's house brand, it delivers basic quality without flair or frills. For budget-conscious visitors who need a decent place to crash without splurging on premium properties like the Venetian or Wynn, it serves its purpose adequately, if uninspiringly.

Poor Service Overshadows Great Atmosphere Despite an awesome atmosphere, this establishment fails on service fundamentals. After waiting 10 minutes at an outdoor table on a slow Sunday, staff including the bartender and server made eye contact but never approached to take our order. Unacceptable inattentiveness. **Rating: ★☆☆☆☆**

A Tale of Two Cities: Beauty Marred by Over-Enforcement This reviewer presents a conflicted perspective on what appears to be a beautiful urban destination. While acknowledging the city's strengths—excellent restaurants, compelling points of interest, and quality shopping—their experience is ultimately overshadowed by what they perceive as excessive municipal enforcement. The most striking complaint involves parking enforcement. The reviewer describes an oppressive system where downtown residents face constant scrutiny from meter attendants, allegedly deployed at a ratio of one officer per two blocks. Street cleaning regulations requiring residents to move vehicles 3-5 times weekly by 1pm seem particularly burdensome. With claimed annual revenues of $30 million from parking violations, the reviewer suggests enforcement has become revenue generation rather than public service. More unusually, the review describes police issuing on-the-spot fines to pedestrians crossing against traffic signals, processing payments immediately via credit card—a practice the reviewer finds excessive compared to American cities. Their temporary roommate's record of over 100 tickets across 12 years, many contested, supports their assertion of aggressive enforcement. The reviewer's repeated use of terms like "parasites" and "nanny state" reveals deep frustration with what they perceive as a city prioritizing revenue over resident quality of life. Whether these enforcement practices truly involve incentive programs remains unverified, but the reviewer's experience clearly transformed their visit from enjoyable to oppressive. For potential visitors, this serves as a cautionary tale about destinations where municipal enforcement may overshadow cultural attractions.

A Disappointing Massage Experience: When Relaxation Falls Flat My visit to this establishment was unfortunately memorable for all the wrong reasons. From the moment I arrived at the empty reception area, red flags appeared. After waiting 3-4 minutes with no staff in sight, an employee finally entered—having just returned from a smoke break, evident from the overpowering smell of cigarettes. The 45-minute reflexology foot massage I'd anticipated turned out to be thoroughly mediocre. Despite politely requesting firm pressure, my preference was ignored, leaving me with a lackluster treatment that failed to deliver any meaningful relaxation. The experience became so underwhelming that I found myself writing this review during the actual massage—a testament to how disengaged I felt. The ambiance proved equally problematic. The massage room shared a wall with Little Caesar's Pizza, and their bustling kitchen operations were clearly audible throughout my session. While their manager seemed pleasant and respectful toward employees, the constant kitchen noise completely destroyed any semblance of tranquility. The most egregious moment came midway through when the masseuse sneezed directly on my feet. Looking back, I should have ended the session immediately, though I'm still unsure why I didn't. I'm awarding two stars solely because the facility itself appears clean and well-maintained. Perhaps this was simply an off day, but the combination of inattentive service, inadequate technique, disruptive noise, and poor hygiene makes it impossible to recommend. Despite wanting this to become my regular spot, I won't be returning.

Disappointing Experience at Wicked Spoon The Wicked Spoon proved to be the worst buffet I've experienced. After an incredibly long initial wait, we paid $35 per person only to face another lengthy line—approximately 1.5 hours total. Service was poor, with servers never returning for drink refills. Most disappointing was the very limited food variety, contradicting all the hype surrounding this establishment. Save your money and time—you'll regret visiting. Don't believe the positive reviews; this buffet fails to deliver on its promises.

Aggressive Upselling Overshadows Quality Service Despite excellent detailing work, this car wash loses points for extremely pushy sales tactics. Staff aggressively promoted scratch repair services despite clear disinterest from the customer. The reviewer emphasized wanting only a basic wash, not additional services. While the cleaning crew deserves praise for thorough work, the uncomfortable sales pressure significantly diminished the overall experience.
**Delicious Croquettas and Excellent Service** Really good food, especially the croquettas! Service is great too. Plus you get a free glass of sangria when you check-in on Yelp. Two thumbs up!

Excellent Gym with Minor Crowding Issues As a long-standing lifetime member, this facility consistently delivers the excellence expected from the brand. The gym offers comprehensive amenities including a pool, diverse fitness classes, abundant machines, and a well-equipped weight area. The location maintains high cleanliness standards and provides convenient freeway access. However, the sole drawback is overcrowding during peak times, which can occasionally compromise workout comfort. Despite this membership volume issue, the gym remains a solid choice for fitness enthusiasts seeking quality facilities.

**Exceptional Dining Experience with Unforgettable Dumplings** This restaurant offers outstanding cuisine in a warm, inviting atmosphere. The unique dumplings are extraordinary and memorable. A must-visit destination that guarantees return trips to Vegas.

A Disappointing Experience: Poor Service and Stale Coffee This establishment at Mandalay Bay falls significantly short of expectations. Arriving three minutes before closing, customers were met with confusing and contradictory service. Despite being asked to order, staff claimed they were out of crepes—while simultaneously preparing them for other customers. The explanation then shifted to being "closed," creating an unprofessional and frustrating experience. The service issues extended beyond poor communication. The coffee served was clearly old, turning an unappetizing gray when cream was added. For a location within a premium hotel like Mandalay Bay, this level of service is unacceptable. **Management Concerns:** The establishment desperately needs better oversight and friendlier staff. While employees may be dissatisfied with their positions, taking frustrations out on customers is counterproductive and drives business away. **Bottom Line:** The combination of inconsistent service, stale products, and unwelcoming staff makes this location impossible to recommend. Hotel guests and visitors deserve far better, especially given Mandalay Bay's premium positioning. Management intervention is urgently needed to address these systemic service failures.

A Late-Night Lifesaver at Hard Rock Hotel Mr. Luckys proved to be the perfect 24-7 dining solution at the Hard Rock Hotel and Casino. Despite arriving after a casino event when the restaurant was packed, our party of four was promptly seated. Service remained impressively efficient, with our food arriving in just 10 minutes. The veggie burger with goat cheese was absolutely amazing, accompanied by hot, crispy sweet potato fries that were simply delicious. Even during peak hours, the kitchen maintained excellent quality and speed. This convenient location and reliable service make Mr. Luckys an ideal spot for any time hunger strikes. It's a hidden gem worth discovering sooner rather than later!

Disappointing Breakfast Experience - Look Elsewhere Unfortunately, this establishment doesn't live up to its hype. My wife and I were hopeful but left disappointed. The chicken fried steak was excessively salty and greasy, showing a fundamental lack of understanding of this American classic. For this side of town, better options exist. Hash House offers authentic breakfast fare, while Omelette House provides superior value and flavor. It's frustrating that finding a quality breakfast spot in this area remains challenging. Save your money and visit the recommended alternatives instead.

Disappointing First Visit: Lack of Guidance and Care As a first-time dog owner, I visited this clinic hoping to use my free exam and consultation from my puppy adoption kit. Unfortunately, I left feeling completely unimpressed and disappointed. The staff member repeatedly asked if I needed anything else, but never proactively offered the guidance I desperately needed as a new pet parent. I was hoping for breed-specific advice and essential care information, but received nothing. The interaction felt like speaking with someone inexperienced in their field, making communication frustrating and unproductive. Dr. Jarred Forrest's examination was equally disappointing. He appeared standoffish and rushed, going straight through the motions without genuine engagement. His demeanor clearly suggested someone who doesn't enjoy their profession, which was concerning for my puppy's care. I left the clinic with the same questions and concerns I arrived with—essentially no better informed than before. For a veterinary practice, failing to educate and reassure a first-time pet owner is unacceptable. They lack the interest and skills necessary to make clients feel valued and well-informed. I won't be returning.

A Nightmare Experience: Broken Promises and Endless Frustration If there were an option for negative stars, this company would deserve it. My experience has been nothing short of a catastrophic failure in customer service, billing accuracy, and basic business operations. ## The Suspension That Never Was When I requested to suspend my service due to personal hardships, I was explicitly told the cost would be $20 per month. Instead, I received bills for $48.59 and then $50.37. After multiple reassurances that my account was properly suspended, I discovered during yet another call that my account was actually still *active*. Multiple representatives had failed to process my suspension request correctly, yet none bothered to verify or follow up. ## Customer Service Failures Getting through to a representative is already challenging enough, but when you finally reach someone, the experience only worsens. Endless hold times are standard, and the information provided is consistently unreliable. I've spoken with several representatives, each apparently unaware of what previous agents had documented or promised. While Marina, my most recent contact, demonstrated patience, I was told a manager would return my call within 24 hours. As someone who works in retail management myself, this response time is unacceptable and demonstrates a complete disregard for customer concerns. ## The Bottom Line Currently, I'm waiting for my former roommates to return equipment so I can finally terminate this contract. This company cannot execute basic operations like account suspensions, provides faulty service with unreliable internet connections, and demonstrates consistent dishonesty in billing and customer communications. I wouldn't recommend this service to anyone—not even my worst enemy. There are undoubtedly better providers available who actually value their customers and deliver on their promises.

Mixed Experience at Budget-Friendly Massage Spa This establishment offers excellent value with a $39 introductory massage and flexible packages. The massages are professional, relaxing, and performed in clean facilities. However, several drawbacks exist: a questionable $7 upcharge for deep tissue work, sparse and cold massage rooms, limited peak-hour availability, and absence of aromatherapy or spa ambiance. The strip-mall setting reinforces the utilitarian feel. **Bottom line:** Great for budget-conscious massage seekers, but those expecting a luxurious spa atmosphere should look elsewhere. Best suited for straightforward therapeutic massage rather than pampering experiences.

A Colorful Stop for Flags and Sports Souvenirs This unassuming shop lives up to its name, specializing in flags and sporting memorabilia with a smattering of tourist items. The vibrant flag display immediately catches the eye, featuring an eclectic mix of countries that seem randomly selected rather than following any particular theme. The sports merchandise collection is equally unpredictable, stocking popular teams like Texas, USC, and Ohio State alongside local favorites Arizona and ASU. Interestingly, they also carry items from recent Fiesta Bowl participants, making it a potential goldmine for finding discounted championship merchandise. While the selection might not appeal to everyone, the pricing is reasonable and fair. It's an adequate destination for picking up standard Arizona tourist souvenirs or discovering unexpected bargains on college sports gear. The store serves its purpose well for casual souvenir hunters, even if serious collectors might find the inventory too haphazard for their tastes.

Mixed Experience: Pizza Overhyped, But Bar Bianco Shines I have to agree with fellow Yelpers—I don't get the hype. The pizza is good, but is it worth a two-hour wait? Absolutely not. Our server seemed to be having an off day, delivering service with an audible groan and making us feel distinctly unwelcome. However, there's a silver lining: Bar Bianco next door is wonderful! The atmosphere is cozy and warm, and the service matches perfectly. I've visited multiple times and consistently have great experiences there. Skip the main restaurant and head straight to Bar Bianco instead.

Functional Neighborhood Mall with Basic Amenities This mall serves its purpose as a convenient local shopping center, though it lacks distinctive features that would make it a destination spot. The main draw is the presence of a Dillard's department store, one of only three remaining in Las Vegas, alongside the more common Kohl's and Macy's locations. While the Dillard's itself is fairly ordinary outside of special clearance sales, the mall proves practical for everyday needs. Visitors can access essential services like eyeglass prescription updates and cell phone upgrades, plus enjoy acceptable food court options. It's a reliable, no-frills shopping venue that adequately meets neighborhood requirements without offering anything particularly memorable or unique.

A Wine Lover's Paradise with Outstanding Bruschetta We were thrilled to discover Postino's had opened closer to our neighborhood, and it's quickly become our go-to hangout spot. After several visits, we've sampled the Bruschetta, Grilled Cheese, and Pub Board, with the bruschetta emerging as the clear standout. The bruschetta selection is exceptional—particularly the Brie & Apples with Fig Spread, Prosciutto with Figs & Mascarpone, and Ricotta with Dates & Pistachios. These flavor combinations are simply divine. While the Pub Board offers generous portions and the Grilled Cheese comes with delightful dipping sauces, neither quite reaches the excellence of the bruschetta. Wine enthusiasts will appreciate the $5 glass pricing, making it easy to enjoy quality wine without breaking the bank. However, be prepared for lengthy wait times, especially during evening hours. The relaxed atmosphere encourages guests to linger over wine and conversation, which means estimated wait times often prove optimistic. Despite the waits, Postino's delivers a consistently enjoyable experience that keeps us coming back for more of that incredible bruschetta.

A Superior Asian Market Experience: Clean, Organized, and Comprehensive This Asian supermarket stands out as a refreshing alternative to the often-chaotic 99 Ranch Market experience. The store's cleanliness and organization immediately set it apart, while the stress-free parking situation makes shopping considerably more pleasant. Unlike some competitors, there's no unpleasant odor permeating the aisles. The market serves as a comprehensive one-stop destination for all Asian culinary needs. Upon entering, customers are greeted by a food stall and bakery, offering convenient meal options for those too busy to cook. The grocery selection is impressively diverse, representing Japanese, Korean, Filipino, Chinese, and Vietnamese cuisines. Fresh seafood enthusiasts will appreciate the live aquarium tanks featuring notably large lobsters and sushi-grade fish. The nostalgic candy selection includes childhood favorites like Haw Flakes wafer candies, White Rabbit candy, Ramune soda, fish crackers, and various potato chips. The produce section excels in offering hard-to-find tropical fruits including tamarind, lychee, Philippine mangoes, dragon fruit, rambutan, mangosteen, and jackfruit. Perhaps most notably, the shopping atmosphere remains civilized and courteous—a welcome departure from the aggressive cart-wielding shoppers sometimes encountered elsewhere. This store successfully combines authenticity with comfort and accessibility.

Convenient Neighborhood Spot with Solid Service This local establishment excels in convenience and service rather than culinary excellence. The food quality is average, but the attentive staff ensures minimal wait times for orders. Weekly trivia nights and daily beer specials add entertainment value, with all beers reasonably priced. Menu highlights include the standout pretzel with beer cheese and fresh-made onion rings. The venue caters well to sports fans with individual TVs in each booth plus numerous flat screens throughout, allowing personalized viewing experiences. While not a destination for exceptional cuisine, it's an ideal neighborhood hangout for casual dining, drinks, and watching games in a comfortable setting with efficient service.

A Mixed Experience: Great Banh Mi, Disappointing Pho Despite the scorching 106-degree temperature, I ventured to this Vietnamese restaurant craving both pho and banh mi. Unfortunately, the experience was largely underwhelming, saved only by one standout item. ## Cleanliness Concerns The visit started on a troubling note with cloudy water glasses, one containing white residue on the inside—an immediate red flag for any dining establishment. ## The Disappointments **Meatball Pho**: This dish fell significantly short of expectations. The meatballs were tiny, numbering only about six pieces, with a rubbery texture and complete lack of flavor. While the broth was passable, it failed to deliver the rich, delicious taste one expects from authentic pho. **Shredded Pork/Grilled Pork Rice Plate**: The portion sizes were severely imbalanced. While rice was plentiful, the grilled pork measured merely one-third cup.
