More disappointing was the "shredded pork," which was predominantly tripe with only two actual pork pieces—a deceptive presentation. ## The Saving Grace **Pork Special Banh Mi**: This sandwich alone earned the restaurant its second star. The bread delivered a satisfying crunch with each bite, and the pork inside was well-seasoned and flavorful. This item alone warrants a return visit. ## Final Verdict While the banh mi shows promise, the poor hygiene, disappointing pho, and misrepresented rice plate make this establishment difficult to recommend for anything beyond that single sandwich offering.

Avoid This Storage Facility: Poor Conditions and Terrible Service This Madison area storage facility fails to deliver on its promises of dry, secure storage. Items developed yellow mold and bikes rusted due to inadequate climate control. Management was unhelpful and rude when addressing concerns, instead insisting on additional insurance coverage. Despite high costs, the facility provides substandard conditions and poor customer service. Students and residents should explore alternative storage options rather than risk damage to their belongings at this location.

Disappointing Saturday Night Buffet Experience This restaurant's Saturday night "unlimited wine and lobster" promotion proved misleading and underwhelming. The unlimited offer only applies to house wine, while lobster is limited to one Maine lobster per two guests. Worse yet, the lobster was severely overcooked and flavorless, rendering it inedible. While the crabs and shrimp showed decent freshness and some other items were palatable, these positives couldn't salvage the experience. The overall disappointment was significant enough that the reviewer won't return or even bother requesting a refund. The deceptive advertising combined with poor execution makes this buffet a poor value proposition despite some redeeming qualities.

Decent place overall This restaurant delivers on service and ambiance, with friendly, efficient staff and a clean, well-maintained environment. However, the food falls short of expectations. The quesadilla lacks cheese—a fundamental ingredient—while the rice, though acceptable, comes in disappointingly small portions. At least the restrooms maintain the establishment's cleanliness standards.

A Disappointing Experience with Local Business I genuinely wanted to support this local store when ordering my nursery furniture, having always enjoyed browsing there. Unfortunately, what should have been an exciting pregnancy milestone turned into a frustrating nightmare. The store's disorganization is staggering. Getting order updates proved nearly impossible – calls and emails went unreturned despite promises to follow up. Only the store owner, Karen, seems to have any information, yet she's perpetually unavailable. This lack of communication was particularly stressful during pregnancy. My furniture order took over six months to arrive. Near the end, instead of a courtesy follow-up, I received a threatening call demanding immediate credit card payment for the balance or they'd cancel my order. This happened during my ninth month of pregnancy – completely unprofessional and unnecessarily aggressive, especially considering they'd only attempted to reach me once before. The dishonesty was equally troubling. Staff claimed Karen was out when I visited to check on my order, only for her to walk out from the back moments later. Why lie about something so easily disproven? While I now have a beautiful baby girl I love shopping for, this store has permanently lost my business. When you work on commission, treating customers poorly is indeed a "big mistake, big, huge." Local businesses deserve support, but only when they respect their customers.

**Mixed Experience: Pet-Friendly But Beware of Noise Issues** The accommodations were decent, and the pet-friendly policy is definitely a plus for dog owners. However, our stay was significantly impacted by poor communication regarding late-night events. A very loud party near the pool continued well past 1am, despite repeated assurances it would end soon. Staff first promised it would stop at 1:20am, then pushed it to 2am. This was particularly problematic as we had an early morning departure. Management failed to notify guests about the scheduled event beforehand. If you're looking for a quiet, restful stay, proceed with caution and inquire about planned activities. This property seems better suited for party-goers than early risers.

Mixed Experience: Great Coffee, Poor Service While the coffee quality at this establishment is consistently excellent, and a handful of baristas truly shine, the overall customer service experience leaves much to be desired. The majority of staff members lack the warmth and hospitality expected in a coffee shop environment. Basic courtesies like greetings, smiles, or proactive service are notably absent. Instead, customers are met with silent stares at the counter, creating an unwelcoming atmosphere. Despite the reliably good coffee, the lackluster employee interactions significantly detract from the overall experience. For a business where ambiance and friendly service are as important as the product itself, this represents a crucial area needing improvement.

**A Tale of Two Experiences** Came here last night and the ambiance is very cool and laid back. However on Saturdays is a different story. It's like being in a mini club and actually being able to sit, eat, and get drinks fast. I recommend this place! It's very cool! Not to mention being able to see the whole view of the Vegas strip—always a plus.

An Outstanding Dental Experience After 30 Years of Searching After three decades of dissatisfaction with dentists, I finally found Dr. Kindt five years ago, and he has completely transformed my perception of dental care. He is genuinely the best dentist I've ever encountered, making me wish I had discovered him sooner. Dr. Kindt distinguishes himself through his gentle, caring approach and exceptional communication skills. He thoroughly explains procedures, reasons for treatment, and consistently checks on patient comfort throughout appointments—a rare quality among dental professionals. Beyond Dr. Kindt himself, his entire staff maintains the same level of professionalism and friendliness. The office is immaculately clean and modern, with minimal wait times—typically just a few minutes. My wife is now a patient, and we plan to bring our children once they're old enough. I very highly recommend Dr. Kindt to anyone seeking exceptional dental care!

A Complimentary Stay at Luxor: Young, Vibrant, But Watch Those Resort Fees My three-day stay at Luxor Las Vegas came courtesy of a timeshare presentation, so I'll skip the price commentary—except to mention the $20 daily resort fee, which seems absurd for such a profitable establishment. Still, that's Vegas for you. **Location and Check-In** Situated adjacent to Mandalay Bay, parking proved initially confusing, though we eventually figured it out. Signage to check-in was clear, and the front desk staff were genuinely pleasant, making arrival smooth and welcoming. **The Room Experience** Our 18th-floor accommodation exceeded expectations in several ways. Unlike many Vegas properties, the hotel wasn't overwhelmed by cigarette smoke—a refreshing surprise. The room was impeccably clean with fresh scents, and the bathroom met cleanliness standards without hesitation. **Important tip:** Request a room near the elevators! Ours required quite a trek down the hallway, which became exhausting when carrying luggage or purchases. The view was absolutely spectacular: the Sphinx, Las Vegas Boulevard, and MGM Grand stretched before us. Friday midnight treated us to an unexpected 10-minute fireworks display over MGM Grand (apparently celebrating Rose.Rabbit.Lie's opening). I found myself returning repeatedly to watch the sunsets. **Amenities and Atmosphere** Luxor offers comprehensive entertainment: food court, multiple bars, nightclub, steakhouse, and full casino with blackjack, poker, and slots. The vibe definitely targets the 21-to-40 crowd, evidenced by numerous bars and nightlife venues. **Value Consideration** While my stay was complimentary, I overheard neighboring guests paid $700 for several nights. At that rate, I'm uncertain about the value proposition. However, if you find discounted rates on Vegas.com or similar sites, Luxor represents a solid choice for younger travelers seeking clean accommodations with vibrant nightlife access. **Bottom line:** Great for the right demographic and price point, with excellent views and cleanliness, just remember that elevator proximity tip!

Solid Alternative to Yard House with Electric Hockey Atmosphere This Westgate spot serves as a convenient backup when Yard House's hour-long wait becomes impractical. The venue caters heavily to hockey enthusiasts, with numerous screens broadcasting games and a boisterous crowd to match. While the energetic, loud atmosphere appeals to die-hard fans cheering for the Coyotes, it may overwhelm those seeking a quieter dining experience. It's a decent choice for sports lovers, though the reviewer clearly considers Yard House the superior option when timing permits.

A Cautionary Tale: Food Safety Concerns at Campus Indian Restaurant This establishment's convenient campus location may explain its popularity among students, but convenience shouldn't overshadow quality and safety concerns. My experience here was genuinely troubling, culminating in severe food poisoning after consuming a mango lassi and buffet items during a professional lunch interview. Over several years, I've witnessed a steady decline in food quality. The dishes are consistently oily, lacking freshness, and poorly prepared. While students may appreciate ethnic dining options unavailable in their hometowns, this restaurant falls significantly short of authentic Indian cuisine standards. The food poisoning incident left me incapacitated for an entire day—an unacceptable outcome for any dining establishment. Despite the restaurant's continued student patronage, I cannot recommend it to anyone prioritizing food safety and quality. **Bottom line:** Proceed with extreme caution, if at all.

Mixed Experience: Strong in Some Areas, Weak in Others Decent paint selection but limited scale models and railroad supplies. Excels in hobby tools and RC products. Staff assistance inconsistent. Best suited for customers who know exactly what they need. Casting products selection particularly sparse.

A Thrilling Second Visit with Fresh Perspectives Returning to this spectacular show proved just as entertaining as the first visit, revealing new details and nuances previously missed. The audience interaction ensures each performance feels unique and engaging. Sitting close to the left side this time offered an intimate viewing experience. While proximity made it challenging to capture the entire stage, witnessing every muscle movement and facial expression from the performers added incredible depth to the show. My boyfriend was thoroughly impressed, appreciating not only the risqué elements but particularly the remarkable athleticism displayed throughout. Every aspect—from the stunning costumes to the clever jokes—demonstrates exceptional attention to detail. The performers' dedication shines through in every moment. Pro tip: Check the NY NY website for buy-one-get-one-free deals. While you can't select specific seats, you can choose your preferred section, making this amazing show even more accessible.

A Middling Lunch Experience: When Average Just Doesn't Cut It When searching for a satisfying lunch spot, diners hope for more than just mediocrity. Unfortunately, this recent visit to Sprecher's restaurant delivered an experience that fell squarely into "forgettable" territory, drawing unfavorable comparisons to chain establishments like Applebee's. ## The Food: Lacking Excitement The meal began with cheese curds that immediately disappointed. With only 14-16 pieces served, portion size raised eyebrows, but worse were the execution issues: half overcooked and all disappointingly greasy and soggy. These appetizers set an unfortunate tone for what followed. The entrées painted a picture of consistent mediocrity. While the burger achieved a perfect medium cook, it lacked the flavor punch that makes burgers memorable. The chicken sandwich proved decent but uninspiring. Only the Caesar salad and wrap earned respectable marks, though even the salad suffered from sparse chicken portions. Side dishes continued the trend—sweet potato fries arrived limp and soggy, while asparagus came woody and excessively buttered, drowning in grease rather than showcasing fresh vegetable flavor. ## Service and Value Concerns Service proved merely adequate, with minimal attentiveness. The most jarring surprise came at billing: $2.50 for a 10-ounce glass of root beer, followed by $2 per refill. This pricing structure seemed excessive and left a sour taste beyond the food itself. At $67 for four people without alcoholic beverages, the value proposition failed to justify the experience. For lunch pricing, diners rightfully expect either superior quality or generous portions—Sprecher delivered neither. ## The Verdict While the interior ambiance and Sprecher beer selection earned praise, they couldn't salvage an otherwise underwhelming experience. With superior local pubs offering better food, attentive service, and reasonable pricing, there's little incentive to return. Sometimes average simply isn't good enough, especially when better alternatives exist nearby. **Rating: 2.5/5 stars**

Convenient Stop, But Poutine Lacks Punch This Montreal poutine spot served as a convenient pitstop during an afternoon walk when my companion needed rest and I had to take a work call. While the restaurant delivered functional service, the poutine itself was disappointingly bland considering Montreal's reputation for this iconic dish. The menu heavily focuses on poutine variations with limited alternatives, and prices seemed steep for what's essentially comfort food. The rickety interior courtyard dining space offers some quirky charm, though it doesn't compensate for the lackluster food quality. The reality is that Montreal boasts countless superior poutine options throughout the city. This spot isn't terrible, but there's simply nothing memorable or distinctive about it. Worth visiting only if you're already nearby and desperate.

A Solid Target with Room for Improvement This Target location makes a strong first impression with its spacious, well-lit parking lot and visible security presence. The interior maintains the same brightness and cleanliness you'd expect from a quality Target store, comparable to the Falls Church location. However, there are some notable shortcomings. The store was out of stock on a specific item I needed, which was disappointing. More concerning was the restroom condition – while relatively cleaner than some retail facilities, it still required attention. The sticky floors and several unusable toilets were problematic and detracted from the otherwise pleasant shopping experience. Despite these issues, this Target remains a convenient option for basic shopping needs when in the area. It's certainly a step above Walmart, though there's definitely room for improvement in inventory management and restroom maintenance. Three stars feels fair for a decent store that could be great with some attention to detail.
Quick Late-Night Fix with Killer Nachos Perfect post-bar munchies spot on State Street. Fast service, convenient late hours, and those pulled pork nachos absolutely hit the spot after nights out.

Delightful Donut Shop with Exceptional Service This beloved establishment offers delicious fresh donuts, welcoming staff, quality coffee, and convenient early hours. Arrive early for the best selection of hot donuts before they sell out!

**One Star Wonder: A Disappointing First and Last Visit** This Quiznos location fails to live up to its reputation of being superior to Subway. The food quality ranges from poor to terrible, with unappetizing taste throughout. Service is frustratingly slow, compounding an already negative experience. Save your money and time—this reviewer's first visit will definitely be their last.

Exceptional Service at Boulevard Salon After disappointing experiences at chain salons like Fantastic Sam's and Supercuts, I discovered Boulevard Salon through Yelp's glowing reviews. I booked with Jessica and couldn't be happier with my decision. Jessica is truly a master stylist who listened carefully and delivered exactly the haircut I envisioned. The professionalism and attention to detail were outstanding from start to finish. I highly recommend Boulevard Salon, particularly Jessica. If you're seeking quality salon services, you definitely won't be disappointed with this gem!

A Thrilling Tribute to the King of Pop The Crown Theatre at Rio hosts an extraordinary Michael Jackson tribute show that delivers an authentic concert experience. This performer proves to be the ultimate carbon copy of the legendary entertainer, capturing everything from mannerisms and persona to physical build and intricate details with remarkable precision. **The Performance** While the show starts slowly, it builds momentum into an electrifying experience. The highlight arrives during "Smooth Criminal," featuring the iconic lean in the signature white suit and hat—a moment alone worth the admission price. The performer scores an impressive 99/100, demonstrating masterful recreation of MJ's legendary stage presence and interactive crowd engagement. **Minor Shortcomings** The backup dancers, though competent, lack the razor-sharp timing and crispness expected from such a production. Additionally, absent tracks from the *Off the Wall* album represent a missed opportunity for fans of Jackson's complete catalog. **Value and Atmosphere** With affordable, reasonable pricing and a concert-like environment, this show offers the most viable solution for experiencing Michael Jackson's magic posthumously. The service proves adequate, neither exceptional nor disappointing. **Final Verdict: B+** For anyone who missed seeing Michael Jackson live, this tribute performance delivers genuine entertainment and remarkable authenticity that justifies every penny spent.

Disappointing Convention Center Experience This convention center continues to be a source of frustration for exhibitors. The complete lack of dedicated parking for a venue of this size is utterly baffling and creates significant logistical challenges. The loading and unloading process is particularly problematic. Union staff show little patience or understanding, issuing tickets within minutes even when exhibitors are actively unloading materials. Expecting vendors to empty an entire vehicle in under a minute is completely unrealistic. The parking arrangement forces exhibitors to use remote lots at the Venetian or Palazzo, requiring a 20-minute walk to reach the venue. This is especially burdensome when transporting booth materials and equipment. As show sizes increase, these issues become more acute. What was merely inconvenient has become nearly unbearable. For businesses required to exhibit here repeatedly, the experience is frustrating and unprofessional. The facility desperately needs to reconsider its parking infrastructure and loading policies to better serve its exhibitors.

Disappointing Dining Experience Despite Friendly Service While the service was pleasant, this restaurant falls short in several key areas. The burgers were notably bland and messy, with canned green chilies and "roasted" garlic that appeared merely grilled. The homemade potato chips were excessively greasy, and steak fries raised concerns about oil freshness. On the positive side, romaine lettuce was fresh and the marble rye bread option was welcome. However, given the competitive lunch prices in the area and the cluttered, dust-collecting décor, there are better dining options nearby. The overall experience was underwhelming, with execution failing to match expectations.

Loyal Customer for 5 Years - Consistently Excellent Service I used to bounce around to whoever could fit me into their schedule last minute until I went to Frankie 5 years ago. Since then I've only been getting my hair cut from her. She does a great job every time and is always in a good mood. 5 stars from me.

Mixed Experience at Nearby Spot While the location is conveniently close to home and promises future visits, the service speed left much to be desired. Waiting 25 minutes just to pay for a beer seems excessive, even on a busy night. Opening and closing tabs proved equally time-consuming. Though understandable given the crowd, the glacial pace was frustrating. The proximity factor and forgiving attitude suggest potential, but efficiency improvements would elevate the experience considerably.

Solid Dining Experience with Generous Portions This establishment offers a typical bar-and-grill atmosphere, though the separate dining area provides a quieter, less crowded experience. The menu features standard fare with some pleasant surprises. While the penne dish with spinach and chicken was decent—though somewhat picked over—it reheated excellently for next-day lunch. The standout items were undoubtedly the sweet potato fries and garlic bread, which elevated the meal considerably. Most impressive was the portion size, which far exceeded expectations and provided great value. The pasta held up well quality-wise, making it a satisfying choice. Overall, it's a respectable option for casual dining, particularly if you're seeking generous servings in a relaxed setting away from typical bar noise.

A Pizza Place That Feels Like Family When searching for the perfect pizza joint, it's rare to find a place that combines exceptional food with outstanding customer service, but this establishment delivers on both fronts. Since my very first visit, I've been consistently impressed by the quality and variety offered here. What truly sets this pizzeria apart is the personal touch provided by owners Jodi and Mark. From day one, they've created a welcoming atmosphere that makes every customer feel like family. Their commitment to hospitality goes beyond typical restaurant service—they genuinely care about each guest's experience. The food quality is consistently excellent, with nothing disappointing on the menu. But what's truly remarkable is their customer-first philosophy: they never say no. If they have the ingredients, they'll create your perfect pizza, even going so far as to make a whole pizza with every slice customized differently if that's what you want. Their dedication to customer satisfaction is evident in how they handle feedback, using it to ensure your next visit is even better. This level of service, combined with delicious food, makes this pizza place truly deserving of its reputation as the best in town.

A Welcoming Starbucks Worth the Extra Drive This Starbucks location stands out for its friendly, smiling staff and inviting atmosphere. Despite being situated on a busy street, the café offers plenty of available seating and surprisingly isn't overcrowded. The warm service and comfortable environment make it worth bypassing a closer location. The staff takes time to be personable rather than rushing through orders, creating a more pleasant coffee experience. For those seeking a relaxing spot with excellent customer service, this Starbucks proves that a slightly longer drive can make all the difference in your daily coffee routine.

Nobu Hotel Barcelona: A Disappointing Departure from Brand Standards When the Nobu name appears on a property, guests naturally expect a certain level of luxury, service, and thoughtful design. Unfortunately, the Nobu Hotel in Barcelona falls dramatically short of these expectations, operating more as a renovated wing within the existing Cesar Hotel rather than a standalone luxury destination. ## What's Missing The most striking aspect of this property is what it lacks. Despite bearing the prestigious Nobu name, guests will find no lobby, no spa, no bar, and no pool. There isn't even exterior signage indicating the hotel's existence. Instead, visitors encounter a modest two-person check-in desk, three modern elevators, and 181 rooms—essentially a refurbished section of the Cesar building rather than a true hotel experience. For travelers seeking the comprehensive amenities typically associated with luxury hospitality brands, this stripped-down approach proves severely disappointing. ## Design Over Function While the hotel promotes its Japanese modern aesthetic, the execution prioritizes style over practicality. The rooms feature doorless showers with controls positioned at the far end, ensuring guests get soaked when turning on the water and endure cold temperatures while showering. When concerns about the absence of bathtubs were raised, staff suggested using the provided wooden shower stool—a solution that hardly compensates for the design flaw. ## Service Failures Perhaps most troubling are the repeated service breakdowns. Despite advance arrangements for a special birthday detail (with agreement to pay), nothing was delivered. Promised Japanese-style tea upon arrival never materialized. Turn-down service was absent the first night. These aren't minor oversights—they represent fundamental failures in hospitality basics. ## Inflexible Management When legitimate concerns were raised with management after the first night, the response was disappointingly rigid. Rather than attempting to remedy the situation or show flexibility given the clear service failures, management insisted on charging for all reserved nights despite the guest's desire to leave. Even intervention from American Express—through whom the reservation was made—couldn't persuade management to offer any accommodation or credit. ## The Bottom Line If you're staying at the Cesar and happen upon renovated Nobu-branded rooms, you might be pleasantly surprised by the updated accommodations. However, if you're booking specifically because of the Nobu name and expecting the luxury, facilities, and service standards that name implies, prepare for significant disappointment. This property simply doesn't deliver the Nobu experience.

Not Worth the Visit Can't say I'm a fan of this establishment. Having frequented Sizzler's throughout my childhood, this restaurant carries a distinct "Sizzler-ish" atmosphere, though unfortunately falls short of those standards—and disappointingly lacks the beloved cheesy bread. Ironically, it's even located in a former Sizzler building. We opted for the soup and salad bar, which proved underwhelming. The ingredient quality was subpar, featuring wilted lettuce that looked particularly unappetizing. The cheese sauce was covered with an unpleasant layer of congealed goop that was downright off-putting. I settled for chicken wings and selective salad items. The soup selection was disappointingly limited—only navy bean and French onion available during our visit. Service was notably sluggish. Getting staff attention for refills and fresh plates required considerable waiting and effort. Ultimately, everything offered here could be found at a casino EDR, and nothing justified the price point. While I haven't sampled their menu entrees, the overall experience provides little incentive to return and explore further options.

**A Delightful Show with Adorable Rescued Pets** This show is absolutely darling! The pets are incredibly cute and clearly adore Mr. Popovich and their dedicated human caretakers who rescued them. Mr. Popovich himself is both an amazing acrobat and an adorable clown, leading a cast of exceptionally talented gymnasts and performers. Pro tip: Book VIP assigned seats in advance to avoid long lines for general admission seating. Since the theater is completely flat with no elevated back rows, securing a good seat is essential for optimal stage viewing. The upgraded seating is definitely worth the investment for this charming performance!

Solid Choice for Casual Japanese Dining This unassuming Japanese eatery delivers quality teppanyaki at wallet-friendly prices. While the ambiance won't suit romantic dates or business meetings, it's perfect for anyone seeking authentic Japanese food without the premium price tag. A reliable neighborhood spot that prioritizes good food and value over fancy presentation.

Long Wait, Disappointing Pizza Visited for lunch on December 28th, arriving at 11:30am only to face a 90-minute wait—apparently standard here. While the service was good, the pizza fell short of expectations given the glowing reviews I'd read beforehand. It was merely okay, nothing special. When you're asking customers to wait that long, the food needs to be exceptional to justify it. Having experienced Serious Pie in Seattle multiple times, their pizza is significantly better, and we've never encountered such lengthy waits there. For the time investment required, this place simply doesn't deliver.

Exceptional Authentic Pizza with Perfect Execution This pizzeria delivers an outstanding dining experience with ideally balanced sauce and cheese, expertly crafted wood-fired crust, and delicious starters worthy of Italian tradition.

A Hidden Gem for Breakfast Lovers Looking for a cozy breakfast spot that won't break the bank? This quiet little restaurant exceeded all expectations during our weekend visit. The portions are incredibly generous – easily enough to share. My boyfriend's three-pancake meal with bacon and eggs was impressive, featuring fluffy pancakes that put iHop and Denny's to shame, both in quality and size (literally double!). My omelet with sourdough toast was equally satisfying, served on surprisingly large, thick-cut bread instead of standard slices. The food quality and reasonable pricing make this place a standout choice. Everything tasted delicious and fresh. The charming décor creates a welcoming atmosphere, and the service was attentive and friendly. The only minor drawback was slightly longer wait times, even with few customers present. However, the excellent food and pleasant environment more than compensated. We're definitely returning to sample their hot sandwiches. Highly recommended!

Disappointing Casino Experience Marred by Poor Design This casino merits only 2 stars, primarily due to its frustratingly poor parking garage design—genuinely one of the worst I've encountered. The property's cheap construction is evident in the inadequate drainage system; moderate rainfall consistently causes flooding behind the IP as water rushes through the garage, overwhelming the insufficient drainage channel. The casino itself is mediocre at best, with superior alternatives available in nearly every direction. The gaming floor predominantly features penny slots and currently suffers from ongoing construction chaos, making the environment less than appealing. I'm cautiously optimistic that Project Linq's completion might bring improvements worth seeing. However, until these renovations finish, I'll avoid the IP unless attending a show in the upstairs venue. There are simply too many better options nearby.

Excellent Service and Professional Staff The staff at this location are friendly, professional, and highly knowledgeable. Travis, the store manager, demonstrates exceptional product expertise. My iPhone 6 purchase experience was flawless, with the phone arriving over a week early. Unlike other stores, there was no pushy sales tactics or unnecessary upselling. The team's genuine helpfulness and expertise make this a reliable choice for future purchases. Highly recommended for quality service.

Informative but Unsettling Experience This exhibit proved educational and well-presented, but deeply uncomfortable for sensitive viewers. While the anatomical displays offered valuable information—particularly appreciated by our medical student friend—the presentation of real human bodies felt disturbing and emotionally difficult. The baby specimens were especially distressing. Combined with the steep admission price, this made for a thought-provoking yet somber visit. Recommended only for those with strong constitutions and genuine scientific interest.

An Exceptional Steakhouse Experience Worth the Return Trip My husband and I recently dined at this establishment while visiting my brother, his fiancé, and her extended family—who happen to be regulars. Despite my initial hesitation about ordering seafood in a landlocked state (thanks to a horrible past experience), our custom seafood platter exceeded all expectations. Everything arrived fresh, perfectly cooked, and free from the rubbery, waterlogged texture I'd feared. Even the raw oysters tasted remarkably fresh, which impressed this Pacific Northwest native currently living on the California coast. The steaks were cooked to perfection, served on properly heated plates—a detail that speaks volumes about kitchen standards. Our attentive waiter served sides individually at the beginning, including my selections of creamed corn, asparagus, and sweet potato fries, all prepared flawlessly and served hot. We concluded with a dessert platter featuring everything on the menu: key lime pie, chocolate-covered strawberries, and various other delicious options. The presentation was fantastic, and every bite delivered. The service exemplified high-end dining standards. Our drinks never dropped below half-full, demonstrating the staff's attentiveness to details many diners might overlook. The atmosphere remained pleasant throughout, with only a brief noise issue from a neighboring table that quickly self-corrected when they noticed the entire dining room's attention. The experience proved so memorable that we're planning another visit during our next trip to see my brother. This restaurant clearly understands what makes exceptional dining.

Disappointing Teppanyaki Experience While the atmosphere was enjoyable, this teppanyaki restaurant fell short in several key areas. The food quality was merely okay, and portions were disappointingly small given the premium pricing. More concerning was the poor service—our chef mixed up orders and attempted to overcharge our group compared to friends who ordered identical items. When confronted about the billing discrepancy, he offered no apology whatsoever, demonstrating a lack of basic customer service skills. For a special dining experience, there are definitely better teppanyaki options available. Consider looking elsewhere for your hibachi needs.

Bait-and-Switch Pricing Ruined Experience Extremely disappointed with deceptive pricing practices. Initially quoted $10 for a polish change, then staff offered to clip cuticles without mentioning additional charges. Final bill jumped to $20—double the original quote. For that price, a complete pedicure is available elsewhere. This misleading approach feels like a deliberate ripoff. Clear upfront pricing is essential; this business lacks transparency and integrity. Cannot recommend.

**Disappointing Experience - Not Authentic Mexican** Bland, flavorless food that fell far short of authentic Mexican cuisine expectations. As an LA visitor, this was a letdown that ruined my evening. Would not return.

A Classy Asian Fusion Experience Worth Every Penny Sensi delivers an exceptional Asian fusion dining experience that justifies its premium pricing. On our second visit, my husband and I were once again impressed by the restaurant's consistent quality and sophisticated atmosphere. The pork potstickers remain absolutely unreal – we devoured them with enthusiasm. My Filet Mignon, enhanced by substituting the black truffle béarnaise sauce for the peppercorn, proved to be an inspired choice that elevated the dish beautifully. The ambiance strikes the perfect balance between elegance and comfort. The glass-walled kitchen provides entertaining views of chefs at work, adding an engaging element to the dining experience. During our Sunday evening visit, the quiet atmosphere provided a welcome respite after a busy weekend. Our server demonstrated excellent professionalism, offering helpful guidance without being intrusive – perfectly suited to our desire for a peaceful meal together. For those with room remaining, the Ice Bubble dessert – featuring sorbet or gelato served in a stunning ice bowl – provides a memorable finale. Sensi consistently delivers exceptional food, inviting atmosphere, and attentive service. Highly recommended for special occasions or anyone seeking top-tier Asian fusion cuisine.

Aggressive Sales Tactics and Disappointing Atmosphere This cigar lounge fails on multiple fronts. The aggressive sales approach at the entrance feels more like a car dealership than a relaxing retreat. The owner comes across as pompous, and there's an uncomfortable class division between members and non-members. The "lounge" area features impractical dinner table chairs rather than comfortable seating. The cigar selection is mediocre at best, and the inconvenient parking situation—with only one entrance and exit—adds to the frustration. Overall, a big disappointment for anyone seeking a quality cigar experience.

Almost Naked in Vegas: Hot Guys, Cheap Venue The performance space falls short of expectations—lacking a proper stage and giving the show an unfortunately cheap atmosphere, as other reviewers noted. While the dancing and stripping veers toward cheesy territory, the performers themselves mostly deliver on the eye candy factor. It's decent entertainment, though the venue significantly detracts from the overall experience.

A Steakhouse That Delivers on All Fronts Smith & Wollensky stands out as a top-tier dining destination that excels across multiple dimensions. The restaurant captures the essence of a traditional steakhouse with its speakeasy-inspired decor and lounge atmosphere, creating an ambiance that's both sophisticated and inviting. The service is exceptional, with attentive staff who understand the steakhouse experience. Behind the bar, some of the city's finest bartenders craft excellent cocktails to complement your meal. While some reviews vary, this reviewer maintains a consistent approach: judging a steakhouse by its signature offering—the steak itself. Specifically, the filet mignon serves as the ultimate benchmark, and Smith & Wollensky passes this test with flying colors. Though the menu offers various options including lamb, pork chops, and ribs, the quality of their perfectly prepared filet demonstrates why this establishment deserves its reputation. For anyone seeking an above-average steakhouse experience, Smith & Wollensky comes highly recommended.

A Food Lover's Paradise on Princes Street **Mark & Spencer Simply Food Review** For anyone who appreciates quality prepared foods, M&S Simply Food needs no introduction. Their melt-in-your-mouth chocolate cookies, diverse sandwich selection, crisp vegetable pizzas, and the iconic Percy Pigs have earned a devoted following—and I'm proudly among them. The Princes Street branch is particularly impressive due to its substantial size, offering an extensive selection that showcases the best of M&S's food range. However, its prime Edinburgh location means it can become incredibly busy, with queues that sometimes seem endless. But for dedicated fans, not even the crowds can diminish the appeal of those beloved Percy Pigs. ## A Convenient Shopping Break During a recent Topshop expedition—exhausting work for any dedicated shopper—I found myself craving the chicken couscous salad box with pumpkin, green beans, and balsamic vinegar dressing. Making a beeline for the refrigerated section, I quickly secured my prize. The temptation of browsing led to additional purchases: a salmon and cream cheese sandwich, a juice box, and naturally, a cookie. ## Hidden Gem: The Café What many shoppers might overlook is this branch's own café area—a welcome discovery that transforms a quick food stop into a proper dining experience. Settling down to enjoy my substantial lunch, every bite confirmed why M&S Simply Food commands such loyalty. **The Verdict:** Despite the inevitable crowds, this Simply Food branch delivers exceptional quality and variety. Whether you're a Percy Pig enthusiast or simply appreciate well-prepared food, it's worth the visit.

Frustrating Experience Despite Friendly Staff While the staff members are pleasant, this location falls far short of acceptable standards. The restaurant consistently has multiple homeless individuals inside, creating an uncomfortable atmosphere for paying customers. Most concerning is the inexplicably slow service – waiting 10 minutes for a small order of curly fries is unacceptable. Though management can't control external factors affecting the environment, they absolutely can improve service speed. When customers feel rushed to leave due to uncomfortable surroundings, efficient service becomes crucial. This location needs significant operational improvements to meet basic fast-food expectations.

A Disappointing Lunch Experience During NBA Finals I selected this establishment for an NBA Finals lunch break, but the experience was thoroughly disappointing from start to finish. After arriving, I waited an incredible 15 minutes just to receive a menu. When the waitress finally appeared, she seemed genuinely annoyed about having to work, which set an uncomfortable tone. The restaurant was only half-full with minimal activity, making the excessive wait time and poor attitude inexplicable. Scanning the menu, I noticed prices seemed inflated for an off-the-Strip sports bar lunch venue. The entire staff appeared miserable—depressed or angry—resembling what I could only describe as a Siberian gulag crew. After waiting another five minutes without service, despite actively trying to flag someone down, I abandoned hope and left hungry. With countless similar establishments lining Sunset, I deeply regret wasting half my lunch hour at this particular location.

Disappointing Pre-Prom Dinner at Fire Water My friends and I chose Fire Water for our pre-prom dinner, noting their 90 health rating. Unfortunately, the experience fell short of expectations from start to finish. The inconsistencies began immediately when my pineapple juice arrived in an unusually small glass that didn't justify the price. When I ordered a second one later, it came in a larger glass for the same cost, which was confusing and frustrating. The Caesar salad was unremarkable—nothing beyond typical. While our entrees were well-portioned, they severely lacked flavor and seasoning. The dessert situation was particularly disappointing; my first choice tasted frozen, and the replacement they offered wasn't much better. Service was another significant issue, as our waiter rarely checked on our table throughout the meal. For a special occasion like prom, this restaurant failed to deliver on quality, consistency, or service. I won't be returning to Fire Water and cannot recommend it for important celebrations.

A Disappointing Alternative: Impatient Service and Underwhelming Sushi After being a devoted fan of Naked Fish Sushi Bar across town, I eagerly searched for a closer alternative and decided to try this frequently-passed establishment. Unfortunately, my experience fell drastically short of expectations. The problems began immediately upon entering. The restaurant was uncomfortably cold, and even the tap water tasted peculiar—possibly from unclean glasses. While service was adequate after ordering, the staff's impatience beforehand was palpable. They repeatedly approached our table asking if we were ready to order, despite the extensive menu requiring considerable time to review—nearly ten minutes in my case. The pricing structure clearly pushes customers toward the all-you-can-eat option at $26 for dinner, with individual rolls priced excessively high at over $11 each. I sampled two half-portions: the rainbow roll proved acceptable but unremarkable, while the "happy ending" roll was genuinely disappointing. This reimagined Philadelphia roll featuring lemon slices and garlic ponzu sauce suffered from overpowering citrus and garlic flavors that completely dominated the delicate fish, leaving an unpleasant aftertaste. Given the abundance of positive reviews, my expectations were admittedly elevated. Unfortunately, this establishment cannot compete with Naked Fish's quality, making the extra drive worthwhile for superior sushi and hospitable service.

A Music Store That Hits All the Right Notes This music store stands out for its impressive selection and genuinely helpful staff who take time to explain products thoroughly. The guitar shop, led by Andy, deserves special mention—despite being consistently busy, he remains friendly and delivers quality setups, typically with next-day turnaround. While occasionally requiring a second visit for adjustments, the service remains reliable. The real gem is their 2-year setup plan at approximately $35, offering eight setups worth around $30 each—an exceptional value that's renewable every two years. This alone makes purchasing here worthwhile. Beyond guitars, all departments maintain high standards, and the store's try-before-you-buy policy works seamlessly with their online platform. Their lowest price guarantee adds another compelling reason to shop here. Minor setup adjustments aside, this store combines knowledgeable staff, great policies, and competitive pricing. Whether you're browsing in-store or buying online, they've created a customer-friendly experience that keeps musicians coming back. **Rating: Highly Recommended**

A Disappointing Experience That Won't Be Repeated When a friend generously gifted us a Groupon voucher offering $40 worth of dining for $20, my partner and I decided to give this restaurant a try. The online menu looked promising, so we made reservations with hopeful expectations. Unfortunately, what followed was an evening of consistently poor service and underwhelming food that left us certain we won't be returning. ## Poor First Impressions Our troubles began immediately upon arrival. There was no signage or staff communication indicating that guests with reservations could bypass the waiting line. While this wasn't a major issue, it set the tone for the confusion that would characterize our entire visit. ## Neglectful Service Once seated, we were essentially ignored for the first 15 minutes. After finally ordering drinks, we never received refills throughout the entire meal—a basic service expectation at any restaurant. Our waiter was conspicuously absent, checking on us only sporadically and rushing past without properly engaging when we needed assistance. ## Subpar Food Quality The appetizers arrived after 30 minutes and were immediately disappointing. The lobster bisque was served lukewarm and contained no actual lobster—only two ravioli sitting at the bottom of an oversized bowl. The Caesar salad consisted of half a romaine heart, sliced lengthwise including the bitter core, forcing us to perform surgery on our own salad before we could eat it. ## Main Course Mishap Our veal entrée arrived 45-55 minutes after ordering and had an unpleasant, off-putting taste that made it difficult to finish. When our waiter finally asked about the meal, he gave me barely enough time to nod before disappearing again. ## The Final Straw Even requesting our check proved challenging—our waiter ignored our first attempt and took an additional eight minutes to respond. Throughout our frustrating experience, we noticed the general manager observing our obvious dissatisfaction but never approached to address our concerns. We left minimal gratuity, which I rarely do, but felt justified given the circumstances. With one-star service, two-star food quality, and nothing unique on the menu, there's simply no compelling reason to return.

Painfully Slow Service Overshadows Good Food Despite decent food quality, this Mother's Day 2013 visit was marred by excruciatingly slow service. A two-hour ordeal with apparently only one server, busser, and cook left us waiting an hour just for our meals. While the apologetic server offered complimentary appetizers and the food ultimately satisfied, the glacial pace was unacceptable. The proximity to our home makes it disappointing, but we won't be returning. Better staffing is desperately needed.

Deceptive "Loyalty" Offer Ruins Customer Trust What appeared to be an attractive owners loyalty promotion quickly soured when nearly $2,000 in surprise add-on fees—dubbed the "Coulter package"—were revealed at purchase time. The unexpected charges were so egregious that this couple now uses the term as household shorthand for corporate price gouging. When legitimate businesses disguise true costs until the final moment, they don't just lose a sale—they create lasting negative brand associations that customers will remember and share.

Good Food, Poor Service at Sushi Samba While Sushi Samba delivered on culinary excellence, the service experience was disappointing. Seated promptly after our show, we enjoyed a stellar cucumber cocktail and exceptional appetizers. The salt and pepper squid was a standout, and every roll arrived fresh and delicious. Unfortunately, our waiter was clearly overwhelmed and disorganized. We constantly had to flag him down for basic needs, and he never proactively checked on our table. Getting the check became an ordeal that dragged on far too long. Having visited Sushi Samba locations in NYC and Miami with consistently good service, this location's staff shortcomings were particularly noticeable. Great food deserves equally great service.

DMV Visit: A Necessary Evil Going to the DMV (or perhaps it's called MVD now?) is never something I look forward to. As a matter of fact, I pretty much dread it and procrastinate it as much as possible. This was the case over the last few weeks. I finally decided to legally change my last name (five years into marriage). Step two of the process was a visit to the DMV to get a new license. I found a time in my schedule on a Wednesday morning that I could make work, and I went for it. I figured it couldn't take more than an hour to do so, or could it? ## The Long Wait It sure could..... it was a slow day for them, according to the woman that I worked with, after I was called to window 18 to get my new photo taken. Even on a supposedly "slow day," it still took me over an hour and a half to get in and out. ## The Atmosphere No one seemed happy to be working there (or to be visiting there), but I guess that's part of the reason that it's not a fun place to go. You get what you expect - nothing more and nothing less. Take a driving test, register a vehicle, get a new license, do what you need to do..... the fine folks at this office will take care of you, just make sure you have all of the documentation prior, and make sure you're not on a tight schedule. ## Moving Forward All of that being said, I'm glad that part of my visit is done. Now onto the next steps of the name change!

A Disappointing Visit to Charlotte's Crepe Cellar Despite its reputation as a popular Charlotte dining destination, my recent visit to Crepe Cellar left me feeling distinctly underwhelmed. From lackluster service to overhyped menu items, the experience fell short of expectations in several key areas. ## Service That Missed the Mark Arriving on a weekday evening, my husband and I found ourselves as the sole diners for a considerable period. While our waitress wasn't overtly rude or unpleasant, her demeanor suggested disinterest rather than hospitality. She seemed to have other priorities, checking on us infrequently and without enthusiasm. There was no attempt to describe menu highlights or engage meaningfully with our dining experience. Perhaps she was simply trying to avoid being overbearing, but the result felt more like neglect than respectful space. ## Mixed Results on the Menu We shared three items: the house salad, fish and chips, and the much-lauded bananas foster crepe. The house salad started promisingly but was sabotaged by an overpoweringly garlicky dressing that made finishing even half a challenge—unusual for someone who typically enjoys salad. The fish and chips proved to be the evening's highlight. The fish itself was perfectly executed with crispy breading encasing tender, moist fish—fresh-tasting without any unpleasant fishiness. Unfortunately, the fries, though properly cooked, were excessively salty, and the tartar sauce was merely adequate rather than memorable. ## The Infamous Crepe Falls Flat Then came the bananas foster crepe, which numerous reviews had praised enthusiastically. This was our most significant disappointment. Given the hype, I anticipated something spectacular. Instead, the crepe was utterly unremarkable—not offensive, just boring. I've genuinely had better homemade crepes from friends who'd just learned the technique that same day. The disconnect between reputation and reality was jarring. ## Final Verdict While I appreciate having tried Crepe Cellar, I'm uncertain about returning. First impressions matter considerably, and this one suggested an establishment resting on its laurels rather than consistently delivering quality. Between the disengaged service and underwhelming signature dish, the experience was more sleep-inducing than satisfying. Charlotte surely offers better dining options worth exploring.

A Disappointing Decline: Why I'll Never Return to Seasons 52 Biltmore My relationship with Seasons 52 began promisingly at their Sacramento location, where an exceptional first experience prompted me to contact corporate and eagerly visit the Biltmore location near home. Unfortunately, what followed was a steady decline across three visits that ultimately destroyed any loyalty I had developed. ## Service That Misses the Mark The problems began with staff prioritization issues. Sitting at the bar, I experienced repeated neglect as employees seemed more interested in entertaining themselves than attending to customers. In an industry literally called "service," this fundamental failure was striking and frustrating. ## The Soup Incident The breaking point came during a holiday visit when I ordered two steak and mushroom soups to-go. Upon arriving home, I discovered they'd given me completely wrong items—an unacceptable mistake that necessitated a return trip. ## Management's Dismissive Response Arriving at 11:01am the next day to avoid the lunch rush, I waited 22 minutes while the manager attended a staff meeting. His eventual appearance included zero apologies—not for the incorrect order, not for my extended wait, nothing. His immediate assumption was "You want a refund, right?" rather than asking if I still wanted the correct soup. While he provided a refund and $25-off card, his dismissive attitude felt more transactional than apologetic. ## The Final Insult Forty-five days later, when presenting the $25-off card, the bartender informed me it was a seasonal promotion no longer valid—rendering the manager's gesture meaningless. ## Corporate Connection Concerns Knowing Darden Restaurants (owners of Olive Garden and Red Lobster) operates Seasons 52 raises questions about their understanding of fine dining expectations versus casual chain restaurant standards. **Bottom line:** Never again—not even for free. This establishment has forgotten that customer service means actually serving customers.

A Historic Cinema Turned Beloved Brewery The Vogel brewery has found its home in Ettlingen's former cinema, creating a unique dining destination. Most memorable is their Sunday brunch accompanied by lively jazz music—an experience worth seeking out if still available. Their signature Vogelbräu beer is excellent and available at both locations: Ettlingen and Karlsruhe. Despite lunch crowds, service remains impressively efficient. A charming spot combining good beer, food, and atmosphere.

Disappointing Stay Despite High Expectations After driving past this property numerous times, we finally decided to stop in, but unfortunately encountered multiple issues throughout our visit. Our experience began poorly with disorganized valet service that provided conflicting directions and slow luggage handling. The Mexican restaurant proved equally frustrating with extended wait times due to understaffing, incomplete orders, and inattentive service requiring multiple requests for refills. Room amenities were problematic—the ice machine was non-functional, with staff unconvincingly blaming other guests rather than addressing the issue promptly. We were forced to trek to the first floor for ice. The bathtub wouldn't hold water, making it unusable for our child. Even the Newcastle bottled beers tasted off, suggesting improper storage or heat exposure. While we managed through these inconveniences, this may have simply been an off day for the establishment.

Best drunk food ever! Walk out of Marquee on the third floor of Cosmo and you will see a small door entry to drunk pizza heaven! If you break it down, it is a simple pizza, similar to Sbarro but the alcohol in your system make it taste so much better! The prices are a bit high, but after spending all that money while in Vegas, what's 12 bucks for 2 slices of pizza or $39 for a whole pie? Be prepared for long lines, drunk people and a very small cramped inside.

Solid Bagel Spot in Arizona Enjoyed lunch at this bagel shop today. The selection is impressive and significantly better than chain alternatives in Arizona, though it doesn't quite match authentic New York bagels. Standout features include bagels with toppings on both sides, quality Boar's Head meats, and Snapple beverages. Perfect for a quick, satisfying breakfast or lunch option.

Exceptional Service and Delicious Breakfast at [Restaurant Name] Our inaugural visit exceeded expectations! Travis provided outstanding, attentive service that rivaled Disney-level hospitality. The strawberry cream cheese French toast impressed, but the chili relleno omelette was absolutely phenomenal—our definite favorite. We're already planning our return visit to this gem!

A Budget-Friendly Vegas Stay with Character (and Maybe Ghosts?) For travelers seeking value on the Strip, this property delivers impressive bang for your buck. The standout feature is their generous upgrade policy—receiving complimentary upgrades to strip views and deluxe accommodations upon check-in twice during one week demonstrates genuine hospitality. The staff consistently proves friendly and helpful throughout. Located in the Chrysler tower, navigating to your room can be challenging with luggage or children. The bell desk assistance is strongly recommended due to the maze-like layout. One notable quirk: a burger restaurant vent apparently channels directly into the 21st-floor hallway, creating persistent food odors. Room amenities are basic—no fridge or microwave—and bathrooms show their age. However, the exceptionally plush, comfortable beds compensate significantly. The casino maintains a pleasantly uncrowded atmosphere, and having Hershey's World on-site adds entertainment value. The paranormal element deserves mention: unexplained electrical phenomena including lights and television turning on/off independently, plus returning to darkened rooms despite leaving lights on. Whether you believe in ghosts or chalk it up to electrical issues, it's certainly memorable. **Bottom line:** Despite quirks and outdated features, the combination of affordable rates, complimentary upgrades, excellent staff, and unique character makes this a solid budget choice.

Mixed Experience at Fusion Casino Spot Met friends here for pre-gaming drinks and appetizers. The food leans fusion rather than authentic Japanese - if you're seeking genuine flavors, Ichiza is the better choice. Appetizers were merely adequate, nothing memorable. The atmosphere was notably loud, though attractive hosts at the entrance added appeal. Strong drinks and attentive service were definite highlights. However, pricing seems steep for a local casino establishment. **Bottom line:** Good for drinks, skip for food.

A Delightful Independent Asian Gem This charming independent restaurant has quickly become a new favorite, surpassing even wagamama. The star attraction? Exceptional dumplings that are simply irresistible. The pork dumplings proved to be the perfect light meal, while the vegetable version offered a pleasant spicy kick alongside those essential greens. Both varieties were delicious and left a lasting impression. The atmosphere beautifully blends Eastern and Western aesthetics, featuring wooden floorboards and simple wall paintings that create genuine character without overwhelming the space. The extensive menu offers plenty of variety, making it an ideal spot for exploring Japanese cuisine. This restaurant definitely warrants a return visit with companions, and there's genuine excitement about venturing beyond the dumpling menu. For anyone seeking quality Asian cuisine from an independent establishment, this spot delivers on all fronts.

A New Breed of Accounting Firm I despise accounting, yet I genuinely look forward to my weekly meetings with Tina and her talented crew at AccountingProse. They represent a refreshing departure from traditional number crunchers. What sets them apart is their commitment to innovation—constantly updating tools and processes, even abandoning outdated systems for proven new solutions that actually reduce their billable hours. This unselfish approach puts clients' needs first, demonstrating rare integrity in the industry. The team is smart, efficient, detail-oriented, and incredibly hardworking. If you're seeking accountants who actively work to improve your business operations rather than simply maintaining books, AccountingProse is worth every penny.

A Disappointing Experience: Why This Bakery Misses the Mark When a business undergoes new management, customers typically hope for positive changes and improvements. Unfortunately, this bakery proves that ownership changes don't always translate to better service or quality. After multiple visits, my husband and I have concluded this establishment simply isn't worth returning to. ## Customer Service Falls Flat The most glaring issue is the consistently poor customer service. With the exception of one pleasant Francophone woman working morning shifts, the staff appears genuinely unhappy to serve customers. What's particularly frustrating is encountering a newer employee who refuses to communicate in English, despite other staff members being bilingual. This creates an unwelcoming atmosphere that makes every visit uncomfortable. ## Order Accuracy Problems Attention to detail seems nonexistent here. On separate occasions, we've received completely wrong items – a chocolate chip cookie instead of the requested scone, and ham replacing turkey on a sandwich. These weren't mistakes made during rush hours; the establishment was practically empty. Such errors demonstrate a fundamental lack of care toward customers and their orders. ## Poor Value for Money Perhaps most shocking is the price-to-quality ratio. The "deli sandwiches" are laughably skimpy, featuring just one paper-thin slice of meat, minimal cheese, and a single lettuce leaf. When requesting additional vegetables like tomatoes, customers are met with arbitrary rules about breakfast-only items. The $10.95 meal deal includes this inadequate sandwich, a small juice, tiny salad, and minimal dessert – before taxes. This pricing seems outrageous for what you actually receive. ## Quality Concerns The refrigerated pastries taste stale and carry an unpleasant refrigerator flavor, suggesting they're far from fresh. While the breads are passable, they're significantly overpriced for what they are. ## Additional Frustrations Adding insult to injury, there's a strict $20 minimum for credit card purchases. Staff have reportedly refused transactions just cents below this threshold, creating unnecessary inconvenience for customers. ## Final Verdict Despite new management, this bakery maintains the same problems that likely plagued it previously. Between indifferent service, incorrect orders, poor value, questionable quality, and inflexible policies, there's simply no compelling reason to give this establishment your business. Save your money and find a bakery that actually values its customers. **Rating: 0 stars (if possible)**

A Pho Lover's Delight: Blue Moon Delivers on Taste and Value As someone who's always seeking the perfect bowl of Pho, I'm thrilled to report that Blue Moon has significantly improved since my last visit. While their infamous Pho Challenge features a bowl so massive it'll make you "slouch in a fetal position," the regular portions are perfectly satisfying without being overwhelming. What truly stands out is the exceptional value – at approximately $3.50 per bowl, you're getting authentic Vietnamese cuisine without breaking the bank. The restaurant features modest, modern décor that creates a comfortable dining atmosphere, while the service team stays attentive and efficient throughout your meal. Whether you're a Pho enthusiast or casual diner, Blue Moon offers genuine flavor at unbeatable prices. Full belly guaranteed – just skip the challenge unless you're exceptionally hungry!

A Burger Experience Worth Writing Home About This establishment serves what might be the finest burger and fries combination available. The Banh Mi Burger exemplifies culinary excellence—perfectly cooked, exceptionally juicy, and thoughtfully composed. Fresh herbs and daikon provide a satisfying textural contrast that elevates each bite beyond ordinary burger fare. The truffle fries, while difficult to compare without prior experience, prove undeniably delicious and complement the burger beautifully. The Vietnamese Coffee falls slightly short of expectations, suffering from excessive regular milk rather than the traditional condensed milk, resulting in a disappointingly light flavor profile. This remains the meal's only notable shortcoming. Service quality deserves particular recognition. Observing management actively participating in operational tasks—removing trash and cleaning tables during busy periods—demonstrates commendable leadership rarely witnessed in dining establishments. The interior maintains excellent cleanliness and pleasant aesthetics. However, two minor detractors emerged: excessively loud music inappropriate for the time of day, and a clientele heavily skewed toward hipster demographics. Despite these negligible inconveniences, neither the atmospheric concerns nor the customer demographic diminish the exceptional quality of the food. This restaurant delivers an outstanding dining experience that transcends its minor imperfections, making it highly recommended for burger enthusiasts.

Chick-fil-A: Excellence in Fast Food, Despite the Sunday Situation When it comes to fast-food chicken, Chick-fil-A has carved out a special place in the culinary landscape, ranking alongside heavyweights like Chipotle and In-N-Out. However, there's one point of contention that keeps this establishment from perfection: their controversial Sunday closure policy. ## The Sunday Debate The reviewer's father sees the Sunday closing as a demonstration of principled commitment, refusing to compromise beliefs for profit. The reviewer, however, takes a more pragmatic stance – when you want chicken, you want chicken, regardless of the day. It's a debate that encapsulates the tension between corporate values and consumer convenience, and both perspectives have merit. ## Quality That Speaks for Itself Setting aside the scheduling disagreement, Chick-fil-A delivers exceptional quality. The chicken is consistently juicy, tender, and flavorful, complemented generously with pickles for those who appreciate them. The variety of sauce options adds a personalized touch to each meal, allowing customers to feel involved in crafting their perfect sandwich – even if that sense of accomplishment might be slightly exaggerated. ## Beverage Options Done Right The fountain drink selection deserves special recognition, offering both Coke Zero and Diet Dr Pepper as zero-calorie alternatives. In an era of increasing health consciousness, this variety is refreshing. The reviewer makes a valid point about the peculiarity of consuming 240 empty calories from regular soda, though acknowledges the occasional hangover exception. The suggestion for touch-screen Coke Freestyle machines would be a welcome upgrade. ## Exceptional Customer Service Perhaps most impressive is the consistently outstanding service. Every employee seems genuinely pleasant and helpful, suggesting this isn't coincidental but rather part of systematic training. Whether this stems from having Sundays off or simply strong company culture remains unclear, but the result is undeniable: customers feel valued and appreciated. **The Bottom Line:** Despite the Sunday inconvenience, Chick-fil-A delivers premium fast food with remarkable consistency and service that sets industry standards.

A Disappointing Family Lunch Experience Our Saturday family lunch at this establishment was thoroughly underwhelming. For $28, we fed four people, but the low price came with serious quality compromises. We sampled three chicken dishes: peppered chicken, General's chicken, and an unidentified mystery chicken. All were horrid. The General's chicken was particularly offensive, tasting like fried liver rather than chicken—so bad I had to spit it out. Even the Mongolian BBQ, typically a safe bet, was disappointing. I'd never encountered bad MBBQ until now. While nobody got sick afterward, that's hardly a ringing endorsement. This experience was so memorably poor that it prompted my first-ever restaurant review. We definitely won't be returning, and I suspect the five-star reviews must be from employees or mistaken diners.

Disappointing Experience at Urban Taco I had high hopes when Urban Taco opened in the Central Corridor, but my visit fell short of expectations. The store-bought chips (seemingly Tostitos) weren't authentic, and the cucumber salsa lacked the crunch and spice needed to elevate it. All three street tacos I sampled were underseasoned. While they're an improvement over Americas Tacos, there's significant room for growth. As someone with Hispanic heritage, I'd strongly recommend making homemade tortilla chips and properly seasoning the dishes—these changes would make a world of difference.

Disappointing Store Standards and Presentation This Poundstretcher location falls significantly short of acceptable retail standards. The store interior appears dirty and poorly maintained, with worn-out fixtures creating an unwelcoming shopping environment. Staff presentation is particularly concerning, with descriptions of unkempt appearances and unprofessional attire being common. The reviewer notes a stark contrast with competitor Poundland, which apparently maintains superior presentation standards. Interestingly, they observe that Poundstretcher's out-of-town retail park locations perform much better than their in-town stores, suggesting inconsistent management standards across the chain. While staff friendliness receives acknowledgment, their unprofessional appearance undermines the overall shopping experience. The chain clearly needs comprehensive improvement in store maintenance and employee presentation standards.

Disappointing Brunch Experience: Three Strikes and We're Out After three visits to this neighborhood restaurant this year, we've reluctantly decided it won't become our regular spot despite living around the corner. Our most recent Sunday brunch with friends highlighted persistent issues that have plagued each visit. The inventory management remains baffling—this time they were inexplicably out of chorizo and diet Coke, basic items any restaurant should stock adequately. While our waitress consistently provides friendly service, the experience suffers from more significant problems. The brunch menu proved expensive and underwhelming. The waffles arrived exceptionally dry, served only with whipped cream and fruit topping. When requesting syrup, we were pointedly informed none was available—an odd choice for a waffle dish. Other menu items featured surprisingly small portions with minimal food cost, yet commanded prices between $10-14. Most disappointing was the complete absence of engagement from the owner/chef, despite guests sitting within ten feet of him. His only notable interaction involved publicly arguing with a family over an online coupon—an uncomfortable scene we witnessed while paying full price for subpar food. This coupon dispute appears to be a recurring issue, as we've observed billing disagreements during each visit. The combination of inadequate inventory, overpriced mediocre food, poor value, and absent hospitality has exhausted our patience. Three chances were generous, but this restaurant has definitively struck out.

A Disappointing Experience: Atrocious Service and Subpar Sushi Our visit to this establishment was utterly disappointing from start to finish. Despite the restaurant not being busy, we endured a 45-minute wait just to receive our first roll, which was merely acceptable. What followed was even worse—our waiter vanished for another 30 minutes before checking on us. The subsequent rolls were shockingly mediocre; we've honestly had better sushi from grocery stores. When we received a dish that didn't match its menu description and requested it be corrected, the staff flatly refused our reasonable request. After spending two frustrating hours with minimal service and $65 lighter, we left still hungry. The experience reached its nadir when our waiter had the audacity to insult our palates, comparing our tastes to a casual chain restaurant. This level of unprofessionalism was absolutely unacceptable. My wife, who has experience working in upscale sushi establishments, was appalled by the disrespect and lack of basic hospitality. The overpriced, bland sushi combined with the staff's terrible attitudes makes this place impossible to recommend. We're genuinely puzzled by the positive reviews this restaurant has received. For truly exceptional sushi, we highly recommend visiting Harumi Sushi at 114 W Adams St instead.

Outstanding First Visit Based on Yelp Recommendation Discovered this gem through Yelp and ordered the daily special: Jerk Mahi-Mahi with blueberry vanilla cream sauce, collard greens, and mashed sweet potatoes. The Ice Pick (sweet tea with vodka) perfectly complemented the meal. Absolutely delicious! Grateful to fellow Yelpers for this excellent recommendation. Highly satisfied first-time experience.

A Sunday Brunch Adventure: Fiesta Champagne Breakfast Review After spotting an advertisement for the Fiesta champagne breakfast, my craving for a mimosa led us to this conveniently located spot on a Sunday morning. At $8.99 with the card, it proved to be a worthwhile visit with mostly delicious offerings. ## The Good and the Great The buffet impressed with its vast selection, though keeping everything warm and fresh presented the usual buffet challenges. The menudo stood out remarkably—surprisingly better than most Mexican restaurants! The dessert spread was exceptional, featuring an incredible variety. I tried a mini bran-raisin muffin (about one-sixth to one-eighth the size of jumbo muffins), which was absolutely perfect in both taste and portion. ## What's Available The selection included made-to-order omelets (expect a line), various soups including albondigas and menudo, and Chinese options. While the Chinese food disappointed overall, the eggroll was surprisingly good. Fresh fruit options were limited to melon and cantaloupe, which I enjoyed with cottage cheese. ## Value Proposition Monday through Wednesday offers 2-for-1 buffets with the card—though as I joked, I don't need buffets *that* often! Despite minor shortcomings in the fresh fruit department and keeping everything piping hot, the variety, quality, and price point make this a place I'd definitely revisit for a weekend brunch.

All About the Bottom Line Long-time Pure Fitness member here, now transitioning to LA Fitness. This is a no-frills facility - come prepared to just work out. The club is smaller with no separate class rooms or real amenities. Fair warning: those "free" training sessions are primarily sales pitches for expensive personal training at $65+ per hour. Be ready to politely decline. The focus here is clearly on revenue generation rather than member support, so you'll need to be self-sufficient with your fitness routine. Bring independence and realistic expectations.

Mixed Experience at Hidden Catholic Church This modest Catholic church offers an interesting stop for visitors of various denominations. While the location proves challenging to find—tucked back in a parking lot past the Wynn and Encore rather than streetside—it's worth seeking out. The worship experience can be inconsistent, with sermons varying in quality from visit to visit. However, the church compensates with thoughtful amenities, including a charming gift shop that adds to the overall experience. Despite not being the reviewer's primary denomination, the welcoming atmosphere encouraged a return visit, making it a worthwhile destination for those seeking spiritual reflection.

A Disastrous Nail Salon Experience: When $85 Buys Nothing But Disappointment As someone who typically doesn't complain about nail services, this experience was shockingly unacceptable. From start to finish, everything that could go wrong did go wrong. The technician's extremely shaky hands resulted in multiple cuts throughout the service—more than I could count. The application was equally troubling, with nails extending one and a half times beyond my actual nail beds, creating an unnatural and uncomfortable appearance. I requested a pink and white design, but the execution was disastrous. The white portions were completely inconsistent across all nails. One nail particularly stood out with white measuring three-eighths of an inch on one side and only one-eighth on the other—a glaring asymmetry impossible to ignore. Hygiene concerns added another layer of disappointment. The equipment used for scrubbing appeared unsanitary, stored carelessly in a dirty cup. Despite voicing my concerns multiple times, the technician seemed unwilling or unable to listen. He only attempted to smooth the nails after my third complaint, demonstrating poor customer service and lack of attention to detail. After spending $85, I'm now forced to visit another salon tomorrow for a complete redo. I cannot trust this establishment to correct their mistakes. This experience serves as a cautionary tale—sometimes the lowest price comes with the highest cost.

**Exceptional Service from All Pro Window Tint** I've trusted All Pro Window Tint for two cars and my home, and David consistently delivers outstanding results. His punctuality is impeccable, and the quality of work is excellent. What sets him apart is his honest, no-pressure approach to customer service. Every experience has left me 100% satisfied. I wholeheartedly recommend David to anyone needing window tinting services.

A Once-Beloved Restaurant's Dramatic Decline This establishment was once a cherished dining destination for my wife and me during the original founders' tenure. The previous owners created a warm, welcoming atmosphere, always making time to connect with patrons—even sitting down for a casual soda during busy shifts.
