Don't skip the unique ice cream flavors like baklava and Mexican chocolate—they're conversation starters and taste sensations rolled into one. ## Final Verdict Bacchanal truly lives up to its name, delivering an afternoon of unapologetic gluttony and indulgence. Come hungry, wear your stretchiest pants, and prepare to sample at least one of everything. This buffet sets the gold standard for Vegas dining excess—in the best possible way.

Cool Little Place in a Rough Neighborhood - But Worth the Adventure Tucked away in what can only be described as a manufacturing wasteland, this restaurant occupies possibly the worst location imaginable. The surrounding area is so challenging that even GPS seems to give up, potentially landing you at a nearby Bojangles instead of your intended destination. I say this as someone who thought they'd already experienced the roughest parts of town—this area might actually top it. But here's the thing: push through the sketchy surroundings and confusing navigation, because what awaits is genuinely worth the effort. My visit was for their "Dining in the Dark" event, a charitable fundraiser benefiting the visually challenged. This meant experiencing the restaurant quite differently than typical patrons—specifically, with blindfolds on for the entire meal. Unlike those reality TV shows featuring night-vision cameras and questionable behavior, our experience was authentic and dignified, with actual blindfolds required since we were dining alongside other guests. It provided built-in entertainment for the sighted diners, who seemed to enjoy watching us "normals" fumble through our meal. **The Service Experience** Evaluating service proved challenging under the circumstances. I deliberately avoided drinking much water, terrified of spilling it on myself, my companions, or anywhere else. My glass may have sat empty the entire evening—I'll never know. The pacing felt somewhat slow, though this seems entirely reasonable given staff were managing twenty blindfolded diners while explaining each course, all while maintaining service for regular customers. **The Food: Phenomenal** The food itself was outstanding. My only complaint? Portion size. When you're concentrating exclusively on taste without visual distractions, food becomes exponentially better. I'm certain I consumed things I wouldn't normally order, and probably looked absolutely ridiculous doing so, but the experience was immensely enjoyable. The menu featured oxtail-stuffed ravioli, veal strip loin with ostrich paté, purple Peruvian potatoes, and lemoncello pancetta on almond shortbread. Whether this represents their typical offerings or was specially prepared for our event remains unclear, but every bite tasted phenomenal. **Bottom Line** Despite the horrible location and navigation challenges, this hidden gem delivers a unique, worthwhile dining experience.

Delicious Dining Experience Worth Repeating Exceptional meal from start to finish! Every dish, including perfectly seasoned okra, impressed. The consistently delicious food guarantees our return visit soon.

Unprofessional Timeshare Operation With Serious Concerns This company represents everything wrong with timeshare marketing. Despite requiring a one-star rating just to leave feedback, even that feels too generous for this operation. **Deceptive Practices**: The "free" offers are nothing but bait for timeshare presentations. As numerous reviews confirm, this is a classic timeshare scam designed to pressure unsuspecting visitors into poor financial decisions. **Management Problems**: The leadership, particularly Dave and Bob, allegedly avoid confrontation by timing their visits when legitimate business owners aren't present. They refuse to address complaints or take responsibility for their staff's actions. **Safety Concerns**: Most alarmingly, reports indicate an employee stalked a female worker around the resort. Management allegedly ignored this serious issue and continued scheduling the individual even after property owners banned them from the premises. **Customer Impact**: Operating near this setup means constantly hearing customer complaints, suggesting widespread dissatisfaction with their tactics. The single positive review amid overwhelming negativity speaks volumes. Avoid this company entirely—their business practices are questionable at best, dangerous at worst.

Disappointing Mexican Food Experience This restaurant falls far short of authentic Mexican and New Mexican cuisine standards. Despite three visits, each experience proved consistently disappointing with bland, flavorless food and microwaved cheese lacking any spice. The excessive use of styrofoam packaging and plastic utensils adds to the poor dining experience. While the location near Solo Cafe makes it convenient after studying, the lackluster quality never justifies the cost. Save your money and seek better options elsewhere for genuine, flavorful Mexican food.

A Perfect Late-Night Spot for Comfort Food This establishment proved to be an ideal destination for satisfying late-night cravings, whether needing a caffeine boost or post-celebration comfort food. During a pre-show visit, the burger impressed with its perfectly cooked, juicy patty that avoided greasiness, though the bun could have benefited from additional toasting. The waffle fries were a standout—fantastically crunchy with a pleasant kick. The staff's willingness to customize a milkshake demonstrated excellent customer service, resulting in a thick, rich, and delicious treat. A return visit featured their complete fries sampler, which proved fabulous across the board. The fat fries resembled eating a baked potato—a delightful surprise. Meanwhile, the skinny fries achieved the perfect balance of crispiness without being overdone. The combination of quality food, accommodating service, and strategic location makes this spot perfect for pre-gaming or late-night refueling between activities.

Great Food and Service This all-you-can-eat buffet excels with its quality beef kalbi and excellent spicy pork. The marinades are well-balanced and not overly salty. While the side dish selection is limited compared to typical Korean restaurants—offering white and red kimchi, pickled onions, and garlic stems, but missing staples like roasted black beans and spinach—the overall experience is highly satisfying. The restaurant is particularly recommended for big meat eaters. The combination of good food, service, and value makes it worth returning to and recommending to others.

Hidden Gem Delivers Authentic Excellence Above Expectations Don't let appearances fool you at NiuKee, a second-story establishment tucked away on an unassuming side street. While the exterior screams "hole in the wall" more than fine dining, this Diners, Drive-Ins and Dives-worthy spot proves why you shouldn't judge a restaurant by its facade. Drawn in by enthusiastic Yelp reviews, I discovered a place that compensates for its lackluster aesthetics with exceptional service and genuinely authentic cuisine. The food delivers on every front: savory, fresh, and served in impressively generous portions that justify every penny. The standout dish? The hot and spicy peanut chicken is an absolute must-try that lives up to the hype. NiuKee exemplifies that sometimes the best culinary experiences hide in the most unexpected places.

Overpriced Disappointment in Vegas If you're looking to spend serious money on a Vegas club experience, this isn't the place. While the terrace might appeal to table-reservation guests, the overall venue falls drastically short. The club is cramped, uncomfortably hot, and frankly boring compared to the hundreds of superior options Vegas offers. The experience perfectly combines every nightclub annoyance: an overcrowded dance floor where movement is impossible, frustratingly long drink lines, and an insufferable crowd. Even for non-club enthusiasts, the unreasonable prices make this particularly grating. With so many better alternatives available on the Strip, there's simply no reason to waste your money here.

Hidden Gem for Vegetarian Cuisine This restaurant has converted even non-vegetarians into regulars. While initially planning to sample the entire menu, certain dishes proved so irresistible that repeat orders became inevitable. The lunch specials offer exceptional value and generous portions. Despite basic tableware, the outstanding food quality more than compensates. The chutney bar stands out as a highlight, particularly the addictive pickled accompaniments that could easily be enjoyed on their own. A must-visit spot.

A Reliable Lunch Spot with Great Value The lunch gyro consistently delivers with its tender, delicious meat, complemented by excellent fries. The oversized cups make the $2 iced tea feel like a fair deal compared to other restaurants where you might feel shortchanged. Service is reliably quick, and the restaurant's layout ensures every seat has a TV view—perfect for catching the game during lunch. The sports-friendly atmosphere makes it an ideal spot for groups. However, there's one notable drawback: inconsistent music volume. During a recent Friday lunch visit with coworkers, the music was cranked to club-level loudness, making conversation difficult. While this hasn't been an issue on previous visits, it's worth noting for those seeking a quieter dining experience. Overall, it's a solid choice for lunch, offering quality food and good value.

Disappointing Experience at Special Anniversary Event This venue severely underperformed during what should have been a memorable 40th wedding anniversary vow renewal. The event required months of planning and cross-country travel, making the unprofessional execution particularly frustrating. The most egregious issue was the videographer forgetting to bring out the camera, forcing the heartfelt speech to be completely redone. While staff attempted to salvage the situation by calling it a "practice run," the emotional moment was irreparably damaged. Additionally, the lack of door management resulted in repeated interruptions during the ceremony, further disrupting the special occasion. While the venue shows potential, these fundamental lapses in professionalism are unacceptable for milestone celebrations. Until they significantly improve their attention to detail and event coordination, I cannot recommend this location for important family events.

Disappointing Service Overshadows Good Food I've dined at this establishment several times without issue, but my recent visit left much to be desired. Despite available seating in the dining area, the hostess seated us in the bar section on Super Bowl Sunday—an unfortunate choice given the excessive noise level and my existing headache. The experience began promisingly when a young male waiter took our order professionally. However, a waitress named Ingrid soon informed us she'd be taking over our table. Unfortunately, Ingrid provided virtually no service. Other staff members delivered our appetizers, entrées, and desserts while she remained conspicuously absent. Dirty dishes accumulated at our table's edge despite her walking past multiple times, and my dessert arrived melted and mushy from sitting too long. Most frustrating was watching Ingrid and three other waitresses attentively serve a large party of 8-10 guests nearby while completely neglecting other patrons. As someone who typically tips generously, I left only 50 cents—a clear message about my dissatisfaction. While the food itself was delicious (aside from my compromised dessert and a half-missing strawberry), excellent cuisine cannot compensate for poor customer service. In the restaurant business, attentive service should be paramount. This experience has made me reconsider future visits.

Disappointing First Visit, But Willing to Give Another Chance My inaugural experience at this establishment left much to be desired. The limited menu offered few enticing options, so I defaulted to what should have been a safe choice: chicken wings. Unfortunately, they fell well below the standard set by virtually every other Vegas bar. Ordered medium hot, the wings arrived looking unappetizing—over-processed, heavily breaded, and clearly low-quality. The hot sauce, served in a plastic container, was equally disappointing. The blue cheese was perhaps worst of all: a packet containing runny, flavorless goo that bore little resemblance to proper blue cheese dressing. The sole bright spot was our server, who proved both friendly and efficient throughout the meal. However, the staff's evident pride in their Mexican offerings has piqued my curiosity enough to warrant a return visit, hoping their specialty dishes fare considerably better than their wings.

**A Salad Lover's Paradise with Friendly Service** This restaurant excels at fresh, delicious salads with impressive variety—every option tried has been a winner. The friendly staff creates a welcoming atmosphere that enhances the dining experience. While the pastas remain untested, they look appealing. The soups are consistently excellent, though be sure to request bread for dipping to complete the experience. A reliably satisfying choice for healthy, flavorful meals.

Perfect Strip Location with Great Amenities This is a beautiful theater. It can be very busy because it is on the strip but it is very clean and in a prime spot for meeting up with friends. I will definitely be going back to see more movies here. There is so much to do before and after the show.

A Solid Venue Elevated by Its Live Music I visited the Granary with Kate K to enjoy Caroline Gilmour's fabulous performance. Having been here several times previously, I'd rate it as just okay—but the music events in the Loft truly give this venue its edge. The Loft, aptly named for its top-storey location, offers an intimate gig space with its own bar and additional room to the left of the entrance. It's worth arriving early to dine on the mezzanine floor beforehand. We opted for the bread and oils platter alongside chips with parmesan—simple choices that are hard to fault, and the service was pleasingly quick. For those interested in upcoming performances, music information is readily available on the Granary's website. Overall, it's the live music that transforms this otherwise average venue into something special.

A Scene Worth Visiting, Even If the Food Is Just Average This bustling sushi spot delivers an undeniable atmosphere that compensates for its middle-of-the-road cuisine. Visiting on a packed Friday night, the energy was immediately apparent—the restaurant was filled to capacity with an attractive, attentive staff that clearly takes hospitality seriously. Seated at the sushi bar, the friendly chefs provided solid service, preparing a decent Shrimp Tempura roll that, while good, didn't quite reach memorable status. The Shrimp Shumai proved disappointing with an overly doughy consistency that lacked the proper dumpling texture. However, service excellence shone through with a beautiful, attentive waitress who delivered water, hot miso soup, and steamed edamame within two minutes of seating. The real stars here are the ambiance and staff. House music creates an inviting, unpretentious scene that encourages return visits despite the average food quality. The Hakutsuru Superior sake deserves special mention—a sweet variety best enjoyed straight, not wasted on sake bombs. The four-star rating reflects the phenomenal staff and vibrant atmosphere rather than culinary excellence. There seems to be an unspoken aesthetic standard for front-of-house employees, with only sushi chefs representing male staff members. While the food won't wow you, the combination of friendly service, great music, and lively scene makes this establishment worth experiencing. Come for the vibe and competent service; just temper your expectations about the cuisine.

A Pittsburgh Institution That's Worth Seeing, If Not Always Eating When planning our road trip through Pittsburgh, PA, my girlfriend and I did what most travelers do—we consulted Google for the city's must-see attractions. Primanti Brothers consistently appeared on every "things to do" and "what not to miss" list, so we decided to experience this legendary sandwich shop for ourselves. **Location and Atmosphere** The restaurant's convenient 24-hour operation makes it accessible for any schedule, and parking is manageable with both a small dedicated lot and free street parking after 6pm. Walking inside feels like stepping into a time capsule. With 80 years of history, Primanti Brothers wears its heritage proudly on its walls—literally. Framed newspaper clippings, celebrity photographs, and cheeky "Bite Me...Primanti Brothers" t-shirts create a nostalgic atmosphere reminiscent of classic American diners. The setup is refreshingly straightforward: an open kitchen where you can watch your food being prepared, an adjoining bar area, and a simple wall-mounted placard menu. One practical note: they're cash-only, though an ATM at the entrance saves unprepared visitors from disappointment. **Menu and Options** Fair warning to vegetarians and pescatarians: your choices are limited. Among the predominantly meat-centric menu, you'll find only two fish options, one egg sandwich, and a cheese sandwich. What makes Primanti Brothers distinctive is their signature preparation—every sandwich arrives loaded with french fries, coleslaw, and tomato piled directly onto your protein of choice, all squeezed between two thick slices of white bread. **The Taste Test** My girlfriend and I shared a cheese deluxe sandwich, and our reactions diverged significantly. She thoroughly enjoyed her portion, particularly praising the perfectly greasy fries. Unfortunately, I found mine disappointing. The coleslaw provided a welcome tangy crunch to an otherwise bland sandwich, but several elements fell flat: the cheese was sparse, the bread lacked flavor, and the fries arrived soggy and underseasoned. Adding salt improved them somewhat, but couldn't fully redeem the experience. **Final Verdict** Visiting Primanti Brothers felt more like checking off a cultural landmark than discovering a culinary gem. The reasonable pricing softened the blow of my mediocre meal, and I appreciate having experienced this Pittsburgh tradition. However, if you're short on time or have limited appetite, skipping it wouldn't be tragic. It's worth visiting once for the atmosphere and local flavor, but perhaps manage your gastronomic expectations accordingly.

A Regular's Haven Despite the Haze Big Dog's has earned my loyal patronage, even though the cigarette smoke-filled atmosphere can be unbearable at times. As a self-proclaimed tough cookie, I've learned to overlook this drawback because they excel in the essentials: beer, food, and service. The beer selection stands out in a city dominated by Budweiser products, offering a refreshing dive into local and craft options. The menu is equally impressive, featuring delicious cheese curds and twice-baked wings that keep me coming back. They even accommodate different dietary preferences with veggie burgers. What truly sets Big Dog's apart is their exceptional service. Sitting at tables near the bar, I've experienced consistently outstanding attention from multiple waitresses. They're attentive without being intrusive—my beer never drops below a quarter full before refills are offered, and service quality remains steady regardless of how long I linger. This would easily be a five-star establishment if not for the persistent proximity of smokers. Still, Big Dog's deserves my business every day.

A Flavorful Deep Dive into Cajun Seafood Excellence This welcoming seafood establishment immediately impressed with attentive hospitality, offering diners their choice of seating upon arrival. The relaxed atmosphere set the stage for an exceptional culinary experience. ## Menu Customization at Its Finest The restaurant's flexible ordering system features three heat levels and three distinct seasonings, allowing complete personalization. Our party ordered one pound of snow crab legs with Cravin' Cajun seasoning at medium heat, plus one pound of shrimp with mixed Cajun seasonings. Complementary sides included corn and sweet potato fries. ## Outstanding Service Makes the Difference Our server demonstrated remarkable attentiveness throughout the meal, elevating the entire dining experience. Their recommendation of sweet potato fries proved invaluable, especially paired with remoulade sauce—a spicy Cajun mayo that adds authentic cultural flair. Even for those typically skeptical of sweet potatoes, this combination offers an adventurous and worthwhile departure from ordinary sides. ## Seafood Quality Shines Through The snow crab legs achieved perfect seasoning balance, where spices enhanced rather than overwhelmed the naturally sweet, juicy crab meat. The same thoughtful preparation elevated the shrimp. This careful sourcing and preparation demonstrates the restaurant's commitment to quality seafood selection. The corn deserves special mention—simply delicious when drenched in the flavorful bag juices. ## Final Verdict This establishment successfully combines quality ingredients, customizable options, and genuine hospitality. The experience warrants return visits to explore additional menu offerings. Highly recommended for seafood enthusiasts seeking authentic Cajun flavors.

Mixed Experience at Local Wing Spot After trying this wing restaurant for the first time since moving to the area, we found it to be an average experience. While hoping for impressive happy hour deals, the specials were merely so-so. Service issues were noticeable, as we ate halfway through our wings before receiving plates or a bone container, suggesting understaffing problems. The wings themselves were just okay, not quite matching up to our usual spot. On the positive side, the restaurant features typical fun décor and multiple large TVs for sports viewing. The staff was friendly, though service moved slowly. Overall, this location serves as an occasional alternative but likely won't replace our regular wing destination due to inconsistent service and average food quality.

**Disappointing Breakfast Experience - Look Elsewhere** After three visits, this establishment continues to underwhelm. While the wait staff is pleasant, the food quality is consistently mediocre. My recent order of corned beef hash arrived burnt, and the poached eggs were overcooked despite minimal crowd. With superior breakfast options nearby, I cannot recommend this restaurant. Save your time and money.

A Disappointing Dining Experience: Poor Service and Subpar Food Our visit to this restaurant was regrettable from start to finish. Despite only three occupied tables and four servers on duty, the service was inexcusably poor. Upon arrival, we were shouted at from across the room to seat ourselves, only to find four out of five available tables still dirty with previous diners' remnants. Our server immediately announced she was new and, unable to locate a pen, attempted to memorize our order. This resulted in multiple return trips just to take our drink and food orders separately. The inefficiency set the tone for the entire meal. The food quality matched the poor service. While the frog legs were acceptable, they had an unpleasantly fishy taste. We ordered wild boar sandwich and meatloaf but received only the sandwich, which proved bland and chewy. Our server vanished entirely, leaving us with an incomplete order. When we placed our credit card on the table—the universal signal for departure—she finally reappeared. Remarkably, the dirty tables from our arrival remained uncleared throughout our visit. The only redeeming feature was the animal display centerpiece. The otherwise plain décor, combined with terrible food and service, makes this one of the worst dining experiences we've encountered. We won't return.

Disappointing Main Course Despite Promising Start We visited for dinner with high expectations, but left feeling let down. The appetizers were fantastic—the fresh guacamole, queso fundido, and chicken quesadilla were amazing and built our anticipation for the main course. Unfortunately, the entrees didn't live up to the promising start. We ordered the carne asada burrito without black beans, but the meat was completely flavorless. The burrito was mostly filled with bland, unseasoned rice that tasted like nothing. While the service was attentive with three servers looking after us, the disappointing quality of the main dishes overshadowed the positive aspects. The stark contrast between the excellent appetizers and lackluster entrees made the experience even more frustrating.

A Disappointing Dining Experience This restaurant visit was unfortunately memorable for all the wrong reasons. Upon entering, I was immediately struck by an unpleasant, musty odor that permeated the space—hardly the ambiance one expects from an upscale establishment. The supposedly "amazing views" consisted of nothing more than neighboring casino rooftops and parking structures. The culinary execution was equally disappointing. My medium filet arrived severely undercooked, while the complimentary bread, though warm, was stale. For $225 before tip—covering two steak and lobster dinners, drinks, desserts, and coffee—the value simply wasn't there. I'd rate the food a mediocre 2 out of 5 stars. Service issues compounded the experience, with our waiter spilling water across the table and offering only a casual "Oops" as acknowledgment. As a Las Vegas resident, it's disheartening that I cannot recommend this establishment to visiting family and friends. I will not be returning.

A Loyal Fan's Long-Time Love Affair I've been a devoted customer of this establishment since before it became a Yelp hotspot, and my loyalty remains unwavering. Yes, I'll admit upfront: it's not cheap, and the wait times are legendary. In fact, they're so long you might genuinely wonder if your order was forgotten. My survival strategy? Get your drink, fill it, drain it, and repeat. By your second or third refill, your food should finally arrive. Some might call me boring, but I prefer "extremely loyal." When I find something I love, I stick with it religiously. For me, that's the Chicken Parmesan with pasta salad – it has never disappointed. Living in California means I only visit when seeing family, making this restaurant a mandatory stop three to four times annually. It's become part of my travel ritual. The portions are so generous that I inevitably head home for a two-hour food coma afterward before resuming family time. Despite the cost and wait, this place holds a special spot in my heart and stomach. For those willing to be patient and bring a healthy appetite, it's absolutely worth the experience.

Meh. I've Experienced Better: A Disappointing 24-Hour Dining Option This casino café falls squarely into the "last resort" category of dining establishments. While its 24-hour operation provides convenience for hotel guests unwilling to venture elsewhere, that's essentially where the positives end. **Inconsistent Service** The service quality fluctuates dramatically between visits. Some experiences feature attentive, tip-worthy waitstaff, while others leave much to be desired. This unpredictability makes each visit a gamble—appropriate for a casino setting, perhaps, but frustrating for diners seeking reliability. **Shrinking Menu Selection** Perhaps most disappointing is the dramatic menu reduction over recent years. What once offered abundant variety across multiple pages has been reduced to a sparse cardboard rectangle with limited options. This downsizing significantly restricts dining choices, especially problematic for a supposedly full-service restaurant. **Quantity Over Quality** The food itself proves underwhelming. The signature massive burgers prioritize size over flavor—enormous portions that even competitive eaters would find challenging, yet lacking the taste to justify their intimidating proportions. Being big doesn't compensate for being bland. **Overpriced Mediocrity** Expect to spend approximately $20 per person for decidedly average fare. While these prices reflect typical Vegas casino restaurant markups and the lack of late-night competition, they don't represent good value. **Better Alternatives** For those with transportation, the nearby In-N-Out across I-15 offers superior quality at better prices. Only choose this café when absolutely necessary—when time constraints or circumstances leave no other option.

Exceptional Service and Honest Diagnosis at German Motors of Mesa When stranded far from my regular shop, I discovered German Motors of Mesa and couldn't have been luckier. Nate provided incredibly thorough, detailed diagnosis and could have easily overcharged a desperate customer, but instead kept my bill under $100. His transparent communication throughout the entire process was refreshing and professional. The personal touch, including meeting his mom, added warmth to an already outstanding experience. This is honest, expert VW service at its finest. My GTI VR6 is back on the road thanks to Nate's integrity and expertise. German Motors of Mesa has earned a lifelong customer through exceptional service that restored both my car and faith in automotive shops.

A Cautionary Tale: When Hype Doesn't Match Reality **An Honest Assessment of an Overhyped Establishment** After giving this restaurant multiple chances, I feel compelled to share my disappointing experiences. Despite the perpetual crowds and trendy atmosphere, this establishment exemplifies style over substance in the most frustrating way. ## The Atmosphere Problem The scene here is exhausting. Endless lines snake around the building while patrons—many sporting pristine workout clothes that clearly haven't seen actual exercise—create an atmosphere of pretension rather than genuine dining enjoyment. The crowd feels more interested in being seen than actually enjoying quality food. ## The Food Falls Flat Unfortunately, the menu doesn't justify the hype. The commuter sandwich arrived greasy and utterly tasteless—genuinely unappetizing. The egg white omelet lacked any discernible flavor, suggesting minimal seasoning or care in preparation. Even their signature croque proved underwhelming; something I could easily replicate at home with better results and significantly less grease. The lunch menu offers equally uninspiring options—basic sandwiches with nothing special to distinguish them from homemade versions. Even the pizza disappoints, rounding out a consistently mediocre experience across their entire menu. ## Customer Service Concerns Perhaps most telling was management's complete lack of response to my detailed feedback email sent six months ago. This silence speaks volumes about their priorities and suggests they're comfortable riding the wave of popularity without addressing legitimate concerns. ## The Bottom Line Coming from California with exposure to diverse, quality dining options, I recognize overpriced mediocrity when I encounter it. This establishment succeeds through marketing and location rather than culinary merit. Numerous restaurants offering dishes under $5 provide exponentially better flavor and value. Save your money and time. This trendy spot prioritizes appearance over quality, leaving customers with forgettable food at premium prices. **Rating: Not Recommended**

Mixed Results: Great Cookies, Disappointing Cake While the irresistible aroma of fresh cookies makes this spot hard to pass by, my experience with their cookie cake warrants only 3 stars. The service and pricing deserve 4 stars, but the cake itself was genuinely disappointing. Unlike their phenomenal cookies (perfect for sweet tooth cravings), the cake tastes completely different. Quality drops dramatically once it cools—literally as soon as it's finished being made, it loses its appeal. Though reasonably priced, the cakes simply don't compare to their superior cookies. My recommendation? Skip the cake and stick with their excellent cookies instead. They offer fantastic deals like buy-5-get-1-free and mini chocolate chip cookie cups for just $5.99. These treats deliver the quality the cakes lack.

Disastrous Dining Experience - Zero Stars An absolute nightmare from start to finish. Despite booking over a week ahead for a special trip from Detroit, we encountered four separate problems before even being seated. The staff proved consistently rude, unhelpful, and poorly trained throughout our visit. What should have been a memorable celebration became an evening we'd rather forget. Save yourself the trouble and head to Top of the Rock instead—anywhere would be better than this establishment.

Mixed Experience: Good Burrito, Gloomy Atmosphere While the food at this establishment delivers on quality, the overall dining experience leaves much to be desired due to staff demeanor and service issues. **The Good:** The veggie burrito proved to be genuinely satisfying, featuring cheese, sour cream, salsa, hot sauce, rice, and black beans. The generous portion of hot sauce—applied by the ladle-full—initially caused concern but ultimately enhanced the flavor profile considerably. The vegetables were fresh and flavorful, and the practice of mixing ingredients before wrapping creates better distribution throughout the burrito. The proportions were generally well-balanced, though slightly more rice and beans with less sour cream would have been ideal. **The Not-So-Good:** The atmosphere was notably uncomfortable, with staff members appearing visibly unhappy and disengaged. Employees spoke too quietly to hear properly, and service moved at a sluggish pace. The collective mood behind the counter suggested genuine misery rather than simple workplace fatigue. Additionally, the burrito arrived lukewarm—a common complaint with fast-casual chains but disappointing nonetheless. **Bottom Line:** Despite the underwhelming service experience and staff morale issues, the quality of the burrito itself warrants a return visit. A little workplace positivity would significantly improve the customer experience. **Rating: 3/5**

A Mature Perspective on Surrender's Electric Atmosphere As someone beyond the typical club demographic, I've found Surrender to be an exceptional venue that transcends age barriers. The club consistently books top-tier talent, creating unforgettable experiences like witnessing hundreds of enthusiastic clubgoers bouncing to Skrillex's dubstep beats—almost concert-pit intensity in a nightclub setting. While Surrender's interior is relatively intimate, it brilliantly connects to the expansive Encore Beach Club, providing a perfect escape for anyone feeling overwhelmed. This dual-space design offers flexibility that enhances the overall experience. The security staff deserves praise for their professional, welcoming approach—a refreshing change from other venues where bouncers can be unnecessarily aggressive toward male patrons. However, respect the velvet ropes and queue properly; they take these protocols seriously. Yes, drinks command premium prices, but given the Wynn/Encore pedigree, this is expected. The exceptional music curation, sophisticated décor, and vibrant atmosphere justify the investment. For anyone seeking world-class entertainment in an accessible, well-designed space, Surrender delivers consistently impressive experiences that appeal across generations.

Disappointing Nail Salon Experience This conveniently located nail salon falls short of expectations, primarily due to cleanliness concerns and overall condition. While the French manicure service was acceptable, the facility requires significant improvements to compete with other area salons. The lack of cleanliness was particularly off-putting, making the longer drive to Southwest locations seem worthwhile in comparison. Despite its proximity to home, this salon doesn't earn a recommendation. For a better experience, consider exploring other options in town.

A Solid Neighborhood Bar with Room for Improvement This establishment serves as a convenient watering hole, particularly for those staying nearby. The bar setup features an interesting configuration with two small TVs facing the counter and two large screens positioned behind it. While one screen appears backward initially, it's actually oriented for restaurant-side patrons—a functional but somewhat awkward solution. The real highlight here is the staff. Bartenders Dale and Cassie create a welcoming atmosphere that makes solo visitors feel comfortable. Their personable service elevates the experience considerably. Pricing proves reasonable, with tap beer running just over $2—a refreshing change for those accustomed to inflated metropolitan prices. The venue offers practical amenities including weekday happy hour specials and themed nights like Thursday ladies' night. However, the establishment faces one significant drawback: early closing times. Shutting down at 10pm, even on weekends, severely limits its appeal and competitive edge against chains like Hooters that maintain later hours. For casual drinks and friendly service in a laid-back setting, this spot delivers adequately. It's particularly convenient for hotel guests seeking a nearby option. However, extended hours would dramatically improve its viability as a go-to destination for evening entertainment. Overall, it's a decent choice for early evening drinks with personable service.

Unacceptable Service and Broken Commitments Despite having corporate contract and reservations made a month in advance at the Hyatt Regency Montreal, our arrival was met with dismissive treatment and avoidance from staff. After persistent inquiries about our rooms, management finally admitted to a "mix up" and relegated us to a Comfort Inn South, 30 minutes away, via taxi. This complete failure to honor confirmed reservations and the unprofessional handling of the situation is unacceptable for a Hyatt property. Our company is terminating our contract immediately.

Mixed Experience: Excellent Clinic, Disappointing Pharmacy This CVS location offers contrasting service quality between departments. The MinuteClinic deserves praise, with practitioner Sarah providing immediate, friendly, and helpful care for a sore throat complaint. The walk-in clinic experience was seamless and professional, earning a strong recommendation. However, the pharmacy falls short with notably slow service and less-than-courteous staff interactions. While the clinic excels at addressing immediate healthcare needs, patients should consider filling prescriptions at alternative pharmacies for better service. **Bottom line:** Perfect for quick medical consultations, but plan to take your prescription elsewhere.

A Disappointing Turn at Once-Beloved Theater Until recently, this theater seemed like the perfect entertainment destination. The concept was exceptional: comfortable seating, full menu service during movies, attentive waitstaff, alcoholic beverage options, and the convenience of having popcorn delivered directly to your seat. It represented everything a modern moviegoer could want. Unfortunately, a disturbing incident has permanently changed my perspective on this establishment. During what should have been an enjoyable evening with my girlfriend, her sister, and her son, our experience took an shocking turn. A staff member, claiming to be the manager, approached us mid-movie with accusations that we had brought a dog into the theater. He demanded we remove this alleged animal to our vehicle. We immediately offered to let him search our seating area and belongings. Despite conducting this search and finding absolutely nothing, he continued insisting we had a dog because another employee supposedly witnessed one. The accusation seemed particularly suspicious given that we were the only non-Caucasian patrons in that screening. Most disturbingly, despite proving the accusation false, management refused our refund request and forced us to leave. The entire situation felt discriminatory and targeted. This unprofessional handling of a baseless complaint, combined with the potentially racist undertones, means I cannot recommend this theater. What was once a five-star experience became the worst theater encounter I've ever experienced.

Excellent Garden Center for Seed Selection and Customer Service As a newcomer to the Madison area and passionate gardener, I was thrilled to discover this garden center based on friends' recommendations. The seed selection exceeded my expectations, featuring the complete Seed Savers collection, an extensive Baker Creek variety, and numerous other quality brands. The customer service was exceptional. Alyssa, a knowledgeable clerk, provided invaluable assistance in selecting seeds and choosing an orchid. The store appeared to be undergoing renovations during my visit. Pricing was competitive with typical garden centers, though the furniture selection reflected higher-end quality with corresponding prices. The checkout experience was efficient and thoughtful – staff carefully wrapped my orchid for cold weather protection, a considerate touch absent from big-box retailers like Home Depot. The store's commitment to customer care and quality products has earned my loyalty. I'm eagerly anticipating a return visit during warmer weather to explore their plant selection for my new lawn's landscaping project.

Worth the Wait, But Bring Your Wallet I finally caught Papi Queso at Food Truck Fridays in South End after hearing endless buzz about their gourmet grilled cheese. My friend and I shared the Green Monster and Mushroom and Leek sandwiches, both arriving perfectly executed with crispy, golden-brown exteriors and gloriously melty interiors. The Mushroom and Leek was my favorite, showcasing creative flavor combinations that set this truck apart. However, there are some caveats. The portions are modest—think wonder bread-sized toast—and prices feel steep for what you receive. Add in the considerable wait time during peak hours, and it's an investment of both time and money. Bottom line: Papi Queso delivers genuinely delicious, inventive grilled cheese that's worth trying at least once. Just manage your expectations about portions and timing, and definitely bring some extra "chedda" for the experience.

Good Food, But Firearms Policy Is a Dealbreaker The food quality here is undeniably excellent, earning genuine praise from this reviewer. However, the establishment prominently displays "no guns" signage at the entrance, which became an insurmountable issue. Despite appreciating the cuisine, the reviewer cannot patronize businesses with such policies due to personal principles and concern for friends who carry firearms legally. The potential legal consequences for armed companions make this restaurant off-limits, regardless of culinary merit. A disappointing situation where politics override palate.

Appalling Experience at Big O Tires - A Cautionary Tale This Big O location exemplifies everything wrong with automotive service. The staff's rudeness was matched only by their aggressive upselling tactics and dishonest pricing practices. While other Big O branches provided acceptable service previously, this catastrophic experience has permanently ended my patronage of the entire chain. Costco's tire center nearby offers superior service, honest recommendations, and respectful staff. Avoid this location entirely.

Late Night Sushi: A Tale of Two Experiences Visiting this establishment minutes before closing proved to be a study in contrasts. While the sushi's flavor earned a respectable 4/5, the preparation was disappointingly sloppy (2/5), with uneven rolling and inconsistent cuts that suggested rushed work. Though understandable given the timing, such poor execution seems inexcusable for any sushi restaurant. However, the service absolutely shone, earning a perfect 5/5. The staff remained gracious and accommodating despite the late hour, demonstrating genuine hospitality. If only the kitchen matched the front-of-house's professionalism, this could be a stellar dining destination.

Disappointing Experience with Poor Service This restaurant fails to meet expectations with subpar food quality that doesn't compare favorably to chain alternatives. Order accuracy is problematic, and staff showed indifference when mistakes were reported. The combination of unsatisfactory cuisine and inadequate customer service makes this establishment difficult to recommend.

A Haven for Vape Enthusiasts: Vapor Bombz Delivers Excellence Vapor Bombz stands out as an exceptional vape shop that combines quality products with outstanding hospitality. From the moment you enter, the welcoming atmosphere sets the tone for a memorable visit. The staff's attentive greeting and willingness to assist creates an inviting environment. The shop's tasting bar allows customers to sample various flavors before purchasing—a thoughtful touch that led to discovering a perfect coffee-flavored option for morning sessions. Product selection is impressive, with competitive pricing that reflects industry standards. What truly distinguishes Vapor Bombz is the comfortable lounge area featuring couches where patrons can relax and enjoy their purchases. This communal space transforms a simple retail transaction into a social experience. The combination of knowledgeable staff, quality inventory, and a laid-back ambiance makes Vapor Bombz more than just a shop—it's a destination worth returning to.

Disappointing Service Overshadows Decent Food Despite good food, poor service, inattentive staff during busy NFL playoff game, and limited craft beer selection make this establishment hard to recommend for future visits.

Excellent Sunday Breakfast Buffet Experience Planet Hollywood offers one of the Strip's best buffets with great selection and reasonable pricing. Our Sunday morning visit at 8am was perfectly timed - no crowds, no wait, and immediate seating. The quality-to-value ratio here is outstanding, making it a top breakfast choice in Las Vegas.

Overpriced Disappointment at Sushisamba Vegas Sushisamba fails to live up to its reputation, delivering an underwhelming experience that's simply not worth the premium price tag. Despite locations in major cities like Chicago and New York, this Vegas outpost leaves much to be desired. The most glaring issue is the value proposition—tiny portions at inflated prices that feel like highway robbery. When you're paying $2-4 per individual piece of a roll, expectations run high, yet the execution falls flat. The culinary missteps are concerning. A charbroiled steak roll tasted overwhelmingly of charcoal, completely overpowering any other flavors. Their "special" sauces, like key lime mayo, come across as gimmicky rather than innovative, seemingly designed to mask mediocrity rather than enhance quality ingredients. Even presentation disappointed, with rolls lacking the visual appeal expected from an upscale establishment. The frustrating reality? The rolls themselves were adequate—perfectly acceptable at a reasonably-priced neighborhood sushi spot. However, when charging premium prices, Sushisamba should deliver premium quality, which they simply don't. **Bottom line:** Save your money and find better sushi elsewhere in Vegas. Sushisamba needs to seriously reconsider their pricing structure and step up their game.

A-Ok Mall Experience with Notable Parking Challenges This shopping center offers a decent selection of stores and dining options, though a complete exploration wasn't possible during a visit focused on Painting with a Twist. The retail mix includes appealing options like Anthropologie, Ann Taylor, and Learning Express toy store, with more stores available throughout the complex. The dining selection proves robust, featuring a full-sized Panera Bread, Chinese cuisine, Starbucks, Houlihans, and Mitchell's Fish Market. The upcoming addition of A BRGR promises to enhance the food court further. However, the parking situation significantly detracts from the overall experience. On a Saturday afternoon, finding a spot proved extremely challenging despite the mall's modest size. The upper lot was completely full, forcing patrons to navigate to the lower level, which was equally congested. Securing a space required patiently waiting for departing customers. The lower level access presents additional concerns. The narrow hill/road leading down creates a white-knuckle experience, especially for larger vehicles. The combination of the steep incline and awkward bend makes navigation unnecessarily stressful. While the mall offers solid shopping and dining options, the severe parking limitations and difficult lower-level access prevent it from achieving a higher rating. These logistical challenges could discourage repeat visits.

Mixed Experience at Village Indian Restaurant: Style Over Substance This Indian restaurant in the Gay Village presents an interesting paradox between appearance and execution. While the establishment boasts attractive decor, pleasant ambiance, and an appealing menu design, the actual dining experience falls short of expectations. **Food Quality and Authenticity** The cuisine represents a Bangladeshi interpretation of Indian food rather than traditional Indian preparation methods, which may disappoint purists. While appetizers and certain curry dishes perform adequately, signature items like Biryani fail to impress. The food quality remains merely average, particularly disappointing given the premium pricing common throughout this tourist-oriented strip. **Service Shortcomings** The service staff demonstrates superficial friendliness but lacks attentiveness when needed. Servers frequently congregate around the bar for conversation rather than monitoring their tables. Most notably, the unusual practice of requiring customers to walk to the bar area for credit card payment deviates from standard restaurant protocol and creates unnecessary inconvenience. **Value Assessment** The elevated prices reflect the location's tourist market positioning rather than food quality. While the pricing structure aligns with neighboring establishments, it doesn't justify the mediocre culinary experience. **Final Verdict** Despite its visual appeal, this restaurant prioritizes aesthetics over authentic cuisine and professional service. Unless seeking emergency refuge or desperate for familiar cultural surroundings, there's little reason to return. The establishment serves as a cautionary example that attractive presentation cannot compensate for lackluster food and inattentive service.

**Avoid This CPK Location at All Costs** This California Pizza Kitchen falls far short of expectations. Overpriced, mediocre pizza combined with inattentive service creates a disappointing experience. Staff appeared unhappy and disengaged, leaving customers waiting twenty minutes just to pay their check. The complete absence of customer service and friendly atmosphere makes this location unworthy of your time or money.

**Disappointing Service Mars Otherwise Good Food** While the food quality remains enjoyable, our recent Friday night experience was marred by unacceptable service issues. Our simple order of salad and pork schnitzel inexplicably took an hour to arrive, with no explanation or apology from staff. The outdoor dining area was littered with approximately 15 cigarette butts near the main entrance—hardly appetizing for diners. Management should prohibit staff from smoking by the door and maintain cleaner surroundings. The kitchen needs to address serious timing issues; such basic dishes shouldn't require an hour's wait. Until service improves significantly, we cannot recommend this establishment despite decent food.

A Surprisingly Upscale "Dive" with Delicious Happy Hour Deals Dive Bar & Grill defies its name with a warm, clean, and inviting atmosphere complemented by excellent waitstaff. The happy hour experience proved exceptional, featuring generous half-priced appetizers including standout fried crimini mushrooms that were remarkably juicy, hummus with vegetables, and satisfying cheesesteak sliders. The draft beer selection nicely rounded out the meal, making it an ideal spot to catch the Penguins game. The quality and portion sizes exceeded expectations, especially considering the happy hour pricing. The restaurant's name remains puzzling given its upscale feel—though the abundance of fish dishes on the menu offers one possible explanation. This establishment successfully combines sports bar functionality with quality food and service, making it a destination worth revisiting for both casual dining and game-watching occasions.

Exceptional Local Luggage Store with Outstanding Service This downtown gem offers an impressive selection of luggage and travel accessories, led by knowledgeable owner/manager Dean who provides expert guidance on product selection. The store features a generous 30-day return policy and represents exactly why supporting local businesses matters. If you're seeking quality luggage with personalized service, this is your destination.

Disappointing Food Despite Nice Atmosphere I had high hopes for this new crepes and waffle spot, but the food fell short. My waffle arrived cold and was topped with grainy chocolate spread. The crepe, though served hot, turned out bland and soggy. On the positive side, the ambience is pleasant and the La Prima coffee was excellent. However, until they significantly improve their food quality, I won't be returning. The location has potential, but execution needs work.

Worth the Journey: Solid Burgers and Excellent Shakes Despite the distance traveled, this burger joint delivered a satisfying experience. The customizable burgers feature generous toppings and quality ingredients. While fries and sauces require separate ordering à la carte, the standout shakes are exceptional. Note that fries run on the thinner side, which may not suit everyone's preference, though they're still well-prepared. Overall, a worthwhile destination for burger enthusiasts.

A Reliable Lunch Spot with Authentic Thai Flavor As a regular visitor who works nearby, Thai Hut has become my go-to lunch destination at least twice monthly. This no-frills establishment excels where it matters most: delicious food and genuinely unpretentious staff who create a welcoming atmosphere. The lunch experience is exceptional, with meals costing around $10 including tip. Service is consistently hot and fast, even during peak hours. The Cashew Nut Chicken stands out as a personal favorite, while their curry offerings are equally outstanding. Pro tip: request the spice and sauce tray and experiment with their toasted ground pepper for an extra flavor boost. My limited dinner visits revealed a surprisingly expanded menu worth exploring. The pineapple fried rice, unavailable at lunch, is absolutely spectacular. Whether you're seeking a quick lunch or leisurely dinner, Thai Hut delivers authentic Thai cuisine without pretension or breaking the bank.

Solid Burger Experience with Premium Pricing The burger impressed with its generous size and fresh, quality meat cooked to order. Service was excellent throughout. However, pricing runs high, especially since menu items are sold separately rather than as combos. While the burger and drink cost more than expected, the quality and portion size help justify the premium price for this made-to-order meal.

When Late-Night Fast Food Goes Wrong: A Cautionary Tale This McDonald's location serves as a prime example of how operational inconsistencies can frustrate even the most patient customers. As one of the few 24-hour locations remaining in the Valley after economic cutbacks, this restaurant struggles under the weight of being an inadequate solution to area-wide demand. ## The Problems Are Systemic The decision to consolidate late-night service to just a handful of locations has created predictable consequences. Without proper communication through their store locator and facing overwhelming demand after bar closings, this McDonald's buckles under pressure. The ferociously long lines aren't surprising when nearby locations on Camelback and Indian School remain closed during overnight hours. ## Operational Confusion Reigns Perhaps most baffling is the seemingly arbitrary menu availability. Arriving at 3:45 AM becomes a gamble—will it be breakfast or lunch? The schedule appears to follow no logical pattern, which stands in stark contrast to competitors like Jack in the Box, who've mastered simultaneous menu service. The shake machine situation epitomizes poor operational planning. Cleaning schedules that don't account for business volume, overnight temperatures, or customer demand demonstrate a lack of adaptability. When temperatures exceed 100 degrees overnight, perhaps 7 AM would be a more sensible cleaning time. ## The Speed Problem Most damning is the service pace. Fast food employees engaging in extended conversations about morning news while customers wait in line represents a fundamental misunderstanding of the business model. This isn't a neighborhood café—it's supposed to be fast food. **The Bottom Line:** This location reflects broader corporate decisions that prioritize cost-cutting over customer experience, leaving one understaffed, overwhelmed restaurant to serve an entire region's late-night needs. **Rating: ★☆☆☆☆**

A Solid Burger Experience with Room for Improvement The Habit Burger Grill offers a satisfying meal that draws favorable comparisons to other popular burger chains. The double charburger stands out as the highlight—juicy and well-prepared, with quality reminiscent of Fatburger's offerings. At just over $10 for a combo meal, the value proposition seems reasonable at first glance. The coffee ice cream shake delivers on its promise of real ice cream, though it falls short on actual coffee flavor and lacks real coffee pieces that would elevate the experience. The sweet potato fries, while superior to their disappointingly limp regular fries, need more seasoning and could benefit from battering or glazing to truly distinguish themselves. While this meal provides a decent dining experience worth trying once, it doesn't quite justify becoming a regular destination at its price point. The burger alone makes it worthwhile, but inconsistencies in side offerings prevent this from being an exceptional value.

A Dynamic Dining Experience with Room for Refinement Elements restaurant has become a monthly pilgrimage for food enthusiasts seeking innovative cuisine, thanks largely to Chef Beau's ever-evolving menu. The constantly rotating offerings, which change approximately once monthly, showcase seasonal ingredients and local produce while maintaining several core dishes that have become signature staples. ## The Menu Philosophy Chef Beau's approach centers on what's fresh, what's in season, and presumably, his creative inspiration of the moment. Regular attendees can anticipate seeing certain items make recurring appearances: Foie Gras, Escargot, Elemental Soup, Duck Breast, Filet Mignon, and various seafood preparations. However, these stalwarts appear in different iterations, creating what diners affectionately call a "Mouth Party." ## Hits and Misses The dining experience at Elements proves consistently inconsistent. While the restaurant earns a solid four-star rating, that elusive fifth star remains just out of reach due to occasional misfires. The March 2011 menu exemplified this pattern—the Elemental soup disappointed with its weak, water-based mushroom bouillon, the calamari seemed amateurish, and the duck breast failed to impress. Conversely, standout dishes demonstrate Chef Beau's capabilities. The Foie Gras preparations consistently deliver, and the five-spice pork osso buco with Buddha buns hit every note perfectly. The Kurobuta Pork Belly Fried Rice has achieved killer status among regulars, and escargot preparations—whether in pot pie form, wontons, or phyllo-wrapped spring rolls—reliably satisfy. When ordering 7-8 dishes per visit, expect most to impress while one or two fall flat. The Foie Gras pudding missed the mark, and oversized dayboat scallops lacked their characteristic nutty sweetness and proper sear. ## The Complete Package Beyond the food, Elements offers exceptional ambiance. Reserving an outdoor table 40 minutes before sunset provides one of the area's finest dining backdrops, combining excellent cuisine with spectacular views. For adventurous diners willing to forgive occasional missteps in exchange for creative, seasonally-driven cuisine and breathtaking sunset views, Elements delivers a compelling experience worth visiting monthly.

A Different Take on Bánh Mì This establishment offers an unconventional approach to Vietnamese sandwiches that may disappoint traditionalists. The BBQ pork sandwich, while generously sized, deviates significantly from classic preparations. Most notably, the traditional liver pâté is replaced with oil and green onion, creating an unfamiliar flavor profile. The pork itself lacks proper seasoning, tasting primarily of soy sauce before grilling—a far cry from authentic bánh mì flavors. At nearly three dollars per sandwich, it's considerably pricier than San Jose's offerings ($1.50 each with buy-two-get-one-free deals). Despite being open for over six months, the restaurant remains surprisingly empty, which speaks volumes. The recent addition of a new menu board hasn't changed the fundamental issues with execution and value. For those accustomed to quality Bay Area bánh mì, this spot falls short of expectations.

A Deliciously Overwhelming Experience at This Mexican Gem From the moment the complimentary fried tortillas arrived at our table, I knew we were in for something special. These warm, perfectly crisped chips paired beautifully with their homemade salsa—chunky with fresh tomatoes, vegetables, and herbs that tasted genuinely authentic. The fiesta plate served as a delicious preview of what was to come. Though my partner and I split it, the generous portion left us surprisingly satisfied. Yet when the enchilada style burrito arrived, my appetite mysteriously returned in full force. This burrito was nothing short of spectacular. The meat had that perfect charred, barbecued quality that made every bite irresistible. The accompanying sides complemented the main dish flawlessly, creating a harmonious plate of flavors. I found myself in that wonderful dilemma of being ridiculously full yet tempted to keep eating because everything tasted too good. Despite initially saving room for dessert, I couldn't resist finishing every last bite—and I regret nothing! **Highly recommend for anyone seeking authentic, flavor-packed Mexican cuisine.**

**Mixed Experience with Redemptive Service** While the fajitas were mediocre, this restaurant delivered decent value overall. The chips, salsa, and cold beer met expectations, and service proved excellent. Unfortunately, a fish taco arrived dangerously undercooked—cold in the middle. However, the attentive waiter immediately removed it from the bill without hesitation. This professional recovery from a serious kitchen error, combined with the pleasant atmosphere and good service, makes a return visit worthwhile despite the culinary misstep.

A Pricey Lesson in Las Vegas Disappointment When visiting Las Vegas, you expect to overspend on frivolous indulgences—but at least they should be enjoyable. Unfortunately, my experience at Serendipity 3 exemplified expensive regret without the fun. Located conveniently outside our hotel, we decided to try their famous frozen hot chocolate on a sweltering day. Rather than dining inside, we opted for the take-out window for a quick treat. After paying $11 each for the basic Frrrozen Hot Chocolate, we settled near the water misters, anticipating something special. The disappointment was swift and crushing. What sounded exotic and fancy—"frozen hot chocolate"—turned out to be nothing more than a glorified chocolate milkshake, worth perhaps $2-3 at most. There was nothing interesting, exciting, or innovative about it. Even the taste failed to justify the premium price tag. Perhaps the sit-down restaurant experience would have been better, but I doubt the drink itself would have improved. The frozen hot chocolate simply doesn't deliver on its promising name or inflated cost. It's a clear case of style over substance, banking on novelty branding rather than quality. While Serendipity 3 might work for some visitors seeking the Instagram-worthy Vegas experience, those looking for genuine value and taste should look elsewhere. The only redeeming quality? The attractive font on their menu. That, unfortunately, doesn't warrant a return visit or another $11 expenditure. **Rating: ★☆☆☆☆**

Frustrated Beyond Measure: Zero Service, Zero Stars It's nearly impossible to review a restaurant's cuisine when you've never actually been served. Despite two separate attempts to dine here, I've yet to taste a single dish. **Visit #1 - Saturday Night Chaos:** The venue was packed—patio, bar, and dining room overflowing. The interior noise level was unbearable, practically requiring earplugs. We requested outdoor seating with a quoted 10-minute wait. After 20 minutes without being called, the hostess had vanished entirely, forcing us to leave. The waiting area placement directly blocks the entrance, creating constant traffic jams as guests squeeze past waiting parties. Absolutely poor planning! **Visit #2 - Friday Afternoon Disappointment:** Arriving at 4:30pm seemed promising—no wait! We were immediately seated outside, then completely forgotten. After 25 frustrating minutes without any server acknowledgment, we informed the host upon leaving. Their indifferent response spoke volumes. **Additional Concerns:** A glance at the menu revealed significantly overpriced drinks, adding insult to injury. **Final Verdict:** Clear mismanagement from top to bottom. Between the chaotic layout, disappearing staff, and apparent lack of customer service standards, this establishment won't receive a third chance from me. Save yourself the frustration!

Disappointing Experience: Small Portions, High Prices, and Questionable Quality Our visit to this establishment left much to be desired, despite competent service from our attentive waitress who maintained our drink levels throughout the meal. Unfortunately, the positives ended there. The portion sizes were surprisingly small for the price point. The presentation felt deceptive—food arrives in a large, funky-shaped red bowl, but you're actually served from a tiny silver "cat dish." This transparent tactic seemed designed to create an illusion of value that quickly dissolved upon closer inspection. The food quality itself raised serious concerns. While the fried rice appeared acceptable, the noodles were genuinely disgusting—extremely greasy and drowned in overly sugary sauces. Worse yet, they caused stomach discomfort later in the day, something I should have anticipated given their appearance. The posted calorie counts on the wall seemed suspiciously low, likely excluding carbohydrates and sauces from their calculations. The dining environment compounded our dissatisfaction. With four people at our cramped table, I felt afraid to move my elbow. The tight seating arrangement created an uncomfortable, sardined-in atmosphere that detracted from any enjoyment of the meal. For $45 before tip (and yes, there were prominent signs reminding you to tip), the value proposition was terrible. Two members of our party reported feeling hungry again later that day—an inexcusable outcome after spending that much on lunch. For comparison, the Great Greek on Warm Springs offers family meals at similar prices that provide multiple days' worth of food. The self-service model, combined with navigating cramped tables and receiving minimal portions, created too much work and aggravation for what you receive. While not a complete disaster, this establishment treats customers like "knuckleheads" who won't notice the poor value. Unless specifically requested by companions, I won't return. There are simply better options available for your dining dollar.

A Disappointing Dining Disaster at Aria's Newest Restaurant When you're responsible for choosing a restaurant for your group, you want everything to go perfectly. Unfortunately, my experience at this Aria establishment was anything but perfect, leaving me with regrets and a significantly lighter wallet. I made a 7:45pm reservation based on positive Yelp reviews, hoping to enjoy a leisurely dinner before catching the 10pm Cirque du Soleil show at Bellagio. Red flag number one: the restaurant was nearly empty on what should have been a busy evening. We soon discovered why. **Service Nightmares** The service was absolutely horrendous. Our waiter disappeared for approximately 30 minutes toward the end of our meal, forcing us to literally run to make our show. But the service failures started much earlier. When we ordered the shellfish appetizer, both my friend and I explicitly requested it cold. It arrived hot. When we sent it back, rather than apologizing, our waiter actually argued with us, insisting we'd ordered it hot. Rule number one in hospitality: don't tell customers they're wrong. Additionally, despite having what appeared to be a fantastic cocktail menu, he never mentioned it until I specifically asked. **Lackluster Food** The entrees were equally disappointing. My salmon arrived swimming in an overly salty soup that completely overwhelmed the dish. Worse, the fish itself was severely undercooked—practically sushi-grade when I'd expected it cooked. My friend's dish earned similar "ick" faces across the table. Hoping to salvage something from the evening, I ordered chestnut ice cream for dessert. How could ice cream go wrong? Apparently easily—it had a chalky, unpleasant texture that was completely off-putting. **Bottom Line** At approximately $125 per person, this meal was outrageously overpriced for the quality delivered. Las Vegas offers countless incredible dining options, and this restaurant simply doesn't deserve to be among them. Don't let a handful of reviews mislead you. Two weeks later, I'm still disappointed by this experience. Save your money and time for one of Vegas's truly great restaurants instead.

This reviewer clearly loves Lee Lee's for its excellent selection of Hawaiian products, particularly praising their Aloha Shoyu offerings and other island favorites. They're especially impressed with the meat section and find the produce quality satisfactory. However, they've noticed the store is out of stock on Hawaiian Sun frozen concentrate, especially the Lilikoi (passionfruit) flavor. They also suggest Lee Lee's should consider carrying Primo Island Lager beer to round out their Hawaiian product selection.

A Neighborhood Gem with Outstanding Quality and Service This beloved Arizona establishment has earned its stellar reputation through consistently excellent food and service. The "Pick Two" option stands out, featuring generous turkey sandwiches loaded with fresh vegetables on wholesome 9-grain bread, paired with impressive garden salads that exceed typical side dish expectations. The spring mix base comes topped with carrots, peppers, and mushrooms, complemented by delicious honey mustard dressing. The diverse menu offers equally impressive options, including The East Coast Panini with pastrami and sauerkraut on rye, and The Scottsdale featuring roast beef with red peppers on sourdough. The red potato salad receives particular praise as another standout side. Beyond the food, the service truly shines. Counter staff consistently deliver friendly, efficient service with impressive accuracy—orders arrive quickly without mistakes. This combination of quality ingredients, flavorful preparations, and exceptional service makes this a must-visit local favorite.

A Return Visit After Years: Alexander Michael's Falls Short of Memory After a hiatus of several years, I recently returned to Alexander Michael's, a restaurant that was once a regular haunt of mine. While nostalgia drew me back on a cold winter night, the experience left me with mixed feelings about this once-beloved spot. ## Atmosphere and Ambiance The interior maintains its signature dark, intimate atmosphere with flickering candles and close table arrangements—perfect for a chilly evening. However, the parking situation remains problematic. Finding a spot down a side street, I was struck by how unsettling the darkness felt; it's the kind of place where you genuinely want a "buddy system" to walk safely to your car. ## Service Shortcomings While we were seated promptly, the service quality deteriorated from there. Our waitress wasn't overtly rude, but she was notably absent throughout our meal. For such a small establishment, attentive service should be straightforward, yet we felt largely neglected. This lack of presence significantly detracted from the overall experience. ## Food Quality Concerns The cuisine proved similarly disappointing. I ordered the London broil sandwich with soup, priced at $9.50. The "crab" soup arrived made with imitation crab—something I believe shouldn't legally qualify as crab soup. The sandwich contained ample meat that was adequately tender but lacked distinctive flavor, resulting in a decidedly average meal. ## Final Verdict Years have seemingly not been kind to Alexander Michael's. The menu feels limited and slightly overpriced for what's delivered. Both the food and service lack the spark that once made this a destination restaurant. While I'm willing to give it another chance eventually, it won't be anytime soon. Sometimes memories are better left undisturbed. **Rating: 2/5 stars**

**Hidden Gem for Live Music** Excellent venue with consistently great bands and affordable drinks. The relaxed atmosphere offers a refreshing escape from Mill Avenue's chaos. Perfect spot for enjoying live music without the typical crowds and pretension.

Mixed Experience at Kabuki's: Great Sushi, Some Disappointments After catching a movie, we visited Kabuki's and were seated quickly with a view of the sushi bar. Service was adequate, though drink refills lagged. The highlights included excellent sliced raw beef and superb yellowtail with generous portions. Tuna, octopus, gyoza, and miso soup were all good. However, the chicken and beef teriyaki were merely okay, and the char sui ramen disappointed with what tasted like store-bought noodles. The iced green tea was delicious. Prices were reasonable, but we were shocked they'd run out of fatty tuna on a Saturday night—unacceptable for a sushi restaurant. Overall, decent but inconsistent.

A Modern Cinema Experience with Outstanding Cheese Popcorn This relatively new cinema, open for approximately seven months, offers an impressive moviegoing experience that combines comfort, technology, and exceptional concessions. While not perfect, it delivers enough quality features to warrant serious consideration from local film enthusiasts. ## The Standout Feature The cheese popcorn deserves special mention as potentially the best available at any movie theater. This seemingly small detail speaks volumes about the establishment's attention to food quality, complemented by a food lounge offering reasonably priced options that exceed typical cinema fare. ## Modern Amenities and Options The facility boasts fully digital projection across all theaters, with 3D capability throughout. Moviegoers can choose from various viewing experiences, including DBox motion seats and Star Class (21+ only) screenings. Standard evening tickets cost $9.75, with upcharges of $2 for Star Class, $3 for 3D, and $8 for DBox motion seats—pricing that remains competitive given the amenities offered. ## Exceptional Comfort The intimate 40-seat theater configuration features wide, side-by-side seating with generous legroom. The thoughtful design eliminates foot traffic in front of viewers, while red call buttons allow patrons to summon waitstaff during the film for orders or assistance. The staff demonstrates professionalism and friendliness throughout the experience. ## The Acoustic Issue The primary drawback involves inadequate soundproofing between theaters. Audio bleed from adjacent screenings creates noticeable distractions during quieter film moments—a significant concern worthy of management attention, particularly for a facility this new. ## Final Verdict Despite soundproofing concerns, this cinema successfully combines comfort, technology, and quality concessions into an enjoyable package. The venue works particularly well for deal-seekers using platforms like Groupon or LivingSocial. Most importantly, don't miss that cheese popcorn—it truly elevates the entire experience.

Really Wanted to Like This Place But..... Our experience at this BBQ restaurant started with promise but ultimately fell short of expectations. The pulled pork quesadilla appetizer was excellent—flavorful, juicy, and perfectly complemented by sour cream and spicy salsa. This impressive start had us optimistic for the main course. Unfortunately, dinner was disappointing. My flatiron steak arrived overcooked at well done instead of the requested medium, lacking flavor and character. While I considered sending it back, I decided against it. The accompanying BBQ sauces didn't salvage the dish—the molasses sauce was excessively sweet, the vinegar sauce too sour, and the mustard sauce tasted like plain Grey Poupon rather than proper BBQ sauce. Even worse were my wife's ribs, which arrived extremely dry and crispy—practically inedible and a complete waste of good meat. They rank among the worst ribs we've ever encountered. Madison desperately needs a quality BBQ establishment, and we had high hopes for this place. Unfortunately, based on this experience, it doesn't meet the standard. Without that stellar appetizer, this would have been a one-star review. The restaurant shows potential but needs significant improvement in execution and consistency. **Rating: 2/5 stars**

Liars and Thieves: A Decade-Long Problem at Fry's After ten years, Fry's Electronics continues their questionable practice of reselling returned items as new at full price. As a former employee, I witnessed this firsthand, and unfortunately, nothing has changed. Recently needing memory urgently, I reluctantly gave them another chance since no other local stores carried it. Upon receiving obviously used merchandise, staff insisted "we test all memory." Trusting their assurances about such easily testable products proved foolish—the memory was completely non-functional, clearly never tested. This experience confirms Fry's hasn't reformed their deceptive practices of charging full price for untested, returned merchandise while claiming quality assurance. Their "testing" policy is apparently fictional. **Lesson learned:** Amazon's delivery wait is infinitely preferable to Fry's fraudulent guarantees. At least online orders actually work.

Nightmare Experience: Lost Luggage, Unresponsive Service, and Hidden Costs This airline proved to be a complete disaster. They lost my bag yet still charged handling fees. When it finally arrived half-empty, customer service was unreachable. Return flight issues with online check-in added frustration. Ultimately cost more than competitors while delivering terrible service.

HORRIBLE HORRIBLE HORRIBLE!! Stay Away! One of the things they rave about here is how your pets stay out all day. That's nice, but what about the people that don't pay for the all-day play?
