Simply answered: Your dog will sit in a tiny cement cage for the entire time you're away! The kennel reminded me of the amount of space they have at the animal shelter! Do not just let them take your dog without looking at the kennel! Hot, dirty, smelly and cramped! I wouldn't leave my dog there if they paid me! Look for places that encourage you to drop them off for a free day of play or places that require a meet and greet prior to the day you drop them off. The place I ended up taking my dog asked about 50 questions on an intake form. These people only wanted to know how to feed him! **Bottom line:** Avoid this facility and find somewhere that truly cares about your pet's wellbeing.

A Reliable Choice for Family Photos Despite Some Changes Since the birth of our first child, Portrait Innovations has been our go-to photography company. While things have evolved over the years—the CD no longer includes hi-res pictures, and you generally get less for your money—there's one feature that remains unbeatable: the convenience of walking out with finished pictures in hand less than an hour after your session. Throughout our experience, the photographers have consistently been friendly and professional. Having recently relocated from South Carolina, where we knew the staff well and always had excellent experiences, we approached our latest session with high expectations. During this visit, the store was extremely busy due to an ending promotion, which typically creates hectic conditions. Despite the chaos, the photographer and most staff members maintained their friendly demeanor and provided great service. However, one employee—who appeared to be the manager—stood out negatively. She seemed snippy whenever asked questions, creating an uncomfortable atmosphere that contrasted sharply with the rest of the team's warmth. Despite this one disappointing interaction, the overall experience remained positive. The quality of our pictures once again met our expectations, and the friendly service from the majority of the staff overshadowed the manager's attitude. We're pleased with our photos and fully intend to return next year for our children's annual pictures.

**Outstanding BBQ Burger at Unbeatable Value** This BBQ burger ranks among the best I've ever tasted. While I can't pinpoint exactly what made it exceptional, every element came together perfectly. Having tried premium burgers costing $15-25 elsewhere, this reasonably-priced option surpassed them all. Highly impressive and absolutely worth trying.

Mixed Experience: Good Recovery, But Lingering Issues This Taco Bell location delivers an inconsistent experience that ultimately balances out to mediocre. While our initial visit was disappointing—featuring excessively greasy tacos with slippery soft shells and soggy hard shells—the management deserves credit for making things right on our return visit. The staff demonstrates friendliness and general competency, with the manager actively ensuring customer satisfaction. When the food isn't problematic, it's actually quite good, making this a viable option when craving tacos in the area. However, a significant concern remains: a persistent sewer smell permeated the dining area for over a week without any posted acknowledgment or apparent remediation efforts. This unsanitary atmosphere makes dining inside unpleasant. **The verdict:** Stick to the drive-through if visiting this location. While they've shown they can deliver quality food and service when things go right, the unaddressed odor issue prevents this from being a comfortable dine-in destination.

**Outstanding Massage Therapist Who Truly Cares** Jill is an exceptional massage therapist whose business name "Be Well" perfectly reflects her commitment to clients' health and happiness. She genuinely embodies wellness principles and delivers outstanding therapeutic care. Highly recommended as the best massage therapist in the West. Thank you, Jill!

Whoa! What a Turn Up for the Books! While the food itself remains consistent with my previous visits, this establishment truly deserves recognition for outstanding customer service that warrants an extra star. I ordered my regular grilled pear salad and chicken broth soup, though the wait seemed longer than usual. When my order finally arrived, the server demonstrated remarkable honesty by presenting me with two salads instead of one. The first was my correctly prepared pear salad. The second was his initial attempt, which featured the wrong dressing. Rather than discarding his mistake, he offered me both salads—keeping the correct order and gifting me the Caesar-dressed version free of charge. Though the original preparation tasted better, the "incorrect" salad was perfectly enjoyable. I happily consumed both salads plus my soup, grinning throughout the entire meal. This level of honesty and generosity in customer service goes a long way. Such genuine care for customers makes all the difference. Thanks immensely, team!

A Mixed Experience at This New Family Restaurant Finally, a family restaurant has breathed new life into this building that used to house a Beefeaters. I visited with my mother and sister, and the atmosphere was genuinely welcoming and pleasant. We started with the macaroni and cheese appetizer, which was absolutely delicious—the texture and cheese flavor were perfectly balanced. My sister's pork ribs were another winner, tender and flavorful, complemented by a corn salad that had a delightful salsa-like quality. Unfortunately, not everything hit the mark. My mother's catfish was disappointingly oily and overly salty. My broccoli and cauliflower casserole suffered similar issues—too salty, excessively cheesy, with insufficient broccoli and an overwhelming amount of onions. Our server started attentively but lost momentum midway through our meal, forgetting items and disappearing until we requested the bill. Despite these inconsistencies, the restaurant shows promise. I'd consider returning to try other menu options.

Mixed Experience at The Luxor: Great Deal, But Location and Hassles Detract My friend and I scored an excellent package deal through Priceline for a three-night stay at The Luxor, and while there were some pleasant surprises, several drawbacks made this a one-time experience for us. ## The Good Surprises We arrived approximately five hours before the standard check-in time, expecting to simply store our luggage and explore the city. To our pleasant surprise, the hotel offered early check-in as a courtesy, allowing us to settle in immediately and start our vacation without delay. Our room on the 20th floor was notably spacious and featured beautiful views of both the pool area and the surrounding mountains. The unique elevator experience, traveling at an angle due to the pyramid's distinctive architecture, was initially unsettling but became an interesting quirk of the stay. ## Room Amenities Fall Short Despite the room's size and view, basic amenities were surprisingly lacking. The shower had absolutely no shelving for toiletries, creating an inconvenient daily hassle. More surprisingly for a Las Vegas hotel, there was no mini fridge, coffee maker, or microwave—amenities many travelers have come to expect as standard. ## Dining and Shopping Conveniences The hotel offers numerous food options, including a food court, several restaurants, and remarkably, three Starbucks locations throughout the property. Endless slushie stations provided refreshment options while exploring the casino floor. The hallway views overlooking the mezzanine were visually impressive. However, the 24-hour convenience shops practice predatory pricing, charging $11 for a bottle of Advil. I strongly recommend visiting one of the Walgreens locations on the strip for any necessities. ## The Harassment Problem The most frustrating aspect of our stay was the constant harassment from suited individuals positioned throughout the hotel, particularly around the casino. They repeatedly approached us asking where we were from and whether we were single, attempting to sell vouchers or timeshares. By trip's end, we resorted to shaking our heads "no" the moment they opened their mouths. ## Pool and Location Limitations The pool closes at 7:00 PM, which severely limited our use since we typically explored the strip during those hours. The pool itself was relatively small with chained-off sections presumably reserved for private events. We managed only one brief 30-minute pool visit. The hotel's location at the far end of the strip made walking to most attractions time-consuming and exhausting. ## Final Verdict While the early check-in and spacious room were appreciated, the persistent harassment, limited amenities, restrictive pool hours, and inconvenient location make it unlikely I'll return to The Luxor despite the attractive pricing.

I don't understand this place. This quirky tiger-themed bar has character with its old-school jukebox and free popcorn, but the drawbacks outweigh the charm. The tiny space features only one bartender, causing lengthy wait times. No tap beers and limited bottled selection disappoint. It's cash-only without an on-site ATM, and the bouncer checking for carry-outs feels excessive. Despite the unique décor, the limited music genres and overall inconveniences make this spot hard to recommend. **Meh. No thanks.**

**A Fun Dining Spot with Standout Fish Sandwich** Hulu's offers an enjoyable dining experience with original, tasty entrees. The blackened Mahi fish sandwich is a standout—perfectly mild on a delicious bun. Both the accompanying slaw and sweet potato fries complement it well. Their brunch menu also impresses. The friendly, prompt service adds to the overall appeal, making Hulu's worth repeated visits for consistently satisfying meals.

A Fun Latin Spot with Great Vibes and Minor Limitations This quirky venue successfully combines multiple entertainment options - restaurant, dance club, and karaoke bar - creating a lively atmosphere. The late-night kitchen is a major plus, allowing guests to enjoy food alongside drinks and dancing. The music selection, primarily Cumbia with Latin variety, keeps energy high. However, the extremely small dance floor significantly limits movement. The crowd attracts a diverse mix of ages, though some patrons can be uncomfortable. On the positive side, staff members are friendly and provide quick, attentive service, enhancing the overall experience at this unique establishment.

A Disappointing Seventh Visit Overshadows Previous Experiences After six decent visits to this establishment, my seventh and most recent experience on Saturday was unfortunately disastrous enough to reconsider future patronage. The problems began at the express line, where despite clearly requesting no whipped cream on all drinks, every single beverage arrived topped with it. Additionally, the nachos and chips from the express line were so poor in quality that I wouldn't consume them even if complimentary. Hoping for better service, we requested proper seating and ordered another frozen hot chocolate—again specifying no whipped cream. Predictably, it arrived with whipped cream once more. The frustration mounted when my highly anticipated nachos with sour cream, meat, and guacamole proved inedible due to excessively salty meat. After just two bites, we had to abandon the dish entirely. Despite this terrible experience, I'm awarding three stars based on the six previous acceptable visits. However, this latest visit has significantly dampened my enthusiasm for returning. **Helpful tip:** If you're only ordering their famous frozen hot chocolate, the express line offers considerably larger portions and faster service compared to restaurant seating, making it the superior choice for beverages alone.

Disappointing Relocation Falls Short of Original The move from Chandler failed to recapture the original's charm, starting with an unwelcoming bike chain entrance. The venue appears run-down and stripped of beloved features like the all-you-can-eat fry bar and fresh veggie toppings for burgers. Most notably absent is the signature stage with surrounding bar for entertainment viewing. Despite ample space and a Vegas location, the establishment lacks the expected glitz and atmosphere that made the original memorable. This poor imitation disappoints longtime fans hoping for an improved experience.

Mixed First Impressions at This Compact Gaming Spot This reviewer admits uncertainty about their assessment after a brief initial visit. The venue's intimate size created an unexpectedly cramped atmosphere with only 20 patrons present, prompting a quick exit. The beer selection appeared limited at 5-8 taps—insufficient for this particular visitor's preferences. However, they acknowledge not realizing games were complimentary during this first encounter. The intriguing menu items, particularly bacon-wrapped corn dogs, have piqued their interest enough to warrant a return visit. They're open to revising their opinion after properly experiencing the establishment's offerings over drinks and food. A preliminary, incomplete assessment awaiting validation.

**Luxurious Stay with Minor Hiccups** The Luxor delivered a memorable experience with its beautiful suite and exceptional staff who were both helpful and pleasant. While room charging proved inconsistent across hotel services, the overall stay impressed. The private pool and cabanas are highly recommended despite the premium cost—the limited access creates a more exclusive, relaxing atmosphere worth the extra investment.

A Hidden Gem in the North Valley: Press at City North Delivers Excellence In a world dominated by corporate coffee chains, finding an independent café that excels in atmosphere, service, and quality can feel like discovering a hidden treasure. Press at City North is precisely that treasure, and it's quickly becoming the north valley's worst-kept secret. Despite being open for only about a month, Press has already cultivated a steady stream of patrons throughout the day. What draws people in isn't just convenience—it's the complete package that keeps them coming back. ## Beyond Basic Coffee Press offers an impressive menu that extends far beyond your standard café fare. Their coffee selections are expertly crafted, avoiding the burnt or overly sweetened pitfalls common at chain establishments. Served in oversized San Francisco-style mugs, each beverage feels like a proper experience rather than just a caffeine delivery system. The menu also features tea, hot chocolate, imported beer, and an extensive wine selection boasting approximately thirty varieties ranging from $5 to $16 per glass. For wine enthusiasts, the periodic tastings provide an excellent opportunity to explore their curated collection. The lunch menu deserves special mention, offering fresh sandwiches and salads that rival those found at gourmet bistros. This isn't grab-and-go quality—it's food worth lingering over. ## Atmosphere That Inspires What truly sets Press apart is its exceptional atmosphere. Situated on a quiet corner within the City North shops, the space features large windows that open onto a shaded terrace during pleasant weather. The interior design thoughtfully accommodates various needs: a granite bar with tall stools perfect for laptop work and people-watching, a large oak table ideal for group meetings, and comfortable leather couches for relaxation. The lighting deserves particular praise—soft enough to create ambiance yet bright enough for reading and working. Evening visits transform the space with candlelight, creating an atmosphere that must be experienced firsthand. The carefully curated background music complements rather than dominates the environment. ## Service That Stands Out Perhaps most impressive is the staff, who provide service that makes this month-old establishment feel like a beloved neighborhood institution. Informed, helpful, and genuinely invested in customer experience, the team creates connections that have regulars on a first-name basis within just a few visits. For north valley residents, Press at City North represents everything a local café should be. With free WiFi for patrons and proximity to restaurants like Kona Grill, it's the perfect spot to spend an entire day. Skip Desert Ridge, forget Starbucks—Press is the destination worth your time.

A Downtown Las Vegas Gem Worth Visiting Triple George has emerged as a welcome addition to downtown Las Vegas's dining scene, offering quality cuisine beyond the casino confines. While prices lean toward Strip levels—costing it a star—the exceptional food makes up for it. The ribeye stood out as perfectly cooked, a rarity that hadn't been experienced in months. The crab-stuffed shrimp proved equally impressive with bold, satisfying flavors. Appetizers included a caprese salad and goat cheese marinara, with the former being the preferred choice, though both were enjoyable. For beverages, consider ordering from the adjacent Mob Bar—their cocktail menu offers superior options worth the extra wait. The bourbon basket and Real McCoy come highly recommended, though some ginger-based drinks may disappoint. Currently, ongoing construction outside detracts from the ambiance. However, once completed, this establishment promises to become a regular destination for those seeking quality dining in downtown Las Vegas without casino crowds.

Great pizza! Crust is airy and crisp..... Oh, so tasty! Seem to use high quality ingredients. This is hands-down my favorite pizza in Phoenix. I always seem to crave Pino's on Sundays, so I find myself frustrated that they are closed. Dear Pino's, We know you need a day to yourself, but please, please, PLEASE..... stay open on Sundays!

Restaurant Falls Short: Poor Service and Mediocre Food Disappoint This establishment fails to live up to its reputation. Service was notably slow and impersonal, while the food proved merely adequate. The lifeless atmosphere contradicts positive online reviews. Based on this disappointing experience, a return visit seems unlikely.

A Premium Shopping Experience Worth Every Penny AJ's Fine Foods delivers an upscale grocery experience that justifies its higher price point through exceptional quality and service. This isn't your average supermarket, and that's precisely the appeal. **What Makes AJ's Special** The store consistently impresses with its generous sampling program, offering at least four high-quality samples during each visit. The immaculate store environment, knowledgeable staff, and top-tier specialty departments—including the deli, butcher, and bakery—demonstrate why premium pricing exists. Quality service and cleanliness require investment, and AJ's delivers on both fronts. **An Outstanding Wine Selection** The wine department truly stands out as exceptional. Unlike big-box retailers, AJ's carries prestigious labels including Turley, Shafer, Foxen, Gaja, Châteauneuf-du-Pape, quality Barolos, and Bonacorsi. This curated selection caters to serious wine enthusiasts seeking bottles unavailable at warehouse stores. **Gourmet Without the Pretension** While AJ's focuses on gourmet and specialty items rather than trendy health foods, their product selection hits the sweet spot for food lovers. From Paula Deen's complete marinade line to numerous other premium offerings, the inventory balances accessibility with sophistication. **The Bottom Line** Yes, AJ's costs more than conventional grocery stores, but the value proposition is clear. Exceptional service, cleanliness, quality products, and an unmatched wine selection create a shopping environment that transforms a routine errand into an enjoyable experience. For customers who appreciate the difference between adequate and excellent, AJ's proves that you truly get what you pay for. The premium experience justifies the premium prices. **Rating: A+**

A Philosophy Lover's Hidden Gem in Chandler As a devoted Philosophy products enthusiast, I was surprised to discover there are only two standalone Philosophy stores in all of Arizona. When an irresistible Groupon offer ($50 worth of products for just $25) appeared, I couldn't resist making the trek down the 101 to the Chandler location at Casa Paloma, despite its considerable distance from my home. The store itself is impressively sized, featuring virtually the entire Philosophy collection available for testing and exploration. For skincare addicts like myself, it's paradise – though I exercised restraint to avoid creating an overwhelming fragrance combination of flowers, raspberry, and countless other scents. What truly sets this location apart is the staff's approach. They're knowledgeable and helpful without being pushy – the perfect balance that encourages genuine browsing and, ultimately, purchasing. This hands-off yet available style creates a comfortable shopping environment. While the Chandler location isn't convenient for regular visits, I've now found my go-to destination for hard-to-find or newly released Philosophy items that haven't reached department stores, Sephora, or Ulta yet. For serious Philosophy fans seeking the complete collection or exclusive releases, this Casa Paloma location is worth the drive. The combination of extensive product selection and pleasant shopping experience makes it a valuable resource for Arizona Philosophy enthusiasts. **Rating: 4/5 stars**

Good Value Sushi with Smart Ordering Strategy This sushi spot offers solid value for money, though it requires some savvy ordering to maximize your experience. The key is visiting during busy hours and sticking with popular dishes, which ensures better freshness due to higher turnover rates. While made-to-order sushi guarantees the freshest option, expect a longer wait time. It's an honest assessment—not claiming to be the best sushi in town, but delivering a reliable, quick, and affordable meal. Perfect for those seeking a healthy lunch or dinner without breaking the bank. Know what to order, time your visit right, and you'll enjoy a satisfying dining experience.

A Surprisingly Entertaining Evening at the Tournament I'll admit, this wasn't exactly on my bucket list. While searching for a dinner spot with my mother-in-law, she spotted the sign and expressed her longtime curiosity about this type of show. I figured why not—eat with my hands, watch shirtless men on horseback, and save some casino money for a few hours. The meal exceeded my low expectations. The Cornish game hen was properly cooked and accompanied by tomato soup, broccoli, potatoes, a biscuit, and dessert. Eating with your hands adds to the medieval atmosphere and honestly, it's just fun. We cheered for Norway, and the show cleverly ensures every section wins something to maintain engagement throughout. The choreography was solid, sound effects impressive, and overall quite entertaining. It's genuinely good family-friendly entertainment that delivers exactly what it promises—a fun, interactive experience worth the price of admission.

Uninspired Chain Dining with One Saving Grace Max & Erma's fails to distinguish itself in the crowded chain restaurant landscape, offering little to justify repeat visits. The reviewer grudgingly returns only for obligatory family gatherings held in their back room, wishing instead for casual home-based get-togethers. After sampling much of the menu through these forced occasions, the consensus is clear: most dishes rank average or below. The sole standout? Their tortilla soup, which consistently delivers quality worth ordering. Everything else disappoints. The restaurant's "Free Cookie Wednesday" promotion seems like a weak attempt at generating traffic, especially when compared to competitors like Eat N' Park, where complimentary cookies are standard fare. Even Ruby Tuesday's manages to outshine Max & Erma's with their salad bar offering. Unless you're specifically craving their tortilla soup or attending a private event, this establishment offers little reason to choose it over alternatives. The lackluster menu and minimal distinguishing features make it forgettable in every sense.

A Slice of the Big Apple in Vegas: NY, NY Hotel Review After a decade-long hiatus from Sin City, I chose the New York-New York Hotel & Casino for my return visit – an ironic choice, perhaps, given that I'm actually from New York. While the experience had its ups and downs, the hotel's prime location and entertainment options made it a reasonable, if imperfect, choice for a Vegas getaway. ## Location: The Sweet Spot on the Strip NY, NY boasts an enviable position on the southern portion of the Strip. Within easy walking distance, you'll find MGM, Luxor, and Mandalay Bay to the south, while the impressive CityCenter complex, Planet Hollywood, and the Bellagio are all accessible to the north. For tourists wanting to explore multiple properties without constantly hailing cabs, this central location proves invaluable. ## Check-In Challenges and Room Disappointments Arriving after midnight on a Friday, I expected Vegas's 24/7 service mentality to be in full effect. Instead, I encountered a substantial line with only two staff members processing guests. The promised room wasn't available, so management substituted a "Madison"-style room in the smoking section – clearly designed for accessibility needs. While I appreciated the extra space, the room's amenities left much to be desired. The television reception was frustratingly poor, the doorless shower setup lacked proper drainage slope (resulting in water leakage), and most bizarrely, the toilet consistently required two flushes to function properly. Though the hotel did admirably minimize cigarette odors within the room, the hallway wasn't as successful in this regard. ## Hotel Amenities Shine Brighter Fortunately, the hotel's public areas significantly outperformed the room experience. The roller coaster proved genuinely thrilling and entertaining, while the diverse restaurant selection authentically captures New York's culinary spirit – from steakhouses and Italian eateries to Nathan's Famous hot dogs. The casino floor was adequate, though I noticed a disproportionate number of slot machines and video poker terminals compared to card game tables. Free parking is a welcome perk in the Strip's chaotic traffic environment, though the mandatory $20 daily resort fee (offering questionable value) dampens this benefit. ## The Value Proposition Would I return? Possibly, but price matters. The weekday rate of approximately $60 per night seems fair for what's offered, while the $130 weekend rate feels steep given the room quality issues. The hotel successfully replicates New York City's aesthetic, even if it can't capture the authentic experience, and provides ample entertainment without leaving the property. For budget-conscious travelers visiting midweek, NY, NY represents solid value. Weekend visitors paying premium rates might want to explore other options unless the location and theme particularly appeal to them.

Avoid like the plague. Dishonest in every respect. To preface my review, I will say that ultimately we received our furniture "kind of" as ordered. However, it took us over a month of calling and working with this place to get our actual order delivered. Huddle did everything to put the responsibility of their mistake on us! Huddle delivered a MUCH smaller chair than we ordered. Let's just say that I hardly fit in the chair we received, so I certainly would not have ordered it. We tried out the chair in the showroom, and it was nice and roomy. After telling Huddle they made a mistake, not only does Huddle say it's not their problem, they tell us to speak with the manufacturer. Meanwhile, we had already gone to the website of the manufacturer and found our chair as ordered, and verified that the chair we received was about 6 inches smaller all around. Here's the funny, and seriously DISHONEST and SHADY part: Huddle had obviously contacted the manufacturer, because the next day, they changed the measurements on their website, AND had the balls to try to act like the new measurements were the real ones and had been there the entire time! FOLKS, we're talking about 6 inches. Not a minimal difference. They are obviously not technically savvy either, as changing a website is EASY to track. This was an incredibly frustrating experience with terrible customer service. The deliberate deception regarding product specifications is unacceptable. I cannot recommend this company.

A Mall Lover's Take on Chandler Fashion Center As someone who grew up frequenting mega-malls, I approached Chandler Fashion Center with seasoned expertise. While it's not extraordinarily special, it perfectly serves its purpose as an "urban indoor hike" destination with friends. The mall's layout offers multiple pathways creating an interesting navigational challenge, with diverse "micro habitats" throughout. The food court provides solid options, including the irresistible Hot Dog on a Stick – because who can resist breaded, deep-fried meat on a stick? I spent considerable time in Macy's while exploring most of the shopping center. We concluded our visit at Cheesecake Factory, indulging perhaps too generously (though that's a review for another day). **Bottom line:** Chandler Fashion Center delivers a satisfying shopping experience when you need a retail fix. **Pro tip:** Never mall-shop alone! Bring friends who'll provide honest opinions without competing for the same purchases. Their critical eye proves invaluable when making decisions.

A Trendy Spot That Doesn't Quite Deliver on Value Walking into this trendy Asian fusion restaurant at the Palms, you're immediately struck by the awesome atmosphere. The space screams modern sophistication, and the service is decent enough. However, when it comes to the most crucial element—the food and whether it justifies the premium pricing—this establishment falls somewhat short. **Drinks and Starters** The cocktails, including the Godzilla and Dragonfly, were enjoyable but nothing extraordinary, especially considering Vegas's competitive $10+ cocktail scene. The rock shrimp tempura arrived cutely presented in a Chinese takeout box but was disappointingly heavy on mayo. While reasonably sized for $15, Shibuya's version surpasses it in flavor. **Sushi Selection** Despite requesting twice that all sushi arrive without wasabi, our Toro came with it anyway—frustrating for those who genuinely dislike it. On the positive side, both the yellowtail and Toro were exceptionally fresh, buttery, and flavorful. The Palms roll, however, was a complete miss. The no-rice presentation resulted in something resembling a "gooey fish ball" that we couldn't finish. **The Duck Dilemma** The duck was undeniably delicious, but at $30, it's hard to ignore that PF Chang's offers an equally satisfying version for roughly $12. While premium pricing is expected at the Palms, value-conscious diners should take note. **Final Verdict** This restaurant offers a pleasant evening with its stylish ambiance, but it doesn't stand out in Vegas's crowded Asian fusion scene. With so many exceptional options where you can spend $150 on dinner, this spot feels mediocre by comparison. I'd return if friends insisted, but it wouldn't be my first choice for a special night out.

Solid Food & Service, But Bring Earplugs The Gritty delivers on fundamentals: good food, quality drinks, and excellent service. However, their generous birthday promotion (unlimited soda or beer refills) has created an unintended consequence—constant chaos. This isn't about wait times; it's about noise levels that make conversation nearly impossible. Whether dodging rowdy college students, rambunctious ten-year-olds, or midlife crisis celebrations, expect a dining experience conducted largely in silence. Not the peaceful kind—the "I literally cannot hear my dining companion" kind. Unless your party brings a megaphone, meaningful conversation is off the table. Great for solo dining; challenging for anyone hoping to actually talk.

Disappointing BBQ Experience: When Convenience Isn't Worth It After trying this BBQ establishment located conveniently close to home, I'm disappointed to report it falls far short of authentic barbecue standards. As the only BBQ option within a 20-minute radius, I had high hopes – unfortunately, they were quickly dashed. ## Red Flags From the Start My first warning sign came during a 7pm phone call inquiring about rib availability. The owner revealed that leftover ribs get frozen and sometimes aren't consumed for 2-3 days. While I appreciated his honesty, this raised immediate concerns about freshness. ## The Microwave Incident Upon arriving at the restaurant, I witnessed the owner microwaving my ribs to "warm them up." This shocking discovery prompted questions about their preparation process. I learned they don't even have a smoker on-site – all meat is prepared at their Buckeye location and delivered later in the day. This centralized cooking model fundamentally contradicts traditional BBQ practices where meat is smoked fresh on premises. ## The Taste Test Ordering sauce on the side proved wise, allowing me to properly evaluate the meat quality. The results were disheartening: - **Sauce**: Resembled tangy ketchup with no distinctive character - **Meat**: Tasted exactly like reheated leftovers from a microwave - **Texture**: Dry and lacking the moisture and smokiness expected from quality BBQ The experience was identical to microwaving day-old ribs at home – hardly what you'd expect from a restaurant specializing in barbecue. ## Final Verdict While technically edible (preventing a one-star rating), this establishment earns my lowest possible recommendation. The combination of reheated, delivered meat and microwave preparation methods creates an experience that barely qualifies as BBQ. **My advice**: Invest the extra driving time to reach an authentic BBQ joint where meat is smoked fresh on-site. The additional effort will reward you with genuine barbecue worth eating.

Premium RAW Denim Worth the Investment If you haven't experienced RAW denim, you're missing out on exceptional quality—though your wallet will definitely feel the impact. Despite the premium price point, these jeans deliver outstanding value. **Insider Tip:** Their V-neck tees offer remarkable value at $30 for a 2-pack. Available in multiple colors, these high-quality shirts provide the best fit you'll find. It's an affordable entry point to experience their superior craftsmanship and attention to detail in garment construction.

Mixed Experience at Restaurant Falls Short of Expectations After two visits to this establishment, I'm left questioning the overwhelmingly positive reviews. My first experience with the spicy chicken wrap was disappointing—the dish was bland, sloppily prepared, and confusingly assembled, leaving me unable to determine whether it was intended to be served hot or cold. Hoping for better results after transitioning to a vegetarian diet, I returned to try their vegan chicken sandwich with avocado. Unfortunately, the experience didn't improve. Despite requesting no tomatoes, they arrived on my sandwich anyway. More concerning was the minimal avocado—just a few meager slivers—and the overall lackluster taste. I'm genuinely puzzled by the enthusiastic praise other reviewers have given this restaurant. The quality simply doesn't match the hype. For a superior vegetarian experience, I strongly recommend Baguette Cafe instead, where any sandwich can be customized for vegetarians with significantly better results. The food quality and attention to detail at Baguette Cafe far surpasses what this restaurant offers, making it my clear preference for future meals.

Disappointing Dining Experience Falls Short of Vegas Standards This restaurant fails to deliver on multiple fronts, with subpar service, lackluster food, and an overall underwhelming experience. Given Las Vegas's abundant superior dining options, visitors should definitely skip this establishment and explore better alternatives elsewhere.

Absolute Disaster: Zero Service, Zero Communication This company epitomizes failure in every aspect. They failed to show up for the scheduled appointment, leaving me waiting for a service that never materialized. Communication is non-existent—phone calls go unanswered and emails receive no response. After reporting to Living Social, my next step involves the Better Business Bureau. Save yourself the frustration and avoid this unreliable company completely.

This is my favorite nail spot. The actual store is beautiful and exceptionally clean. Whoever designed it truly understood aesthetics. I love their different pedicure options. The mocha smells amazing. The stone massage is so relaxing. They also do waxing and I have been so happy with my results. Looking forward to getting a facial next week.

Solid Appliance Selection in a Compact Space After The Great Indoors closed, we discovered this Sears appliance showroom as an alternative. While the store feels cramped due to its small footprint and dense layout—with appliances lining both walls plus a center row—it offers an impressive selection beyond just Kenmore brands. The showroom features modern induction cooktops alongside traditional gas and electric smooth-top options in 30" and 36" sizes. We were pleasantly surprised by the variety and found prices competitive with Home Depot and Lowe's. **Bottom Line:** Despite the claustrophobic feel, this location delivers solid appliance choices at reasonable prices. As always, comparison shopping is recommended to ensure you're getting the best deal for your specific needs.

The Vig Uptown: Great Food and Atmosphere, But Service Falls Short Last night's Yelp mixer at The Vig Uptown was an interesting study in contrasts. What started as an event for 10 RSVPs turned into a lively gathering of over 20 social Yelpers, eager to experience what this establishment had to offer. **The Good News** The food was undeniably impressive. Our group sampled an array of happy hour items including crab and artichoke dip, hummus, guacamole and salsa, and chicken flatbread. Every single item was delicious – not a single disappointment among them. The manager's attentiveness was also noteworthy, checking on our party multiple times throughout the evening to ensure satisfaction. **The Service Problem** Unfortunately, the waiter appeared completely overwhelmed by our group's size and staggered arrival times. During my 90-minute visit (5:00-6:30pm), I managed to order only one drink. When I spotted an interesting cocktail and inquired about it, the waiter insisted The Vig didn't serve what I was describing – despite having seen it moments earlier. More troubling, he didn't offer an alternative or check if I wanted anything else. This service deficit affected the entire party. Multiple Yelpers expressed wanting another round of their "scrumptious alcoholic beverages," but opportunities never materialized. I would have easily ordered two or three drinks with proper service. **The Verdict** Excellent food and management can't overcome poor service execution. Two stars reflects this disappointing experience – The Vig Uptown has potential but needs stronger wait staff.

Subpar Business Hotel with Disappointing Amenities **Poor Choice for Business Travelers** This hotel fails to meet professional standards with an unsuitable atmosphere and lackluster dining options (NOBU excluded). The internet connectivity is exceptionally poor—arguably the slowest available—making business operations nearly impossible. Overall experience warrants a C- rating. Not recommended for business purposes.

Overhyped Poutine Paradise Falls Short of Expectations After finally visiting the legendary La Banquise, I found myself underwhelmed by Montreal's supposed poutine mecca. While my Obelix and my wife's classic poutine were enjoyable, the fundamental components—fries, cheese curds, and gravy—didn't justify the establishment's towering reputation. The specialty toppings are certainly fun and creative, making the elaborate poutines worth trying. However, the hefty prices feel outrageous for what you're getting. La Banquise offers a decent experience that's worth visiting once, perhaps twice for the novelty factor. Ultimately, this iconic spot doesn't deserve its pedestal status. Montreal's poutine scene has much more to offer, including gems like Decarie Hot-Dog. La Banquise is good, but far from the best.

A Shocking Confrontation: When Customer Service Goes Completely Wrong What should have been a simple shopping trip turned into an incredibly uncomfortable and bizarre encounter that left me questioning everything about customer service and proper protocol. After enjoying lunch with my family at a nearby restaurant, we decided to pop into this store for a few essentials and some beer for an afternoon by the pool. It seemed like a straightforward errand—nothing could have prepared me for what happened next. ## The Incident I completed my purchase, grabbed my bags and 12-pack, and headed toward the exit while waiting for my wife and kids. As we prepared to leave, a woman suddenly positioned herself in front of me, blocking my path. Initially thinking it was an accident, I even apologized for being in her way. However, when she deliberately moved to block me again, I realized something strange was happening. This woman, mumbling incoherently under her breath, continued preventing me from leaving the store. She positioned herself with her back to me, physically blocking the exit while I stood there with my receipt clearly visible in my hand. The situation escalated when she began shouting for "Matt," asking if he'd checked me out, making it painfully clear she was accusing me of theft. ## The Aftermath When the manager finally arrived, he quickly confirmed I was "good" and led the woman away. What made matters worse was another employee's comment that "a lot of people steal beer" from them—as if that somehow justified treating paying customers like criminals. I had my receipt the entire time. I was with my family. Yet this person felt entitled to physically prevent me from leaving and publicly accuse me of theft without any basis whatsoever. This experience was not only humiliating but completely unacceptable. I'll be contacting the general manager for answers about proper procedures and how they plan to prevent law-abiding customers from being harassed in the future.

A Hidden Gem Worth Discovering: Merci Restaurant Review Stumbling upon Merci on a quiet Sunday morning proved to be a delightful surprise. Despite the sparse crowd—which initially raised concerns—this establishment quickly demonstrated why it deserves more attention. The eggs Florentine were exceptional, perfectly complemented by an outstanding almond croissant. A thoughtful touch of fresh salad greens accompanied the breakfast, elevating the presentation beyond typical brunch fare. The coffee truly stole the show: bold, authentic java that far surpassed standard drip coffee expectations. Service presented a mixed experience. While one younger blonde server seemed distracted, Taylor—the attentive Hawaiian or Japanese server—displayed remarkable professionalism and efficiency. Her dedication to hospitality suggests a promising career ahead. Merci is indeed a hidden gem offering quality food, excellent coffee, and potential for consistently excellent service. This underrated spot deserves your visit.

Pretty Good Authentic Mexican Spot Worth Revisiting After one visit, this restaurant shows promise with fairly authentic Mexican cuisine. The carne asada tacos deliver on flavor, making them a highlight of the menu. However, portion sizes leave something to be desired. At the current price point, receiving only two tacos feels insufficient—three to four would offer better value. Despite the limited quantity, the overall experience was decent enough to warrant a return visit.

A Disappointing Pizza Experience: Savings Not Worth the Sacrifice While this north Scottsdale/Cave Creek pizzeria offered below-average pricing and punctual service, the quality fell drastically short of expectations. This proved to be one of the most disappointing pizzas I've encountered—so much so that my father and I discarded the entire pie after just one slice each. The only redeeming quality was a decent crust. Unfortunately, everything else missed the mark. The sauce had an unmistakable canned taste, lacking any fresh or authentic flavor. The cheese resembled plastic in both taste and texture, which was particularly off-putting. Most concerning was the chicken topping: instead of grilled or seasoned chicken pieces, they used sliced deep-fried cutlets simply placed on top. The bottom line: the modest savings aren't worth compromising your meal. **Proceed with extreme caution.**

Inexcusable Service Failure This restaurant visit was an absolute disaster from start to finish. Despite the server explicitly directing the host to seat us, we were completely ignored for 20 minutes while tables seated after us received prompt attention. The blatant disregard felt deliberate and offensive, as multiple staff members bypassed our table without acknowledgment. We left without ordering, hungry and insulted. When a restaurant can't perform the basic function of acknowledging customers, it doesn't deserve a second chance. We'll never return and strongly advise others to avoid this establishment.

Outstanding Bead Store with Exceptional Turquoise Selection Al's Beads has earned a permanent spot on my Arizona travel itinerary. The store excels in authentic stone quality, fair pricing, and knowledgeable staff assistance. Their turquoise collection is so impressive that I've decided it's my exclusive source for this gemstone. Highly recommended for serious bead enthusiasts.

**Great Diner with Great Diner Food** This 24/7 establishment delivers authentic diner fare despite its less-than-ideal location in a seedier neighborhood. The friendly staff consistently provides welcoming service, making it a reliable choice for classic comfort food like steak and eggs. While the atmosphere isn't fancy, the quality and availability make up for any lack of glamour. It's the perfect spot when cravings hit at any hour. Just one important caveat: this is a cash-only establishment, so come prepared or risk an unpleasant surprise at the register. Overall, a solid, dependable option for traditional diner grub.

Consistent Quality and Great Atmosphere I've been here on several occasions and I've always enjoyed the experience. The outdoor area looks like it's currently under construction, but if it remains pretty similar, it's an ideal place to hang out and catch up with friends. Inside is a little loud with music. I usually get the tacos but friends have always liked their food too. The churros and the agua frescas are amazing!

Mixed Experience at XS Nightclub: Great Venue, Poor Service XS ranks among the finest nightclubs I've visited, but my recent experience on Saturday, December 13th was deeply disappointing. This was my third visit, and unfortunately, the second time I encountered disrespectful staff behavior. The treatment I received was so humiliating that I'm reconsidering future visits. As a paying customer, I expected basic courtesy and professionalism. Instead, the staff's attitude completely ruined what should have been an enjoyable evening. The disconnect between the venue's premium reputation and the actual service quality is concerning. I genuinely hope other guests don't experience similar treatment. Management at both the hotel and nightclub should seriously evaluate their staff's customer service practices. The venue deserves better representation.

A Disappointing Return Visit Ends in Food Poisoning Despite giving Jason's Deli a second chance based on a friend's recommendation, this visit turned into a nightmare. After the first bite of a hummus wrap, stomach problems began immediately. What started as mild discomfort quickly escalated into severe food poisoning after consuming the olive-laden wrap. This experience resulted in the worst food-related illness the reviewer has ever encountered. The exact cause remains uncertain, but this cautionary tale serves as a warning to potential diners. Proceed with extreme caution when considering this establishment for your next meal.
Skip This Disappointing Sushi Spot Small, overpriced sashimi portions and forgettable service make this all-you-can-eat sushi bar a complete miss. The name indeed says it all—pass on this one.
Reliable Chinese Takeout Spot This is our go-to chinese take out. The food is good, service is average and the prices are good. All the traditional menu items. Never had a bad experience.

Disappointing Burger Experience with Mediocre Frozen Hot Chocolate The burgers looked appealing but were disappointingly dry. Their famous frozen hot chocolate was merely okay—nothing special that couldn't be replicated at home. Overall, underwhelming visit.

A Disappointing Dining Experience Not Worth Your Money This restaurant fell dramatically short of expectations during our post-movie visit. The empty dining room on a Friday night should have been our warning sign. The margaritas were subpar – frankly, chain restaurants like Chili's serve better cocktails. Our volcano nachos arrived disappointingly lukewarm with partially melted cheese, setting the tone for the evening. The kids' meal was equally disappointing, featuring only onions and squash as the vegetable option. Every dish that followed maintained the same low quality. For a $70 bill, the experience was unacceptably poor. While I typically don't voice complaints in restaurants, the overall mediocrity left me too exhausted to address it. I'm writing this review hoping to spare others from wasting their money on overpriced, substandard food. There are far better dining options available near the AMC theater. Save yourself the disappointment and choose elsewhere.

Health Inspector's Nightmare: A DQ to Avoid **Rating: ★☆☆☆☆** This Dairy Queen desperately needs attention. The counter area was so unsanitary that dining outside near the dumpsters seemed more appealing. The only silver lining? A convenient recycling drop-off spot we discovered while escaping the interior grime.

The M rocks my socks (or something like that). Maybe it's the proximity, but I'm here constantly. The gaming minimums hit that sweet spot, and crowds are never an issue. The spa, salon, and pool area all deliver quality experiences. The atmosphere and decor create a welcoming vibe throughout. Food-wise, this place excels. Their buffet ranks among Vegas's best, and that Chicago Dog at the deli? Absolutely awesome. Beer enthusiasts will appreciate one of the city's finest selections. What really sets The M apart is their treatment of locals—they genuinely know how to make regulars feel valued and appreciated.

A Slice of France in Las Vegas This brasserie-style restaurant stands out as my absolute favorite Vegas destination. The authentic French atmosphere transports you straight to France, while the exceptional cuisine keeps me dreaming about return visits. The foie gras surpasses even Eiffel Tower's version—it's simply amazing. My recent mussels were cooked to perfection, and the red berry meringue proved heavenly. Combined with attentive service, this establishment deserves recommendation to anyone appreciating fine dining. **Rating: ★★★★★** *Highly recommended for discerning palates.*

A Classy Vegas Retreat with Minor Drawbacks The Signature offers a refreshing escape from the typical Vegas chaos of smoke-filled casinos and overwhelming crowds. This gated community provides a mansion-like entrance experience that sets an upscale tone from arrival. The Junior Suite impresses with its thoughtful amenities, including a well-appointed kitchen, a bedroom featuring a TV that dramatically rises from its stand, and an expansive bathroom complete with jacuzzi. The property exudes sophistication throughout, and the front desk staff proves exceptionally helpful, even assisting intoxicated guests at 3am with room location assistance. However, some drawbacks exist. The patio view disappoints, overlooking the airport and vacant lots rather than the iconic Strip. The location, while peaceful, sits slightly removed from main attractions, requiring longer walks and potentially hazardous street crossings when returning on foot. Despite these minor inconveniences, The Signature delivers a classy, quieter Vegas alternative. Perfect for those seeking respite from the Strip's intensity while maintaining proximity to the action. The upscale accommodations and attentive service make it a worthwhile choice for a special occasion.

**Not Worth the Drive or the Price** While the twinkling lights are admittedly pretty and the lakeside light show offers a pleasant moment, this ZooLights experience falls disappointingly short. Even on a Tuesday night, the crowds were overwhelming, making it difficult to simply walk through. For $10 per person, you get roughly an hour of viewing before running out of things to see. When you factor in a lengthy drive, the value proposition crumbles entirely. A movie ticket would provide double the entertainment time for similar or less cost. Unless you live nearby, skip this overcrowded, overpriced holiday attraction.

Exceptional Service and Delicious Fare Worth Returning For Jason provided outstanding, knowledgeable service while the cabernet blend and green julienne impressed. This memorable dining experience guarantees a return visit.

Disappointing Experience Despite High Expectations I had high hopes for this establishment given the premium pricing and extended wait time, but unfortunately left feeling underwhelmed. While the restaurant's ambiance is attractive and the food presentation visually appealing, the taste simply didn't match the impressive display. During my dinner visit, I sampled the crab legs, shrimp, and prime rib—standard buffet fare that wasn't particularly memorable. The prime rib, while flavorful, was excessively salty. The dessert selection proved most disappointing, lacking crème brûlée and featuring a yogurt sorbet that tasted disturbingly like spoiled milk. Service was adequate but imperfect, with our drink orders arriving incorrectly. Our seating location far from the buffet stations necessitated strategic loading of plates to minimize trips. Ultimately, this venue doesn't justify its price point. I've enjoyed superior dining experiences at more affordable establishments elsewhere. For what this restaurant charges, I expected exceptional quality that simply wasn't delivered. I cannot recommend this location based on value or culinary execution.

A Disastrous Evening at La Casa: Chaos Behind the Scenes Our Friday night visit to La Casa with a party of six turned into an endurance test rather than an enjoyable dining experience. The restaurant appeared to be in complete operational meltdown, with an entirely new wait staff (hired just one day prior), no visible manager, and only a single cook handling all orders. Most concerning was watching staff frantically transport supplies from their sister restaurant through the front door as they ran out of basic ingredients. We ordered four tapas and two entrées, but our first dish didn't arrive until 90 minutes after ordering. Two additional tapas and one entrée trickled out 30 minutes later. After waiting three full hours, we finally canceled the remaining items—including a simple salad—that never materialized. While the food quality was passable, the catastrophic service and organizational chaos overshadowed everything. This establishment desperately needs professional intervention. Until major management changes occur, we cannot recommend La Casa and won't be returning.

A Heartbreaking Experience with Zero Customer Compassion This pawn shop demonstrated a complete lack of empathy during what was already a difficult situation. After realizing we had mistakenly sold irreplaceable heirloom jewelry, we contacted them within just one business day hoping to rectify the mistake. What followed was a deeply disappointing and hurtful experience. ## Unwillingness to Help Despite the sentimental value and quick turnaround time, the company showed zero flexibility. While they may not have been "legally" obligated to return our items, a compassionate business would have considered making an exception given the unusual circumstances. Instead, they treated this purely as a profit opportunity. ## Unreasonable Demands and Poor Treatment We offered $1,000 compensation for their one day of inconvenience—a generous offer by any standard. They rejected it, demanding $4,000 above their purchase price instead. When my husband agreed and arrived with the money, the situation became even worse. After initially accepting, the employee suddenly changed his mind and told him to return at 3 PM. ## Adding Insult to Injury My distressed husband requested they not take further action until we could return. Their response? A nasty email telling me never to contact them again. This level of rudeness and insensitivity is inexcusable. This company cares only about quick profits, not customers or doing what's right. I sincerely hope they never experience such heartbreak themselves. **Rating: ★☆☆☆☆**

Consistently Excellent Quality and Service This Outback location stands out as one of the west valley's most reliable dining options. After comparing ribs across multiple chains including Texas Roadhouse, Mimi's, and Dillon's, Outback's fall-off-the-bone ribs are noticeably superior. The restaurant maintains impressive consistency across their entire menu, delivering quality meals and service every visit. A dependable choice for consistently satisfying dining.

Sweet Pursuit: A Cupcake Quest Begins Embarking on a delightful mission to discover the ultimate cupcake, I ventured into Cake Cafe to sample their peanut butter offerings. The verdict? Solidly satisfying, though not quite transcendent. I polished off every crumb without hesitation, which speaks volumes about their quality, even if fireworks didn't explode in my mouth. The real question lingers: Am I simply lacking that notorious sweet tooth, or were these cupcakes merely adequate? Only continued exploration of the local dessert scene will reveal the truth. What elevated the experience was the exceptional service—the counter staff proved genuinely helpful and welcoming. As a bonus, they serve coffee drinks, making this the ideal spot for combining your sugar rush with a caffeine boost. The delicious research continues, and honestly, I couldn't be more excited about this tasty assignment!

Setting the Record Straight: A Fair Assessment Let me address some misconceptions floating around about this establishment. **Price Point Reality** This is not an upscale or pricey Mexican restaurant. Nice decor doesn't automatically equal fancy dining. The current owners inherited the building's aesthetic from Gardunos—it doesn't reflect their pricing strategy. A four-item dinner combo costs $14. That's reasonable by any measure. **Happy Hour Exists** Contrary to some claims, they absolutely have happy hour: Monday-Friday, 3-6:30pm. House margaritas (10oz) are $3, and 19oz Hornitos run $6. Check their website. **Food Quality** The food is exactly what it should be—good, solid Mexican fare. This isn't Barrio Cafe or some trendy LA/Vegas cantina, and it doesn't pretend to be. It's simply a really good neighborhood Mexican restaurant delivering quality at fair prices. The negative reviews seem misguided. Judge this place for what it actually is, not what some reviewers mistakenly expected. Now I'm craving enchiladas myself.

A Tourist Trap That'll Empty Your Wallet If you're looking for an overpriced, underwhelming experience, the Venetian's gondola ride delivers disappointingly on all fronts. ## Navigation Nightmare The journey begins with confusion. Finding the indoor ride requires extensive walking through the casino, and staff members provide contradictory directions. Your best bet? Ignore them entirely and follow overhead signage instead. ## Eight Minutes of "Magic" We chose the outdoor ride on a beautiful day, hoping for something memorable. What we got was an eight-minute float after standing in lengthy queues, costing $20 per person while sharing our gondola with strangers. The only redeeming quality was our gondolier, a former Sydney resident who provided pleasant conversation about our shared hometown. ## Photography Fiasco The photo package proved equally disappointing. Of three pictures taken, only one was remotely acceptable. The pricing structure forces you to buy two photos minimum, with a third thrown in "free"—meaning we paid for mediocre shots we didn't want. For a professional photography operation, the quality was shockingly poor. My Android phone produces better results. ## The Verdict This experience epitomizes everything wrong with Vegas tourist attractions: overpriced, rushed, and ultimately forgettable. While I can check it off my bucket list, that's the only satisfaction gained. Save your money for literally anything else on the Strip. **Rating: Skip it entirely unless you enjoy wasting money.**

A Surprisingly Pleasant Experience at David's Bridal When I scheduled my appointment at David's Bridal, I'll admit my expectations were fairly low. After reading countless mixed reviews about the chain's various locations, I was bracing myself for a potentially frustrating experience. However, the Phoenix location proved to be a pleasant surprise that exceeded my admittedly modest expectations. ## First Impressions Matter The online appointment booking process was refreshingly convenient and straightforward. Upon arrival, I was immediately struck by how bright and clean the store appeared—a significant departure from some of the darker, more cramped bridal shops I'd visited previously. The staff member who greeted me was genuinely friendly and accommodating, allowing me to browse freely for about twenty minutes since I'd arrived early for my appointment. ## The Consultant Experience My consultant, Brittani, was the highlight of my visit. Unlike some retail experiences where salespeople can feel pushy or disingenuous, Brittani struck the perfect balance of being helpful, friendly, and authentic. She had already pulled all my favorite dresses that I'd selected online before my appointment began, which demonstrated excellent preparation and attention to detail. ## The Inevitable Disappointments Unfortunately, not everything went smoothly. My absolute favorite dress wasn't available in regular sizes at the store, despite being listed online in my size. They only carried it in plus sizes, which was genuinely disappointing. Additionally, the bustier they provided was both ill-fitting and had visible makeup stains—not exactly what you want when trying on your potential wedding dress. ## Practical Observations The dress quality varied considerably. Some gowns featured beautiful fabrics and construction, while others were noticeably cheaper in feel and appearance. I strongly recommend doing your homework beforehand and selecting dresses online to maximize your appointment time. This approach helps you avoid wasting precious minutes flipping through bagged dresses or relying solely on consultant selections. Be warned: alterations at David's Bridal come with a hefty price tag. Factor this into your budget planning. Also, try booking a weekday daytime appointment if possible. My 2pm Monday slot meant I had Brittani's undivided attention and enjoyed a relatively quiet, stress-free shopping environment. ## The Verdict While I ultimately found my dress elsewhere the following day, I genuinely enjoyed my David's Bridal experience. Their price range ($200 to $1200+) accommodates virtually any budget, and their selection is impressive for the value. I'm definitely returning for bridesmaid dresses and accessories—their color coordination options are particularly excellent. One caveat: their call center became somewhat aggressive after I canceled a follow-up appointment, calling multiple times daily. However, once I explicitly requested they stop, the calls ceased immediately. This seems like a corporate policy issue rather than a reflection of the individual store. For budget-conscious brides seeking variety and convenience, this David's Bridal location is worth visiting.

A Food Network Favorite That Delivers on Breakfast I'm a sucker for restaurants featured on The Food Network or Top Chef, and I love a hearty breakfast. Over Easy perfectly satisfies both cravings. Arriving around 10:30am, we only waited about 10 minutes. I ordered the Tammy—egg whites with spinach, Swiss cheese, garlic, and onion on an English muffin—while Ryan chose the cheddar-jalapeño biscuits with sausage gravy. Those waffle dogs are definitely on my list for next time. My sandwich was delicious, and the sweet potato tater tots were amazing. The portions are generous but manageable when you're hungry. Ryan's biscuits and gravy were phenomenal—easily the best we found during our Minneapolis hunt. This is exactly the type of place I'll bring visitors to impress them with my local knowledge. Over Easy truly lives up to its Food Network reputation.

A Rocky Start Redeemed by Excellent Management and Food When my friend expressed interest in celebrating her birthday at this restaurant, I made a reservation online for 8:45 PM on February 10th. Despite arriving slightly late at 9 PM due to difficulty finding the location, the hostesses were very welcoming when I apologized. I mentioned it was my friend's birthday and left her name with them before being seated near the kitchen. The atmosphere and maintenance of the establishment immediately impressed me. However, the service experience began on a disappointing note. After ordering water with lemon, my waiter forgot the lemons twice, never returning with them. When I ordered the chopped salad appetizer, it took 30 minutes to arrive—and only after my friend had joined me and I reminded him about it. That said, the salad itself was excellent: well-portioned with robust flavor for just 175 calories. For our entrées, we selected the light mahimahi and lemon chicken. Both dishes exceeded expectations. The mahimahi was fresh, perfectly cooked, and generously portioned, while the lemon chicken was juicy without being overpowering, accompanied by abundant vegetables. The kitchen clearly deserved compliments. When my water glass sat empty despite my waiter passing by multiple times, I requested both a refill and the manager. She arrived already aware of the service failures—the missing lemons, delayed salad, and overall poor attention. Her response was exemplary: she personally apologized, brought my friend a complimentary birthday dessert, discounted our check, and took over serving our table herself. Despite the initial service issues, the outstanding food quality and exceptional management response have earned my recommendation. I would absolutely return to this restaurant, confident that my first experience was an anomaly rather than the standard.

**Delightful Cupcakes with Perfect Balance** I absolutely love this cupcakery! Their cupcakes are consistently light and moist with just the right amount of frosting and wonderful flavors. The fun glitter topping is charming. The cherry cupcake with a real cherry baked inside was exceptional, though I'm disappointed it's not currently available.

Disappointing Return Visit: Quality Issues Persist Another visit yields similar underwhelming results. The brisket remains excessively fatty, while four of five ribs were acceptable—the last being entirely gristle. The rubbery salad disappointed, though sides proved merely adequate. Consistency problems continue unresolved.

Spectacular Views, But the Dining Experience Falls Short **A Case of Style Over Substance at this Phoenix Restaurant** While the panoramic vistas from this establishment genuinely surpass those at Hilton's Different Pointe of View, the culinary execution leaves much to be desired. Our experience with a Travelzoo dinner voucher revealed significant inconsistencies that overshadowed the stunning scenery. **Disappointing First Impressions** The evening began with appetizers that set a concerning tone. The butternut risotto arrived disappointingly bland, while the shrimp cake, though flavorful, was undermined by sauces that added nothing to the dish. The second course proved even more problematic—portion sizes varied wildly across our party, something that would likely provoke Chef Ramsay's infamous wrath. The tomato fennel soup was unremarkable, and the green salad, while tasty, suffered from poor plating. **Entrees That Miss the Mark** The main courses continued the trend of mediocrity. The beef medallions resembled an upscale frozen dinner, with overly sweet gravy that couldn't justify the premium price point. The fish trio, served over couscous, was competently cooked but ultimately unsatisfying with noticeably small portions throughout. **Dessert and Beverage Disappointments** Despite our server's enthusiastic description of the chocolate swirl cheesecake as "phenomenal," store-bought alternatives would provide better value. The espresso crème brûlée was heavy on cream and light on the signature caramelized topping. The wine selection proved particularly troubling—watered-down and stale-tasting, resembling a bottle left open overnight. **Service Concerns** Professional service standards weren't met either. Our server's profanity-laced reaction to splitting checks among our large party was wholly inappropriate for fine dining. **The Bottom Line** Even with our voucher, the final bill reached $55 after gratuity (calculated on the original $120 tab) and tax. While the views warrant a visit, perhaps during daylight hours, the food quality simply doesn't justify returning for a meal.

**Extremely Poor Service Overshadows Quality Food** Despite good food, service was unacceptably bad. Waited 30 minutes for drinks, then discovered our meal was never started after another 20 minutes. Had to get water myself from the bar. Completely unacceptable experience. Won't return.

A Mixed Experience at All-You-Can-Eat Sushi When my family visited and I wanted to introduce them to all-you-can-eat (AYCE) sushi, I chose this restaurant for their first experience. Despite an hour-long wait, we were seated in half of the "VIP room" near the cash register, which accommodated our party of six. ## Quality of Food The timing of our visit proved fortunate, as the fish quality was exceptional. The standout items of the evening included the pork belly, surf clam, octopus, and yellowtail, which everyone thoroughly enjoyed. However, I noticed the fish-to-rice ratio on some nigiri pieces had decreased compared to my previous visit, which was slightly disappointing. ## Accommodation Concerns A significant issue arose regarding dietary restrictions. Several nigiri items, including albacore and seared varieties, come pre-seasoned with ponzu sauce containing wheat. When we requested these without the sauce for gluten-free needs, our server explained that the sushi chefs prepare items in batches and couldn't accommodate modifications. This inflexibility earns only 3 stars. Sitting at the bar might have yielded different results with direct chef interaction. ## Dessert Selection The dessert menu appears to rotate. While my previous visit featured plum wine jelly, this time only crème brûlée, chocolate mousse, and ice cream were available. Overall, while the fish quality impressed, the lack of flexibility for dietary needs was frustrating.

A Hidden Gem for Thai Lunch: Quick Service and Bold Flavors Finding a reliable lunch spot near work can be challenging, but this Thai restaurant exceeded expectations on a first visit. Located conveniently close to the office, it offers the perfect combination of speed, flavor, and welcoming service—ideal for professionals squeezing lunch between meetings. ## Exceptional Service from Start to Finish The experience began with a phone call to place a takeout order. Julia, the hostess, answered with unexpected enthusiasm and genuine helpfulness. As a first-time customer, her recommendations were invaluable, and the promised 5-10 minute turnaround was music to the ears of anyone watching the clock. Upon arrival, the restaurant's modern aesthetic with Thai touches provided a refreshing alternative to traditional heavily-decorated Thai establishments. The atmosphere suggests this venue could easily transition from quick lunch spot to dinner date destination. ## The Food: Hits and Near-Misses **Pad Thai (Medium Spice):** The spice level was executed perfectly—enough heat to enhance flavor without overwhelming the palate. The portion size was generous, though the protein distribution was disappointing with only one shrimp and three chicken pieces among abundant thin noodles. **Pad Krapow:** This dish was the clear winner. Ordered with tofu at medium spice level, it arrived with rice on the side and delivered outstanding flavor. While the vegetable variety could have been broader (heavy on onions), the overall execution warranted five stars and immediate regret for not ordering it personally. ## The Bottom Line At $8.95 per lunch entrée, this restaurant offers excellent value. The genuine 5-10 minute wait time makes it perfect for time-crunched lunches. Julia's friendly service and local area knowledge added unexpected value to the experience. **Pro tip:** Be specific about your desired spice level—the kitchen takes these requests seriously and delivers accordingly. This hidden gem, discovered through the Entertainment Book, deserves regular visits and recommendations to colleagues seeking quality Thai cuisine near the workplace.

A Lavish Splurge With Mixed Results When spontaneity meets fine dining in Las Vegas, expectations run high—especially when celebrating a milestone birthday. Our impromptu visit to this upscale establishment delivered an evening of contrasts: stunning ambiance paired with disappointing value. **The Atmosphere** The restaurant immediately impresses with its sophisticated environment. Dimly lit interiors, statuesque hostesses, and impeccably mannered staff create an atmosphere of luxury that makes diners feel transported into high society, regardless of their actual tax bracket. The aesthetic alone justifies some excitement. **The Highlights** Ironically, the complimentary offerings outshone the main event. The tuna tartare amuse-bouche proved delicious, while the bacon and sourdough bread served with whipped butter and salt became a memorable highlight worth reminiscing about later. The table wine, selected from the more affordable options, delivered a pleasing balance of sweetness and bitterness that complemented the meal perfectly. **The Disappointments** Unfortunately, the actual entrées failed to justify their premium pricing. While the gnocchi proved reasonably priced and tasty, and both the steak and lamb demonstrated quality preparation, nothing reached extraordinary levels. Most concerning were the server's recommendations—two dishes ordered based on staff suggestions arrived literally tasteless, a significant oversight for an establishment of this caliber. **The Value Question** Herein lies the fundamental issue: exceptional pricing demands exceptional food. When complimentary items outperform expensive entrées, something's amiss. The elegant atmosphere, while pleasant, doesn't compensate for the cost-to-quality ratio. As noted, similar ambiance can be recreated with strategically placed candles at home. **Final Verdict** For special occasions requiring impressive surroundings, this restaurant delivers aesthetically. However, unless you're prepared for substantial spending with moderate culinary payoff, consider alternatives. The experience remains positive overall, but the memorable moments came from what wasn't charged—a telling commentary on this lavish establishment's priorities.

Disappointing Decline at Food Fight Corporation Location This restaurant ranks among the worst in Food Fight Corporation's portfolio. Service is frustratingly slow, and food quality has noticeably declined. The discontinued gluten-free pie options further diminish its appeal for dietary-conscious customers seeking alternatives.

Mixed Experience at Hard Rock Hotel: Great for Summer Visits, Lacking for Casino Entertainment Our stay at the Hard Rock Hotel's all-suites tower presented a decidedly mixed experience that potential guests should carefully consider before booking. ## The Positives The suite offers excellent value in terms of space, and the beds provided comfortable sleeping arrangements. The hotel truly shines in its culinary offerings—Culinary Dropout delivered an exceptional dining experience, while the 24-hour diner consistently provided quality meals. For summer visitors interested in pool activities or attending specific concerts, this property could work well. ## Significant Disappointments Despite being marketed as a new tower, our room showed troubling signs of neglect. Couches displayed prominent staining, non-functional light switches suggested poor maintenance, and the outdated iPod dock required an entire day to sync. Most problematically, the television quality was so poor that dark scenes became completely unwatchable, resulting in a movie refund. The $20 daily refrigerator fee seems excessive for a suite accommodation. ## Dead Casino Atmosphere The casino environment proved particularly disappointing. The poker room rarely had more than one table operating, yet inexplicably ran 1-3 games. The once-famous central bar sat empty, having lost its reputation as a social destination. Even during Super Bowl weekend, the property felt eerily vacant. ## Final Verdict Unless you're specifically visiting for summer pool access or a particular concert, better options exist elsewhere for gambling and entertainment variety.

A Reliable Neighborhood Gem This local Thai restaurant delivers consistently excellent food in a welcoming atmosphere. The menu offers reliable favorites like Spicy Noodle, Orange Chicken, and Cashew Chicken, while adventurous diners will find quality across all offerings. With attentive service and spotless conditions, it's become our dependable go-to spot.

Disappointing Experience at Smashburger: High Hopes, Lackluster Results After hearing numerous recommendations, I arrived at Smashburger with considerable anticipation. The restaurant's atmosphere promised something special, with an intriguing menu featuring creative flavor combinations that seemed genuinely appealing. Unfortunately, the execution fell dramatically short of expectations. I ordered a burger with pepper jack cheese, guacamole, and jalapeños on a chipotle bun—a combination that sounded absolutely delicious on paper. However, the reality was deeply disappointing: the patty was tasteless and excessively oily, with overly crispy, burnt edges from aggressive grilling. My husband's BBQ burger with fried onions suffered identical issues. The accompanying Smashfries were equally problematic—greasy and resembling overcooked frozen fries, with imperceptible rosemary seasoning. While many patrons apparently love this establishment, our experience was unfortunately subpar. Perhaps we caught them on an off day, but the overall quality didn't justify the restaurant's reputation.
