This dismissive attitude essentially blamed us for not appreciating their minimal effort. Had this been my kitchen, I would have been mortified sending such a dish to paying customers. The stark contrast with Nittaya's Secret Kitchen illustrates proper customer service. When they experienced a kitchen mixup resulting in staggered entree service, they immediately apologized, accepted responsibility, and asked how to improve the situation. They didn't deflect by claiming other diners were satisfied—they simply made it right. Every restaurant has off days. The true measure of quality lies in accountability and genuine effort to resolve problems. This establishment failed spectacularly on both counts. Had this disaster occurred earlier, we would have gladly chosen another venue for our rehearsal dinner. Consider yourself warned: accommodations promised aren't necessarily accommodations delivered. **Rating: ★☆☆☆☆**

AHHHHMAZING! That Sums It Up! Absolutely wonderful resort with outstanding service at the residence club. The staff ensures guests feel pampered and welcome, going above and beyond to guarantee happiness. The grounds are beautifully maintained, peaceful, and perfect for de-stressing and rejuvenation. The Ocotillo Grill at the residence club pool offers exceptional food and service. The fish tacos and shrimp salad are outstanding, and the agave mojito is a must-try beverage. The Four Seasons delivered a superb stay from start to finish. The combination of impeccable grounds, attentive service, and excellent dining creates an unforgettable experience that leaves guests eager to return for another visit.

Mixed Review: Monorail Has Limited Appeal While the monorail serves as a reliable transportation option during heavy traffic, this reviewer found traditional methods more practical overall. The convenience of a $5 24-hour bus pass outweighed the monorail's benefits, eliminating lengthy walks through hotels to reach stations. With affordable car rentals and complimentary hotel parking widely available, the reviewer suggests the monorail works best as a traffic-jam backup rather than a primary transportation choice in the city.

Mixed Experience with Standout Dishes at Budget-Friendly Prices This restaurant delivers exceptional value, serving a feast for three under $50. While service was friendly, it lagged in speed. The Italian wedding soup disappointed with minimal meatballs, and the pizza only impressed with its sauce. However, several items shined: the fries with gravy proved to be a favorite appetizer, while the jumbo hot wings featured generous meat portions and classic Red Hot butter sauce. The chicken parmesan sandwich stole the show as one of the best available anywhere, boasting perfectly moist chicken. The fish sandwich fell flat in comparison. Despite mixed results earning three stars overall, this establishment comes recommended for budget-conscious diners seeking decent fare—or exceptional meals if ordering the standout chicken parm sandwich.

A Once-Favorite Spot Now Marred by Poor Service This restaurant holds a special place in my heart, having been my go-to spot before moving to Ottawa. I was thrilled to discover a location near my new home upon returning. The food remains exceptional – their steak paired with a fully loaded baked potato is unbeatable, complemented perfectly by gloriously greasy garlic bread and their signature blue-jacked lemonade. However, my most recent visit was disappointingly terrible. The service issues were numerous and frustrating: an excessively long wait just to see our waiter, appetizers arriving simultaneously with entrees, and missing basic utensils. When I finally flagged down staff for a fork and knife, the delay meant my meal had already gone cold. To make matters worse, my drink sat empty, no water was offered, and shockingly, our waiter never returned to check on us. Despite the outstanding food quality, the abysmal service has driven me away. Until they address these serious staffing and service problems, I cannot recommend or return to this establishment.

Priced Out of a Good Thing This establishment does so much right that it deserves four or five stars, but there's one dealbreaker: the prices are simply too high. The coffee quality is excellent and their business strategy is sound, but the cost puts it out of reach for regular visits. If they were merely the most expensive option in town while still being accessible, this would be a frequent stop. Instead, the pricing feels exclusionary, creating an uncomfortable divide between those with ample disposable income and everyone else. Until they reconsider their pricing structure, this won't be a returning destination, despite all its other merits.

Limited Amenities but Scenic Views at Racing Event Attended WERA races on a side track away from the main speedway. Basic facilities were adequate with available bathroom access. However, cellular service was extremely poor—Verizon 3G smartphones had virtually no signal. The location offered some compensation with excellent views of Air Force base aircraft landings and the Las Vegas Strip skyline. Acceptable for racing enthusiasts willing to overlook connectivity issues.

Disappointing Compared to Other Locations We visited this restaurant taking advantage of their Cirque Du Soleil discount package, receiving $10-$15 off the all-you-can-eat rodizio per person. While the deal seemed reasonable, the experience fell short of expectations, especially when compared to the Pampas location in Palo Alto. The service style was disappointing – seafood arrived on plates rather than the traditional skewers, which detracted from the authentic rodizio experience. The side dishes were merely adequate, nothing memorable or impressive. The atmosphere and food quality suggested this venue might be better suited for a casual night out with friends rather than an intimate dinner. Overall, despite the discount making it affordable, the lackluster execution and comparison to superior locations made this a mediocre dining experience that's hard to recommend.

Disappointing Return Visit: Higher Prices, Lower Quality After giving Iruna a second chance during happy hour with friends, this restaurant continues to disappoint on multiple fronts. **Service Issues Start Early** The evening began poorly when the host claimed no outdoor seating was available without properly checking. This seemingly minor detail resulted in a $50 price difference, as indoor seating disqualified us from happy hour pricing—information not disclosed upfront. **Limited Bright Spots** The wine selection and red sangria were the only redeeming qualities of the entire experience. **Consistent Quality Problems** The food failures were numerous and concerning: - Pan con Tomato arrived missing its key ingredients (tomato, garlic, and salt), essentially serving plain bread - Spinach and goat cheese sticks came burnt, indicating basic cooking failures that even casual chains avoid - Portion sizes were minimal considering the premium prices **Poor Value Proposition** Spending over $100 for two people isn't unreasonable when the food is exceptional or the ambiance memorable. Unfortunately, Iruna delivers neither. The experience was so unsatisfying that we left hungry and continued to another restaurant. This second visit confirms the initial impression—Iruna cannot justify its pricing with its current quality standards. **Rating: ★☆☆☆☆**

A Bittersweet Farewell to 98 South The closure of 98 South left a void for those who appreciated its sophisticated atmosphere. The restaurant's dark wood accents, curated wall art, and stunning bar area created an inviting space that many patrons cherished. These aesthetic touches set 98 South apart from typical dining establishments in the area. The cheese platter proved to be a memorable culinary experience, introducing diners to exceptional varieties like Drunken Goat and St. Andre's. For cheese enthusiasts, these discoveries alone made visits worthwhile. The online menus, still accessible, showcase what could have been—tantalizing dishes that remained untried. The fish and chips, glimpsed at a neighboring table, looked particularly impressive with its beautiful presentation. However, not every experience met expectations. The Black Pearl cocktail—a mixture of Bombay Sapphire, Blue Curacao, Chambord, and sweet & sour—disappointed significantly with its medicinal Dimetapp-like taste. This misstep in mixology proved memorable for all the wrong reasons. Beyond the food and drinks, customer service shortcomings tarnished the overall experience. When a pair of Brighton tortoise-shell sunglasses went missing, management's failure to follow up demonstrated a lack of attention to guest concerns. While 98 South offered aesthetic appeal and some culinary highlights, inconsistent execution in both beverages and customer care prevented it from achieving its full potential.

Excellent Tamales with Minor Drawbacks These tamales rank among the best I've tasted. We tried pork, beef, green corn, and chicken varieties—all delicious. However, the small portion size prevents a perfect rating. Service could be friendlier at the counter. Limited operating hours are inconvenient, though the convenient location compensates. Despite these minor issues, we'll definitely return for these outstanding tamales.

Health Concerns Force Loyal Customer Away Severe food poisoning forced this devoted patron to abandon their once-beloved restaurant after a nightlong illness. The situation appears systemic, as a friend experienced similar symptoms at the downtown location, raising serious concerns about grill sanitation practices. Despite their previous affection for the establishment, safety concerns now prevent their return. This cautionary review highlights potential widespread food safety issues that others should consider before dining.

Disappointing Experience Despite Excellent Service from Albert My friends and I visited this highly-rated restaurant during our teachers conference, expecting an exceptional dining experience. Unfortunately, it fell far short of expectations. While our server Albert was outstanding—friendly, funny, and attentive—his colleague John was dismissive and rushed us through our meal before audaciously requesting a 20% tip from our party of five. The food was profoundly disappointing and overpriced, even by Vegas standards. The $50 filet lacked flavor and failed to justify its premium price point. Everything on the menu seemed excessively expensive without delivering corresponding quality. Despite Albert's commendable service, the subpar cuisine and poor treatment from other staff ensure we won't be returning to this overrated establishment.

A Brunch with High Expectations and Mixed Results When dining at a celebrity chef restaurant, expectations naturally run high. After all, these establishments trade on reputation, culinary expertise, and the promise of an exceptional experience. My recent visit to this Border Brunch left me with mixed feelings—the food was undeniably good, but it fell short of the excellence I anticipated, continuing a disappointing trend I've noticed with celebrity chef venues lately. The restaurant offers a $29.99 all-you-can-eat breakfast tapas experience, with an optional $5 upgrade for bottomless mimosas. My friends and I went for the full package. I started with an orange mimosa, which, despite my self-inflicted hangover from the previous night, proved to be well-crafted and refreshing. Under better circumstances, I'm sure I would have appreciated it even more. ## The Tapas Selection The Breakfast Enchilada delivered serious heat—perhaps too much. While the flavors were complex and interesting, the spice level was intense enough to give me heartburn right there at the table. Not exactly the gentle start to brunch I was hoping for. The Skirt Steak & Egg emerged as my second favorite dish. The steak was perfectly cooked, complemented nicely by the egg, and the accompanying guacamole added a fresh element that tied everything together. The Peruvian Shrimp & Grits presented an unexpected combination that actually worked quite well. However, I must voice a common frustration: serving shrimp covered in sauce while leaving the tails attached forces diners to fish through the dish and eat with their fingers to avoid crunching on shells. It's an unnecessary inconvenience that detracts from an otherwise enjoyable plate. The Pancakes—I can't recall their exact menu name—were essentially miniature pancakes loaded with chocolate chips. Think of them as a sugar rush delivered on a plate, perfect for those with a serious sweet tooth. ## The Clear Winner The Chorizo and Egg Tacos were, without question, the star of the show. These tacos were so good that I found myself wishing I'd simply ordered multiple plates of them instead of sampling the variety. Even now, thinking about those tacos makes me crave them. Receiving two per plate was a generous touch that didn't go unnoticed. ## The Bottom Line Despite some genuinely enjoyable dishes, the pricing feels inflated for what you receive. The brunch could easily be $5 cheaper and still represent fair value. The fact that coffee costs $8—which I reluctantly declined despite desperately wanting it—exemplifies the pricing disconnect. While the chef may have an impressive pedigree, the food doesn't quite justify these premium prices, especially considering the numerous excellent alternatives available throughout Las Vegas. Would I return? Probably only for those exceptional chorizo and egg tacos.

A Happy Hour That Leaves You Wanting More: American Fish at Aria Tucked away on the second level of the Aria, near the Zarkana theaters, American Fish presents a beautiful dining experience that unfortunately doesn't quite deliver when it comes to their happy hour offerings. While the ambiance is stunning and the quality of food is undeniable, diners should be prepared for portion sizes that leave much to be desired and prices that still feel steep, even with happy hour discounts. ## Atmosphere and Setting The restaurant's design is truly impressive, featuring one of the most striking concepts you'll find on the Las Vegas Strip. A beautiful mural of trees adorns the wall behind the bar, while a gorgeous blue ceiling creates an almost ethereal atmosphere over the dining area. The vibe strikes a balance between energetic and comfortable, with noise levels that remain pleasant, especially at the bar. However, finding the restaurant can be an adventure in itself, as it's somewhat hidden on the casino's second level – don't hesitate to ask for directions. ## The Happy Hour Experience American Fish opens at 5 PM, coinciding with the start of their happy hour. The bartender was refreshingly honest, warning guests upfront that the happy hour portions would be small. Unfortunately, "small" turned out to be an understatement. The lobster roll, which arrives as two bite-sized pieces on rectangles of bread rather than traditional crackers, barely qualifies as an appetizer despite its delicious flavor. At less than pinky-finger size, it's hard to justify the cost. The fries represent the best value on the happy hour menu, though paying $5 for French fries still feels excessive. For those feeling adventurous, the beef tartare offers an interesting experience – finely diced beef served with a bread crouton in a bowl. The standout dish, however, was the King Crab Louie: essentially refined deviled eggs with crab filling that were so good they inspired plans for home recreation. ## Value Proposition The drink specials fare slightly better than the food, though $7 cocktails aren't exactly a steal, and the selection is limited to just three specialty options. The reality is that two or three plates won't satisfy your hunger, and you'll need to adjust your budget accordingly. While the quality of ingredients and preparation is evident, the portions simply don't match the price point, even during happy hour. ## Final Verdict American Fish operates in the Aria, and the pricing reflects that premium location. If you're visiting for happy hour, come prepared to spend more than you might expect or leave feeling disappointed. The restaurant would benefit from slightly more generous portions – at least three lobster rolls per order wouldn't be unreasonable. For those willing to save up for a full dinner experience, the quality suggests it might be worthwhile. However, as a happy hour destination, American Fish falls somewhere in the middle of the pack – neither the best nor the worst Las Vegas has to offer, but certainly leaving room for improvement.

Mediocre Fare in a Pleasant Setting This establishment offers a mixed experience that ultimately falls short of memorable. While the atmosphere proves adequate with laptop-friendly seating and appealing decor, the culinary execution disappoints. A lukewarm burrito exemplifies the kitchen's lackluster performance, delivering merely edible rather than crave-worthy dishes. The service shines as the highlight, with attentive yet unobtrusive staff. The interesting location provides some redemption, but overall, this spot barely meets expectations—functional rather than exceptional.

A Disappointing Salon Experience: When Customer Service Falls Short Walking into a salon appointment should be an exciting experience, but my recent visit turned into a frustrating encounter that left me walking out empty-handed. After purchasing a Groupon and scheduling an appointment with a stylist named Jan, I arrived with high hopes that quickly deteriorated. ## Poor First Impression From the moment Jan greeted me, something felt off. Her brief "hi, I'm Jan" followed by immediately walking away as I attempted to introduce myself set an unwelcoming tone. Despite my initial reservations, I decided to proceed with the appointment, hoping the awkward introduction was just a fluke. ## Communication Breakdown Things went downhill rapidly when I showed Jan a photo of my desired hair color. She immediately mentioned additional charges, which seemed reasonable enough. However, when I politely asked for clarification on the pricing, she became noticeably offended. Her demeanor shifted from cold to outright rude, and she abruptly refused to perform the color service I wanted. ## The Final Straw My simple request to understand the total cost—considering I'd already purchased a Groupon—was met with hostility. Jan retrieved a price list but refused to provide a straightforward answer. When she began raising her voice to explain different services, I'd had enough and left. The receptionist seemed understanding when I explained the situation at the front desk, but offered no alternative appointments. While Groupon provided credit back, the entire experience was a waste of time and left me disappointed. Transparent pricing and respectful communication shouldn't be too much to expect from any business.

Disappointing Service Plan Experience - Buyer Beware I purchased a vehicle from this dealership two years ago along with a $3,000 MPP service plan covering 72 months. The salesman promised comprehensive coverage including oil changes, battery replacement, brake pads, and nearly everything else imaginable - supposedly their "top of the line plan." Unfortunately, reality has been drastically different. After bringing my car in twice over two years, absolutely nothing has been covered under this plan. Zero services. This represents either severe misrepresentation during the sales process or an essentially worthless service plan. For $3,000, I expected at least basic maintenance coverage as promised. Instead, I've received nothing but disappointment and wasted money. I will not be returning to this dealership for future purchases.

Discriminatory Pricing Practices Alleged at Local Barbershop A customer has raised serious concerns about discriminatory treatment at this establishment, claiming to have been charged $2 more than a friend for an identical haircut. The reviewer alleges a pattern of prejudice, stating that four other minority friends experienced similar pricing discrepancies. Describing the shop as both racist and homophobic, the customer expressed feeling unwelcome and undervalued. They've vowed to take their business elsewhere and, alongside affected friends, plan to alert media outlets about these alleged discriminatory practices. These accusations warrant serious attention and investigation.

Poor Customer Service Overshadows Promotional Offer This medical scrubs retailer unfortunately fails to deliver on basic customer service expectations. Despite receiving a 30% nursing appreciation coupon, the shopping experience was marred by exceptionally poor staff attitude during a second visit. The employee in question displayed unwelcoming behavior that actively discouraged purchasing. When customers feel uncomfortable entering a store and encounter unaccommodating staff, it defeats the purpose of promotional offers meant to build loyalty and drive sales. **The Bottom Line:** This location lost a potential $200+ sale due to one employee's negative attitude. For healthcare professionals seeking scrubs and medical footwear, the Russell Road location offers a more welcoming alternative. Retail success depends on staff who understand customer service basics—something this establishment desperately needs to address. Until management resolves these personnel issues, shoppers should consider other options where their business is genuinely appreciated. **Rating: ★☆☆☆☆**

**Disappointing Experience with Minimal Redeeming Qualities** This establishment falls short on multiple fronts. Service proves consistently poor, with only one cocktail waitress providing adequate attention. Food quality disappoints—most dishes are unappetizing, though wings reach acceptable standards. Free pool nights and two-star rating barely salvage an otherwise regrettable venue.

Mixed Feelings About Our Local Farmer's Market While I appreciate having a farmer's market in Arizona, the experience leaves much to be desired. The produce selection is disappointingly limited, making a supplementary grocery store trip necessary. I'm particularly surprised by the lack of citrus, peppers, and herbs—items that thrive in Arizona's climate. The pricing is another significant concern. Some meats and produce are extremely expensive, often double what you'd pay elsewhere. While I want to support local vendors, such steep markups make it difficult to justify. My typical $40-50 visit yields only a small amount of fresh produce, with most purchases being packaged items like salsa, sauces, and honey. On the positive side, the market accepts credit cards and runs efficiently. Their decision to move operations into the Scottsdale baseball stadium during summer months is smart, providing much-needed relief from Arizona's extreme heat. Overall, it's a decent option with room for improvement, particularly in produce variety and pricing competitiveness.

Beware of Hidden Fees and Misleading Information This gym operates on deceptive practices that should concern potential members. Despite advertised $9.99 memberships, customers are hit with undisclosed annual fees after being explicitly told otherwise during registration. The management issues run deep. The check-in staff handles new member registrations without proper training or knowledge of contract terms. Even more alarming, employees use other people's login credentials to process registrations—a serious security and accountability red flag. When problems arise, don't expect resolution from management. The manager deflects responsibility rather than addressing legitimate complaints about misinformation and unauthorized charges. Multiple customers report similar experiences with hidden fees and rude staff behavior. The facility's condition matches its business practices—poorly maintained and reflecting the low membership price. The positive reviews appear questionable given the consistent pattern of complaints about deceptive billing practices, inadequate staff training, and dismissive management. Save yourself the frustration and find a gym with transparent pricing, properly trained staff, and management that values honest customer relationships.

A Disappointing Dining Experience: When Friendliness Can't Save the Food It's always difficult to write a scathing review, especially when the staff is genuinely friendly and welcoming. However, honesty compels me to share my deeply disappointing experience at this Chinese restaurant, where pleasant service was unfortunately the only redeeming quality of an otherwise regrettable meal. ## The Menu: A Red Flag Upon arrival, we were presented with an unusually extensive menu for a restaurant of this size. While variety can be appealing, the sheer number of options raised immediate concerns about ingredient freshness and turnover. How could an establishment of modest proportions possibly maintain such vast inventory without relying heavily on frozen stocks? ## The Appetizers: Frozen Beginnings My suspicions were confirmed when the appetizers arrived. They were unmistakably cooked from frozen—not necessarily a dealbreaker, but certainly not confidence-inspiring. The drinks, meanwhile, carried an unpleasant rubbery taste reminiscent of tap water filtered through old tubing, though admittedly this has become disappointingly common. ## The Main Courses: A Culinary Catastrophe The real problems emerged with the main entrees. We ordered two beef dishes, chicken, and shrimp, all at typical Chinese restaurant prices. The portions appeared smaller than standard, and the presentation left much to be desired. ### The Beef: Inedible and Unidentifiable The first beef dish was genuinely the toughest, most gristle-laden meat I've encountered. No utensil—fork, knife, or even determined teeth—could properly break it down. Each piece required several minutes of cutting and another ten of relentless chewing just to swallow. I'm not exaggerating when I say that aged beef jerky would have been more tender. My dining companion actually felt ill after consuming the second beef dish, which, while softer, lacked any recognizable beef flavor and was of questionable quality. ### The Chicken: Best of the Worst The chicken, consisting entirely of dark meat, was subpar in both appearance and taste. However, compared to the disastrous beef options, it was relatively the "best" dish—a low bar indeed. ### The Shrimp: Unpleasant Details The shrimp came with its digestive tract completely intact—an unappetizing oversight that any respectable kitchen should avoid. ## The Aftermath The meal's effects lingered long after we left, manifesting as severe stomach cramps and a persistent foul taste that no amount of brushing or rinsing could eliminate. This physical discomfort was perhaps the most concerning aspect of the entire experience. ## Final Verdict Despite the genuinely friendly staff, I cannot recommend this restaurant. The quality of ingredients appears severely compromised, with what seems to be the cheapest possible cuts of meat and frozen components dominating the menu. While I'm certain they must excel at something, our ordering managed to completely miss it. The positive reviews elsewhere truly baffle me—perhaps we caught them on an exceptionally bad day, or perhaps standards vary wildly. Regardless, this was a meal that stuck with me for all the wrong reasons.

Frustrating Pre-Flight Dining Disaster This airport location delivers an absolutely unacceptable experience. Despite the restaurant being only quarter-full at 6am Monday, service was painfully slow: 10 minutes for seating, another 10 at the bar before being served, and 20 more until food arrived—right when boarding began. Completely missed my meal due to poor management and glacial service. Avoid this location entirely.

Disappointing Service Mars Otherwise Pleasant Shopping Experience As a self-proclaimed Juicy Couture enthusiast, I was initially pleased when a friendly brunette greeted my fiancée and me upon entering the store. We browsed comfortably for about an hour, ultimately purchasing a necklace and headband. However, our positive experience was completely ruined as we were leaving. Another staff member made an incredibly rude comment about us "FINALLY leaving," which was both unprofessional and offensive. While I chose to ignore the remark to avoid escalation, my fiancé was understandably upset. I've since contacted corporate to report this incident. It's unfortunate that one employee's poor behavior can tarnish an otherwise enjoyable shopping trip. Such unprofessionalism has no place in retail.

A Mixed Experience: Great Food Marred by Poor Service Our party of four opted for the $100 prix fixe dinner, hoping for a memorable evening. The experience proved to be frustratingly inconsistent, with some culinary highlights overshadowed by significant service failures. ## The Highs The meal began promisingly with an excellent bread basket featuring delicious pretzel bread. The edamame appetizer was exceptional—quite possibly the best I've ever tasted. Our side of mac and cheese was also excellent, delivering comfort food executed at a high level. The dessert, a playful "junk food" creation dominated by cotton candy, made for an attractive presentation and fun conclusion. ## The Lows Unfortunately, several issues detracted from the experience. My wife's fish dish had such unappealing presentation that it's surprising she finished it. My chicken curry arrived in a soup bowl with considerable broth, requiring a spoon. After the waiter mentioned this need, he vanished completely. This began a frustrating saga: no server appeared for over ten minutes, forcing me to request a spoon at the bar. The first attempt yielded an inappropriately small teaspoon and an apology. Another ten minutes passed before a proper tablespoon arrived. Throughout the evening, basic service elements failed—we couldn't even get water refills. ## Final Verdict While certain dishes showcased genuine culinary talent, the abysmal service made this $100-per-person meal (before tax and tip) thoroughly unenjoyable. Las Vegas offers countless exceptional dining experiences with attentive service. Given the competition and this disappointing performance, there's simply no compelling reason to return.

**Disappointing Service Overshadows Quality Inventory** While this vintage modern showroom boasts stunning furnishings and an impressive collection of mid-century pieces, the experience is marred by the owner's rude and indifferent attitude. At premium prices, customers deserve exceptional service. With friendlier mid-century shops available elsewhere in town, it's difficult to recommend this establishment despite its quality inventory.

A Year Later, Still Missing the Mark Returning after a full year, I hoped for improvement, but unfortunately my experience remained lackluster. Arriving on a Wednesday at 11pm, we discovered the kitchen was already closed—disappointing for a venue known for late-night dining. While the atmosphere had its moments with a cozy fireplace and an excellent music selection, the execution fell short where it mattered most. Our server was pleasant and attentive, but the drinks were severely watered down. Serving cocktails in pint glasses only emphasized the dilution problem, making them practically undrinkable. This marks two visits with consistently poor cocktail quality. For an establishment that should excel at bar service, these repeated failures are concerning. Unless significant improvements are made to their beverage program and kitchen hours, I likely won't return for drinks. The ambiance alone can't compensate for such fundamental shortcomings.

A Solid Happy Hour Destination with Great Value Kona Grill has become our go-to spot for happy hour, and after multiple visits, it's clear why this place attracts consistent crowds. Their generous happy hour schedule—running weekdays from 3-7 PM and 10 PM-midnight, Saturday afternoons, and all day Sunday—makes it accessible for various schedules, though this convenience means you'll often find the place packed, especially during post-work hours on weekdays. **The Value Proposition** The happy hour pricing is genuinely impressive, featuring half-off appetizers, select items for $6, and discounted drinks. This competitive pricing, combined with quality food and pleasant ambiance, creates an attractive package. The service manages to remain decent despite the constant rush, which deserves recognition. **Menu Highlights and Misses** While the sushi selection is adequate, it won't blow you away. The Wave Roll offers refreshing flavors, though the $6 price point feels slightly steep. The Crab Crunch stands out as another worthwhile option, but overall, sushi enthusiasts seeking exceptional rolls should visit a dedicated Japanese restaurant. The real star is the two-burgers-for-$6 deal. These smaller-sized burgers feature high-quality meat and excellent toppings, accompanied by fries. This has become my consistent order and represents outstanding value. Other appetizers prove hit-or-miss. The potstickers disappointed with their loose, poorly-bound meat, though others in my group enjoyed them. The lettuce wraps and calamari both deliver solid performances—everything falls into the "pretty good" category rather than extraordinary. **Final Verdict** Kona Grill excels as a happy hour destination, ranking among the most generous establishments in terms of both specials and timing. While nothing reaches "OMG" status, the consistent quality, reasonable prices, and extensive happy hour windows make it worth repeated visits. Just arrive early or be prepared to grab seats at the sushi bar during peak times.

I'd Skip It: A Disappointing Casino Dining Experience This establishment fails on multiple fronts. Despite being a quick-service venue, expect significant waits. The menu lacks any healthy options whatsoever, forcing diners into 2000-calorie meals regardless of selection. Adding insult to injury, you'll endure secondhand smoke throughout your meal—an unpleasant atmosphere that diminishes any enjoyment. Surprisingly, prices aren't competitive either. One would expect casino eateries to offer value, keeping patrons gambling longer, but this venue defies that logic with overpriced offerings. Between the lengthy waits, unhealthy fare, smoky environment, and inflated prices, there's simply no reason to dine here.

Meh...just meh. This Outback Steakhouse-style franchise delivers exactly what you'd expect: consistency without much excitement. Despite being in Matthews, NC, the place was surprisingly packed on a Friday night at 8:30pm with a 20-minute wait—unusual for the area. The food proved hit-or-miss. My NY strip arrived cooked perfectly to medium specification, juicy and satisfying. However, my girlfriend's Dallas Filet disappointed with unexpected fattiness—a real problem for a cut that should be lean. She also disliked the bacon-infused green beans, though personally, I'm always on board with bacon in any form. The service was competent and attentive throughout our meal. Overall, this is a reliable but unremarkable dining option. The food quality sits squarely in average territory—nothing offensive, nothing memorable. While I wouldn't rule out returning, it's definitely not somewhere I'm rushing back to anytime soon. If you're looking for a safe, predictable steakhouse experience, this fits the bill perfectly.

Exquisite French Dining at La Porte Restaurant La Porte delivers an exceptional contemporary French experience under Chef Thierry Rouyé's masterful direction. The eight-course tasting menu ($90) represents extraordinary value, featuring impeccably presented dishes that feel truly decadent. Highlights include an innovative cod emulsion with scallops and blood sausage, luxurious foie gras paired with a whimsical potato foam shot, perfectly executed squab, and an elegant blue cheese roulade accompanied by wine-braised pear. Beyond the inspired cuisine, the hospitality elevates the experience considerably. Pascale, the chef's wife, manages the front of house with grace and attentiveness that makes guests feel genuinely spoiled. La Porte successfully combines culinary artistry with warm, personalized service—a rare combination that makes this restaurant a standout destination for refined French dining.

A Breakfast Gem Worth the Crowd Where do I start? I'm in love with this restaurant for breakfast, and here's why you should be too. Don't let the crowds fool you. While there are always plenty of people waiting, the turnover is remarkably efficient. I've never waited longer than 15-20 minutes, even during peak hours. So don't just drive by thinking it's too crowded—it's absolutely worth stopping. What makes this place exceptional is the staff. Despite the constant rush, service never falters. The host managing the waiting list runs operations like a well-oiled machine, and every waiter and waitress I've encountered has been polite and attentive. The kitchen somehow handles the volume without compromising quality or speed—food arrives hot, fresh, and fast. This has become my go-to spot for out-of-town guests, and every single one has fallen in love with it. Between the efficient service, friendly atmosphere, and consistently delicious food, this breakfast spot has earned its popularity. It's a rare find that lives up to the hype.

Disappointing Visit Marred by Multiple Service Failures This establishment fails to deliver despite premium pricing. Upon arrival, customers encounter a sweltering environment without functioning air conditioning—unacceptable given the cost. The beverage situation proves equally frustrating: the soda machine is out of order, and while tea remains available, the ice machine is also broken. Staff offer only apologies without compensation or refunds for the subpar service. Being forced to consume hot "iced" tea in an uncomfortably warm dining room while waiting for food creates an entirely unsatisfactory experience that doesn't warrant a return visit.

A Disappointing Dining Experience: Proceed with Caution This restaurant falls dramatically short of expectations, particularly given its surprisingly positive reviews. During our visit a couple years ago, multiple aspects of the meal were severely underwhelming. The pricing was excessive considering the quality received. The food itself was disappointingly mushy and bland, reminiscent of subpar institutional dining. When the bread becomes the highlight of your meal, something has gone seriously wrong. The salads were particularly uninspired—essentially just iceberg lettuce with minimal toppings. Most telling was my fiancé's reaction. He's typically not picky and will eat practically anything, yet when our server inquired about the meal, he could only manage an unenthusiastic "eh." That speaks volumes. For comparison, I'd choose The Olive Garden ten times over this establishment, despite not being particularly fond of it either. The area offers far superior dining options like North, Chelsea's Kitchen, and Los Sombreros that provide much better value and quality. Save your money and choose literally any alternative venue. If the system allowed zero stars, that would be my rating.

Disappointing Experience at Vietnamese Spot I really wanted to like this place, but unfortunately, it fell short of expectations. I ordered the banh mi and a vermicelli plate with grilled meat and egg rolls, and both were just mediocre at best. The banh mi was particularly disappointing compared to Lee's Sandwiches—the bread was too dense and resembled a sub roll rather than a proper baguette. While the pricing seemed fair for comparable establishments, the quality simply wasn't there. Adding to the disappointment, the neighborhood felt sketchy. Visiting on a weekday afternoon around 3pm, I encountered some strange characters loitering out front, which made the experience uncomfortable. Perhaps the pho is better, but based on what I tried, I can't recommend this place. There are better Vietnamese options elsewhere.

A Taste of Louisiana in Pittsburgh: Authentic Cajun Cuisine Worth Discovering As a Louisiana native transplanted to Pittsburgh, finding authentic Cajun food has been nearly impossible—until now. This restaurant was a welcome surprise that actually delivers on its promise of genuine Louisiana flavors. ## The Food: Outstanding and Authentic The cuisine here is genuinely delicious and reminiscent of home cooking from Louisiana. The chef deserves special recognition for being accommodating and helpful with special requests. What started as a simple inquiry turned into an entire meal that was an amazingly delicious experience, capturing the authentic taste of Louisiana that's so rare in this region. ## Areas for Improvement Unfortunately, the dining experience had some significant shortcomings. The bartender's Hurricane cocktail was the oddest version I've encountered—it seemed they weren't familiar with the proper preparation. More concerning was the service quality. Our waitress appeared unfamiliar with the menu, serving us an étouffée tasting without the accompanying rice and failing to check back on us. We ended up eating it improperly, which diminished what was otherwise good food. ## Final Thoughts For a restaurant serving cuisine unfamiliar to most Pittsburgh residents, having knowledgeable servers is crucial. As someone in the service industry, these gaps in service were disappointing. However, the exceptional food quality and the chef's dedication make this place worth visiting despite the service issues.

Pizza Bonati Crafton: A Two-Hour Wait for Cold Pizza **When "Fast Food" Takes Forever** Pizza Bonati's Crafton location turned what should have been a simple dinner order into a frustrating two-hour ordeal that revealed serious problems with their service standards and customer care philosophy. **The Timeline of Disappointment** Ordering at 7:20 PM with a promised 30-40 minute delivery, the experience quickly deteriorated. After an hour passed without delivery, attempts to contact the restaurant proved futile—the phone simply rang endlessly with no answer. Even calling their sister location in Bellevue yielded no assistance, with staff showing complete indifference to the situation. The inability to reach anyone meant there was no way to cancel the order or get updates. Customers were left in limbo, unable to make alternative dinner arrangements while waiting for food that may or may not arrive. **The Final Insult** When the pizza finally arrived at 9:20 PM—a full two hours late—the delivery came with no apology, no explanation, and no discount. Worse yet, the pizza arrived cold with warm soda, suggesting it had been sitting somewhere for an extended period. **The Bigger Problem** The complete absence of any attempt to compensate for the terrible service suggests this isn't an isolated incident but rather an accepted standard of operation. Quality establishments recognize service failures and make amends; Pizza Bonati showed no such concern. **The Bottom Line** Even under ideal circumstances, the food quality barely justifies a normal delivery time. Combined with unreliable service, unanswered phones, and zero accountability, Pizza Bonati Crafton simply isn't worth the risk. Numerous better options exist in the Robinson area that actually value their customers' time and money.

Mixed Experience at Strip Nightclub - VIP Treatment Saves the Day This Las Vegas nightclub appears to be struggling with attendance, as evidenced by our Friday night visit with complimentary VIP service. Despite the sparse crowd, the venue offers some redeeming qualities worth noting. The club features two distinct areas: a terrace with stunning Strip views and an interior nightclub with dance floor. The terrace stands out as the highlight, offering breathtaking panoramas and live weekend entertainment. While the overall atmosphere suffered from low attendance, our VIP bottle service experience was exceptional. The dance floor provides solid entertainment with an excellent music variety—we were fortunate to experience celebrity guest DJ Flavor Flav, who delivered an impressive set. **Bottom Line:** If you have the budget, bottle service and VIP access transform this venue into an authentic Strip nightlife experience. However, without these premium perks, the sparse crowds might disappoint. The spectacular terrace views alone make it worth considering for those seeking Instagram-worthy moments.

A Hidden BBQ Gem Worth Discovering Sometimes the best restaurants are the ones we almost overlook. This BBQ establishment, despite its long-standing presence in the neighborhood, easily blends into the background with its cliche diner appearance. Many passersby might not even realize it specializes in award-winning barbecue until they dig deeper. ## Atmosphere and Accolades Upon entering, visitors are greeted by an interesting pink color scheme that cleverly complements the pig theme throughout. The walls showcase numerous awards from Thee Pitts Again, testament to the restaurant's BBQ credentials and giving diners confidence they're in capable hands. ## Menu Highlights and Misses The smoked wings appetizer stands out as a must-order item. These wings deliver exceptional flavor, though requesting sauce on the side allows the natural smokiness to shine through rather than being overwhelmed. **Important note for those with gluten sensitivities**: exercise caution with the BBQ sauce, as it may contain problematic ingredients. The pulled pork sandwich earns high marks for its juicy, smoky qualities with appealing fattiness. However, the brisket proves somewhat disappointing—notably dry without sauce accompaniment. On the brighter side, the grilled vegetables provide an excellent alternative to traditional sides, and the Miss Piggy Ice Cream Soda, while pricey, delivers memorable flavor. ## A Disappointing Decision One frustrating aspect involves their discontinued rattlesnake BBQ. Despite advertising this specialty "when in season," the restaurant no longer offers it due to complaints from offended customers. This decision to eliminate a unique menu item rather than simply allowing personal choice seems unnecessarily restrictive. ## Final Verdict Despite minor disappointments, this BBQ joint delivers quality food worth experiencing. The combination of award-winning meats, unique offerings, and standout appetizers makes it worthy of return visits. Just manage expectations accordingly and don't hesitate to customize your order.

**Consistently Perfect Pizza with Room for Growth** This pizzeria has clearly hit its stride, with early operational issues now resolved and pizzas coming out flawlessly. The decor surpasses their Eastern location, creating an appealing atmosphere. However, there's potential for elevation: menu rotation like a weekly pizza special would add excitement, while upgrading from generic gelato to Art of Flavor or house-made options would enhance desserts. Most notably, replacing plastic plates with ceramic would better match the quality food and prevent the awkward steak knife situation. Despite these minor critiques, the reviewer maintains genuine affection for Novecento and its improved offerings.

Terrible Customer Service and Overpriced This establishment attempts to overcharge customers at every opportunity. Staff members are condescending and argumentative, demonstrating no understanding of proper customer service. The experience was a complete waste of both time and money. The disrespectful treatment and inflated prices make this business absolutely not worth visiting. Save yourself the frustration and avoid this place entirely.

**Great Spot with Minor Flaws** This restaurant offers an enjoyable dining experience with solid food and excellent drink specials. While my grilled wings were slightly overcooked, my boyfriend's grilled cheese burger was delicious. The happy hour is fantastic, featuring an impressive bourbon selection from local distilleries, with $3 bourbons on Wednesdays. The neat atmosphere and quality drinks make this a place worth revisiting soon.

Hidden Gem for Japanese Goods in Las Vegas This compact store impressively stocks a wide variety of Japanese products, defying expectations for its size. While prices run slightly higher than comparable California locations, it's understandable given the market. For locals, this would easily become a go-to destination. Having experience with similar stores in San Francisco's Japantown, San Gabriel, and Little Tokyo, the product selection here is remarkably comparable despite less competition. The merchandise quality and variety match what you'd find in these established Japanese shopping districts. Pro tip: Don't miss Caked directly across the street to complete your visit to this excellent shopping spot.

Standing in Line at Jean Philippe: A Pastry Lover's Dream Worth the Wait When you spot the snaking line at Jean Philippe Patisserie in the Bellagio, your first instinct might be to keep walking. But here's the verdict after personal experience: absolutely join that queue. This isn't just hype—it's genuinely worth every minute of waiting. ## The Experience Arriving around 11:00 AM on a weekday proved to be perfect timing. The line, while substantial, moves surprisingly quickly as it winds past beautiful display counters. Everything is clearly labeled, giving you ample time to plan your order before reaching the counter. This late-morning sweet spot often features the shortest wait times of the day. ## The Star Attraction While Bouchon Bakery's Almond Brioche has earned its stellar reputation, Jean Philippe's version deserves the crown. After conducting thorough "research" at both establishments, Jean Philippe's rendition stands as the absolute best—ever. The quality and execution are simply unmatched. ## Important Considerations The Bellagio location does have notable limitations. Seating is extremely scarce, with only a handful of tables scattered throughout the casino concourse. Expect to wander around hoping to claim a spot, though fellow pastry enthusiasts are generally willing to share tables. Wheelchair accessibility, while possible, presents challenges given the cramped layout and winding queue. ## The Alternative For those seeking a more comfortable experience, the City Center location reportedly offers identical pastries with significantly better seating and accessibility. This makes it an attractive option for groups or anyone requiring special accommodations. ## Bottom Line Despite the crowds and seating challenges, Jean Philippe Patisserie delivers on its promise. Whether you choose the Bellagio or City Center location, make the stop. Sometimes the best things in Las Vegas really do require a little patience—and this is definitely one of those times.

Convenient Late-Night Spot with Quality Food This restaurant is perfect for those working late hours, staying open late and welcoming customers even five minutes before closing. The food quality exceeds typical budget Chinese/Asian establishments. Staff are helpful with recommendations when asked. The chicken fried rice is particularly noteworthy and worth ordering as a go-to choice.

A Shocking Display of Poor Customer Service and Unprofessionalism I'm not one to complain, but my recent experiences at Paulene's salon compelled me to create a Yelp account specifically to share this warning. I am absolutely disgusted by the way this establishment conducts business, particularly given my history as a loyal customer. For quite some time, I've been a regular client at Paulene's, even referring friends and purchasing gift certificates. Unfortunately, my loyalty has been met with consistently poor service and inexcusably rude treatment. ## Repeated Quality Issues My problems began when my gel manicures started peeling off just days after application – not once, but twice. Most recently, a technician used what appeared to be a stale bottle of gel polish, resulting in thick, uneven coverage. Her solution to "fix" the problem was bizarre: applying regular nail polish over the gel. Anyone familiar with gel manicures knows this peels off almost immediately. True to form, the polish began peeling within 48 hours. When I returned as the technician had insisted, she redid my nails with a fresh bottle in a similar color. I offered to pay for this service, but she refused payment beyond an additional tip (despite my having already tipped 20% two days earlier). ## The Final Straw Today's appointment was the absolute last straw. My nail technician (who sits in the front far left corner) was rude from the moment I sat down, refusing even to respond when I asked how her day was. When I politely requested an additional swipe of top coat on one nail, she became argumentative. Then came the shocking part: she actually *screamed* at me, claiming I had demanded a "new color" during my previous visit (a complete misrepresentation of events). She suggested I stick to regular polish so I could change colors myself – essentially telling a paying customer to do it herself. I firmly but professionally told her that as a paying client who tips generously, I expect quality service. I also informed her I would never return. The woman receiving a pedicure next to me was so appalled by what she witnessed that she waited outside to speak with me, applauding me for standing up for myself. Something tells me Paulene's lost two customers that day.

**Outdated Theater Only Worth It for Discount Matinees** This AMC location survives solely on its $6 matinee pricing, as virtually everything else about the experience falls short. The facility shows its age with rundown features and inadequate cleaning, particularly noticeable in the bathrooms. Concession prices remain steep at $6 for a small popcorn, which is disappointingly served from pre-bagged bulk storage kept lukewarm under heat lamps rather than freshly popped. Safety concerns arise during winter months, with minimal snow and ice removal beyond the immediate entrance. Staff responsiveness to hazards appears lacking, with icy sidewalks going unaddressed despite patron complaints. For a superior movie-going experience, Marcus Point Cinema on the west side offers significantly better facilities, cleanliness, and overall value, making it the clearly preferable choice for anything beyond budget-conscious matinee screenings.

Average Vietnamese Fare Falls Short of California Standards As a California native familiar with authentic Vietnamese cuisine, this restaurant proved disappointing. While the lime-infused water was a pleasant touch, the food itself was merely average at best. Nothing memorable or exceptional about the dishes. Overall experience: underwhelming and forgettable.

Fukuburger: A Food Truck Revolution Worth Following Fukuburger represents everything the modern food truck movement has achieved in transforming public perception of mobile kitchens. Gone are the days when food trucks were dismissed as questionable "roach coaches." Today, establishments like Fukuburger command almost cult-like devotion, and for good reason. What sets Fukuburger apart is their innovative Asian-Pacific Island fusion menu and remarkable consistency in execution. After numerous visits sampling their entire burger lineup, standouts include the'Kinoko' mushroom burger and the signature'Fuku-Burger' (lucky burger). However, the true star is the Nagadog—an absolute must-order that redefines what a hot dog can be. The Nagadog achieves perfection through its carefully balanced components: the satisfying snap of hot-link sausage, creamy wasabi mayo, and the tangy crunch of kimchi. It's arguably the finest hot dog available anywhere. Beyond burgers and dogs, Fukuburger offers heartier fare like the'Loco Moco' and'Naga Moco'—comfort food dishes featuring either hamburger patty or hot-link sausage atop rice, crowned with a fried egg and savory gravy. These warming meals are perfect for cooler weather. Fukuburger's success stems from their commitment to unique, well-executed offerings that keep customers returning. They've proven that food trucks can deliver restaurant-quality experiences, building a loyal following that continues to grow. This isn't just a food truck—it's a destination.

Efficient Layout, But Overwhelming Crowds Jet operates on an unconventional schedule, opening only Friday, Saturday, and Monday nights. The venue features a strategic design clearly optimized for maximum alcohol service. The main room boasts a massive rectangular layout with bars running the entire length on both sides, while bottle service tables bookend a central dance floor in the middle section. A back room offers additional relief with its own bar, smaller dance floor, and more bottle service options—potentially your best bet for actually getting a drink. However, Monday's Industry Night presents a serious problem: overcrowding. Despite limited Monday nightlife alternatives elsewhere, Jet becomes uncomfortably packed, making it difficult to move or enjoy yourself. While the layout is efficient in theory, the excessive crowds undermine the experience considerably.

**Great Pool, But Hotel Falls Short** Chose this venue for our wedding, but left disappointed. Staff was rude and restaurants grossly overpriced, even by Vegas standards. We escaped to the Mirage next door most of our stay. The one redeeming feature? The pool was genuinely excellent. Expected better overall.

Disappointing Service Overshadows Quality Selection While Sur La Table offers an impressive product selection that warranted a return visit for cutting boards, the customer service experience was deeply troubling. Being ignored, constantly interrupted, and treated poorly by staff falls far below acceptable retail standards, especially in Pittsburgh's typically friendly service environment. The stark contrast with competitors like Williams Sonoma and In the Kitchen highlights how poor service can drive customers away despite quality merchandise. When shoppers are willing to endure traffic and parking challenges rather than return to a conveniently located store, it signals a serious service problem. Sur La Table must address staff training and customer interaction protocols. Even excellent products cannot compensate for consistently negative interpersonal experiences that leave customers feeling disrespected and undervalued.

DirecTV Review: Convenience Issues and Contract Concerns Override Technical Features Having experienced DirecTV both previously and currently, I feel compelled to share an honest assessment of their service. While the technology has its merits, several operational frustrations significantly impact the overall user experience. ## Contract and Pricing Transparency The most significant concern involves DirecTV's contract structure. They lock customers into agreements that seem reasonable initially, but prices increase substantially when contracts expire. This information exists in the fine print, making it easy to overlook. Potential subscribers should carefully review contract terms before committing. ## Genie System Performance The new Genie receiver offers modern features but exhibits noticeable performance issues. Remote control response time lags considerably, creating frustrating delays during navigation. The search functionality proves particularly disappointing, struggling to locate shows scheduled a month or more in advance. Comparatively, Dish Network's equipment responds more quickly and searches more effectively. ## System Dependencies and Reliability A critical design flaw involves the slave units in secondary rooms requiring the main unit to operate continuously. Even for basic television viewing without accessing recorded content, the entire system depends on the main receiver remaining powered and functional. This creates unnecessary electricity consumption and complications during simple activities like room painting. My experience relocating the main unit illustrated these reliability concerns. After moving it, signal acquisition failed completely, necessitating a technician visit. After testing three different boxes and ninety minutes of troubleshooting, the system inexplicably began working without clear resolution. ## Customer Service Limitations Account management proves unnecessarily cumbersome. Adding or removing programming requires phone calls rather than simple website transactions—a stark contrast to Dish Network's convenient online management. Even more frustrating, the automated phone system cannot complete these changes, ultimately requiring representative interaction anyway. ## Signal Quality Claims DirecTV representatives claim superior signal reliability during storms, particularly monsoons. However, previous experience contradicted these assertions, with regular weather-related interruptions. Whether improvements have been implemented remains to be seen. **Overall assessment:** While DirecTV provides adequate service, operational inconveniences and transparency issues warrant careful consideration before subscribing.

A Solid Neighborhood Watering Hole Without the Frills Nestled on North Davidson Street, this NoDa establishment embodies the essence of what a straightforward neighborhood bar should be. From the moment you enter, the layout reveals itself completely: a clear sightline travels from the interior bar through the back door, past the patio bar, and onto an expansive deck adorned with beer signage and cornhole boards. The dimly lit interior maintains its cave-like atmosphere regardless of the time of day, requiring a brief adjustment period when transitioning back to sunlight after a few rounds. This characteristic darkness contributes to the bar's unpretentious ambiance. One notable improvement since North Carolina's smoking ban has been the absence of that lingering cigarette smell that once required immediate wardrobe fumigation. The cleaner air has undoubtedly enhanced the overall experience. **Food and Entertainment** The menu features predictable bar fare without attempting culinary innovation: sandwiches named after local streets, mountainous nacho platters, various burgers, cheesesteaks, and tater tots. The real advantage lies in the kitchen's extended hours, matching the bar's operation times. Those late-night tot baskets prove invaluable when wrapping up an evening of neighborhood drinking. Sports enthusiasts will appreciate the nearly dozen televisions scattered throughout both indoor and outdoor spaces, making this the closest approximation to a sports bar within the arts district. Gaming options include a PlayStation 3 positioned at the bar's end, where patrons can showcase their Modern Warfare skills to an appreciative (or inebriated) audience. **The Verdict** Standard amenities round out the offerings: an internet jukebox streaming Pandora until someone selects specific tracks, an ATM, and the obligatory Golden Tee and Buck Hunter games tucked in the corner. This establishment makes no pretensions about being extraordinary. There are no signature cocktails, revolutionary menu items, or elaborate themes. It's simply a bar—and sometimes that's precisely what's needed. A reliable spot delivering consistent mediocrity in the best possible way.

A Pleasant Korean BBQ Experience with Standout Service My inaugural visit to Woonam Jung left a positive impression, particularly regarding the atmosphere and service quality. The staff's friendly and attentive demeanor was refreshing—it's genuinely uncommon to encounter smiling faces at Korean restaurants, which made the experience more welcoming. The food quality aligned with standard Korean barbecue expectations. While most dishes were satisfactory, the purple Korean rice (likely black/forbidden rice) was a delightful surprise. Its sticky texture and subtle nutty flavor elevated an otherwise ordinary side dish request. Portions proved generous for our party of three hungry diners. We sampled various meats including pork and galbi, accompanied by ample banchan (side dishes). The $80 total for three people represents fair pricing for non-AYCE Korean barbecue. Overall, Woonam Jung delivers solid Korean BBQ with notably superior customer service, making it worth a visit.

A Birthday Dinner Marred by Poor Service Despite Excellent Food My highly anticipated first visit to this restaurant turned into a bittersweet experience that I feel compelled to share. After months of wanting to visit and being surprised by my girlfriend for my birthday, what should have been a memorable celebration became memorable for all the wrong reasons. ## The Food: Outstanding Quality Let me start with the positives—the food was genuinely amazing. I finally got to try the Wellington I'd been craving since watching it on The F Word years ago, and it lived up to every expectation. The quality and preparation were flawless, and my girlfriend's spare ribs were equally impressive. Christina from Hell's Kitchen deserves recognition for the exceptional culinary execution. The kitchen clearly knows what they're doing. ## The Service: Disappointing and Dismissive Unfortunately, our server Chris completely overshadowed the excellent food with condescending and inattentive service. The problems began immediately when we declined cocktails—I was driving, and my girlfriend wasn't in the mood to drink. From that moment, his attitude shifted noticeably. What particularly stung was watching Chris ask every other table in his section if they were celebrating a special occasion, while completely skipping us. I only received a perfunctory acknowledgment after pointing out this discrepancy to neighboring diners within his earshot. The congratulations that followed felt forced and insincere. The order mix-up was another frustrating moment. Chris delivered my Wellington to my girlfriend and her ribs to me, then insisted we had ordered incorrectly when we switched plates in front of him. I'm certain about what I ordered—it was the dish I'd been anticipating for months. The most egregious issue came after we finished eating. With completely clean plates, Chris walked past our table six times—yes, I counted—without checking on us or clearing our table. When I finally had to interrupt him to request the dessert menu, he claimed he thought we were "still working on our meal." How could he possibly think that with empty plates sitting there? By the time he finally cleared our table, we'd lost our appetite for dessert. The magic of the evening had evaporated. ## A Pattern Worth Noting I couldn't help but notice that our neighbors who ordered cocktails and wine received attentive, pleasant service throughout their meal. The contrast was stark and disappointing. ## Final Thoughts I never imagined writing a negative review, especially about a restaurant connected to Gordon Ramsay's shows, which I've enthusiastically followed and discussed with friends. While the food deserves five stars, the service experience has left me uncertain about returning—which breaks my heart given my longtime admiration for Chef Ramsay's work.

Disappointing Dining Experience at Overpriced Establishment This restaurant proved to be a letdown on every front. After our first choice was closed, we hoped for better but were met with uninspired cuisine, lackluster service, and forgettable atmosphere. The menu offerings were shockingly unimaginative. The buffalo chicken salad consisted merely of four boneless chicken pieces on basic iceberg lettuce—hardly worthy of restaurant pricing. Salads offer endless creative possibilities, yet this one fell completely flat. My turkey melt was equally unremarkable and forgettable. Given its location in an upscale neighborhood and status as a newer establishment, expectations were considerably higher. Unfortunately, the reality was boring, overpriced fare that failed to satisfy. For those seeking standard food without the premium markup, Culvers offers better value. This restaurant feels more like an overpriced cafeteria than a destination worth visiting.

Disappointing Vegan Experience Despite Good Intentions While I appreciate having vegan options available, especially in an area where plant-based restaurants are scarce, my experience here was unfortunately terrible. Despite having a generous budget that allowed me to sample extensively, nearly everything disappointed. The chili was merely acceptable, but the vegan chicken nuggets were flavorless and had an unpleasant, tough texture. The "chicken" wings arrived oddly presented on sticks, were badly burned, and difficult to eat. The avocado salad was passable, though that's hardly impressive given salad's simplicity. The southern plate was the absolute worst—I managed only one bite of the mac and cheese and collard greens before discarding everything. It was genuinely inedible. I genuinely want vegan establishments to succeed, particularly in the South where plant-based dining remains limited. However, this restaurant desperately needs to improve its food quality to demonstrate how delicious vegan cuisine can truly be. Better execution would serve both customers and the vegan movement far better.

Quick Bite with Great Service at Shibuya Our large group needed last-minute seating, and Shibuya came through beautifully. The tasting menu impressed us across the board, with standout kampachi sashimi that was absolutely delicious. The kitchen graciously accommodated dietary requests, substituting soy wrappers for seaweed without hesitation or extra charges. Our servers were attentive and friendly throughout. The only disappointment was the winter menu's beef dish, which arrived cold and lacked tenderness. Despite this minor setback, the overall experience was excellent, and we'd definitely return for another visit.

A Costly Disappointment: Surveillance Camera Installation Gone Wrong I recently paid $600 for surveillance camera installation, and it turned into an absolute nightmare. The experience was so poor that I feel compelled to warn others about this service. The installation team arrived unprepared and immediately created problems. They drilled numerous unnecessary holes throughout my walls, leaving my home damaged. Most concerning was their refusal to mount the cameras properly along the roofline of my two-story home. Their excuse? They didn't have ladders tall enough to reach the appropriate height. The result was embarrassingly tacky: black wires running across the middle of my house at a reachable level, making the cameras vulnerable to tampering. Anyone could easily pull down both the cameras and wiring—completely defeating the purpose of a security system. When I contacted management to complain, they took days to process my refund and flatly refused to repair the holes their team had created in my walls. This unacceptable response has left me considering legal action. If you own a two-story home and need surveillance camera installation, avoid this service entirely. The lack of proper equipment, poor workmanship, and refusal to take responsibility for damages make them unreliable. Instead, invest in a professional service that has appropriate equipment and stands behind their work. Don't make my expensive mistake.

Mixed Experience: Great Atmosphere, Questionable Food and Service This establishment offers a genuinely appealing happy hour and an impressive patio space that initially draws you in. However, the dining experience quickly deteriorates from there. The turkey burger, despite being enthusiastically recommended by our server, was a major disappointment. Rather than the promised exceptional quality, it tasted questionable enough to raise concerns about ingredient freshness. The overly eager recommendation felt suspiciously like an attempt to move inventory. The most shocking incident involved our table's nachos. After we began eating, staff returned to inform us the plate was meant for another table—then proceeded to take our partially eaten nachos and deliver them to those guests. This wasn't a misunderstanding; they actually served our picked-over food to unsuspecting customers. This unprecedented breach of basic food service standards overshadowed any positive aspects of the visit. While the ambiance and drink specials have merit, the combination of subpar food quality and alarming service practices makes it impossible to recommend this restaurant until serious improvements are made.

A Frustrating Fast Food Experience That Wasn't Fast At All Against my better judgment, I stopped at this Taco Bell location for a quick snack on my way home Friday evening. What should have been a convenient pit stop turned into an exercise in patience that left me thoroughly disappointed. Upon arrival, I noticed the drive-thru line had wrapped around the building, prompting me to park and head inside, hoping to save time and avoid frustration. Unfortunately, this strategy backfired completely. Despite ordering just a standard value meal, the wait time was extraordinarily long—so long that I genuinely believe a sit-down restaurant would have served me faster. The delays weren't isolated to my order either. Other customers experienced similar issues, including a group of friends where one member had completely finished eating while his companions still waited for their meals to arrive. While I'm trying to remain objective and consider this might have been an unusually bad night for the staff, the experience was poor enough that I don't anticipate returning to this location anytime soon. For a fast-food establishment that markets itself on convenience and speed, this visit was anything but quick.

Mixed Value Proposition with Strategic Shopping Required This retailer offers interesting products, but pricing can be steep. Smart shoppers should leverage their $10 off $20 coupon or monitor online sales for better deals. **Pro tip:** Quest protein bars exemplify the pricing disparity—$33 in-store versus $21 during online sales. Always compare prices before purchasing to maximize savings on their inventory.

Quality Repairs and Customer Service That Gets Personal Ullrich's Shoe Repair has proven to be a reliable go-to for various leather repair needs. After breaking a heel last week, they performed an excellent repair job. Their expertise extends beyond shoes - they've successfully resoled shoes, repaired a leather jacket tear, and fixed a damaged purse for this customer and their partner. The shop demonstrates genuine customer appreciation, even featuring satisfied customer reviews on their website's News & Links section. This personal touch reflects their commitment to service. With consistently satisfying results across multiple repair jobs, Ullrich's has earned their trust as a dependable repair shop for leather goods of all kinds.

A Tolerable Stay Only for Location's Sake At $100 per night, this hotel disappoints on multiple fronts. The overwhelming chemical smell permeates the rooms, raising health concerns. Technical issues plague the property—non-functioning internet and broken TV remotes hamper basic amenities. Even the elevator buttons require excessive force to operate. The sole redeeming quality is its prime location, which may prove essential for some travelers. However, the numerous drawbacks make this a last-resort option only. Unless location is absolutely critical and alternatives are unavailable, consider looking elsewhere for better value and comfort. **Proceed with caution if booking.**

**Disappointing Breakfast Experience** Citizens breakfast fell short of expectations. While eggs were cooked correctly to order, cold bacon and underwhelming tater tots with peppers dampened the meal. The unsliced, unbuttered sourdough toast was particularly disappointing. For the premium price, the quality didn't justify the cost—Denny's offers better value and execution.

**Pizza Perfection with Homemade Drinks** Love their BBQ Chicken pizza – the barbecue flavor is irresistible! The Eastern Plaza location offers plenty of parking and spacious seating. House-crafted root beer and berry spritzer add a unique touch. Consistently great pizza paired with friendly service makes this a reliable favorite worth visiting repeatedly.

Not Vegetarian-Friendly and Disappointing Dessert As a health-conscious vegetarian, I found absolutely nothing suitable on the menu. Brought my kids specifically for the chocolate brownie pie, but all three were unimpressed with it. To make matters worse, we waited approximately 15 minutes just to receive the dessert. Between the limited menu options and lackluster food quality, this visit was thoroughly disappointing.
Delicious Chinese Cuisine at Fair Prices Sky has earned its place as our go-to family restaurant with excellent food, reasonable pricing, and trendy ambiance.

Mixed Experience: Excellent Coffee, Poor Service I visited this establishment on a Thursday afternoon around 1 o'clock, just after the lunch rush had subsided. My experience proved to be decidedly mixed, with some genuine highlights overshadowed by frustrating service issues. ## The Good The cappuccino I ordered at the coffee bar was promptly delivered and absolutely excellent—deserving of an A+ rating. The ambience of the space is genuinely appealing, and the display of pastries and baked goods looks truly amazing. Despite the service problems, I must acknowledge that all the staff members were extremely nice and pleasant. ## The Problematic Unfortunately, the service quality was significantly below expectations. After ordering food, I encountered numerous issues. The server seemed distracted, folding napkins while I waited two minutes just to be acknowledged, despite only one person being ahead of me in line. She appeared confused and took my order incorrectly. When my $14 hamburger with avocado arrived, the bacon I'd requested was missing. Additionally, no utensils, napkins, salt and pepper, or condiments were provided—I had to retrieve these myself. Most frustratingly, despite requesting a to-go container three times, I never received one and eventually left without it. ## The Verdict As someone who dines out 7-10 times weekly, this was among the most incompetent service I've experienced recently, despite the pleasant demeanor of the staff. I would return specifically for the coffee, internet access, and perhaps a scone, but wouldn't order full meals again.

A Lively Dining Experience Perfect for Groups and Out-of-Towners This energetic restaurant and entertainment venue offers a unique experience that seems particularly appealing to visitors and large parties. Located in what appears to be a tourist-friendly area, the establishment has generated mixed reviews from locals, but our out-of-town group found plenty to enjoy during our visit. ## Food Quality and Value The standout menu item was undoubtedly the ahi tuna wrap, priced around $13. This generously-sized entrée proved substantial enough to share between two people and was packed with high-quality ahi tuna. The wrap's exceptional flavor profile came from its well-balanced combination of ingredients and dressings, elevating what could have been an ordinary dish into something memorable. For those typically underwhelmed by wraps, this preparation might change your perspective entirely. The restaurant demonstrated impressive hospitality by offering complimentary desserts to multiple parties, including ours.
