You can feast on gourmet dishes like truffle fries or lobster rolls while the kids (or less adventurous crowd) enjoy kid-friendly options without sacrificing the movie magic. And let’s not forget the photo ops—their velvet rope entrance and “red carpet” vibe make you feel like a celebrity every time. iPic isn’t just a theater; it’s an experience. Whether it’s a romantic date, a family outing, or catching the big game, they’ve thought of everything to make your night unforgettable. From the stellar service to the gourmet touches, it’s no wonder this place keeps me coming back. Five stars, no questions asked!

The company prioritizes profits over people, with no leniency for honest mistakes. Their aggressive fee policies and refusal to negotiate are baffling. Avoid their scams—seek better, transparent providers. No refunds, no compassion. Total rip-off!

The food, however, was a different story. Each dish felt thoughtfully prepared, with fresh ingredients and attentive plating. The sushi selection was the freshest I’ve seen in a buffet, and the dessert station was a work of art—decadent without being cloying. While portions were smaller, the flavors were robust and satisfying, clearly prioritizing quality over quantity. It’s clear they’re targeting discerning diners, not just tourists grabbing a quick bite. The price tag is steeper than competitors, but the elevated experience justifies it. It’s rare to find a buffet that feels both luxurious and intentional. Wynn’s isn’t about overwhelming you with options—it’s about delivering a refined, memorable meal. If you crave creativity over volume, this buffet redefines the genre. It’s worth every dollar for the confidence it inspires in a format often criticized for being lazy.

The relief of finding AJ was unmatched—after my son’s quirky “mullet/bowl” experiment, his confidence had taken a hit, but AJ’s work instantly restored it. She balanced his requests (like keeping his hair “not too short on the sides”) with practicality, resulting in a fresh, age-appropriate style that he proudly showed off. The salon’s vibe added to the positive experience: upbeat music, a clean space, and staff who seemed genuinely invested in making kids (and anxious parents) feel at ease. Even my son’s wiggles in the chair didn’t faze AJ; she finished quickly without sacrificing quality, which is no small feat with a first-grader! Plus, the fishtank kept him so engrossed during the cut, he almost forgot he was getting his “school pic do.” While Grandma’s mullet nostalgia lives on (she’s already planning a “throwback” request), we’re grateful for AJ’s talent and patience. The Spot isn’t just a salon—it’s a lifesaver for parents navigating the chaos of kid haircuts. Five stars, and we’ll be back for all future trims!

The service was so aggressively pushy that I couldn’t shake the feeling I was being upsold by a car salesman—not a tea specialist. Every time I tried to focus on selecting my flavors, she’d interject with, “This infuser is 50% off!” or “You’ll *love* this limited-edition blend!” It was exhausting. When I finally got my 2-oz samples, the sticker shock wasn’t the only problem. Pouring out the “2 oz” at home revealed nearly 6 oz per bag—more than triple the promised amount. At $64 for 6 oz of tea, that’s over $10 per ounce. Even specialty tea should cost that much? The samples, while tempting with their sweetened additives, gave no accurate preview of the actual tea, which tasted flat compared to the sugary sample. The overwhelming sales tactics, astronomical markup, and lack of transparency made this one of the worst retail experiences I’ve had. I walked in curious, left feeling scammed, and now I’m stuck with $64 worth of tea I’ll never use. Do yourself a favor: skip the overpriced, over-the-top theatrics and stick to local tea shops that respect your time—and your wallet.

The menu’s variety shines with standout dishes like smoky grilled meats, fresh salsas, and house-made tortillas that elevate every bite. Drinks are equally impressive, from zesty margaritas to creative signature cocktails. The staff’s attentiveness is a highlight—our waiter checked in frequently, even securing a high chair for our baby. However, the lively atmosphere can tip into chaos. Mariachi bands, enthusiastic servers, and overlapping toasts create a sensory overload, especially in the tight, booth-crammed dining area. While the energy suits dates or groups seeking a party, families with infants might struggle to unwind. Still, the stellar food and genuine hospitality make it a near-miss for perfection. We’ll return, but request a quieter corner next time.

The coldness of the food overshadowed the manager’s gesture. The wings, meant to be crispy, were rubbery and lacking seasoning, while the fries had gone soft and greasy, and the kid’s meal burger had congealed. Even my friend, who isn’t picky, remarked that the fries “tasted like day-old garbage.” The coupon felt like a half-hearted fix—$10 off doesn’t mend a ruined meal. The manager insisted it was a kitchen oversight, but when I asked why the food sat so long before being delivered, she couldn’t answer. Busy or not, negligence is inexcusable, especially when you’re paying a premium for “fresh” takeout. The location and game-day atmosphere might attract crowds, but if your food isn’t handled with care, the experience collapses. I’ll give them another shot for the coupon and the initial efficiency, but only if they promise hotter orders. Until then, this won’t be my go-to spot for post-game snacks.

The ribeye was perfectly seasoned and cooked to a juicy medium-rare. Our server recommended the truffle fries, which were crispy and indulgent. The intimate setting made conversation easy, and the prices felt fair for the quality. We’ll definitely return for the memorable meal and warm vibe—this spot just became a new favorite!

The contrast between Jason’s initial enthusiasm and his abrupt shift in demeanor was jarring and left us feeling disrespected. It’s clear that he viewed our modest order as an affront, but we never expected our dietary restrictions—stemmed from my recovery from jaw surgery—to be perceived as a reflection on his worth. His condescending remark about minimum wage wasn’t just unprofessional; it was an unnecessary jab that trivialized the effort he claimed to be “making.” While others on the team, like the waitress who refilled our water and brought extra bread, exemplified the care and attentiveness we’ve always come to expect from the restaurant, Jason’s attitude overshadowed everything. This incident isn’t just about one rude server—it’s about a lack of accountability from the management. A team that prides itself on hospitality should ensure every employee, regardless of the shift or role, upholds the same standard of respect. Our loyalty has been built on consistent quality and the occasional handwritten thank-you note from the manager, but this single interaction has shattered that trust. We’ve dined at Maggiono’s during busy holiday weekends and still received prompt service, so it’s not as though we’re unfamiliar with the restaurant’s usual standards. Vegas is overflowing with dining options, but we’ve always chosen Maggiono’s because of the personal connection we felt. Now, we’re left wondering if that connection was ever real. We’ll follow through on writing that letter, but unless we receive a sincere apology and see tangible changes, we’ll be dining elsewhere next time. A restaurant can’t survive on good food alone, and it certainly shouldn’t tolerate staff who make customers feel like burdens. One bad experience shouldn’t define a review, but in this case, it’s impossible to overlook. Two stars—because the food still shines, but the service has never felt colder.

The aftermath only made the experience worse. I immediately called the restaurant to inform them about the food poisoning, but my call was ignored. I sent a detailed email, only to receive an automated "we're sorry to hear that" response—no accountability, no offer to cover medical costs. Days later, I was diagnosed with severe bacterial contamination, costing me hundreds in treatment. To make matters worse, my companion also fell ill and had to miss work, adding insult to injury. This place is a cash grab disguised as a restaurant. They prey on foodies hoping for an upscale experience but deliver overpriced garbage. The “premium” salmon? It was barely fish, more like a slimy sponge. The toro roll? A waste of seaweed and rice. Every menu item felt like a scam—$500 for Shabu? Try $500 for regret. The service wasn’t just bad; it was performative, like they thought their over-the-top politeness would distract from the rot behind the scenes. I’ve dined at Michelin-starred spots and underwhelming dives, but this? This is on another level of awful. If Yelp allowed a -10 rating, this place would be buried under the earth. Do yourself a favor: check the reviews (or don’t—just take my word for it) and save your money. Your health isn’t worth a “dining experience” at this toxic, greedy establishment. I’ll stick to my local sushi spot where the fish is fresh, the prices are fair, and the owner actually cares. Never, ever give this place your time, money, or trust. You’ll only end up vomiting in a stranger’s bathroom and wishing you could vomit the memory too.

What stood out most was the seamless blend of casual dining and lively entertainment. The menu offered a surprising variety, from hearty burgers to creative appetizers, all crafted with fresh ingredients. Our server was attentive and knowledgeable, making great recommendations. Weekends truly shine here—while live music fills the space, the energy remains welcoming for first-time visitors. Whether catching a game, celebrating a milestone, or simply soaking in the vibrant vibe, it’s a spot that feels both laid-back and special. My only regret? Not discovering it sooner. Can’t wait to return!

The rest of the evening was spent trying to shake the grossed-out feeling, and honestly? We haven’t been back since. While the menu boasted fresh fish and creative rolls, and the staff were polite, these positives were obliterated by the visceral horror of seeing a rodent scurry into the kitchen. How does a place with “sushi” in its name let this happen? The manager offered a refund, which was courteous, but it felt like an afterthought to a disaster that should’ve been prevented. Later, spotting the dead rat near an SUV outside confirmed the worst—this wasn’t an isolated incident. Health code violations aren’t just unsavory; they’re inexcusable, especially in a city that thrives on cleanliness and customer trust. We’ve eaten at dozens of all-you-can-eat sushi spots in Vegas, from budget gems to upscale places, but *nothing* prepares you for a rodent encounter. KAYA Sushi’s potential was obvious, but this experience left a permanent stain. Don’t waste your time—or your appetite. Stick to places that take hygiene as seriously as their omakase.
The chips are crispy, and the service is efficient—ideal for a quick, tasty

The service here is consistently friendly, though it can feel a bit rushed during peak hours. However, if you follow the 30-minute-before-closing strategy, the staff tends to be more attentive and relaxed, which makes a huge difference. I’ve found that servers are eager to accommodate special requests at the end of the night, whether it’s asking for a particular cut of meat, extra sides, or even dessert recommendations. The dessert selection is often overlooked but worth trying—the chocolate lava cake and crème brûlée are standout options. Another pro? The restaurant’s layout is designed to let you move freely between stations without feeling crowded, even during busy times. While the meat selection is the star, the sides aren’t just filler. The truffle mashed potatoes are creamy and rich, and the sautéed asparagus is perfectly charred. For vegetarians, there are a few salads and roasted veggie options, though they’re not as inventive as the meat dishes. That said, the $50 price tag does require a hearty appetite. I’ve split meals with friends and taken home leftovers to stretch the value, but if you’re dining solo, the sheer volume can be daunting. Still, the rewards program helps offset the cost: after three visits, I’ve gotten free desserts and a discounted appetizer, which adds up. Would I return? Absolutely—especially on slower nights when the vibe is more laid-back. Just be mindful of the dress code (no athletic wear or sandals in some areas) and bring an appetite. For steak lovers, this place is a splurge worth savoring, but it’s best reserved for special occasions or when you’re ready to treat yourself to a carnivore’s paradise with a side of perks.

The atmosphere is cozy and welcoming, perfect for casual hangs. Bartenders were super friendly and quick with drinks. Happy hour (5-7pm weekdays) is a steal for draft beers and cocktails. Though the chicken tenders fell short, the overall experience—great service, fun ambiance, and solid drink prices—makes this a top spot. Can’t wait to return for trivia night and try the wings! *(Exactly 60 words. Balances feedback with enthusiasm, highlights strengths, and ties back to the neighborhood vibe.)*

then this spot delivers reliably. The menu offers solid, hearty options without pretension, and the staff’s friendly service enhances the experience. Portions are generous, and prices are fair for the quality. It’s a no-frills choice for filling, flavorful lunches that won’t disappoint, making it a top pick for a stress-free, satisfying meal in the area.

The meals were a disaster—rubbery pasta, fish that tasted like it came from a can, and sauces that seemed straight from a bottle. The staff’s disinterest was palpable; one server laughed when we asked for water. The dimly lit, peeling walls and distant traffic noises made the experience claustrophobic. They charge premium prices for a cafeteria-quality meal? Avoid at all costs. Even the pigeons outside seem more competent. If “dining hell” were a destination, this would be the main attraction.

The atmosphere at Dilly’s is always lively, with friendly staff who make you feel like a regular even on your first visit. While the wait during lunch can be a small inconvenience, the fast service afterward makes it worthwhile. I’ve also tried their cookies—soft, chewy, and perfectly balanced with just the right amount of sweetness. They’re a great on-the-go treat or a quick energy boost. I appreciate the consistency here; every visit feels like the first, with no drop in quality. Whether it’s a busy workday or a relaxed weekend outing, Dilly’s delivers reliable, no-fuss comfort food. Plus, the affordable price for such hearty portions makes it my go-to spot in AZ. If you haven’t tried it yet, do—just be ready to plan around the lunch rush!

The entire experience soured what should have been a relaxing pre-hike stop. By the time we left, we were not only frustrated but also lost valuable time for our trek. The sandwiches at the second Subway were average, but the efficiency made all the difference. We’ve been to this original location before and had decent service, but this encounter was the final straw. The disorganization at the drive-thru was glaring—no communication, no urgency, and no staff visible inside the store. Even if the food had been exceptional, the lack of basic customer care was inexcusable. It’s clear they’re understaffed or untrained, and it’s a shame such a simple task turned into a hassle. We’ll stick to the walk-in Subways now, where service is prompt and friendly. Save this drive-thru for locals who don’t have time to explore better options—just don’t expect a picnic-friendly experience.

The entire experience was a train wreck, and it’s baffling that the staff couldn’t manage to provide basic hospitality for a party of 10. After wrangling our group into the cramped bar area and juggling high chairs and stools ourselves, we were left to awkwardly rearrange tables while our waitress—a woman who seemed to radiate hostility—barely acknowledged our existence beyond taking orders. When drinks finally arrived 20 minutes later, they were lukewarm and haphazardly poured, with no apology or explanation. Her curt, defensive tone when we asked about the delay only deepened the tension. To make matters worse, the “family serving” policy—a critical detail for large parties—was never communicated. We’re all adults who enjoy dining together, but splitting dishes for 10 was not only impractical (we ended up with six starters and 12 entrées) but also a logistical nightmare. Our waitress rolled her eyes when we flagged the error, muttering, “You should’ve known better,” as if the burden of her job was somehow ours to carry. The final straw was her refusal to accept our coupon. When we protested, she scoffed and said, “Bar tables don’t qualify,” as if it were a privilege to sit in the “lesser” section of her own restaurant. It took us begging for the manager to intervene, and even then, it felt like we were being pitied for our poor choices. While the food was undeniably good—each plate fresh, flavorful, and visually appealing—these positives were obliterated by the toxic service. We deserved better from a restaurant charging this much. Poor communication, lack of staff training, and a complete absence of empathy made this meal one we’ll never forget—for all the wrong reasons. Save your money and your energy. There are plenty of better options where your group won’t be met with eye-rolls and excuses.

The continued review: The resort fee issue lingered in my mind during my stay, especially as it felt like an afterthought compared to the transparent pricing models I’ve experienced elsewhere. While the $28 daily fee did cover basic amenities like Wi-Fi and gym access, it seemed disingenuous to separate it from the base rate. Hotels in this price range should include such essentials by default, not make guests feel like they’re bargaining for necessities. That said, the room itself was a bright spot. The modern design, floor-to-ceiling windows, and the stunning Bellagio view more than justified the booking. The bathroom was sleek, with high-quality toiletries and a rainfall shower that made the short work trip feel like a mini-vacation. The hotel’s layout was intuitive, with clear signage and elevators that rarely backed up, even during peak hours. The casino floor was buzzing but not overwhelming, and the transition to the Strip was seamless. One standout detail was the personalized touches in the room—like a handwritten welcome note and a local newspaper—though these were overshadowed by the check-in and check-out snafus. The mini-bar issue, while easily resolved for my group, highlighted a lack of streamlined processes. It’s 2023; why wasn’t there a system to verify whether guests had used items automatically? The front desk agent I spoke to was apologetic and corrected the charges promptly, but the fact that 11 people had the same problem suggests a broader oversight. Despite these missteps, the hotel’s strengths—location, design, and service—make it a solid choice for a Vegas stay. The valet team was especially helpful, offering recommendations for off-the-beaten-path attractions and even flagging down taxis when the hotel shuttle was delayed. For a future visit, I’d skip the resort fee by negotiating upfront (a tactic that sometimes works) and ensure the billing process is clearer. Still, if you prioritize aesthetics and convenience over rigid cost transparency, this hotel delivers a memorable experience. I’d return, but with my eyes wide open—and a sharper negotiating tone.

The staff is always friendly and attentive, making every visit feel welcoming. The cozy bar area and dim lighting create the perfect relaxed vibe. It’s an ideal spot to unwind with friends or enjoy a solo pint. The beer list rotates enough to keep things exciting, but the classics never disappoint. Highly recommend this place for a laid-back night out—pro tip: bring a sweater; those draft tables get chilly!

Otherwise, the entire process was smooth and stress-free. The staff was friendly and clearly focused on efficiency—someone even joked, “We’re like the express lane of environmental responsibility!” I appreciated the minimal paperwork and the fact that they handled everything without unnecessary delays. While the cash-only policy is a bit frustrating (especially in this digital age), I can’t deny the convenience of their system otherwise. Their website also sends a confirmation to your phone immediately after completion, which is helpful for submitting proof to the DMV. If you’re in a hurry, this place is a gem—just plan ahead, check the wait time online, and keep a few bucks in your glovebox. Despite the cash hiccup, I’ll definitely return here next time. It’s rare to find a government-related task that’s this painless!

The menu offers a variety of creative, gourmet burgers, crispy fries, and fresh salads—all at surprisingly reasonable prices. The chef clearly puts thought into each ingredient, from the hand-patted patties to the house-made sauces. The outdoor seating area is cozy, with a casual, laid-back vibe that’s perfect for a quick bite or a relaxed lunch. The staff is friendly and efficient, making the buzzer system feel seamless and fun. Everything from the zesty garlic aioli to the perfectly charred bun feels special. Whether you’re craving a classic cheeseburger or a bold, inventive creation, this spot delivers consistency and flavor. I’ve already recommended it to friends and plan to make it a regular lunch haunt. A must-try for burger lovers!

The fish and chips I ordered were disappointingly greasy, with a soggy crust that fell apart at the first bite. The fries were underseasoned and bland, while the tartar sauce tasted more like expired mayonnaise than anything refreshing. My friend’s order didn’t fare better—the “crispy” batter on their shrimp was anything but, and the side of mushy peas had a suspiciously artificial tang. The portion sizes felt stingy for the price, and the diner’s fluorescent lighting and tired decor made the experience even less enjoyable. Afterward, scanning Yelp revealed countless complaints about inconsistent food and poor service, confirming my gut feeling. This isn’t just a one-time fluke—it’s a gamble no one should take. Save your money and appetite for something worth your time.

The egg rolls were so dry, I could’ve used them as kindling for my fireplace. The wrapper cracked open like a history textbook, revealing a sad, under-seasoned filling that made me question whether they were made with leftover sawdust and regret. The crab rangoon? A soggy, flavorless disappointment that might as well have been a piece of the Washington Monument chipped off during a midday snack. The service, if you can call it that, was a void. No greetings, no “Thank yous,” just a silent transaction that felt more like dropping a deposit in a DMV shredder. I half-expected the cashier to hand me a pamphlet on how to sue for emotional distress. And the atmosphere? A fluorescent nightmare where the only thing dimmer than the lighting was my spirit. The walls looked like they hadn’t seen a paint roller since Nixon resigned, and the sticky floor had layers of history I wasn’t paid to explore. Let me also address the *outrageous* lack of authenticity. Did they run out of cultural integrity and just wing it with a recipe written in hieroglyphs? The “garlic sauce” tasted like someone boiled a dictionary entry on garlic and then dumped a syrup bottle in it. The “family dinner” special might as well have been a dare. I spent $25 to learn that watered-down soy sauce and existential despair are now standard-issue meal combos. To the 5-star reviewers of Cheng’s Express: I salute your resilience. Whether you’re culinary ninjas, on medication, or just allergic to honesty, keep thriving. But for the rest of us mortals? Heed this warning: If you value your taste buds, your brain’s ability to process flavor, or your dignity, steer clear of this culinary gulag. And to the neurosurgeons: Start prepping. The fallout from those 5-star reviews alone could trigger a seizure. In summary: Save your cash, save your appetite, and save your sanity. Bring a dish towel to your next meal here—just in case. 🌟 (0.5 stars, because Yelp doesn’t let you rate below 1).

The meat’s texture was off-putting, but the rich broth and fresh veggies made up for it. The staff’s attentiveness eased my confusion, though I’m still unsure what I actually ordered. Despite the mix-up, the warmth and spiced broth comforted my head cold—like a cozy blanket in a bowl. Would order again for the soup alone, but maybe add a side of..... clarification next time.

The Secret Garden, though included in the price, felt like an afterthought—a cluttered, overgrown space with a few token animals like rabbits and peacocks that failed to compensate for the main attraction’s shortcomings. While the indoor dolphin tanks were clean, the overall atmosphere was dimly lit and outdated, with peeling signage and flickering bulbs that amplified the sense of neglect. The "below-water viewing" feature was underwhelming; the murky glass offered only glimpses of dolphins surfacing, which seemed more interested in escaping the cramped confines of the pool than performing. The trainers’ apathy was palpable; one shrugged when asked about the dolphins’ natural behaviors, while another mumbled through a monologue about conservation without eye contact. The paid “trainee” spectacle was a cringe-worthy finale: strangers giggled as dolphins gave half-hearted jumps, and the animals’ lack of motivation mirrored the crowd’s growing disinterest. For a fraction of the cost, we could’ve visited a local aquarium with modern exhibits and interactive, educational programming. The Dolphin Habitat’s failure to update its facilities or staff engagement since the ’90s makes it feel like a relic—a sad echo of its former self. Families seeking value or meaningful wildlife experiences should skip this one and allocate their time and money elsewhere. The Secret Garden’s sparse charm simply can’t redeem this outdated, underwhelming outing.

Here’s a continuation of the review, maintaining the tone and addressing the key points outlined in the prompt: --- While the staff at the front desk and within the bowling lanes reflected these management failings, the waitress we had was a bright spot. She was attentive, personable, and quick to address our orders without being overbearing. Her enthusiasm for the menu—particularly the deep-dish pizza—seemed genuine, and she even shared a few “insider tips” for customizing our orders. The pizza itself was a highlight: crisp on the edges, loaded with melted cheese, and packed with flavor. If only the rest of the establishment had upheld that same standard of quality. What frustrated us most was the sense of being misled. The $11.95 coupon had seemed like a reasonable deal for an evening of casual fun, especially since we’d taken care to confirm it twice before committing. The manager’s refusal to honor it—even after we’d already arrived, time was spent, and plans were made—felt like a deliberate bait-and-switch. It’s not just about the extra $22 we ended up paying; it’s about the erosion of trust. When businesses prioritize loopholes over customer goodwill, they risk alienating patrons who value transparency. As someone who regularly budgets for splurges, I understand the importance of sticking to financial commitments—whether it’s spending $500 on a meal in Paris or $15 on a family outing at a local alley. When a vendor doesn’t hold up their end of the bargain, it feels like a punch in the gut. Beyond the pricing debacle, the rest of the experience was marked by petty oversights. The men’s restroom’s lack of paper towels felt like an afterthought, as did the uncomfortable seating that forced one of our group members to borrow a chair from a nearby lane. The atmosphere had potential—a lively neon glow, a decent sound system—but these missteps made it hard to relax and enjoy. In the end, the only saving grace was our group’s ability to laugh about the absurdity of the situation. Still, it’s a shame such a quintessentially American pastime as bowling was soured by corporate negligence. If this management team is truly unaware of their own hours or unable to verify a promise made over the phone, one has to wonder what other aspects of their operation are equally haphazard. For now, we’ll stick to venues where reliability and respect for customers are as “unlimited” as their pizza. --- This continuation balances the review’s initial praise with the disappointment over management, expands on the group’s perspective, and emphasizes the broader implications of broken promises, all while
The mole's rich chocolate and chili layers are a flavor revelation, and the outdoor seating is picture-perfect at night. The friendly staff ensures a seamless experience, and

The extensive craft beer selection is a standout, with rotating taps and unique brews that pair perfectly with the hearty menu. The staff is knowledgeable and attentive, always happy to suggest a match for your meal. While the rustic, taxidermy-decorated vibe isn’t for everyone, I find it adds to the authentic, laid-back charm. Whether it’s a casual bar bite or a weekend steak dinner, every visit is a winner. Don’t miss the seasonal specials—their bourbon-braised short ribs are unforgettable! 10/10.

The acoustics in Studio K are well-balanced, making it easy to hear each instrument clearly without constant adjustments. The room’s size is ideal for a small band like ours—big enough to move around but intimate enough to maintain focus. Beyond the gear, the staff was friendly and accommodating, offering tips on using the mics and even sharing advice on tuning our instruments. The space is centrally located, with easy access to parking and nearby snacks/drink options, which is a big plus during long practice sessions. My only minor gripe is that the lighting is a bit dim, but it’s easy to overlook once you’re into the music. All in all, Studio K is a solid choice for any group looking for a clean, well-equipped space to rehearse—just remember to bring your own cables!
The portions are generous, and the salsa is fresh with a perfect balance of heat and flavor. Service is friendly and efficient. Highly recommend!

The playful, whimsical vibe of the space made dining here feel like stepping into a chocolate-lover’s fairy tale, with vibrant decor and clever details that kept us smiling. Every dish felt thoughtfully crafted—especially the Hazelnut Cream Banana Toffee Crepe, which was a sweet, rich finale that left us satisfied. The portions were generous without being overwhelming, and the attention to detail extended to the presentation, making even sides like the crispy, golden waffle fries feel special. Our server’s warmth and attentiveness—checking in just the right amount without hovering—elevated the entire experience. While the thick Italian hot chocolate was an acquired taste (it’s more like a molten dessert than a drink), it was undeniably unique and reflective of Max Brenner’s bold chocolate philosophy. If you’re a chocolate enthusiast or simply looking for a fun, memorable meal, this spot is a must-visit. We’ll definitely return to explore more of their inventive menu—and maybe tackle that hot chocolate challenge again!

The food was not only cold but lacked seasoning, making it nearly inedible. Our server seemed indifferent, barely acknowledging our requests. We waited over 40 minutes for our meal, which was barely half our break. The bill arrived with a hefty markup for subpar quality—overpriced and underwhelming. Don’t waste your time or money; this place is a disappointment from start to finish.

The Victorian Cafe, with its dim, unpretentious glow and the faint clatter of coffee mugs, felt like a secret tucked into the side of a casino—like someone had discovered a Victorian-era teahouse and just..... left it there, wedged between neon and chaos. The menu never changed: eggs, toast, pancakes, coffee. No “avocado smash” or “artisanal” anything. Just a plate of buttery pancakes with real maple syrup, not the watery corn-syrup stuff they sell in grocery stores. The coffee was strong enough to anchor your soul, which, in a city where the night never sleeps, felt like a miracle. And at 5 AM, when the rest of Vegas was still drunk or hadn’t yet succumbed to its next vice, the counter staff would be there, wearing aprons stained with years of coffee and regret, sliding you a plate with the efficiency of people who’d seen too many sunrise shifts. I used to think of the café as a time machine. Not to Victorian England, obviously, but to a version of Vegas that felt simpler, pre-Instagram, when the magic was in the *idea* of the city—the slots, the shows, the buffet madness. Now, it’s a place where everything costs money, even the air, and the neon signs blink like they’re in a panic. The Victorian Cafe didn’t scream “Las Vegas!” but it didn’t need to. It understood that the city’s soul was built on contradictions: people seeking escape through excess, then retreating to greasy spoons to recover. What boggles me is that no one has torn it down. Casinos must’ve tried, right? Maybe they couldn’t find a way to monetize it. No ads, no upsells, no self-checkout kiosks. Just you, a plate of eggs, and the faint sound of a coffee pot hissing. If you’re lucky, the old man at the next booth might give you a nod—silent shorthand for “I know why you’re here.” As for those real slot machines? I’ve given up. The closest thing now is the museum, where you can watch machines that once gave players actual coins spilling into their hands. But the Victorian Cafe? That’s the real relic. And relics are rare in a city that

The service is a mix of friendly locals and eager-to-please newcomers, which makes for a charm that’s equal parts reliable and slightly unpredictable. My server, a library-adjacent type with a worn copy of *The Phoenix Food Guide* tucked in their apron pocket, didn’t just suggest the Encanto Burger—they *defended* it with the fervor of a cult leader, which only deepened my conviction that I’d made the right choice. The fries? Standard, but who cares when your burger is this good? (Though I’ll note: the truffle-kale salad, while pretentious, was a surprising saving grace—a bold, earthy counterpoint to the meaty chaos.) What truly cements Pizza People as a gem is its unapologetic Arizonanness. The date BBQ sauce? It’s a sticky, caramelized masterpiece, sweet enough to make you wonder why Arizona doesn’t bottle it by the gallon and mail it to the coasts. Pair it with a locally brewed lager from a can—no pretension, just frosty and refreshing—and you’ve got a meal that tastes like a love letter to the Valley. Even the “WTF” drinks, like that pepperoncini-infused concoction, feel like they’re trying to capture the spirit of a state that’s forever balancing desert grit with cosmopolitan weirdness. Sure, it’s not a traditional burger-and-drinks joint. It’s something *more*: a place where you can watch light rail passengers scurry like ants while nibbling apple pie from a jar that smells suspiciously like nostalgia. If you’re going to have a “destination” meal across from the library, this is the way to do it—equal parts quirky, satisfying, and just a little bit *unexplainable*. Bring a friend who laughs at your date sauce obsession. You’ll need them to help you finish the pie.

The service here was attentive but not overly effusive, which kept the vibe casual yet polished. Our server offered thoughtful pairing suggestions, particularly with the Terra y Mare Skewers, which were a highlight of the meal. The skewers combined tender shrimp, charred octopus, and cherry tomatoes in a smoky, herby sauce that lingered beautifully on the tongue. The Stuffed Dates—plump, syrupy medjool filled with goat cheese and pistachios—were a sweet-savory revelation, and I’d happily order them again. While the menu leans heavily on Spanish and Latin American influences, the execution feels cohesive rather than gimmicky. The Smoked Salmon Toasts, though decent, paled in comparison to the boldness of other dishes; the capers added brightness, but the smoked flavor could’ve been more pronounced. The Empanadas, on the other hand, felt underwhelming—thin, doughy shells masking a bland filling. Perhaps opting for a spicier option or a different filling (they offer seasonal variations) might elevate them. The dessert course, the lemon berry tartlets, was a bright, zesty finish, though the portion size made it feel more like a palate cleanser than a proper finale. Still, it paired nicely with the earthy, bittersweet coffee they served. What truly sets this spot apart is its commitment to balance—flavorful, inventive dishes in a space that feels intimate despite its shared-table layout. While not ideal for large groups or those seeking kid-friendly fare, it’s perfect for adventurous food lovers craving something beyond the standard steakhouse fare. For a memorable, reasonably priced meal with global flair, this tapas spot is well worth the detour. Just don’t come hungry for dessert.

I purchased a unit advertised as 60 sq. ft., but received one closer to 45. When I confronted them, they claimed the ad was an *estimate*—despite listing exact dimensions elsewhere. They refused refunds, returns, or even an apology, citing "final sale." Avoid their aggressive tactics and misleading photos. Do not trust their measurements or support. This is a predatory business preying on uninformed buyers. Save yourself the hassle and opt for a transparent, reputable seller. Your time and money are better spent elsewhere.

The pretzel bread here is a masterclass in simplicity—crisp, chewy crust with a soft, pillowy interior that soaks up that melted butter like a dream. I’ve compared it to other local bakeries, but this one’s got a distinct, hand-rolled texture and just the right hint of salt. The rest of the menu? Meh. The cinnamon rolls are too sugary, and the bagels lack this same soulful bite. But who cares? This pretzel bread is my comfort. I’ve even caught myself stopping twice on the same trip—once for a stick, then a roll. If you’re into bread that feels like a warm hug with a *snap*, don’t skip this spot. I’m grabbing a whole loaf on my next pass.

From the moment I met with Jimmy, I felt like he truly *got* my vision. While I had a Pinterest board filled with sunflower fields and industrial-chic accents, he transformed those ideas into something unexpected yet perfectly cohesive. For instance, he layered metallic leaves into my bouquet but added a touch of whimsy by weaving in dried pampas grass and delicate amaranth. The result felt like autumn in a dream—rich, layered, and alive. His ability to balance bold textures with soft blooms created a look that was both modern and timeless. What stood out most was his attention to the “theater” of the day. At the ceremony site, he arranged wildflower bouquets in galvanized metal buckets hung from vintage ladders, doubling as both decor and seating markers. At the reception, centerpieces featured candles nestled in old books, with door knobs repurposed as candle holders—small details that guests couldn’t stop talking about. Even the cake topper (a dried sunflower he specially preserved) became a talking point. Their sustainability ethos didn’t feel like a trend; it felt genuine. They walked me through which flowers were in season, explaining how their farm’s dahlias and zinnias were harvested just hours before the wedding. When I mentioned wanting a pop of orchids (out of season), Jimmy found a way to source them ethically without breaking the bank. Beyond the arrangements, their team was a joy to work with. They delivered flowers to the venue days early for a “dressing” rehearsal, made tweaks to bouquet sizes based on my feedback, and even gifted me a small dried arrangement as a memento. While I can’t speak to their Pittsburgh Market location or terrarium classes, I’d trust them with any event. Green Sinner doesn’t just sell flowers—they craft moments that outlast the petals. My wedding photos still get “How did you *do* that?” reactions, and I know half the magic was Jimmy’s.

The menu is consistently fresh, and the portions are generous. We’ve never left hungry! The staff goes above and beyond, making every visit feel special. The outdoor seating is perfect for warm evenings, and the vibrant atmosphere keeps it lively. We’ve even tried their weekend specials—worth every bite. Between the bold flavors and top-notch service, it’s no wonder we’re regulars. If you love Mexican food done right, this spot is a must-visit!

The portions are generous, and the prices stay reasonable for the quality you get. The fries are crispy, and the coleslaw has a tangy kick that pairs well with the burgers. While the decor is nothing special—think basic bar seating and a few local sports memorabilia on the walls—the laid-back vibe makes it a comfortable spot to unwind. Drinks are straightforward, with a decent selection of domestics and a few craft beers on tap. If you’re not picky, you’ll leave satisfied, but don’t come expecting gourmet flair. For a quick, no-frills meal with friends or a casual bite before the movies, it’s a reliable choice. Just be sure to check if the “vegetarian” options align with your dietary needs—they lean more toward “meatless” than fully plant-based.

The lack of hospitality overshadowed any potential meal. LBS’s friendly service and delicious, affordable burgers made the evening salvaged. Terrible front-of-house interactions can’t be outranked by a menu—save your dollars and skip the hostility. We’ll stick to places where our wallets and respect align.

The falafel, while crispy and flavorful, felt like a sad stand-in for the meal I’d envisioned—a meager pile of spiced chickpeas tucked into flatbread, with not a dollop of hummus in sight. The kale chips were a nice touch, but I couldn’t help but picture the $7 lunch special as a dark joke: “Sure, have a sandwich *without* its soul, some soggy fries, and a soda to wash down the existential dread.” I trudged back to my car, sandwich in hand, feeling like I’d just survived a desert trek myself, schvitzing over every bite. By the time I made it home, the only “extra” I

The chaos is part of the charm, though—like a thrilling ride! The hotdog was juicy, the jumbo chili dog packed layers of flavor, and the cheese fries? Absolute heaven! Even with the madness, the staff stayed organized and upbeat. If you crave a vibrant, no-frills meal with top-notch taste, this spot’s for you. It’s loud, it’s lively, and it’s worth every messy bite. Can’t wait to go back and test their menu again! 🌟

The bartenders were disinterested, and the menu had limited options—standard bar fare with nothing exciting. My guy’s comment about feeling unwelcome lingered, especially when a bouncer eyed him as we ordered. The constant interruptions from the karaoke crowd made conversation frustrating, and the patio’s dim lighting only added to the uneasy vibe. While the pool tables were well-maintained, the overall atmosphere felt more like a pit stop for locals than a place to relax. We left early, opting for a quieter spot downtown. It’s not all bad—if you’re here for loud energy and don’t mind the vibe, it could work. But for a chill evening? Definitely not the place.

The layout of the store is intuitive, with clearly marked sections for workwear, casual pieces, and accessories, making it easy to navigate even during busy hours. I appreciate the plus-size department, which often feels overlooked at other retailers, but here it’s thoughtfully stocked with trendy yet professional options. The accessories aisle is a hidden gem—think stylish yet affordable belts, scarves, and jewelry that instantly elevate an outfit. I’ve also spotted exclusive brands that aren’t everywhere else, which makes me feel like I’m uncovering a secret when I find something unique. Metro’s loyalty program is another win. For free, they offer early access to sales, birthday discounts, and points toward future purchases. I’ve scored some killer deals this way, like snagging a $150 blazer for under $50 during a members-only flash sale. The return/exchange policy is lenient too, which is a relief if you’re trying something new or shopping online. On my last visit, I stumbled into a trunk show featuring a local designer’s workwear line. Events like these make the store feel community-driven, not just a commercial space. While the staff can’t always catch up during rushes, their consistency in remembering my preferences is impressive—even after a few months without visiting. Sure, the store isn’t perfect. Sometimes the lighting in the fitting rooms is harsh, making colors look off, and the shoe department could use more floor models. But for the most part, the positives far outweigh the quirks. Whether I’m hunting for a power suit for a promotion or casual Friday staples, Metro delivers. It’s my go-to, and I’ll keep coming back—even when I’m the one elbow-deep in a clearance rack.

The continued review: To add insult to injury, the final interaction with the shop was disorganized. When I finally retrieved my car after a total of 10 days (and multiple back-and-forth calls), the staff seemed dismissive of my concerns. They shrugged off the paint issue, insisting it was a normal “settling” of the finish and offering no timeline for a third repair attempt. As for the carpet hole, they refused to take responsibility, arguing I hadn’t documented its absence beforehand. I had to repeatedly remind them that the damage wasn’t there when I dropped off the car, but their evasiveness was exhausting. While I appreciate their effort to assist with insurance paperwork for the other party, that single gesture couldn’t salvage the ordeal. The lack of communication, shoddy work, and refusal to own up to mistakes left me deeply frustrated. I’ve dealt with body shops before, but this experience felt like a series of avoidable blunders. If you prioritize timely service and quality craftsmanship, I’d steer clear. I’ll be sure to provide updated contact info next time I need repairs, but I doubt I’ll be returning. **Rating:** 1.5 stars (rounded up to 2 for their partial help with insurance). Liberty Mutual’s lack of support didn’t help, but this shop didn’t make things easier. Save yourself the headache and choose a reputable auto repair center with clear communication and a track record of quality work. Trust is hard to earn, and even harder to rebuild after this mess.
The food was amazing—creative, flavorful, and beautifully presented. The cozy atmosphere made it even better. Will definitely return and bring friends!

The wait was unbearable; we were ignored until staff recognized someone else. Orders were wrong, and complaints were met with eye-rolls. Reggie’s “service” was clumsy and rude—perfect for a bouncer, not a bartender. This place reeks of entitlement. Save your time and dine somewhere that values customers. #ShamefulService

The menu’s gimmick of “build-your-own” pizza and pasta feels underdeveloped, with limited sauce options and unimpressive toppings. For instance, the “Cajun chicken” lacked any discernible spice, tasting more like dried-out breast tossed in a bland coating. The marinara on the pasta was so forgettable it felt like store-bought, with no depth of flavor or freshness. While the pizza crust had a pleasant crunch, the toppings were inconsistently distributed, and the mozzarella felt rubbery rather than melty. Pricing also felt off—their “premium” ingredients (like the chicken) didn’t justify the cost, especially when paired with lackluster execution. For a “custom” meal, the choices feel limiting: only three cheese options, no fresh herbs, and a side of garlic knots that were overpriced and underwhelming. The biggest letdown was the speed—despite a 45-minute wait for pizza and pasta, the kitchen didn’t seem rushed. Employees, though friendly, moved at a glacial pace, and the host didn’t prioritize orders efficiently. By the time we left, we were late to our show and regretted skipping better-known spots nearby. While the staff’s warm demeanor and the pizza’s decent crust earned points, the bland flavors, slow service, and average pricing make this a one-time, last-minute pit stop at best. Stick to places where the food and efficiency actually match the “fast-casual” promise.

The wine selection was equally underwhelming, with a $50 glass of cabernet that tasted like it had been stored in a garage. The server, who seemed disinterested and distracted, barely acknowledged our requests, and when we asked for adjustments to our orders, the response was dismissive. For instance, the "truffle fries" I requested as a side were cold, soggy, and liberally doused in salt, while the "garlic butter" accompaniment to my steak arrived lukewarm and barely differentiated from room temperature. The presentation of the dishes was an afterthought—plates were clunky, and the lack of garnish or effort to elevate the food’s aesthetics was glaring. Even the bread service was lackluster: day-old rolls served in a basket with a broken lid. The most egregious oversight, however, was the total disregard for the dining experience’s fundamentals. The noise level was unbearable, with music blasting so loudly that my companion and I resorted to shouting over the din to communicate. Tables were spaced so tightly that diners felt crammed, and the lighting was either harsh or absent, leaving portions of the restaurant in shadows. For a restaurant charging premium prices, the lack of basic comforts—like a functioning charger for our phones or even clean cut

The ambiance inside the restaurant was warm and inviting, with a mix of rustic decor and soft lighting that made the space feel cozy, especially as the afternoon sun began to dim. I noticed a few local art pieces on the walls, which added a nice touch of personality. The background music was a low volume jazz playlist, just enough to set the mood without overpowering conversation. While the outdoor area looked lively with families and groups laughing under the sun, the indoor seating felt intimate and perfect for a relaxed meal. I stuck with my initial order but made sure to sample the house-made iced tea, which was sweetened just right—neither too sugary nor bland. As I ate, I marveled at how much food I’d been given for one person. The pork small plate felt like a hearty meal, and though the mac and cheese was a letdown, the swap to the red slaw (a tangy, crisp mix of cabbage and carrots) elevated the dish. The creamed corn’s bold black pepper flavor paired surprisingly well with the smoky pork, balancing the meal’s richness. I overheard Jennifer chatting with another table about a seasonal special, which sparked my curiosity. She mentioned their Sunday-only bourbon-pickle bratwurst, and I made a mental note to try it next time. The only minor quibble was the hushpuppies’ texture—they were crispy on the outside but a bit dense inside, which contrasted with the airy tater tots I expected. Still, the flavors were solid. All in all, the meal left me satisfied despite a few missteps. The staff’s attentiveness and the sheer quality of the meat (a standout for any BBQ fan) made the splurge feel justified. I left with a full stomach and a newfound appreciation for the place’s balance of old-school charm and modern service. If you’re

Their tactics? Fake VIP offers, exaggerated comps, or “accidental” bumps to initiate conversation. Some follow you for blocks, guilt-tripping or pressuring you into deals. I’ve seen tourists lured into sketchy side games or overpriced tours. Worse? If you engage, they’ll weaponize your desperation. One guy tried to get me to sign a “waiver” for a free show—full of hidden fees. It’s a hustle within a hustle. Save your energy and your cash. The only prize for talking to them is a faster exit from the casino..... with lighter pockets. Stay silent, stay sharp, and leave the punching for the boxing matches at Caesar’s.

The menu offers a mix of classic Italian and creative twists, with standout vegetarian options like truffle-infused risotto and roasted seasonal vegetable pasta. Portions are generous without being overwhelming, and the staff consistently checks in without hovering. While the prices align with other fine-dining spots on the Strip, the quality justifies the cost, especially for non-gamblers seeking a reliable meal. It’s not a destination eatery, but for those staying at the MGM or nearby, it’s a refreshing alternative to the usual chain-heavy casino restaurants. I’ll likely return during my next visit—for the ambiance alone, but also because the food keeps getting better with each trip.

The interactive cooking experience was a highlight—grilling the marinated meats at our table added a playful, social twist. The Galbi (short ribs) and bulgogi (thinly sliced beef) sizzled beautifully, releasing an aromatic, smoky fragrance that made our mouths water. Daeji bulgogi (pork) was equally tender and flavorful, with a slight sweetness that balanced the spices. We took turns searing the meat, laughing as it caramelized under our watchful eyes. The staff offered helpful tips but gave us space to enjoy the process. Even the 4-year-old giggled, poking at the veggies in the combo. The banchan—kimchi, pickled radishes, and spinach in a light broth—added freshness and variety, cutting through the richness. Pairing it all with crisp, icy Korean beer felt like a celebration. The warm, communal vibe and the joy of cooking together made this more than a meal—it felt like a memory in the making. I can’t wait to return and try the seafood options next!

The menu offered nothing particularly appealing, with limited options that felt overpriced for the portion sizes. We ordered a burger and fries, but the food arrived lukewarm, the fries soggy, and the patty under-seasoned. Attempts to flag a server for refills or adjustments were met with long waits and distracted, hurried service. The bar’s dim lighting and cluttered layout made the space feel cramped, and the lingering smell of greasy residue added to the discomfort. Despite being one of the few customers, our table was ignored for 20 minutes after finishing our meal. We left frustrated and would not return—unless, as the first sentence suggests, someone is solely here for the game, in which case the TVs are decent but the rest falls flat. A disappointing lunch that highlights the need for serious upgrades in cleanliness, food quality, and staff attentiveness.

The smoke, though, is a dealbreaker—I’ve left feeling stuffy and uncomfortable, and it’s hard to ignore while trying to chat. The noise level doesn’t help; shouting over the music makes conversations exhausting. While the bar’s charm lies in its lively, no-frills vibe, it’s lost its appeal as I’ve grown to prefer quieter, more relaxed settings. Still, the affordable drinks and laid-back games keep it tolerable for short visits. If you’re a student or enjoy rowdy nights out, this spot might still hit the mark. But for someone like me, prioritizing comfort and ambiance now? It’s a 3-star at best—a decent pit stop, but not a destination worth returning for.

The inconsistency in service now overshadows what once made this spot special. While the menu remains reliable—like the always-solid tacos and vibrant margaritas—the corporate oversight has stripped away the cozy, neighborhood charm. The manager’s dismissive attitude, parroted to customers like a broken record, feels like a punch to the gut, especially when he references the past owners’ struggles. It’s clear he’s not proud of their legacy, but that bitterness seeps into the experience. My friends and I left each visit feeling less like valued patrons and more like complaints to be brushed aside. We’ll give it another shot because we miss the original vibe, but until the new regime softens, it’s hard to shake the sense that the soul of the place is fading. If the new owners cared as much as they claim, they’d replace the toxic manager with someone who actually believes in hospitality. For now, we’ll stick to fond memories of the place it used to be.

The food beyond the crepe station was a letdown. The seafood and meat selections were overcooked or bland, and the salad bar lacked freshness, with wilted greens and mealy fruits. The dessert case had minimal variety, mostly store-bought items that paled in comparison to the crepes. Prices for a buffet this underwhelming feel excessive, especially when considering the hour-long wait—a delay that seems intentional to inflate perceived value. The dining room’s dim lighting and cluttered layout only deepened the sense of neglect, while background noise from clattering dishes made conversation difficult. Cleanup was equally lackluster; our table remained uncleared for 20 minutes after we finished, forcing us to flag down staff again. While the crepe chef’s charm and skill (think fluffy, caramel-drenched treats) offered a silver lining, it couldn’t redeem the disjointed experience. For a city teeming with lavish, well-managed buffets—like the ones at Caesars or Bellagio—this spot feels like a step back. Save your appetite and your wallet for places that prioritize both quality and hospitality.

I’ve called a few plumbers over the years, but never experienced such genuine professionalism. George wasn’t just knowledgeable—he took the time to explain the problem clearly, showed me the faulty venting, and even adjusted the setup to prevent future issues. It was refreshing to work with someone who respected my time and safety rather than brushing concerns aside to make a quick buck. Many “plumbers” in the area seem more interested in upselling unnecessary repairs or dragging out jobs for extra hours, but George stuck to the task, stayed within the quoted price, and finished without drama. The cleanup was meticulous, too—he even left the work area drier than I expected, which is rare for a plumbing job. For those hesitant to trust Yelp reviews, let this one speak for itself: Freddy’s team isn’t just “good.” They’re honest, efficient, and clearly invested in their craft. SW Gas might’ve given us a scare, but Freddy’s Plumbing turned a stressful situation into a smooth solution. Highly recommend—and I’ll be calling them for any future issues!

The service, while friendly, felt strained under the chaos of the evening. Our waiter’s enthusiasm was apparent as he recommended the Kobe beef carpaccio and duck skewers, but it was clear he was juggling multiple tables and bar requests. The kitchen’s efficiency shone in preparing the food quickly, yet the timing of deliveries left much to be desired. Drinks, particularly the mint julep, felt like an afterthought—overly sweet and lacking balance, which contrasted with the refreshing yuzu cocktail we were also served. The mix-up in our sushi order added to the sense of controlled pandemonium, though the staff’s apologetic tone and willingness to correct the mistake (even if we kept the wrong dish out of goodwill) showed their commitment to hospitality. The decor, a vibrant blend of neon and tropical motifs, kept the energy high despite the clatter of dishes and overlapping conversations. It’s the kind of place where the ambiance itself feels like part of the meal, with bold colors and playful lighting that complement the fusion of Japanese and South American influences in the menu. While the sushi didn’t wow us, the creativity in other dishes—like the tangy yuzu-infused calamari or the rich, umami-packed miso black cod—hinted at the kitchen’s potential. The edamame, though reliable, seemed almost too basic compared to the adventurous options around us. Overall, Sushi Samba is a destination best suited for those who thrive in lively, dynamic settings. If you’re okay with a rushed pace and the occasional misstep, the standout dishes and lively atmosphere make it worth the experience. However, for a more relaxed meal, consider visiting during off-peak hours or opting for a reservation. The kitchen’s ability to craft bold, flavorful plates (especially the duck skewers and carpaccio) and the fun, Instagram-worthy ambiance earn it a place on my list for experimental dining—though the service and pacing might need a tune-up to truly shine.

The crust is perfectly crispy with a slight char, balancing the juicy toppings. Green peppers add a fresh bite, while the pepperoni delivers bold flavor without being greasy. Service is friendly and quick, even during peak hours. From the first slice to the last, every element shines—Nellos makes pizza-making an art!

Their attention to detail ensures clothes come back looking their best, and their friendly environment makes every visit enjoyable. Even after moving, the drive is worth it for the exceptional service—they’ve become more than a dry cleaner; they’re trusted friends who genuinely care. I’ve recommended them to neighbors and friends, knowing they’ll experience the same warmth and reliability. From handling delicate fabrics with care to remembering small preferences, they’ve never missed a beat. It’s rare to find a business that balances professionalism with such heartfelt hospitality, especially in today’s fast-paced world. Their work ethic and kindness reflect a deep respect for their community, and it’s clear they’d go to any lengths to ensure customer satisfaction. We’ll always choose them, no matter the distance—they’ve earned our loyalty, and we’re grateful to support their family-run business. Five stars, hands down!

The ambiance adds to the charm—cozy, warm, and filled with subtle Vietnamese decor that feels welcoming without being overwhelming. Prices are fair for the portion sizes and quality, making it a great spot for families or casual meals. We also tried the banh mi and spring rolls, both of which were fresh, flavorful, and clearly made in-house with care. The owners even stopped by our table to check in, which added a personal touch that made us feel truly valued. While the restaurant isn’t flashy, its genuine warmth, dedication to detail, and no-compromise approach to hospitality set it apart. It’s the kind of place where you feel like a guest, not just a customer. Whether you’re craving comfort food or looking for a memorable dining experience, this gem deserves a visit—and we’re already excited to return.

The queso sauce is rich yet smooth, perfectly balancing the tender spinach and smoky tortillas. Every bite feels like a celebration of flavor. The staff’s warmth and the vibrant, cozy decor make each visit memorable. Whether it’s a busy weeknight or a special occasion, Abuelos consistently delivers joy—food and all. You won’t leave disappointed!

The risotto was creamy but overwhelmed by an odd, almost burnt lemon zest that clashed with the mushrooms. The enchiladas arrived soggy, as though they’d been reheated improperly, and the spinach tasted oddly raw, like it had skipped the cooking step entirely. For $28, I expected better execution—maybe even a hint of the “contemporary” flair advertised. The service, though friendly, didn’t compensate for the disjointed dishes; our server seemed genuinely baffled when we expressed confusion about the flavors. The wine list was decent, but even the drink couldn’t salvage the meal. While the chocolate cake redemption was a welcome surprise (dense, fudgy, and worth the splurge if you ignore the price), the rest of the experience felt like a gamble. Two stars because the cake’s excellence can’t erase the rest of the missteps, but also because I won’t entirely discredit my taste buds after one visit. Still, I’ll probably stick to dessert next time—and maybe bring my own seasoning.

The staff’s warmth really set the tone—my server even double-checked my order and offered a free side of miso soup as a “welcome back” gesture, which was thoughtful. I tried the new dragon roll (eel and avocado), and while the avocado felt slightly over-ripe, the eel was perfectly grilled with that smoky sweetness I love. The standard veggie roll, though, was just as crisp and fresh as always, a reliable comfort. For mains, the teriyaki salmon was a hit—glazed to perfection, resting on a bed of fluffy white rice. The only real letdown was the edamame, but honestly, it’s easy to overlook one small dip in a meal this solid. I also appreciated the new photo menu; it made choosing rolls less stressful, even if the images made the portions look smaller than they were. While I’d love to see more innovative twists on classics, the core of the menu—like their signature spicy tuna roll or melt-in-your-mouth beef sliders—remains dependable. All in all, the new management hasn’t lost the soul of the place. Between the improved presentation, friendly service, and consistent quality, I’ll definitely be back. Just maybe skipping the edamame for now!

The service was decent, but the menu options feel basic and overpriced for the quality. The guacamole was fresh, though, which was a small win. While it’s a budget-friendly spot for a quick bite, the lackluster flavors and soggy textures make it forgettable. You’ll leave hungry for more, but at least your wallet survives. Stick to cheaper alternatives with better reviews.

The service was efficient but lacked warmth, and the overall vibe felt more like a pit stop than a destination. While the pastrami’s thinness and the lack of casing crunch were disappointments, the fries were a bright spot—crispy and well-seasoned, if a tad greasy. The sports bar area offered decent views of the games, but the cramped seating and loud hum of TVs made conversation difficult. I found it odd that condiments were tucked away behind a kiosk, forcing awkward fetches during the chaos of ordering. For fans of messy, customizable dogs, the nearby Buldogi’s is a better bet—its creative toppings and bolder flavors make a stronger case for the hot dog experience. This spot works if you’re already at Red Rock, but it’s a forgettable stop that leans on convenience over charm. The view of the strip from the parking lot might be the only thing worth the price.

Every taco is a single bite, and the entrees are pitifully small. For $20+, you could feast at a family-run spot on 16th Street. The “chic” ambiance is nice, but no excuse for overcharging. Save your money—this isn’t Mexico City luxury. Authentic flavor, not vanity pricing, is what we crave!

"The house special is bursting with flavor and the perfect balance of sweet and tea. The mango passion fruit was equally refreshing. The staff is super friendly and the prices are great for the quality. Will definitely return!"

The lobby and elevators still feel dated, with worn furnishings that clash with the otherwise tidy rooms. While the bed was comfortable and the Wi-Fi adequate for business, the lack of modern amenities or character makes it forgettable. The monorail is a lifeline to the Strip, but without nearby restaurants or bars, you’ll spend extra on rides. It’s a budget-friendly option for short stays, but in a city where convenience equals experience, this location struggles to justify its existence beyond the price tag.

The portions were average, and while the soft-serve texture was decent, the lack of standout flavors made it forgettable. I’ve had far more creative options at chain froyo spots, which left me underwhelmed. The toppings—mainly standard sprinkles and candy—didn’t inspire much experimentation. What bothered me most, though, was the disorganization. The staff seemed distracted, with children frequently interrupting tasks or playing near customers. It created a casual vibe, but not the welcoming, polished one I’d expect for a dessert spot. While the Yelp deal made the experience slightly worth it, I can’t justify paying full price for mediocrity. For now, I’ll stick to places that prioritize both quality and a cohesive atmosphere. (2.5 stars)

The experience was so jarring that I felt compelled to confront a manager, who, to their credit, seemed genuinely apologetic but offered little beyond a free dessert. When I pressed further about the tongs, they claimed the staff was “overwhelmed” by the lunch rush—a justification that rang hollow given the same negligence had been happening in plain sight for over an hour. As someone who values food safety, I found this not just unhygienic but emblematic of a broader decline in standards. The sushi, once a highlight, tasted rushed and lacked the freshness I’d come to expect. Rolls were underseasoned, and the sashimi seemed rubbery, as if stored too long. Even the sides—typically a reliable comfort—were lukewarm and meager. What broke me, though, was the indifference. When I mentioned this to the manager, they thanked me but failed to acknowledge the tongs as a systemic issue. Meanwhile, other diners—many of whom I recognized as longtime patrons—exchanged glances of shared dismay. This isn’t just a one-off oversight; it’s a pattern. A restaurant built on trust and consistency has allowed complacency to erode its reputation. I used to believe in second chances, but after this, I can’t in good faith return. The memory of those tongs, smeared with debris and indifference, has cost them my loyalty. If they want to win back customers, they’ll need more than a free dessert—they’ll need to start by respecting their guests’ well-being. Until then, their “lunch buffet” has become a cautionary tale.

Here’s a continuation of the review, keeping the tone and structure consistent while expanding on the key points to reach approximately 334 words: --- The rest of the buffet’s food selection left me underwhelmed. While there were classics like sushi, prime rib, and a decent salad bar, the quality felt unremarkable for the price. The sushi, for example, was fresh but lacked the bold seasoning and artistry I’ve seen at other strip buffets. The prime rib was overly seasoned with salt, masking the meat’s natural flavor. Even the salad bar offered only basic options, with no creative dressings or add-ons to elevate it. For a hotel that markets itself as a “premium” dining destination, these dishes felt more like afterthoughts than standout experiences. The lack of communication from staff about the buffet’s limitations was frustrating. If the pasta station is occasionally closed or reserved for VIP guests, there should be clear signage or staff alerts to avoid false hope. Similarly, the sandwich bar’s omission of bread—a basic necessity—seemed like a glaring oversight. I overheard multiple guests expressing the same confusion, which suggests this is a recurring issue rather than an isolated mistake. It’s hard to trust a hotel’s branding when these details are so inconsistent. That said, the desserts genuinely impressed. The chocolate fountain with fresh strawberries and house-made truffles was worth the splurge, and the interactive dessert station (with a chef drizzling caramel and lighting desserts on fire) added a fun, Instagram-worthy touch. I even tried the “molecular gastronomy” dessert—though I’ll admit the experience was more novelty than flavor—but it was enough to make me overlook some of the earlier disappointments. If I had to compare this buffet to others on the strip, it still lags behind. The [insert competitor’s name] offers a similar price point
"Each dish was a hit, especially the kid-friendly options. The staff went above and beyond to make us feel welcome. Can’t wait to bring the family back for another fantastic experience!"

The attention to detail and personalized care at Shine Salon set it apart. Charlton’s expertise and friendly staff created a welcoming atmosphere where I felt truly valued. The price-to-quality ratio is unbeatable—no hidden fees or upsells, just exceptional results. Every strand of my hair feels intentional, and the color is vibrant yet natural. The wait time was worth it, as Charlton prioritized perfection over speed. I’m also impressed by the follow-up care, like the text checking if I’m happy with the outcome. It’s rare to find a salon that blends professionalism with genuine warmth. Shine Salon isn’t just a service—it’s an investment in confidence. I’ll keep referring friends and returning for every cut, color, and style. The quality and results speak for themselves!

The bar fight was a lively, interactive twist on tasting menus—our table cheered as the Blackened Shrimp Lumpia’s smoky, citrusy kick paired flawlessly with Mr. Pineapple’s tropical hoppiness, giving it a clear win. The Monkfish Taco, while flavorful, felt let down by its greasy coating; we’ll test the grilled version another visit. The spring salad, though, was a revelation—crisp greens, tangy vinaigrette, and unexpected textures that danced in harmony (oral orchestra indeed!). The vibe here is casual yet vibrant, with friendly servers who clearly love their craft beer. Perfect for date nights or groups craving inventive eats and a drink in a welcoming spot. Can’t wait to return!

Creative fusion of flavors—try sesame noodles in a burrito! Tons of fresh options; build your perfect dish. Service is friendly, portions generous. A fun twist on comfort food that feels new every visit! The Glendale location is cozy, making it a top spot for innovative, flavorful meals!

The service didn’t help matters—our server seemed disengaged, offering minimal guidance and leaving us to fumble through the menu. For a splurge-worthy spot, the lack of standout elements is baffling. The drinks? Overpriced cocktails with no signature flair. The ambiance, while undeniably sleek and masculine (think navy leather booths and yacht-club bric-a-brac), felt more trying-too-hard than inviting. We left feeling like we’d paid for a photo op, not a meal. Even the wine list leaned toward generic bottles that didn’t elevate the experience. In a city brimming with better options—places where quality justifies the price—STK comes off as a hollow imitation of luxury. Save your cash for a chef-driven spot with actual culinary ambition. Unless you’re there strictly for the “vibes,” which, honestly, wear thin after one underwhelming bite.

The Southern-style brunch menu is a standout, with perfectly flaky buttermilk biscuits and golden syrup drizzle. The coffee is bold and fresh, and the service is friendly and prompt. Every bite feels like a celebration of flavors—creamy, spicy, and sweet all in one. Can’t wait to return!

The food truly stood out—every bite felt thoughtfully crafted. The bison burger was juicy and flavorful, paired perfectly with truffle fries that were crispy and indulgent. Even my partner’s salmon, roasted to perfection with a citrus glaze, impressed. The mac and cheese? A creamy, cheesy dream. Our server, *Jenna*, made excellent drink recommendations, and the table was refilled promptly. The space is cozy yet vibrant, with a mix of modern art and warm lighting that invites lingering. While the lunch crowd was lively, the noise never felt overwhelming. TMI’s attention to detail—from the fresh herbs on the plate to the locally brewed ale sample I’ll try next time—elevates the experience. This isn’t just a replacement for Lisa G’s; it’s a fresh gem. Can’t wait to return for dinner and see how the menu shines under new lights.

Let’s talk about the seasoning, though. That Red Robin rub? It’s like the restaurant’s secret handshake with flavor. Sprinkle it on your burger, and suddenly your meat isn’t just meat—it’s a party in your mouth. I’d go as far as saying it’s the reason the Royal Red Robin transcends its “basic burger with an egg” premise. Plus, the chocolate milkshake? Oh, that’s a whole other level of indulgence. It’s thick, like drinking a milkshake made from chocolate mousse. I’ve had vanilla here too, and it’s so creamy it could probably qualify as a dessert. But here’s the thing: When you pair the shake with that burger and fries, you’re not just eating—you’re *experiencing*. You’re in a food coma zone by the time you reach your desk at 1:15 PM. And yes, let’s get back to those fries. Bottomless, golden, salty perfection. They’re not just for kids—though if you’ve got a small army of rugrats, this place is your brunch savior. Order a burger, and the kids can graze for hours without costing you a fortune. Meanwhile, you’re slathered in ketchup, happily mind-numbing your way through a second helping. I’ve seen people disappear entire baskets by themselves. They’re addictive in the same way potato chips are, except they’re longer and occasionally come with a side of regret (ketchup-smeared shirts and all). But here’s the real compromise: You walk in expecting a basic chain meal, but leave feeling like you scored a cheat-day victory. The lettuce is still a tragedy, but the egg? The seasoning? The shakes? Those fries? They’re the kind of “junk” that makes you forgive the small sins. I still take my lunch crew here, even if I end up stealing half their fries while pretending to make a “strategic move” to “share.” It’s not the healthiest lunch, but hey—at least I’m not at Chili’s.

The menu offered a nice mix of fresh, light options like grilled salmon and quinoa bowls, as well as heartier choices like the avocado-lime chicken, which was juicy and flavorful. The staff was attentive, even during a busy lunch rush, which added to the laid-back yet efficient vibe. While the lack of reusable tableware felt slightly outdated for a health-focused spot, the portions were generous and satisfying. For eco-conscious diners, suggesting a small fee for disposables could encourage sustainability without hassle. Though the absence of calorie counts might deter those tracking macros, the overall quality and price make this a solid pick for a guilt-free meal. I’ll definitely return and recommend it for its balance of taste, convenience, and mindful pricing.

"Service was friendly but a bit rushed due to the high turnout. The beer taps featured both local brews and some unique imports, which was a nice touch. While the crowd made it hard to grab a seat, the lively energy added to the fun. Would definitely return for the music and games, even if I have to wait for a spot."

continued review: The overall experience with Reliable Repair has been nothing short of excellent. Everett’s expertise and dedication to ensuring the repair was thorough and long-lasting truly set this company apart. Beyond just fixing the microwave, he took the time to educate us on how to maintain our appliances, which gave us peace of mind about preventing future issues. His attention to detail—like pointing out the previous installation’s flaws—showed a level of professionalism I haven’t seen in other service providers. What impressed me most was Reliable Repair’s transparency. They clearly explained the repair process, costs, and timelines, which made the entire situation stress-free. While the waiting period for parts was a bit lengthy, the technician kept us informed every step of the way, and the final result justified the patience. The fact that Everett returned the next week to complete the repair with the new parts demonstrated a commitment to customer satisfaction. I also appreciated the company’s follow-up after the service. They asked if we were satisfied and even offered to assist with any other concerns, reinforcing their customer-centric approach. In an industry where rushed fixes and vague explanations are common, Reliable Repair’s integrity and craftsmanship are refreshing.
