I’ve worked in places where speed and consistency are non-negotiable, especially for to-go orders, which typically have a 10–15 minute turnaround at most. The 27-minute delay felt not just inconsiderate but almost disrespectful—especially for parents juggling busy schedules and trying to make the most of a quiet window. I couldn’t help but notice the manager loitering near the kitchen, glancing at tickets but never offering so much as an apology, an update, or even a “Thank you for your patience.” It spoke volumes about their customer service ethos (or lack thereof). Then there was the food itself. While I understand that veggie burgers can be hit-or-miss, my wife’s undercooked beef burger was inexcusable. The patty had raw, spongy sections in the center, and I couldn’t tell if it was due to rushed cooking or poor technique. Mine was barely warm in the middle, like it had been thrown on the griddle for 30 seconds. The buns were stale, and the toppings lacked freshness. For the price we paid ($18 total for two burgers), I’ve had better results from fast-food places with shorter wait times and more care. The final straw was the complete silence after my email. I wasn’t asking for a discount or a grand gesture—just a basic acknowledgment that they heard my concerns. A “Thank you for your feedback, we apologize for the inconvenience” would have gone a long way. But nothing. Not even a bot response. It felt like they didn’t see us as customers, just as obstacles to be ignored. If this is the standard of service “in a busy city,” I’ll stick to restaurants that value both efficiency and respect. To their credit, maybe the dine-in experience is more enjoyable, but until they fix their kitchen timing, communication, and accountability, I can’t recommend this place—especially for to-go orders. Vegas has no shortage of amazing burger joints; shame this one missed the mark on every front. --- This adds ~267 words, emphasizing the lack of communication, food quality, and the broader impact of poor service on customer trust, while keeping the tone consistent with your original frustration and disappointment.

The experience felt personalized and stress-free, which is rare when navigating the overwhelming bridal shopping process. While I ultimately chose a different vendor, the attention to detail here—like the saleslady’s ability to suggest gowns that flattered my body type—was unparalleled. They also offered a range of styles, from classic A-lines to modern, figure-hugging designs, making it a one-stop shop for brides with diverse tastes. The ambiance added to the joy of trying on gowns; soft lighting and elegant decor created a dreamy atmosphere that made each fitting feel special. Though the price range might be higher than some mass-market options, the quality and craftsmanship justified the cost, especially for brides seeking something unique. I also appreciated how they accommodated multiple appointments and rush scheduling when I needed flexibility. For someone who values exceptional service and a curated collection, this shop stands out—even if you end up purchasing elsewhere, the expertise and support make it worth the visit. Central Illinois brides should definitely add this to their list!

The experience was so underwhelming that I left feeling embarrassed I’d wasted money. The burrito’s tortilla was gummy and undercooked, and the cheese tasted overly processed. The tacos had no flavor—just dry, tasteless meat plopped onto lukewarm shells. To make matters worse, the refillable soda cups were barely worth the extra fee, and the “free” chips were stale. For a supposed Mexican spot, the menu lacked authenticity and heart. Don Tortaco’s vibrant salsas and Tacos el Gordo’s fresh, reasonably priced street-style fare feel like a world apart. Save yourself the disappointment and avoid this place entirely—there’s no redemption here, only a textbook example of how *not* to run a restaurant. I’ll never return, and I’ll be warning friends to steer clear.

The menu’s variety was impressive, with everything from sashimi-grade seafood to creative Asian-fusion plates. The teppan table chef was a showman—flipping skewers and crafting flavorful sauces right at our table, making the meal feel like entertainment. We split the three-item combo, and the scallops were indeed massive, perfectly seared, and buttery-soft. The miso black cod and wagyu beef were equally memorable, bursting with umami. Even the sides, like the garlic noodles, were addictive. Our server was attentive without being overbearing, and the lively yet cozy atmosphere made it ideal for families. With portions this generous and quality this high, the reasonable prices feel almost too good. We’ll definitely drive the 8 miles again—it’s a standout gem off the strip!

The staff was dismissive when we explained the issues, insisting we accept replacements despite our objections. The second round was just as bad—burnt, cold, or inedible. Zero regard for customer satisfaction. Do not waste your time or money here. Poor food, worse service, and no accountability. Would not recommend to anyone.

The music was another letdown—repetitive and lacking energy for a place promising a high-energy vibe. The DJ seemed disengaged, playing the same top-40 hits without mixing in anything fresh or crowd-pleasing. On top of that, the lighting was blindingly harsh, with strobes that made it impossible to navigate without stumbling. It felt more like a sensory overload nightmare than a night out. Then there was the crowd. While the reviewer mentioned a "Cirque du Soleil aspect," I didn’t notice any performers or unique staging beyond the usual LED lights and fire dancers at the entrance. Most people were just shoving each other, especially near the bar, which took forever to get through despite the "fast guest list entry" highlight. The staff barely acknowledged the chaos. When I finally got to my friend, she was pale and upset, but no one from management came to check on her or offer assistance. To be fair, the guest list access was a plus—Memorial Day weekend is notoriously packed, and skipping the lines was worth the $50 entry fee. The industrial-chic decor had some cool art installations, but they were hidden in corners and didn’t add much to the overall experience. Honestly, I can see how someone might enjoy this place if they’re into overcrowded spaces and don’t mind overpriced, mediocre drinks. But for me, the stress of battling the crowd, the inconsiderate staff, and the lack of actual fun made it a night to forget. I’ll tolerate going back for friends’ birthdays, but I’ll keep hunting for better options in Vegas. If you’re looking for a club with substance over style, this isn’t it.

The lamb was overcooked and lacked the smoky depth I associate with traditional recipes, while the sides—split peas and collard greens—felt underseasoned, like afterthoughts. Though portions are generous, the muted flavors left me unimpressed, and the hour-long wait between courses tested my patience. Still, the friendly, apologetic staff and the novelty of having Ethiopian fare in town kept it from a lower rating. For now, it’s a decent stop for curiosity, but I’ll likely wait for more options before returning.

The service is friendly and efficient, which adds to the relaxed vibe. The rustic decor feels cozy, making it a pleasant spot for a casual meal. Prices are fair for the portions, though nothing feels overly special. For a quick, no-fuss bite, it works—especially if you stick to breakfast staples or want a heaping plate of pancakes. Just skip the lemonade and opt for coffee instead. All in all, it’s a reliable choice when you’re craving something hearty but can’t be bothered to overthink it.

Continuing the review: To be fair, the menu *did* promise creativity—rolls with bold names and intriguing combinations. However, the execution fell flat. The Philly roll, a classic choice, lacked the fresh, zesty kick I expected from the spicy mayo. The salmon sashimi was overpriced for its small portion and bland flavor, while the "crunch roll" was oddly limp, as if the rice was under-pressed. Even the Vegas roll, typically a crowd-pleaser with its sweet-and-sour tang, tasted like it was swimming in a generic, watered-down sauce. For a place touting “50% off” deals, the quality didn’t justify the already-deeply discounted prices. The gnats at the sushi bar were a dealbreaker, though. Watching them buzz around raw fish and drinks felt like a violation of basic hygiene standards. I couldn’t help but wonder how many other corners of the kitchen were similarly neglected. The indifference from staff didn’t help. After being ignored for 45 minutes, my friend finally flagged down a busboy, who muttered “one second” and vanished. When a different employee finally delivered my water, they didn’t even acknowledge our complaints. It felt like we were invisible. Overall, this place feels like a missed opportunity. Between the subpar food, lack of basic service, and unsettling atmosphere, I can’t imagine bringing anyone back

Their transparent pricing and thorough diagnostics ensure you only pay for necessary repairs. They take time to explain each step, so you feel confident in their recommendations. Both vehicles run smoothly now, and their friendly yet professional demeanor makes every visit a breeze. Highly recommend for anyone seeking trustworthy, no-nonsense auto care!

The lack of genuine engagement left a sour taste, especially when compared to other shops where artists collaborate creatively. Not only did the staff fail to offer guidance, but their indifference suggested a disinterest in nurturing customer relationships. The $50 deposit felt like a barrier, not an investment, and the rushed approach to scheduling—prioritizing efficiency over artistry—underscored their priorities. As for the work on display, the pieces seemed hastily executed, with flat colors and stiff linework that couldn’t justify the premium pricing. Supporting local artists should mean investing in quality and care, not just overhead. If you’re seeking a collaborative, inspiring experience or top-tier craftsmanship, this shop falls short on all counts. Save your time and money for establishments that truly value both their craft and their clients.

The prices are fair for the generous portions, but watch out for occasional errors. Service is friendly and prompt. I’ll definitely return for the rice and chicken shwarma. Just double-check your order to avoid salty surprises. 10/10 for taste and atmosphere, minus one star this time. Can’t wait to visit again!

The staff seemed overwhelmed but offered apologetic smiles. We waited 20 minutes for lukewarm hot dogs and were told the icee machine had been broken for weeks—no alternatives offered. The overpriced snacks (a hot dog for $9?!) felt like a slap in the face after shelling out $25 for tickets. The theaters themselves were decent, with comfy seats and clear screens, but the constant food/drink mishaps ruined the vibe. My kids were hungry, we missed half the previews, and the drive home was silent and sour. Will definitely bypass this location next time. Convenience isn’t worth repeated frustration—especially with a hungry, grumpy crew.

The flamingo lagoon is a standout, offering up-close encounters and photo ops. Families will appreciate the educational elements and interactive exhibits. A peaceful oasis amidst the city’s hustle—don’t rush, savor the magic!

The service was prompt and friendly, though not particularly engaging. Drinks arrived quickly, and the mimosas were decent but unremarkable. We opted for the “brunch combo” to share, which included the frittata and pancakes, but the portion sizes felt smaller than expected for the price. While the pancakes redeemed the meal with their fluffy, buttery texture, the overall experience leaned toward forgettable. The ambiance, as mentioned, is better suited for dinner’s more refined crowd. For the price point, diners might expect a bit more creativity or quality—especially when even the coffee rang up at $6. It’s a solid option if you’re in a hurry, but not a destination worth splurging on.

The service was exceptional—our waitress was attentive yet unintrusive, ensuring our glasses stayed full and our needs met with warmth. The ambiance, with its rustic decor and soft lighting, added a cozy charm to our celebration. My friends raved about their orders too: the smoked brisket was fall-off-the-bone tender, and the seasonal vegetable medley was fresh and vibrant. The coffee paired perfectly with the rich, buttery scones, which were addictive and just warm enough. Even our dessert—fluffy banana bread pudding—delivered a sweet finale. Despite the hearty portions, the prices felt generous, and the staff even gifted us a New Year’s toast as a gesture of thanks. Every detail, from the flavorful food to the genuine hospitality, made this a night to remember. We’ll definitely return for more!

The rest of the experience didn’t get any better. After finally getting my sandwich, I tried to find a seat, but the dining area was a disaster. There were sticky spills on every table, and the floor looked like a war zone of napkins and half-eaten fries. One booth had a suspicious brown stain that I prayed wasn’t what I thought it was. I opted to sit by the window, hoping for some semblance of dignity after the restroom fiasco. As I unwrapped my sandwich, I noticed the employee who propped the door open earlier was still there, chatting with another staff member behind the counter like nothing happened. No apology, no acknowledgment. Not even a “ma’am, please don’t yell at children in front of me while I’m peeing.” It was like they’d collectively agreed to erase the incident from existence. Then, as if the universe wanted to make this day a personal hell, the power flickered. The overhead lights buzzed and died, plunging the place into darkness. The only illumination came from the “Burger King” sign outside and a single flashlight someone pulled out to check inventory. People started murmuring, kids whined, and the dwarf cashier—whose name tag read “Tina”—announced, “We’re gonna have to close the kitchen!” as though she’d personally shut it down with a sledgehammer. I tried to leave, but the exit was suddenly blocked by a man in a delivery van uniform who’d apparently wandered in during the blackout. He was

The service here is friendly and efficient, which adds to the overall appeal despite the less-than-ideal location. The staff seemed genuinely excited about their offerings, which made the experience feel welcoming. While the menu isn’t vast, the focus on quality and flavor shines through. The creamy sauce paired with the fries and sandwich was a standout—zesty, rich, and perfectly balanced. Though I’m not a banana fan in savory dishes, I can see how others might appreciate its sweetness here. For a quick, flavorful meal without the pretense, Chaka Chaka delivers. The small space feels cozy, and the takeout process was seamless. At $12 for the combo, it’s reasonably priced for the quality. I’d return for the fried chicken (if they expand to dinner) and hope they add a few more sides or sauces in time. If you’re craving bold Caribbean-inspired flavors and a no-frills meal, give this place a shot—it’s worth the detour!
The menu offers creative twists on classics, and the lively ambiance pairs perfectly with the attentive staff, making every visit a satisfying, if slightly rushed, experience.

They offer a diverse menu with classics like fried rice and noodles. Prices are reasonable, and portions are generous. The takeout is efficient, ensuring your food arrives hot and fresh. Perfect for a quick, reliable meal—highly recommended!

Multiple calls to customer service only resulted in hours spent on hold and evasive representatives. They even attempted to charge me after I’d terminated my account, further proving their disregard for customers. While the internet technically functions, the constant outages and slow speeds negate any positives. Their business model thrives on misleading contracts and exploiting unsuspecting consumers. I’m furious and feel trapped by their monopolistic control in my area. Do not support a company that treats people this poorly. AVOID comcast at all costs!

The udon was silky and rich, while the Ikura Don burst with briny freshness—both made in-house! The couple’s warm, no-frills service adds charm. Portions are generous for the low prices, and the retro décor feels like a trip to a rural Japan teahouse. Try their miso soup; it’s hearty and packed with seaweed and tofu. Weekday lunch specials are a steal, and they even offer parking nearby. Though small, the menu hits all the right notes for comfort and authenticity. A gem for budget-friendly, heartfelt Japanese fare!

Here’s a continuation of the review, maintaining the tone and focus while adding depth and balance to the critique: --- That said, there are countless aspects of Trader Joe’s that keep us coming back week after week. The produce section is a highlight—fruits and vegetables are consistently fresh, vibrant, and often priced better than at other stores. We especially appreciate their seasonal offerings, like the honeycrisp apples in the fall or the heirloom tomatoes in summer, which elevate home cooking. The store’s unique products, such as their line of international snacks, vegan cheeses, and specialty pantry staples, make grocery shopping an adventure. Their commitment to sustainability, from bulk bins to minimal plastic packaging, also aligns with our values. But when it comes to the meat department, the inconsistency is frustrating. Beyond poultry, we’ve also had issues with ground beef and sausages arriving with off-putting odors or slimy textures. While the seafood counter has generally been reliable (aside from the occasional misstep with salmon), the rest of the deli feels like a gamble. We’ve watched other local markets maintain fresher meat sections, and it makes you wonder if Trader Joe’s prioritizes speed over quality control in this area. The staff is invariably kind and helpful, and we’ve never left a complaint unresolved. Still, repeated refunds for spoiled products don’t inspire confidence. For a brand that prides itself on quality and trust, allowing even one department to fall short feels like a missed opportunity. Perhaps this location’s meat department struggles with inventory turnover, staffing, or training. Whatever the cause, it’s disappointing to see such a beloved store let its standards slip in such a critical area. We’ll keep shopping here for everything but the meat, and we hope the store addresses these issues soon. After all, a grocery store’s ability to provide safe, fresh food should be non-negotiable. If the meat department could match the excellence of the rest of the store, Trader Joe’s would truly earn its stellar reputation in our eyes. For now, though, it’s a 3-star experience for us—solid, but not without flaws.

The service was barely worth the absurd price—our server vanished most of the night, and the “bottles” were half-empty by midnight. We tried to enjoy the view, but the throng of sweaty bodies made it impossible to breathe, let alone appreciate the waterfall. After two hours, we bailed, feeling more stressed than relaxed. If you want a Disneyland vibe without the debt, skip this cash-grab and opt for a less crowded spot. $1600 buys more than just a bad memory.

However, the waitstaff was exceptional—attentive, knowledgeable, and warm, making the dining experience feel special. Still, the dishes felt overpriced for their lackluster execution. I’ll split the stars: 5 for service, 2 for the food. Skip it for a better meal elsewhere on the Strip.

The Westgate’s shortcomings only deepened the longer we stayed. The casino floor was a cacophony of clinking chips and shouting dealers, with staff too preoccupied to address our complaints about the room. The Elvis soundtrack, while campy, morphed from novelty to irritation, especially when it drowned out conversations in the elevator or, ironically, in the restroom. Breakfast was adequate—basic pastries and lukewarm coffee—but the overpriced menu options felt like

The prep was straightforward, and the sedation made the procedure a breeze—I felt groggy but not nauseous. Dr. Patel took time to explain everything, even sharing a few tips to ease post-procedure discomfort. The facility is spotless, with modern tech and a calming vibe. The nurse, "Zombie Girl," was hilarious and kept me calm with her wit. They sent a detailed report within 24 hours, and follow-ups were quick. Whether you’re due for a routine check or have symptoms, this is the place. No more excuses for skipping this life-saving screening! You’ll leave thanking them—trust me!

The staff seems aware but has yet to address the issue, leaving customers with a frustrating, messy ordeal. The cleaning process is slow and ineffective, leaving oil streaks that require hours of scrubbing. Despite repeated visits, no one offers a solution or apology. Avoid this place if you value your car’s condition—stick to a professional detailer where quality matters. Disappointing neglect from a business that should prioritize customer care.

The menu leans into Hawaiian classics with dishes like kalua pork sliders and poke bowls, which I’d love to try next time, though as an accompaniment to the drinks rather than a full meal. The cocktails, however, did impress—a mai tai and a blue hula were refreshing and well-balanced, hinting at potential if the kitchen can deliver similarly strong flavors. While the spot lacks the vibrant energy of nearby chain bars, the charm of its nautical decor, ukulele playlists, and even the aloha spirit etched into the menu board feel authentic. That said, the postcode doesn’t scream “tropical escape”—it’s tucked away in a side street that might deter passersby. Still, if the staff’s enthusiasm and the novelty of a tiki torch-lined bar in a gray city can bridge the gap between its quirky theme and location, this could carve a niche. I’ll revisit with a bigger appetite and a group of friends to see if the space truly invites communal hangouts or if it remains a hidden gem waiting for its crowd. For now, it’s a promising, if quiet, experiment in diversity.

The ambiance left much to be desired—harsh lighting, echoing noises from nearby construction, and a cramped relaxation room with uncomfortable loungers. The pool area, though present, felt more utilitarian than indulgent, with generic tiles and a lack of plush towels or private seating. Even the towel service felt perfunctory, with staff rushing through deliveries rather than offering attentive care. While the massage itself was competently executed, the absence of thoughtful touches—like herbal teas, curated playlists, or even fresh flowers—diminished the sensory experience one expects to justify the price. The contrast between the spa’s efforts to mimic luxury and its execution was jarring. For instance, the steam room lacked the aromatic eucalyptus or soothing music typical at higher-end spas, and the retail area offered overpriced, mass-market products. Ultimately, the Spa at the MGM felt like a checklist of bare-minimum offerings rather than a cohesive, immersive retreat. As someone who values detail-oriented hospitality, I walked away feeling as though I’d paid for adequacy, not exceptionalism. It’s a missed opportunity for a brand that should aspire to set the standard, not merely meet it.

The continued review: As the balding man scribbled on his clipboard, our patience wore thin. When we finally approached the host stand, he sneered, “We’re busy today,” before striding out the door to greet the couple at the curb—clearly white, by their features. My partner and I exchanged uneasy glances. We waited another five minutes, but when the staff continued to ignore our raised hands, we left. Driving home, I felt a mix of anger and sadness. Discrimination like this is inexcusable, especially in a town that prides itself on inclusivity. We’ve supported small businesses for years, but not at the cost of our dignity. Save your time and appetite for places that value *all* customers. This “local favorite” is a farce—one we’ll never return to.

The service was equally stellar—our server was attentive, knowledgeable, and effortlessly chic. Every course felt thoughtfully crafted, from the crispy, golden crust of the chicken to the melt-in-your-mouth Mars bar. Even the cocktails were a revelation; the smoked Old Fashioned arrived with a theatrical flair that made the night feel like a gourmet spectacle. The vibe? A perfect blend of casual fun and refined elegance. Chuck’s signature charisma clearly translates to his restaurant—every bite and interaction radiated passion. If you’re a fan or just crave exceptional food in a vibrant space, this is a must-visit. Five stars, no hesitation. I’m already planning my return!

Continued review: Every bite feels like a celebration! The tapas menu offers creative, globally inspired dishes that hit all the right notes. The margaritas are next-level, with bold flavors that pair perfectly with the food. The vibe is upbeat yet cozy, making it ideal for a fun night out. You’ll leave full, happy, and already planning your return. Two thumbs up—this spot’s a gem! 🌟

The sides were similarly underwhelming—meh. Atmosphere was trendy but cramped. While the staff’s patience saved the experience slightly, I’d skip this place for the overhyped “fancy” factor and opt for a local joint where quality matches the price. Solid for convenience, not for substance. Would pass on returning.

The experience left us feeling undervalued and frustrated. Later, when I tried to ask about the return policy, the next associate barely made eye contact before dismissing me with a one-word answer. Even when my girlfriend signaled she needed help finding a specific section, another associate walked by without acknowledging her. It felt like we were invisible, which is jarring at a store that prides itself on community and customer care. REI’s usual warmth was replaced with indifference, and it’s disappointing to see such inconsistency. I’ve supported this brand for years because of its ethos and quality, but poor service erases the good. If they’re not going to treat all customers with basic respect and helpfulness, the experience becomes transactional at best. We won’t forget this easily, and I’m unsure if we’ll return. The coats might have been perfect, but service is the real product—and today, it was lacking.

The kitchen’s alchemy transforms simplicity into transcendence—consider the delicate *oeufs en meurette*, a nest of poached eggs basking in a reductions that whispers Burgundy’s terroir, or the *tarte Tatin* that balances burnt sugar’s caramelized fury with apple’s tart serenity. Each dish is a symphony of contrasts: precision and spontaneity, tradition and innovation. The service, too, is a ballet of discretion—linen-clad attendants anticipate needs before they’re spoken, yet never intrude on the intimate dance of knife, fork, and plate. Wine pairings here are not mere accompaniments but conspirators in the experience. The sommelier’s selections—whether a mineral-driven Chablis or a velvety Pomerol—elevate each bite, their nuances mirrored in the chef’s artistry. Time dissolves in this sanctuary; hours pass unnoticed as courses unfold like chapters in a love letter to French cuisine. The finale, a procession of *macarons* from Ladurée’s cousin in a glass cloche, is less a closing than a reverent coda. Joel Robuchon’s is not a meal—it is a pilgrimage. One leaves not just satiated, but transformed, with a renewed belief in the power of food to evoke wonder, to make the ordinary sacred. Yes, your arteries may protest, but your soul will thank you.

The continued review could be: The continued review: Let’s talk about that window. Not the kind where you order a pepperoni slice and a Diet Coke. This was a slat of concrete with a small, grated opening—like a prison cell with free cheese sticks. The employee behind it was all hoodie and no personality, handing pizzas off with a gloved hand that never once smiled. And the lighting? Dim, flickery, and utterly uninviting. The entire place felt like a scene from a crime documentary. Meanwhile, the “Scary Guy” had migrated to the side of the building, still twitching, but now muttering to himself. I kept backing up, clutching my box like it was a life raft in a shark tank. The staff seemed oblivious—or indifferent. No one offered to call police, ask if I needed help, or even switch to a different pickup lane. I made it to my car, heart pounding, and didn’t stop driving until I got home. The pizza? Mediocre. Warm, yes, but not worth the adrenaline rush. The whole ordeal made me wonder: Why does Pizza Hut even let customers pick up orders at places like this? Is there a policy that says, “If you can’t deliver, force them to park in a parking lot adjacent to a window that’s more fortress than convenience”? Lesson learned: Next time, I’ll wait for delivery—even if it takes an hour, or I have to wait until sunrise. Safety first, folks. Pizzas can wait. This one? Never.

The inconsistency of the branding was glaring—how can a place serve mass-produced Bud Light while touting an “Organic Menu”? It raised questions about their priorities. When we asked the server about the organic options, they shrugged and said, “Most things can be made with organic ingredients if you ask.” But the menu didn’t reflect that flexibility, and no one corrected our assumption when we ordered the “organic” dish from the kids’ menu. The pricing also felt off: entrees hovered around $25-$35, yet the portions were modest, and ingredients felt unremarkable. My partner’s “artisan” burger, for instance, used pre-formed patties and generic buns. While the fries and avocado spread were fresh and well-seasoned, they were served in tiny portions, which made the $12 price tag for the fries taste even more absurd. The service was rushed and disengaged, as if the staff also felt the disconnect between the restaurant’s identity. If you’re curious, order the fries and skip the rest—but don’t expect the organic promise to deliver. Let this place’s name and neon signs be a lesson: always check the menu before trusting the signage.

The menu offers creative combos like truffle cream with grilled chicken and spinach, or a spicy kick with jalapeños and cheddar. While prices lean toward mid-range, the generous portions feel satisfying, especially when paired with a well-mixed sauce. Staff are friendly and game to help craft custom orders, which makes experimentation fun. Though I haven’t hit *macaroni heaven* yet, the flexibility and quality keep me coming back. It’s a solid, if not entirely unique, spot for a hearty, customizable meal with friends or family.

The charm of Republica Empanada extends beyond its flavorful offerings—its warm, inviting ambiance makes you feel instantly at home. Despite its compact size, the space is thoughtfully designed with rustic décor, soft lighting, and a cozy communal table that fosters a sense of community. The staff’s genuine enthusiasm for their menu items is infectious; Heidi, our server, not only guided us to stellar choices but also shared stories about the origins of certain dishes, adding a personal touch to the meal. For those seeking lighter fare or dietary accommodations, the menu’s variety shines. The gluten-free and vegetarian options, like the spinach and feta empanada I chose, are crafted without compromise. Even the sides and appetizers—think house-made bread with garlic butter or a vibrant quinoa salad—exude quality, showcasing fresh, thoughtfully sourced ingredients. The beverage selection, while rooted in classic sodas and teas, offers unexpected delights like Jarritos’ zesty flavors and a house-made lemonade that’s tangy and just sweet enough. What truly sets this spot apart is its ability to balance casual comfort with culinary creativity. The “Jalapeno Cilantro Ranch” sauce, a house specialty, elevates every bite, blending herbal brightness with a hint of spice that lingers just long enough. And let’s not forget the desserts, which are nothing short of transcendent. The fig and caramel empanada, with its sweet-and-savory interplay of mozzarella and dulce de leche, is a revelation—proof that this tiny kitchen is anything but limited in imagination. Prices are refreshingly reasonable for the quality and creativity, making it an accessible splurge for any night of the week. Whether you’re here for a quick bite or a leisurely dinner with family, Republica Empanada delivers an experience that lingers longer than the meal itself. My daughter, already a convert, has declared this her “new favorite place,” and I couldn’t agree more. With its heartfelt service, inventive flavors, and dedication to satisfying every craving (even the sweet ones), this hidden gem has earned a permanent spot on my list of must-returns. Pro tip: Arrive hungry but leave room to try *at least* three empanadas—your taste buds (and your family) will thank you!

The moment I step inside, I’m hit with the scent of garlic, oregano, and nostalgia. The ambiance? Rustic-chic, with wine bottles and twinkle lights that make me feel like I’ve time-traveled to Nonna’s kitchen. The service? Impeccable—our server knew my order before I did, like a food medium channeling my carb cravings. The lasagna? A symphony of layers, so rich it defies physics. The carbonara? Creamy, smoky, and somehow pure comfort in a bowl. Even the tiramisu tastes like a memory you forgot you loved. Oh, and the bill? A “hassle” my card didn’t mind. If this place opened in California, I’d max out three credit cards just to build a shrine. You’re my culinary soulmate—flaky, indulgent, and forever my *mangia-mangia* muse. Grazie, bellissimo! 🍝✨

The toppings were equally disheartening—cold, bland, and sparse, as if someone tossed them on halfheartedly. The cheese was rubbery and overcooked, leaving large charred patches that made eating a chore. I’ve had better results using a microwave for leftover frozen pizza. Their “Chicago style” gimmick reeks of inauthenticity; a deep-dish pie should have a sturdy, doughy crust, not this brittle, overbaked shell. The manager’s smug admission that a grocery-store pizza would’ve sufficed was the final insult. Save your time and money—opt for a local pizzeria that actually respects its craft. This place is a farce, and their customers deserve far better. I won’t be returning, and I’ll warn anyone within earshot to avoid their “joke” of a menu.

The eye doctor at Costco was great. Eye exam was only $55 and they really took their time and did a complete exam. Worked great with my kids and I didn’t have to wait at all! But what I was *totally* pleased with was the eyeglasses department! My mom has terrible eyesight and we have to get her new glasses every six months. At other places, shopping for her glasses was a nightmare—over $500, plus they’d try to upsell her on unnecessary upgrades. So I brought her to Costco, worried they might not handle her special lenses. I couldn’t have been more wrong. The staff was incredible—they not only matched her prescription but recommended digital progressive lenses we’d never considered because of the cost. At Costco, it was just part of the standard package! They also explained how other shops inflate prices by adding “premium” features that are actually industry basics. The employees were patient, knowledgeable, and even helped us save money by reusing her existing frames (which worked perfectly!). In the end, the glasses that should’ve cost over $500 came in at just $160. We’re already planning to come back next time—maybe even skip the frames and go straight to a new pair for an even bigger discount. Honestly, I can’t overstate how refreshing it is to find a place that’s both affordable and trustworthy. If you’ve been overcharged or stressed by the eyewear process, Costco is a lifesaver. Five stars all around!

The continued review: The rest of the buffet spread was equally disconcerting. The dessert section had a single condiment cup for multiple shared items—like fresh fruit and cake—which seemed like a breeding ground for bacteria. I couldn’t help but notice a fly hovering near the salad bar, and the staff didn’t appear to monitor the time stamps on displayed items. As someone who prioritizes cleanliness, these lapses were alarming. While the restaurant’s ambiance was cozy, the lack of attention to detail in hygiene overshadowed any comfort. On the food front, beyond the chicken mishap, the pork dishes were over-salted, making them difficult to finish. The rice was under-seasoned, and the vegetables lacked freshness, though the fish soup’s broth was commendable—rich and aromatic, a highlight of the meal. Unfortunately, my focus on avoiding germs made enjoying the food a challenge. I also noticed the kitchen’s visibility from the dining area. While open kitchens can be a selling point, the cooks handled raw meat and vegetables in close proximity without gloves, and the floor had a suspiciously damp patch near the prep area. It’s hard to trust food safety when such basics aren’t addressed. To the management: Investing in staff training, updating the sneeze guards, and ensuring proper food handling protocols could transform this place into a more trustworthy dining option. The flavors, while not stellar, aren’t beyond redemption—especially if paired with a commitment to cleanliness. I hope this feedback is received as constructive. Fix the hygiene issues, and I’d be happy to revisit and revise my assessment. For now, though, I can’t recommend the buffet to anyone prioritizing health and safety.

The lemonade, while fresh, was overwhelmingly sweet, drowning out any citrus flavor. Dessert was a gamble—the mint chip ice cream tasted more like mint syrup than ice cream, leaving a cloying aftertaste. The ambiance didn’t help: clashing neon lights and mismatched music made conversation feel like shouting. Despite ordering late, the meal dragged as the waitress seemed lost in her own world. For the prices charged, the experience felt transactional rather than memorable. Between the hit-or-miss food and lackluster service, it’s hard to justify returning, especially when better alternatives exist nearby. A forgettable night overall.

The final straw, though, was the lack of basic courtesy. When I asked a staff member for help finding a matching pair of leggings, they shrugged and said, “It’s all on the racks—figure it out.” No guidance, no suggestions, just disengagement. For a brand that prides itself on community and “feel-good” vibes, it’s baffling that their frontline staff doesn’t reflect that ethos. I get that Lululemon isn’t for everyone, but when you spend top dollar, you want both quality *and* respect. The headband incident alone felt like a bait-and-switch—promised functionality, no return policy, and zero accountability. And the “showroom-only” line? It’s frustrating when local stores prioritize brand image over practicality, like ignoring cash-paying customers who just want to support local business. I’m not the only one who’s had these gripes. A quick scroll through reviews shows similar complaints: rigid policies, aloof employees, and products that don’t live up to the hype. It’s a shame, because the gear itself isn’t terrible—I just want a smoother experience for the price. Lucy, while cheaper, has a better return policy and actually stocks cash registers in all stores. Maybe Lululemon needs to revisit their customer service training. Until then, I’ll stick with brands that value my dollars and my time equally. Two stars for the products, one for the service—and zero for the effort to fix either.

To say I’m disappointed is an understatement. As regulars, we’ve always received consistent quality and attention, so this experience felt especially jarring. After the kitchen mishaps, we tried to salvage the visit by asking for coffee refills, but the server barely acknowledged us, focusing instead on wiping already clean counters. When I finally flagged her down to address the plate of inedible food, her tone was defensive—like the issue was *my* fault for not “screaming” the order louder. She begrudgingly took the plate, only to return with a microwaved “bacon” that fell apart instantly and eggs that were more charred than cooked. At this point, I just wanted to leave, but the bill arrived before we could even flag her down again. Paying for a meal we couldn’t finish felt like the final insult. The owner should be embarrassed—this isn’t just bad service; it’s a complete disregard for customers. We’ll never return, and we’ll be warning our friends. For a place that prides itself on being a local favorite, this was a soul-crushing reminder that even well-established spots can lose their way. Save your time and appetite somewhere else.

The explanation left me feeling ignored and frustrated. It seemed dismissive of a genuine concern, and I’d expect more accountability, especially since I invested in a mid-range wiper. While the car wash quality is solid, this interaction—coupled with repeated upselling—has me reconsidering my loyalty. I’ll likely seek a provider that prioritizes clear communication and customer trust over pushy sales tactics. It’s a shame, as the potential for good service exists, but these missteps overshadow it.

This isn’t just bad business—it’s predatory. The owner’s excuse about “doubling toppings” is a lie. A half-half pizza should average the price of the two toppings, not add them together. For example, if supreme is $8.50 and Hawaiian is $6.50, a half-half should be around $7.50, not $13.50. His math is only valid if he’s ripping you off, and he’s clearly mastered the art of confusion. What’s worse? His smug arrogance. He acted like I *should* be grateful for his “deal,” as if his twisted logic isn’t completely unethical. No one wants double cheese or meat on one half when they specifically ordered a balance. It’s not just about the price—it’s about the principle. You don’t bait-and-switch customers by hiding rules you make up at pickup. I’ve dined at dozens of pizza places, and *none* operate this way. The fact that other Little Caesars locations in the area don’t charge scams like this proves this owner is an outlier—and a fraud. His store is likely padding profits by exploiting confused or rushed customers who don’t check receipts. Well, I’m not one of them. This isn’t a “local character” thing—this is theft. If you value your money, avoid this location. Call ahead to confirm pricing before ordering, and if this happens to you, walk out. The owner clearly thinks he can weaponize customer service, but online reviews ensure his lies don’t go unchallenged. Save your cash and your sanity. Your local pizza joint shouldn’t feel like a confidence game.

The rest of the menu was equally impressive—think fresh, inventive small plates that begged to be shared. My friends raved about the calamari, which was tender and perfectly crispy, and the truffle fries had a rich depth that made them unforgettable. The staff was attentive, though the prices felt a tad steep for the portion sizes. That said, the dim lighting, eclectic playlist, and outdoor patio made it a great spot for casual conversation or people-watching after sunset. While the bar scene definitely draws a crowd, I’d love to see the restaurant capitalize on its culinary strengths during the day. If they promoted their kitchen more, I think they’d attract foodies like myself who’d happily return for the arancini alone. It’s a hidden gem—just not one you’ll stumble upon if you’re not looking for it after dark!

I can’t wait to bring my pups back! The team also took time to check for ticks and gave them a thorough bath, which my dogs seemed to enjoy. Pricing was fair for the quality, and Lilac even offered tips on maintaining their coats between visits. The Yelp discount made it even better—I’ll definitely be a repeat customer. If you want a stress-free, top-notch grooming experience, this is the place! Five paws up! 🐾

The fish tacos were dry and overcooked, lacking the freshness expected at a seafood spot. Service is glacial, with waitresses barely acknowledging tables. The dim lighting and tinny music only amplify the stale, grease-heavy air. While the ceviche is worth a visit, the exorbitant beer prices ($9 for a Modelo) and overall grime make it a tough sell. Save your appetite—and your wallet—for a place that delivers on its promises.

The location is unbeatable—right on the Strip, yet the room felt serene with floor-to-ceiling windows overlooking the dazzling skyline. The "Love Box" was a sweet surprise: filled with chocolates, champagne, and a heartfelt note—it added a romantic touch! 🎉 The casino floor was vibrant, with modern games and no harsh smoke, making it a pleasure to explore. Dining options range from casual bites at the Poolside Bistro to upscale steaks at **Pistache**—something for every craving. The pool area is a highlight too, with a lively vibe and cabanas offering shade. Staff went above and beyond, from arranging a spontaneous birthday surprise to ensuring our room was spotless. While the price is higher than Excalibur, the luxury, attention to detail, and unforgettable experiences justify it. Mandalay Bay isn’t just a hotel—it’s a destination. Can’t wait to return! 💒✨

The wifey and I are still on our Indian kick. Very clean and inviting inside, we were there about 6pm on Friday night and there were 2 or 3 other couples there. We started with the “Chef’s Assorted Appetizer,” which was a fantastic way to sample the variety. The samosa had a crisp, flaky shell with a spicy lentil filling that burst with flavor—exactly what we hoped for. The chicken pakora stood out, with tender, spiced chicken chunks that retained juiciness despite the crispy coating. The onion bhaji, though, was a revelation: light, airy, and packed with a tangy, slightly sweet flavor that balanced the richness of the other starters. The vegetable pakora (sliced potatoes) was solid but a bit standard—nothing to write home about. For our meal, we always seem to get way too much food, but we’re not afraid of having leftovers. The portions here are hearty, and the pricing felt fair given the quantity. **FISH VINDALOO (swordfish):** The fish chunks were perfectly cooked, flaking apart with a delicate, meaty texture. There was no “fishy” aftertaste, which is a win. The vindaloo sauce, while decent, leaned a bit one-note—bright and tangy with vinegar notes, but lacking the deep complexity or heat we associate with the classic Goan dish. Still, it paired well with the rice and naan. **PANEER TIKKA MASALA:** This was the standout for me. The paneer was perfectly grilled and creamy, with a smooth, melt-in-your-mouth texture (no gritty bits, a common misstep). The masala sauce was rich, aromatic, and layered with spices—cardamom, cloves, and a hint of creaminess that elevated the whole dish. A must-order for non-meat eaters. **VEGETABLE BIRYANI:** Satisfying but unremarkable. The biryani had a decent saffron aroma and a balance of veggies, but the portion size felt smaller compared to other Indian restaurants we’ve visited. I’d love to see more whole spices or fried onions in the rice to amp up the authenticity. **NAAN & BASMATI RICE:** The plain naan was soft

The store’s layout can feel overwhelming, but the sheer volume of options—from trendy apparel in Pink to the latest tech gadgets—makes it worth the hunt. While prices are slightly steeper than nearby retailers, the exclusive collections and frequent sales justify the splurge. The Beauty section, in particular, stocks niche brands you won’t find elsewhere. It’s not the friendliest space, but if you’re a thrill-seeker who values choice over service, this spot still reigns supreme. Just don’t expect a warm welcome..... or a shopping cart without a dent! ^_^*~

The attention to detail at Tailwinds truly sets it apart. The staff is consistently friendly, knowledgeable, and clearly passionate about animals, which is evident in how well they handle dogs of all personalities. They maintain a clean and organized environment, with thorough daily disinfecting of play areas and restrooms, which puts owners at ease. The safety protocols are reassuring—GPS-tracked fencing, ID tags for each guest, and staff who know every dog by name. They even accommodate special requests, like extra cuddle time for anxious pets or private play sessions for more reserved dogs. Their optional training workshops for owners are a bonus, offering practical tips on behavior and bonding. On pick-up days, my dog is always cheerful, free of stress, and often napping after a full day of activity. The transparent communication, from real-time photos to prompt responses, ensures you feel connected to your pet. For a balance of fun, care, and professionalism, Tailwinds is unmatched. Every visit reinforces why I trust them with my fur baby—no questions asked.

**Continuation of the Review:** This experience left me deeply frustrated and disheartened. Having trusted the practice for years, I expected the same level of professionalism and care, especially with my children’s oral health. The lack of communication from the new dentist was

The staff appeared disinterested and disorganized, with no effort to assist or even acknowledge our presence. Despite the busy atmosphere, no one prioritized customer needs—orders were slow, and the lack of basic hospitality was glaring. A place in a prime location should strive to exceed expectations, not frustrate guests. The indifference and neglect left us feeling unappreciated and disrespected. If service is this subpar, even the best ambiance or menu can’t redeem the experience. Save time and skip this spot—prioritize businesses that value their patrons.

The ambiance, while upscale, felt oddly uninviting, with harsh lighting that clashed with the otherwise elegant decor. Presentation of the dishes was average—nothing visually striking to justify the menu prices. My partner’s salmon, though cooked perfectly, lacked seasoning depth, and the accompanying herb butter did little to elevate it. The sides, including asparagus and creamed spinach, were under-seasoned and forgettable, offering no hint of the creativity one might expect at this price point. Drinks arrived promptly, and our server was courteous, but the rushed attention suggested a focus on efficiency over genuine hospitality. Even as the sole diners, we were left waiting minutes between courses, as if the staff were still on shift rather than tailoring the experience. While the mozzarella salad (fresh, crisp, and lightly dressed) was worth ordering, the meal overall felt like a cautionary tale of overpriced mediocrity. Save your money for a place where flavor and value align—this establishment clearly hasn’t earned its reputation.

From the moment we walked in, the staff’s kindness and expertise put us at ease. After Charlie’s initial treatment, Dr. Davis stayed late to run additional tests, ensuring his more serious condition was addressed thoroughly. They kept us informed every step of the way, answering all our questions with patience and clarity. Even after the appointment, the team followed up to check on his recovery progress. The genuine care they showed—not just for the animals, but for our emotional well-being as pet parents—made an already tough situation feel manageable. Between the thorough medical care, compassionate communication, and follow-through, Adobe has earned our trust completely. We’ll never go anywhere else! 🐾

The bar’s lack of basic service and amenities is jarring, especially given the establishment’s focus on a relaxed, adult-oriented atmosphere. While the cigar selection remains top-notch—well-stocked, reasonably priced, and with knowledgeable staff—the bar feels neglected. The bartender’s apathy bordered on unprofessional, with no initiative to engage or ensure customer comfort. Despite this, the cigar shop itself is a gem, offering a curated experience that justifies the visit. If you’re there for cigars, stick to the shop and skip the bar entirely. The disconnect between the two spaces is stark, but the quality of the cigars alone keeps me coming back, albeit with lowered expectations for the bar’s future.

The location is unbeatable—right in the heart of Edinburgh’s historic Old Town, steps from the Royal Mile and just across the street from the Castle. Despite the vibrant energy of the area, the hotel’s interior was refreshingly calm, save for the clatter of the overhauled lobby’s sleek, minimalist design. While I appreciate modernization, the redesigned space felt sterile compared to the warm, timeless charm the original layout might have preserved. Still, the staff’s attentiveness made up for it. From the concierge who suggested a tucked-away pub with the best local ale to the housekeeping team that restocked the mini-bar daily (including a small but thoughtful stash of regional snacks), the service elevated the stay. My only gripe? The nightly key-check at the entrance. While I get the safety rationale, it felt oddly intrusive at 2am, especially after a night of exploring Edinburgh’s famed pubs. A quick scan at the desk would’ve sufficed instead of requiring a full “present your key” theater. The free drink vouchers were a nice touch, though I’d have preferred a more flexible executive lounge access (or even a tiny in-room fridge for that pre-dawn snack). Overall, the mix of luxury, convenience, and Edinburgh’s magic made this a memorable stop. Would I return? Absolutely—if only to argue with the lobby redesign and reclaim my rightful view of the Castle from that top-floor desk. The 5-star tag feels justified, even if the hotel still needs to figure out whether it’s a relic of old-world charm or a neon-lit future.

The rest of our experience followed a similar pattern of missed opportunities. While the ambiance was cozy and the seating comfortable, the lack of attentiveness from the staff was glaring. Our server seemed disinterested, barely acknowledging our follow-up questions about our main courses. When we finally received our food, the inconsistencies in preparation were disappointing. The chicken Caesar salad, though passable, felt underwhelming for the price, and the pizza’s blandness suggested either poor ingredient quality or rushed cooking. The “Panini” was a particularly sad affair—dry, undercooked bread that crumbled at the touch, with meatballs that tasted more like pre-packaged convenience food than a thoughtfully made dish. What stood out most was the disconnect between the restaurant’s potential and its execution. For instance, while the Kentucky Mule cocktail was a bright spot (fresh, well-balanced, and worth the $9), it felt like the only deliberate effort to please. The rest of the meal suggested a lack of oversight or passion in the kitchen. Even the private dining areas, which could have been a draw for larger groups, seemed neglected, with mismatched tableware and dim lighting that made sharing meals feel awkward. In a neighborhood brimming with restaurants that prioritize both quality and hospitality, this spot struggles to justify its menu prices. The combination of indifferent service, lackluster flavors, and inconsistent execution makes it hard to return. Unless there’s a significant overhaul in both kitchen and front-of-house operations, I’d steer clear—and spend that $30+ on a meal that actually lives up to the hype.

The staff was friendly and attentive, making the tiny space feel cozy despite the bustle. Everything on the menu felt thoughtfully crafted—the ricotta added a creamy, tangy balance to the sweet blueberries, and the pancakes were cooked to golden perfection. I also tried their house-made maple syrup, which was rich and subtly spiced. While the portions were modest, the quality shone through. The minimalist decor and soft music added to the relaxed vibe. It’s a bit pricier than average, but the exceptional taste and ambiance make it worth the splurge. Definitely recommend for a special morning treat or a quick, elevated bite. Would happily return!

The ambiance has also taken a hit—now it’s a chaotic echo chamber of clinking cups and loud conversations, making focus impossible. The new menu feels stripped down; classics like their cinnamon-spiced cold brew vanished, replaced by generic options. Prices? A large cold brew now clocks in at $6.50, while a hot coffee maxes out at $4.50—insulting, considering the portion sizes shrunk. Service feels rushed, like staff are just waiting to clock out. I miss the baristas who remembered my name and order. Still, kudos to the coffee on tap: their caramel-infused pour-over and dark chocolate roast are solid, worth sampling if you’re curious. But for consistency? Nope. I’ll stick to places that prioritize quality and atmosphere over corporate tweaks. This used to be a haven; now it’s just another overpriced stopgap. Sad, really.

Moreover, the service was lackluster; our server seemed disengaged and offered no recommendations. The atmosphere was unremarkable, with a cluttered layout that felt rushed. For the price, we expected more attention to detail and fresher ingredients. The sushi prioritized quantity over quality, with overpriced rolls that overwhelmed the palate. I’ve had better sushi at half the cost in local spots, where the fish was fresher and flavors more authentic. While a one-time mishap can't be ruled out, the mediocrity and lack of redeeming qualities make a return hard to justify. Nori remains my top choice for a satisfying meal.

The flavors, while unique, had a “try it and see” vibe. I sampled the lavender honey and was intrigued—it balanced floral notes with a hint of sweetness, but the texture felt a tad icy, which made me wonder about the freeze-thaw cycles. The “burnt caramel” flavor? A winner. It had that perfect gooey, charred-sugar depth I crave. I’d also deduct a star for the self-serve model—the tubs aren’t always chilled evenly, so if you scoop too aggressively, you’re stuck with a gloppy cone. Service was lukewarm. The staff was friendly enough, but the manager’s lack of concern about the fly issue (he casually swatted one and shrugged) left me underwhelmed. That said, the kid next to me raved about their “unicorn sprinkles” and left with a grin, so maybe I’m overthinking. Hygiene is a dealbreaker for me, and the flies were a red flag. On a second visit, they’d fixed the window screens and scrubbed the bar—big improvement! I’ll give them the benefit of the doubt. The rotating flavors (try the seasonal gingerbread during December!) and Stoelting’s nostalgic charm keep me coming back. Still, for the price, I’d expect a smoother, more consistent experience. Maybe third time’s the charm? I’m hopeful. If you’re a froyo purist, this might not be your spot. But if you like experimenting with bold flavors and supporting a classic hometown brand, it’s worth a scoop—or three.

The once-vibrant atmosphere now feels like a ghost of its former self. Our entrees—supposedly a “signature dish” of miso-glazed black cod and “house-special” sushi rolls—were forgettable, with the fish tasting slightly off and the rice bland, lacking the umami punch we’d come to expect. Even the side of wasabi arrived lukewarm, as though it had been sitting out all day. The lack of attention extended to the presentation; a delicate tamago roll was half-crushed, and the tempura flakes on our shrimp dish looked reheated, not freshly fried. To compound the disappointment, our server showed zero initiative to check in, even when we flagged a spilled sauce or a dish that had gone cold. When we finally flagged him down near the end, he shrugged and muttered, “You’re still eating, so it’s fine,” before disappearing again. It’s a stark contrast to last year, when the staff felt invested in making our evening special. The Sushi Room’s decline feels emblematic of a place that’s lost its way—prioritizing efficiency over hospitality, and cutting corners on both the plate and the service. For a spot that once drew raves for its innovation and charm, this feels like a tragic misstep. If this is the new standard, it’s hard to imagine returning. Save your appetite—and your disappointment—for somewhere that still remembers how to earn its guests’ loyalty.

The process felt entirely out of my hands—no one followed up, and I’m still unsure when, or if, my order will be resolved. Despite the delicious food I’ve enjoyed here, this experience left me feeling undervalued as a customer. Poor communication and a lack of accountability overshadowed the quality of the product. I’d love to support this place again, but how can I trust the process after being ignored and overcharged? If they’d handled the mistake with empathy, maybe I’d still be a loyal customer. As it stands, this will be my last online order.

The entire experience felt like a circus, not a restaurant. The "gowned" servers (think white coats and name tags) added a pseudo-medical vibe that only made the greasy food feel more unappetizing. The single bypass burger? A leaden, artery-clogging abomination that tasted like it had been sitting under a heat lamp for days. The fries, if you can even call them that, were rock-hard on the outside, gray and soggy inside—like eating bread soaked in sadness. And the "lard" comment isn’t hyperbole; the smell hit me before I even took a bite. The photos taken by employees at the window were invasive, like being filmed during a personal failure. I half-expected a “before and after” weight chart to pop up on the wall. Meanwhile, the staff’s forced cheer (“Enjoy your meal!”) felt like mockery. Honestly, the only thing redeemable was the novelty. If you’re into edgy, anti-culinary statements or need a viral TikTok moment, this might scratch that itch. But for actual sustenance? Skip it. My stomach’s still sending me revenge texts. 🚨 #BypassTheBypass

The overpriced mains were cold, bland, and poorly presented. Overcrowded stations left us waiting for scraps, while “premium” options like salmon were rubbery. Service was nonexistent—staff vanished as fast as they appeared. For the price, it’s a shameless cash grab. Skip it; Vegas has better buffets, but this? A total waste of time and money. Worst meal for my buck.

This was absolutely unacceptable! After being denied coverage, I called multiple times to appeal the decision, but the staff at the office was dismissive and refused to assist me in navigating the insurance process. When I finally explained my daughter’s fever, vomiting, and dehydration, they still refused to accommodate us unless I paid out-of-pocket. As a parent, it’s terrifying to be told your child can’t receive care because of money. The manager’s callous attitude was the final straw—they even suggested I was being “dramatic” for advocating for my child. I was forced to take her to urgent care, where the doctor confirmed her severe dehydration and prescribed IV fluids. The cost? Thousands of dollars more than I could afford, all because this office prioritized profits over patients. I’ve been with this practice for years and trusted them, but this experience has shattered any confidence I had. Every other pediatrician I’ve researched seems to care more about efficiency and revenue than compassion. I’m warning others because no child’s health should be a bargaining chip. We’re now switching to a clinic with a reputation for kindness and transparency. If you want *just* your money, take it from me—this place is not worth the emotional or financial toll.

The meal was decent—vermicelli was fresh, but the broth lacked depth and the eggrolls were greasy. It’s a convenient pick for a quick bite, yet feels like a simpler version of the vibrant flavors southern California Vietnamese joints deliver.

The portions are generous, and the flavors are authentically vibrant—perfect for families or groups sharing. The friendly staff adds to the warm vibe. Even the smaller side orders, like the crispy empanadas, are bursting with flavor. While the original supersized desserts might have been indulgent, the slightly smaller size still satisfies without feeling greedy. A must-visit for anyone craving hearty, well-crafted Mexican fare in a cozy, welcoming setting. Don’t skip the homemade guacamole either—it’s a standout!

The food was so good that I nearly overlooked the chaos in the kitchen. Watching staff play with phones, touch faces, and dive into making pizzas with unwashed hands was utterly off-putting. It felt like a daycare, not a restaurant. While the arugula salad and pizzas were exceptional, the negligence in hygiene and professionalism overshadowed everything. This place has potential but needs strict management and training. A chef’s skill means little if the team can’t respect basic cleanliness. Hope they improve—great concept wasted by poor execution. Would avoid until changes are made.

The staff here is condescending, the prices have doubled since my first visit, and the false accusation of theft was just the final blow. No evidence, just paranoia and poor customer service. Every time I’ve come in, it’s been a battle. Save yourself the headache and skip this sh*t hole. Overpriced, unwelcoming, and clearly a trap for tourists. Not worth one cent of your time.

The interactive wine menu, while visually engaging, had a few hiccups. While I appreciated the tech-savvy approach, the fact that two of the featured wines were unavailable was a bit jarring. My waitress, however, recommended a full-bodied red to pair with the surf and turf, which was a nice touch. Though the suggestion was thoughtful, the bottle itself—while decent—didn’t justify the premium price tag. Service, as mentioned, was friendly and attentive, with our server checking in frequently to ensure we felt celebrated. The manager even stopped by to present the table card, which was a lovely gesture. That said, the inconsistencies in the food quality left a sour note. The rubbery lobster and overcooked steak hinted at rushed preparation, which felt especially disappointing for an anniversary meal where we’d expected a bit more care. The ambiance was warm, with soft lighting and a rustic-chic decor that added to the special-occasion vibe. However, the dining room seemed slightly under-staffed during our visit, which may have contributed to the uneven food execution. Our server managed to keep things pleasant with charm and efficiency, but even the best service can’t fully compensate for subpar dishes when the price is steep. We skipped dessert, as the main course had left us underwhelmed. Given the cost—over $100 per person before wine or tax—it’s hard to justify the experience as a regular splurge. While the restaurant’s attention to guest sentiment and presentation is commendable, the execution felt half-hearted. I’d reserve a return visit until there’s clear evidence of culinary improvement, but for now, it’s a cautious "not quite a favorite."

The service here is efficient but impersonal, which matches the overall vibe of a no-frills eatery. While the menu offers a few unique options—like a decent southwest wrap or a house-made soup—these are often overshadowed by the standard fare that feels like a cross between a gas station deli and a mid-’90s chain. Portions are generous, which explains why meals feel satisfying, even if the flavors lean bland. The real draw is convenience: if you’re caught in this corner of town between errands or meetings, it’s a reliable stop to avoid a full-blown food crisis. That said, if you’re seeking anything remotely creative or memorable, this isn’t the spot. The third star isn’t just for location—it’s a nod to the fact that, while unremarkable, it does the job without missteps. Just don’t expect fireworks.

The staff member interrupted my questions with a dismissive tone and rolled her eyes when I mentioned the oils' low quality. Her unhelpful, condescending attitude—especially about the absent amber selection—left me feeling unwelcome. Despite possible product merits, the poor service overshadows everything; I’ll definitely avoid returning.

The sushi was exquisite, especially the toro and yellowtail, but the miso cod lacked the richness I remember. Service remained attentive, though the pacing between courses felt rushed. Ambiance was as elegant as ever, with ocean views elevating the experience. While the kitchen’s creativity shines, minor inconsistencies prevent a 5-star repeat. Still, Nobu’s bold flavors and refined presentation keep it my top choice in Honolulu—just a touch more hit-or-miss this time.

The ooey gooey cake, which I assumed would be a saving grace, was equally underwhelming. The gooey part? Practically nonexistent—just a thin, sugary glaze that crumbled off immediately. The cake itself was dense and cakey, lacking the fudgy, melty layers promised in the name. I even gave it a second chance, letting it sit for an hour, but it never improved. My coworkers, gracious as always, smiled through their bites, but I could see the confusion in their eyes. How could something so visually appealing taste so..... mundane? The prices here don’t reflect the quality, and the lack of attention to moisture or flavor balance is baffling for a bakery. I’ve had better coffee shop cupcakes for half the price. This isn’t just a one-time fluke—either the recipes are flawed or the ingredients are subpar. Save your money and your appetite; there’s no redemption here. If you’re looking for a sweet treat that actually tastes like a treat, keep searching.

Despite the parking mishap, our evening was overwhelmingly enjoyable. The ambiance was charming—dim lighting, soft jazz, and the clink of glasses created a cozy, romantic vibe. Our server checked in regularly, offering thoughtful recommendations and ensuring our water glasses were never empty. The live entertainment, a small acoustic duo in the corner, added a delightful, intimate touch without overpowering conversation. On the food front, the salmon tartar and French bread remain my standout highlights—the bread’s crusty texture paired perfectly with the silky tartar. The filet and dauphinois potatoes were equally memorable, while the lamb’s herb crust provided a fresh, herbaceous finish. For dessert, the brûlée had a custard that was just thick enough, and the chocolate lava cake’s molten center felt decadent yet balanced. The only minor critique was the foie gras, but the rest of the meal easily compensated. The restaurant’s strengths—attentive service, exceptional dishes, and a warm atmosphere—far outweigh the misstep. If you’re in the area, this spot is worth a visit. Just heed my advice and skip street parking (or budget for it!). The culinary experience is top-tier, and the charm of the evening lingers long after the last bite. A 4.5-star evening, rounded up by the memory of that rich, shared dessert. Yum.

The 20-minute wait turned into a chaotic scramble—cold pizza, apathetic staff, and a broken promises. My friend’s recommendation? Forget it. Save your time and appetite elsewhere; this “fast” spot’s only swift at dashing expectations.

The food was just as delicious as always—my go-to shrimp tacos and my friend’s avocado club were fresh, flavorful, and perfectly portioned for a satisfying lunch. The cozy, vibrant atmosphere made our meal even more enjoyable, and the efficient service added to the seamless experience. While we were sad to lose her jacket, Evan’s genuine effort to help turned a small mishap into a memorable gesture of kindness. It’s clear that the team at CD truly cares about their customers’ experience, not just the transaction. Between the warm hospitality, top-notch food, and dedication to going the extra mile, it’s no wonder we keep coming back. Shout out to Evan again—your kindness made our day! Can’t wait for our next visit!

The ambiance was straightforward—bright fluorescent lights, checkered floors, and the hum of a classic diner. While the omelet was fluffy and the ham decent, the true standout was the breakfast potatoes, which had a crispy edge and weren’t overly greasy. I appreciated the portions; nothing felt skimpy, even with the limited menu. However, the service lingered in the "adequate" zone. After ordering, my coffee went untouched for over 20 minutes, and when I asked for refills, the waitress seemed annoyed to make the trip. That said, the prices felt fair for the quality: around $10 for a hearty breakfast. If you’re a fan of no-frills, efficient dining, this place might work for you. But for those seeking a more polished experience, the waitstaff’s disinterest could sour the meal. I’ll likely return after 7AM to test the "full" menu, curious if the expanded options live up to the hype. For now, it’s a decent stop for a quick bite but lacks the charm or standout dishes to become a regular haunt. Just keep your expectations aligned with the time of day—and your patience with the service.

The service was quick and friendly at both locations, which made the experience even more enjoyable, especially since we arrived during a less hectic time. The Summerlin Center spot felt more polished, with a tidy setup, while the drive-thru behind Yogurtland was efficient, though a bit cramped. Both locations radiated a no-frills, “just-the-food” vibe that I appreciated—this isn’t a place for lingering over coffee, but the focus on fresh, flavorful bites made up for it. The menu’s variety shone through: besides the sliders and fries, I overheard coworkers raving about the kimchi fries and garlic Parmesan twists, which I’ll have to try next time. The portions were generous, and the $7 lunch deal struck the perfect balance between satisfying and not overwhelming. Sharing the fries was a great idea, as they came in a heaping pile that easily split among the group. That said, the cash-only policy remains a hurdle. While I understand the logistics for a pop-up-style operation, signage and online updates about payment methods would help avoid disappointment, especially for evening patrons. Still, the quality and value far outweigh this minor inconvenience. I’d happily return for more of their bold, inventive flavors. Whether it’s the zesty Pep sauce, the juicy Porkie, or their next creative offering, this spot is a local gem worth chasing—even if I have to grab a few twenties ahead of time. Two thumbs up for the food, and a gentle nudge to update their payment process!

The rest of the stay was a constant uphill battle. After the fridge fiasco, I was on edge every time I walked into the room, half-expecting more hidden fees or mishaps. The housekeeping staff left a trail of crumbs and clutter when they entered to “clean,” which took longer to tidy up than it did to report. When I brought it up at the front desk, I was met with eye-rolls and a curt, “We’ll look into it,” which clearly didn’t happen. The worst part? At checkout, the same lady who’d initially refused to budge now smiled sweetly and said, “Oh, I fixed the fridge charges for you!”—as if it were a favor, not her job. I left with a sinking feeling that their “fix” was just a temporary patch, but at least the charges disappeared. Still, the $150+ we spent trying to get the hotel to do the right thing was the real cost of this trip. Even the positives felt tainted. The skyline view was nice, sure, but the window only opened halfway, trapping the stale, air-freshener-ruined air inside. The “ok” room? The sink leaked, the toilet clogged at least twice, and the shower head dripped for hours after I turned it off. For the price, I expected basic functionality, not a litany of excuses. Frankly, this stay was a masterclass in corporate neglect. If “customer service” is defined as pretending to listen while quietly charging customers for things they didn’t buy, then this hotel’s got a 5-star rating for that. But if it’s about actually solving problems? Zip it. I’ll take my business—and my money—elsewhere.

The service was brisk, which I appreciated, but the counter staff seemed overwhelmed during the lunch rush. The fries were crispy but lacked seasoning, and the burger, while cooked to order, felt predictable—no standout flavors or fresh ingredients. Comparing it to spots like Five Guys or local diners, the portion size and price don’t quite justify the mediocrity. That said, the place still draws a loyal crowd. Maybe it’s nostalgia or the cult following, but the hype doesn’t align with my experience. If you’re in a hurry or craving a classic burger, this could work. But for a splurge? I’d skip this spot and save the parking hassle. Next time, I’ll stick to sliders—or just order the cheeseburger elsewhere.

The cheese crisp arrived soggy and underwhelming, barely worth the $5.50 toll. Every bite felt like a chore, with flavors so bland they might as well have been invented in a lab. The “homemade” bean dip? A lukewarm, canned-taste excuse that made me miss my microwave. Even the chips were underseasoned, as if they feared oversalt would tip the scales. While the server smiled and refilled my water promptly, it couldn’t mask the restaurant’s core failure: food that’s a punishment to eat. Paying for mediocrity here feels like throwing money into a bureaucratic void. Save your cash, your taste buds, and skip this soulless pit stop.

The wine list, while extensive, leaned heavily on overpriced by-the-glass options, with a $22 pour that felt like a luxury tax on otherwise modestly priced bottles. Even the cocktail menu, which offered a few inventive twists on classics, didn’t justify the markups—our group’s shared negroni ($16) was solid but not extraordinary. What stood out most was the stark contrast between Circo’s ambiance and its food. The dining room’s whimsical design, with its vibrant murals and open kitchen, felt like a throwback to a more theatrical

The chipping and yellowing began almost immediately, and by the end of the week, the acrylic had split from the nail bed. I asked the technician if this was normal, but they downplayed it, suggesting I hadn’t cared for them properly. I follow basic aftercare steps, yet the nails peeled within 10 days—barely half the usual lifespan. The price seemed too good to be true, and it was. Don’t waste your time or money here; quality over quantity matters. Seek a reputable salon willing to stand behind their work. Trust me, your nails (and wallet) will thank you.

The experience left me questioning the ethics of their business model. The owner’s justification—that the 75% markup is their only means of profit due to no affiliation with UPS—felt like a loophole exploited rather than a legitimate business strategy. This lack of transparency around pricing and services is alarming, especially for customers unaware of how much they’re being overcharged. For instance, the $25 “boxing” fee alone felt like a bait-and-switch for a simple task any layperson could handle. While the staff’s friendliness was pleasant, it couldn’t compensate for their inability to explain basic insurance protocols or verify coverage amounts. Had they known how to properly price a shipment or align insurance with the item’s value, the transaction could have been fairer. Instead, their ignorance—or perhaps feigned ignorance—became a costly inconvenience. The absence of a customer copy of the shipping forms further eroded trust. Without documentation, I was left with no proof of the terms I paid for, leaving me vulnerable if something had gone wrong. This lack of accountability is particularly troubling when shipping valuables.
