The chicken, while flavorful, was a bit of a letdown due to its dryness and oily skin. I appreciate the effort to season it, but it would be great if they could find a way to keep it moist and infuse the flavor into the meat itself. Perhaps they could consider revising their cooking process or using a different technique to achieve a more tender and juicy result. The sides, unfortunately, were a major disappointment. The coleslaw, while not bad, was unremarkable, and the red rice was a strange, cardboard-like flavor that didn't appeal to me. The mac and cheese was a catastrophe – it's a staple in the South, and to get it so wrong is a shame. I'm not sure what kind of cheese they used, but it was definitely not a traditional or appetizing variety. Despite these issues, I do appreciate the variety on the menu, and I'm willing to give them another chance to showcase their skills. Maybe their other dishes, like the burgers or sandwiches, are more impressive. If I do return, I'll be sure to order something different and pay closer attention to the preparation and presentation. It's also worth noting that the covered patio area is a lovely spot to enjoy a meal during warmer weather. The atmosphere is quiet and inviting, and it would be a great place to relax with family or friends. However, the food needs to be on par with the ambiance, and unfortunately, it fell short during our visit. In conclusion, while our experience was disappointing, I'm not ready to write off this establishment just yet. With a bit more attention to detail, improved food quality, and better execution, they could potentially become a favorite among locals and visitors alike. Until then, I'll stick to my grocery store chicken and explore other options for satisfying my cravings. Cheers to hoping they'll take constructive feedback to heart and make the necessary adjustments to elevate their culinary game!

I was thoroughly impressed by the warm and inviting atmosphere of Chompies, and the service was top-notch. Our server was knowledgeable and attentive, making sure everyone in our large group had everything they needed. The portions were generous, to say the least, and I loved the variety of traditional dishes with a modern twist. The fried matzo balls and potato pancakes were definitely highlights, and I appreciated the creative topping options. I also enjoyed trying the Rugulach, which was similar to Baklava but with its own unique flavor profile. The fact that it comes in multiple flavors is a definite bonus. What really stood out to me, though, was the sense of community at Chompies. Meeting fellow Yelpers and hearing about their experiences was a great way to break the ice, and the staff seemed to genuinely care about ensuring everyone had a great time. Whether you're a longtime fan of Jewish deli cuisine or just looking to try something new, Chompies is definitely worth a visit. Just be sure to use the correct address, as the Google Maps listing can be a bit misleading. Thankfully, the deli is conveniently located behind the Chandler Mall, making it easy to find and access. Overall, I'm so glad I got to experience Chompies for the first time, and I'm already looking forward to my next visit!

As I sat at the bar, I couldn't help but notice the lack of enthusiasm from the staff. It seemed like they were just going through the motions, rather than genuinely trying to create a welcoming atmosphere for their customers. The barmaid who served me was friendly enough, but it took her a while to warm up, and even then, she seemed a bit detached. I understand that Mondays can be slow, but that's exactly when you'd think the staff would be more attentive and eager to make a good impression. Despite the subpar service, I did appreciate the overall ambiance of the place. The dark color scheme and comfortable seating areas created a cozy and intimate atmosphere, perfect for a night out with friends or a date. The menu, as I mentioned earlier, looked promising, with a good variety of options to suit different tastes. The fact that they offer two kids' meals is also a plus, making it a potentially family-friendly destination. The selection of scotches and whiskeys is indeed impressive, and I was happy to see some lesser-known brands on the list. This, combined with the Irish-inspired menu items, suggests that the owners have made an effort to create an authentic Irish pub experience. However, it's the little things, like a warm greeting and attentive service, that can make or break a customer's experience. In conclusion, while I was pleased with the quality of the calamari and the overall atmosphere of the place, the lackluster service holds me back from giving it a glowing review. With a bit more attention to customer service and staff training, this could easily become a top destination for those looking for a great Irish pub experience. As it stands, I can only recommend it as an okay place to grab a drink and a bite to eat, but not necessarily a must-visit destination. Perhaps with time and a bit of tweaking, they'll be able to elevate their service to match the quality of their food and drinks.

The combination of disorganization and lack of expertise has left a sour taste in my mouth. I expect a dental office to be able to manage their appointments and procedures more efficiently. The fact that they were overbooked and unable to complete a relatively routine extraction is concerning. While the friendly staff is a plus, it's not enough to outweigh the incompetence and wasted resources. I hope that in the future, they will take steps to improve their scheduling and procedures to avoid putting other patients through the same frustrating experience that I had. Overall, I would advise others to explore alternative options.

The chef's creativity and attention to detail were evident in each course, from the delicate sushi to the rich, savory sauces. Every bite was a masterful balance of flavors and textures. The atmosphere was also noteworthy, with a cozy and intimate setting that added to the overall dining experience. The chef's tasting menu was definitely worth the price, and I appreciated the unique and personalized touches throughout the meal. Overall, I highly recommend this restaurant to anyone looking for an exceptional Japanese dining experience – I'm already counting down the days until my next visit!

Overall, it was a fun experience with a lively atmosphere. The staff were friendly and attentive, despite the crowd. I'd return to watch another game, but might consider arriving earlier to secure a more comfortable seat. The unique souvenir cup was a nice touch, making the visit even more enjoyable.

The modern decor and dim lighting created a sophisticated ambiance, but the noise level was somewhat elevated due to the open layout. Our server was attentive and knowledgeable about the menu, making recommendations when asked. Despite the slow pace, the staff ensured our glasses were always full. While the food was tasty, the portions and prices didn't quite align, leaving us somewhat underwhelmed. Overall, it was a decent dining experience, but not impressive enough to warrant a return visit amidst other available options in the area. Perhaps a revisit could change my opinion.
The aquarium was clean and well-maintained with a variety of marine life on display for all to enjoy.

The lack of foot traffic and limited parking also detract from the experience. Despite its promising concept, the Chinese Culture Center feels like a missed opportunity. With more thoughtful planning and investment, it could have become a vibrant hub for the community. As it stands, the center's isolated location and underwhelming atmosphere make it a disappointment. I hope that in the future, efforts will be made to revitalize this space and create a truly thriving cultural destination that Phoenix can be proud of, but for now, it falls short of expectations and remains a letdown.

Maybe their other dishes are more impressive. The service was friendly, which made up for some of the shortcomings. Overall, it was an average experience, but the convenience and ambiance might bring us back to try again and hopefully be more impressed with their offerings.

Overall, my experiences have been inconsistent, but the exceptional bacon keeps me coming back. The service is generally friendly, although our server seemed a bit overwhelmed this morning. Despite the drawbacks, the atmosphere remains inviting, and I appreciate the ample natural light. However, to win me over, they need to refine their breakfast dishes, particularly the hash browns and pancakes. With some tweaks to their recipes and attention to detail, this establishment could become a top choice for breakfast in the area, especially with their outstanding bacon on the menu. I'll likely give them another try.

Overall, our experience at Mandalay Bay was underwhelming, to say the least. The hotel's attempts to create a luxurious atmosphere fell short, and the numerous missteps we encountered during our stay left a sour taste in our mouths. The room, as I mentioned earlier, was the highlight of our stay, but even that was not enough to make up for the other shortcomings. The lack of a proper closet was a significant inconvenience, and the small, temporary wardrobe they provided was woefully inadequate for our needs. The closure of the Spa was a major disappointment, as it was one of the amenities we were looking forward to using during our stay. The pool area, which we had heard so much about, was overcrowded and noisy, with helicopters and planes constantly flying overhead. The chairs were uncomfortable and dirty, and the $12 Mohito was overpriced and took far too long to arrive. The poor service and lack of attention to detail were evident throughout our stay, from the poorly signed walkways to the pool to the inadequate seating and amenities. Our experience at the Fleur De Lys restaurant was particularly disappointing. The false advertising of their happy hour specials was misleading and frustrating, and the limited selection of drinks and appetizers was not what we had expected. The fact that they only offered popcorn as a complimentary appetizer was almost laughable, and the two-for-one drinks special was not as enticing as it sounded, given the limited options. The $16 glass of wine was overpriced and did not even taste good, which was the final straw for us. In comparison to other hotels on the Strip, Mandalay Bay fell short in many areas. We have stayed at the Encore before and had a much better experience, with a nicer room and better amenities. The room rate was even more competitive at the Encore, which made our decision to stay there instead of Mandalay Bay an easy one. Overall, while Mandalay Bay has its strengths, it needs to work on its weaknesses and improve its services and amenities to compete with other top-tier hotels in Las Vegas. Until then, we will be taking our business (and our wallets) elsewhere.
their unique flavors and freshly baked bread keep me coming back for more, it's a must-visit every time I'm in town, truly the gold standard of sandwich shops.
Disappointing experience overall, prices were reasonable but flavor and quality lacked, not worth a repeat visit for us, especially with other authentic options available in the area.

The quality of food was consistent, but the price point was steep for a morning meal. Considering the Wynn's upscale atmosphere, the buffet's cost was somewhat justified, yet it still felt excessive. Overall, it was a satisfying, albeit pricey, experience that met our expectations without exceeding them. Service was attentive and friendly.

As I reflected on my experience, I couldn't help but think that Applebee's has lost sight of what's truly important: serving quality food that leaves customers satisfied. The 2 for $20 special, which sounded like a great deal on paper, ended up being a letdown. The lack of attention to detail in the kitchen was apparent, from the hard and tasteless mozzarella sticks to the overcooked and dry chicken. It's disappointing to see a restaurant that was once a staple in many communities struggle to deliver on its promises. I've had better experiences at other casual dining chains, where the food is consistently prepared with care and attention to detail. The contrast between Applebee's and its competitors is striking, and it's clear that they need to go back to the drawing board and re-evaluate their menu and cooking techniques. Perhaps it's time for them to focus on using fresh, high-quality ingredients and simplifying their menu to allow for more attention to detail in the kitchen. Until then, I'll be taking my business (and my appetite) elsewhere. To anyone considering trying Applebee's, I would caution against it, at least until they revamp their menu and cooking techniques. And to myself, I say: remember the lesson learned from this experience, and don't be tempted to give Applebee's another chance anytime soon. Two strikes are enough, and it's time to move on to greener pastures.

As we savored our meal, the impeccable service and attention to detail only added to the enchanting atmosphere. Our server was knowledgeable and attentive, happily answering our questions about the menu and making excellent recommendations. The lamb chops were cooked to perfection, and the wine pairing was spot on. The portions were generous, and we left feeling satisfied but not overly stuffed. The real magic happened as the sun set, and the golf course transformed into a picturesque landscape with twinkling lights and the soothing sound of the waterfall. It was truly a night to remember, and I couldn't wait to return with someone special. The high price point was well worth it for the unforgettable experience, and I would highly recommend this restaurant to anyone looking to impress or celebrate a special occasion in style.

I'm disappointed to see the decline in their tofu soup, as it was once a staple for me. However, their bimbimbap remains a highlight, with the combination of tender beef, fresh vegetables, and a perfectly cooked egg creating a flavorful and satisfying dish. The sizzling pot presentation adds to the experience, making it a must-try for anyone visiting Chodang. Despite the drop in quality of their other dishes, I'll continue to return for their exceptional bimbimbap, which remains unparalleled in the east valley. It's a shame the rest of their menu doesn't live up to this standard.

Overall, I was disappointed with the outdated decor and lack of maintenance. The staff was friendly, but it wasn't enough to make up for the hotel's shortcomings. For the price, I expected more amenities and a cleaner environment. The location on the strip was convenient, but I wouldn't recommend Luxor to others unless they renovate and update their facilities. With so many other options available in Las Vegas, I would explore alternative hotels for my next stay. Luxor has potential, but it needs significant improvements.
Always leave full and satisfied, the staff is friendly, and the atmosphere is casual and inviting, making it a great spot for families and casual dining.

The atmosphere was lively and modern, with an open layout that added to its charm. Our server was attentive and knowledgeable, happily answering questions about the menu and drinks. The prices were reasonable, especially considering the generous portion sizes. Overall, I'm excited to come back and try more of their offerings, especially the mango cream ale, which has already become a new favorite of mine.

I'm extremely disappointed in the way this hospital prioritizes profits over pet care. The lack of transparency and cooperation in providing my pup's prescription was appalling. It's unacceptable that they would intentionally delay and make it difficult for me to obtain a copy of the prescription, simply because I found a more affordable option elsewhere. The fact that the director openly admitted to being in the business of selling medications, in addition to providing veterinary services, speaks volumes about their true motives. As a pet owner, it's heartbreaking to see a hospital that is supposed to prioritize the well-being of animals instead focusing on making a quick buck. I would not recommend this hospital to anyone and will be taking my business (and my pup) elsewhere. The memory of their relentless up-selling and medication costs will stay with me, and I hope that others will learn from my experience and avoid this hospital at all costs.

Overall, it's a solid choice for a casual Italian meal. The atmosphere is cozy and inviting, adding to the authentic experience. While the food didn't exceed expectations, it was satisfying and reasonably priced. I'm looking forward to exploring more of their menu on my next visit, hopefully with improved service speed.

I am extremely disappointed and frustrated with the level of service I've received from the dealership. As a customer who has invested a significant amount of money in a luxury vehicle, I expect a certain level of quality and support. Instead, I've been met with incompetence and a lack of accountability. The fact that I had to educate the service department about the known issues with the cameras is appalling. It's clear that they are not taking my concerns seriously and are more interested in making a sale than providing adequate after-sales support. The blocking of my posts on their Facebook page is also a disturbing attempt to silence a dissatisfied customer. I would not recommend this dealership to anyone and would advise others to think twice before purchasing a Range Rover, especially a used one with known issues. The hassle and stress I've experienced are not worth the luxury badge. I expect a resolution to this issue soon, but my confidence in the brand and the dealership has been severely shaken.
"Definitely a unique vibe, fun atmosphere, and outdoor seating area makes it a great spot to unwind and enjoy live music with friends on a warm evening."

I'll make this simple..... Pros: BEAUTIFUL hotel. We stayed in the wrap around balcony suite in the east towers over looking the Bellagio water show. It was gorgeous. Extremely deep bathtub, great showers, COMFY bed situation, and the technology in the room (especially all that you can access just from the TV) was off the chain. Their pool area on the 4th floor was equally gorgeous. Cabanas were very relaxing. Room service breakfast was really good although, FYI, they injecting something in them pancakes because they were Jurassic! Valet service was VERY quick. We never had to wait to long for our car. CONS: Customer service fail! They've got a lot of work to do. We were told because of our VIP Gold card status, our drinks would be comped at the bars in the hotel. NONE of the bartenders new what the hell we were talking about. Every time we tried to do it a manager (who wasn't around) has to be called. It ended up being too much of a hassle each time so we just said forget it. We even went to the designated VIP lounge and they had not been informed. We ordered a roll away bed and some more towels at 1am, went to Drais after hour spot, came back to the room at 7am (we went hard) and no one had even been there. Called two more times and still no one brought anything. Wasn't until we called angry about it that we finally got a "oh the order wasn't entered correctly (all three times???) excuse. Another issue: As I said, we spent a lot of money at this hotel, one of their most expensive suites, poker tourney, VIP status. The problem is VIP means not a damn thing at this hotel. There are no perks! We decided to go to Marque, the club inside the hotel, because they had a hip hop room and we weren't about the house music. We had 3 girls and 4 guys. Everyone dressed lovely. We get there, flash the VIP cards and the bouncer tells us the guy to girl ratio is too low. We need one more girl....I'm not even going to discuss this further. All I'm going to say is, I'm VIP in your hotel and I can't get in your club because I'm short one damn female??? They've only been open about a month. They have a lot of work to do. They need to take better care of their VIP guests. If you're trying to do Vegas VIP...this ain't the place. We've stayed at other hotels VIP and I have to say Encore has been the best as far as perks/customer service goes. That is all. In conclusion, our stay at this hotel was a mixed bag. On one hand, the hotel's physical attributes, such as the room and pool area, were top-notch. However, the customer service and VIP experience were severely lacking. As a VIP guest, I expect a certain level of treatment and perks, which this hotel failed to deliver. The lack of communication and organization among the staff was evident, and it's clear that they have a lot of work to do to improve their services. I would recommend this hotel to those who are looking for a beautiful and comfortable place to stay, but not to those who are expecting a true VIP experience. If you're looking to splurge and be treated like a high-roller, I would suggest looking elsewhere. Perhaps with time and experience, this hotel will be able to iron out its issues and provide the level of service that its VIP guests deserve. For now, I would give this hotel 3 out of 5 stars. The hotel's physical attributes and amenities are definitely worthy of 5 stars, but the poor customer service and VIP experience bring the rating down. I hope that the hotel will take our feedback to heart and make the necessary improvements to provide a better experience for their guests in the future. It's worth noting that the hotel's location is also a major plus, with many popular attractions and amenities within walking distance. However, this is not enough to make up for the hotel's shortcomings in terms of customer service and VIP experience. Overall, I would say that this hotel has a lot of potential, but it needs to work on its weaknesses in order to provide a truly exceptional experience for its guests. Ultimately, whether or not to stay at this hotel depends on your individual priorities and expectations. If you're looking for a beautiful and comfortable place to stay, and don't mind dealing with some potential issues with customer service, then this hotel may be a good choice. However, if you're expecting a true VIP experience with top-notch service and perks, you may want to consider looking elsewhere.
with much better selection and more competitive pricing, making these locations not worth the visit or investment for serious buyers or collectors.

The combination of flavors and textures was absolute perfection. The pistachio gelato was creamy and rich, while the mini cheesecake was a delightful balance of tangy and sweet. The service was also top-notch, with friendly staff and a beautiful display of pastries. If you're a dessert lover like me, Jean Philippe Patisserie is an absolute must-visit when in Las Vegas. I'm already planning my next visit to try more of their heavenly treats!

I can see why Serendipity 3 is a popular spot, especially among tourists and those with a sweet tooth. The atmosphere is definitely unique and Instagram-worthy, with its whimsical decor and colorful accents. The staff was friendly and attentive, which added to the overall experience. However, as I mentioned earlier, the food was nothing special, and I wouldn't go out of my way to try it again. The frozen hot chocolate, on the other hand, was a highlight, and I can see why it's their signature item. If you're in the area and looking for a cool treat to beat the heat, Serendipity 3 is worth stopping by. Just don't expect to be blown away by the food, and be prepared for a potentially long wait, especially during peak hours. Overall, it's a fun and quirky spot that's worth visiting at least once, if only for the frozen hot chocolate and the'gram.

I'm still dreaming about the endless options and the quality of the food. The atmosphere was lively and bustling, with a wide range of patrons from families to couples and solo travelers. The remodel has definitely paid off, as the modern decor and ample seating made for a comfortable dining experience. Our server was friendly and efficient, ensuring that our drinks were always full and clearing our plates promptly. One of the standout features of this buffet was the variety of options. From the seafood station to the carving station, and from the salad bar to the dessert table, there was something for everyone. I was impressed by the attention to detail and the obvious care that the chefs took in preparing each dish. The fact that they could maintain such high quality with such a vast array of options is a testament to their skill and dedication. If I were to offer any criticism, it would be that the buffet can get quite crowded, especially on weekends or during peak travel seasons. However, the staff does an excellent job of managing the flow of traffic and ensuring that everyone has a chance to try all of the delicious options. Overall, I would highly recommend this buffet to anyone visiting Vegas, whether you're a foodie or just looking for a unique dining experience. Be prepared to come hungry and leave satisfied – and don't be surprised if you find yourself planning your next visit before you've even left the building!

Unfortunately, my experiences at Buck & Badger have fallen short of my expectations. The atmosphere, although cozy and inviting, is not enough to make up for the subpar food and slow service. I was really looking forward to having a go-to spot near my workplace, but the prices and portion sizes are just not justified by the quality of the dishes. The fact that I have to pay extra for a side of fries with my already overpriced grilled cheese is just disappointing. I've tried to give them the benefit of the doubt, visiting twice and trying different menu items, but sadly, I won't be returning. With so many other great options in the area, I just can't see myself choosing Buck & Badger again. It's a shame, really, because I think they have potential, but until they revamp their menu and pricing, I'll have to take my business (and my book-reading, fire-enjoying self) elsewhere.

Overall, our experience was disappointing. The lack of beef and peppers in the Kung Pao dishes was noticeable. Although the service was satisfactory, finding a hair in my soup was unsettling. We left unimpressed, still searching for a Chinese restaurant in Vegas that matches the quality of Yu's in Schaumburg, IL, our gold standard for Chinese cuisine.
The staff is friendly, and the atmosphere is cozy and clean, making it a great spot to grab a quick bite or meet with friends, with plenty of seating and free Wi-Fi available.

The overall ambiance was completely uninviting and lacked any semblance of cleanliness. It's clear that the establishment is not prioritizing the customer's experience or health. The fact that they can serve such a subpar product and still manage to keep their doors open is astonishing. As I looked around, I noticed that the decor was outdated and worn out, which added to the overall sense of neglect. The dirty mirrors, unclean tables, and overflowing trash cans created an unpleasant atmosphere that made me question the hygiene standards of the kitchen. Needless to say, my disappointing experience with the pizza was only exacerbated by the unappealing surroundings. I would not recommend this place to anyone and will definitely be taking my business (and my pizza cravings) elsewhere. The memory of that soggy, cheese-less slice will stay with me as a cautionary tale.

Completely unimpressed and disappointed, the lack of attention and care was staggering, especially for a supposed luxury dining experience that utterly failed to deliver on its promises and hefty price tag.

As I reflected on our visit, I realized that maybe we just caught them on an off day. The staff was attentive and apologetic when I mentioned that our pizzas were a bit lacking in toppings, so I'm willing to give them the benefit of the doubt. Perhaps it was just a miscommunication in the kitchen or a new chef still getting familiar with the menu. I do appreciate the effort they put into sourcing high-quality, organic ingredients, and I'm more than happy to support that mission. I'm also excited to try some of their other menu items, such as their salads and sandwiches, which looked fresh and appealing. The vegan options, in particular, seemed intriguing, and I'd love to explore those further. It's great to see a restaurant catering to various dietary needs and preferences, and I appreciate the attention to detail in that regard. Before visiting again, I might check their social media or website to see if they've made any changes to their menu or cooking techniques. It's possible that they've taken customer feedback on board and made some adjustments to improve the overall dining experience. I'm looking forward to giving them another chance to impress me with their flavors and execution. In the meantime, I'd recommend this place to fellow health-conscious foodies who prioritize organic ingredients and sustainable practices. While the pizza may not have blown me away, the restaurant's commitment to using locally sourced produce and natural ingredients is admirable, and I appreciate the transparency about their sourcing. With a bit of tweaking in the kitchen, I have no doubt that this place could become a staple in our household. For now, I'll remain optimistic and hope that my next visit will be a more memorable one.
Overall, it was a decent experience, with convenient options, although the high prices and limited choices were notable drawbacks during my extended stay.

As I sat back to reflect on the meal, I couldn't help but feel grateful for the recommendation from my date. The combination of flavors and textures in each dish was truly impressive, and I appreciated the attention to detail that the chef brought to every aspect of the meal. The summer rolls, with their delicate wrapping and fresh vegetables, were a perfect start to the evening, and the house curry with tofu was a masterclass in balancing spices and flavors. I also appreciated the flexibility of the menu, which allowed me to customize the level of spiciness to my liking. The option to choose from a range of spice levels, from mild to extremely hot, was a nice touch, and I liked that the server was knowledgeable about the different options and could make recommendations. As we finished our meal and prepared to leave, I took a moment to look around the restaurant and appreciate its cozy atmosphere. The decor, while not fancy, was warm and inviting, and the small size of the restaurant made it feel intimate and welcoming. I could see why my date had enjoyed it so much on their previous visit, and I was already looking forward to returning. One thing that might be helpful to note for future visitors is that the restaurant can be a bit tricky to find, especially if you're relying on Google Maps. As I mentioned earlier, the restaurant's name is similar to that of a city in Thailand, which can cause some confusion. But don't let that deter you - the restaurant is well worth seeking out, and the food and service are sure to make it a memorable experience. Overall, I would highly recommend this restaurant to anyone looking for delicious and authentic Thai cuisine. The combination of flavorful dishes, attentive service, and cozy atmosphere make it a must-visit destination for foodies and anyone looking for a great dining experience. I'm already planning my next visit, and I'm excited to try more of the menu items and see what other surprises the chef has in store.

Overall, the experience was pleasant, but not particularly memorable. The atmosphere was lively and festive, with a vibrant decor that added to the ambiance. However, the noise level was a bit high, making it difficult to carry on conversations at times. Despite the minor issues with service and my personal preference for milder flavors, our group enjoyed their meals and left feeling satisfied. The prices were reasonable, especially considering the generous portions and strong drinks. While I wouldn't go out of my way to recommend this place, I also wouldn't discourage anyone from trying it. If you're a fan of spicy Mexican food and a lively atmosphere, you might really enjoy it. For me, though, it's just an okay option – not my favorite, but not bad either.

The staff is always friendly and welcoming to both us and our dogs. They have a great selection of beers and the food is delicious. The outdoor seating area is perfect for warm days, and the kiddie pools are a wonderful touch for hot summer afternoons. Our dogs always have a blast running around and socializing with the other dogs. We've met some great people here too, all with a shared love of dogs. Overall, it's a fantastic spot that we highly recommend to anyone who loves dogs and a fun, relaxed atmosphere.

The atmosphere was casual and inviting, with a cozy patio area perfect for warmer days. Our server was friendly and attentive, making sure we had everything we needed throughout our meal. The prices were very reasonable, especially considering the high quality of the ingredients and the generous portion sizes. Overall, I was thoroughly impressed with my experience and would definitely return for another delicious burger and side of fries. The fact that they source local beers, like the Big Sky I.P.A., is also a big plus in my book. I'm already looking forward to my next visit and trying more of their menu items.

The overall experience was top-notch, exceeding my expectations. Nic's professionalism and kindness made a significant difference, making me feel valued as a customer. I highly recommend this business for its outstanding service and amenities, a truly exceptional experience from start to finish, definitely a repeat customer.

Despite the high prices, the convenience and extended hours make it a viable option. The store's cleanliness and friendly staff are also positives. However, I wish they would reconsider their pricing strategy to make their products more competitive with other local stores and gas stations that offer similar items at lower costs.

Overall, our experience was average, and we left feeling somewhat disappointed. The location on the strip was convenient, but the high prices didn't match the quality of food we received. The shrimp and hamburger were cooked well, but lacked any distinctive flavors or presentation. For a bill of $57, we expected more than just okay food. The suggested tip on the check was also a turn-off, making us feel like the waiter was being too pushy. Despite the nice décor and quick seating, the overall experience was not worth the price, and we likely won't be returning anytime soon.

As we walked out, I couldn't help but feel a sense of disappointment and frustration. The owner's attempt to justify the delay by comparing the number of tables they had the previous Friday to the current day was not only unprofessional but also irrelevant. It's not about the number of tables, it's about being prepared and having a system in place to manage the demand. The fact that they couldn't even get our order of omelets right, which is a relatively simple dish, is a clear indication of the kitchen's incompetence. The patio area where we were seated was nice, but it was clear that the ambiance was not enough to make up for the subpar service. The waitress, although apologetic, seemed overwhelmed and unsure of how to handle the situation. The owner's decision to comp our meal was too little, too late, and it didn't make up for the hour of our time that we wasted waiting. What's even more concerning is that this experience is not an isolated incident. As we were leaving, we noticed a few other tables that had been waiting for a long time, and the looks on their faces were equally disappointed. It's clear that this restaurant has a systemic problem that needs to be addressed. As someone who has worked in the restaurant industry for many years, I understand that mistakes can happen, and it's how you recover from them that matters. However, in this case, the owner's lack of customer service skills and inability to manage the kitchen effectively is a recipe for disaster. It's not just about the food; it's about the experience, and this restaurant failed miserably. I would not recommend this restaurant to anyone, and I would advise the owner to take a long, hard look at their operations and make some serious changes. Hiring more staff, improving kitchen efficiency, and providing customer service training are just a few things that could help turn this restaurant around. Until then, I would suggest that potential customers steer clear of this establishment and take their business elsewhere. In conclusion, our experience at this restaurant was a disaster from start to finish. The long wait times, incompetent kitchen, and lack of customer service made for a frustrating and disappointing experience. The owner's inability to manage the restaurant effectively and provide a good experience for customers is a major concern, and it's clear that this restaurant needs a lot of work before it can be considered a viable option for diners.

The lackluster experience was further amplified by the underwhelming flavors and textures of the cheesesteak itself. The steak slices were overcooked and dry, the provolone cheese was barely melted, and the onions and green peppers were sparse and lacked any real crunch or freshness. For a place that specializes in cheesesteaks, I expected a much more satisfying and filling meal. Unfortunately, PSC failed to deliver on its promise of a authentic Philly-style cheesesteak experience. While I can appreciate the convenience of its location and the potential appeal to late-night revelers, it's not enough to warrant a return visit from me. Perhaps I just caught them on a bad day, but based on my initial impression, I wouldn't recommend PSC to anyone seeking a truly great cheesesteak.

I was shocked and disappointed by Dr. Chuang's sudden decision, especially since we had been loyal patients and always fulfilled our financial obligations. The fact that she prioritized her own interests over our healthcare needs is alarming. Her refusal to accommodate our insurance, despite our willingness to pay upfront, raises concerns about her commitment to patient care. As a result, I would caution others against establishing a relationship with Dr. Chuang, only to risk being dismissed arbitrarily. Trust and reliability are essential in a doctor-patient relationship, and Dr. Chuang has demonstrated that she is not a dependable healthcare provider. I will be taking my business elsewhere and advising friends and family to do the same.

The overall experience was underwhelming and overpriced. I left feeling disappointed and ripped off. For a local establishment, I expected more authenticity and care in their dishes. Unfortunately, this place failed to deliver on even the simplest of Chinese takeout expectations, leaving a bad taste in my mouth, literally and figuratively.

As I reflect on our visit, I can see why this place has garnered such a loyal following. The atmosphere is lively and inviting, with a nostalgic charm that's hard to resist. The old-school decor and vintage sodas add to the retro vibe, making it a great spot to grab a bite with friends or a casual date. One thing that impressed me was the attention to detail in the presentation of the dishes. The sandwiches were carefully crafted, with each ingredient visible and adding to the overall visual appeal. The PBB&J, in particular, was a feast for the eyes, with the vibrant red pepper jelly and fresh rosemary sprigs adding pops of color to the plate. While I appreciated the creativity and richness of the Foie& sandwich, I couldn't help but feel that it was a bit overwhelming. The sheer amount of foie gras and pate was almost too much to handle, and I found myself craving something to cut through the richness. Perhaps a side of pickles or a simple green salad would have provided a welcome contrast to the indulgent sandwich. Despite the minor quibbles, I was impressed by the quality of the ingredients and the care that went into preparing each dish. The bread, in particular, was exceptional – soft and fluffy on the inside, with a crispy crust that added texture to each bite. As we finished our meal and prepared to leave, I couldn't help but feel that this place has a lot of potential. With a few tweaks to the menu and some additional options to balance out the richness of the sandwiches, I could see myself becoming a regular here. For now, I'm looking forward to returning and trying some of the other menu items that caught my eye – the Span-ish and falafel, in particular, seem like great options for a lighter, more balanced meal. Overall, I'd recommend this place to anyone looking for a unique dining experience and a taste of something new and exciting. Just be sure to come hungry, as the portions are generous and the flavors are bold!

The quality of their food is also subpar, with dry meat and stale tortillas. It's clear they're prioritizing profits over customer satisfaction. The watered-down sour cream and sparse sauce servings are just the tip of the iceberg. With so many other affordable and delicious options available, it's not worth settling for this lackluster Taco Bell experience. Save your money and appetite for a better meal elsewhere.

The overall atmosphere has significantly deteriorated. It's disappointing to see a once-thriving spot succumb to greed and neglect. The influx of low-quality products and questionable business practices has driven away loyal vendors and customers alike. The lack of maintenance is evident, with dirty carpets and a general sense of disarray. It's a shame to see this place fall so far from its former charm, now prioritizing quick profits over community and quality.

I was thoroughly impressed with the level of service provided by Lanza AV, and Scott's expertise was evident from the moment he arrived. His ability to quickly diagnose the issue with my tuner and provide a clear explanation of the problem and the available solutions was incredibly helpful. I appreciated that he didn't try to push me into buying a new tuner, but rather presented me with all the options and allowed me to make an informed decision. The installation process was seamless, and Scott's attention to detail was impressive. He made sure that everything was working properly and that I was comfortable using the system before he left. The follow-up call from the office a few days later was a nice touch, and it's clear that Lanza AV is committed to providing excellent customer service. I've already recommended them to friends and family, and I would definitely use their services again in the future. Overall, I'm extremely satisfied with the experience and would highly recommend Lanza AV to anyone in need of home theater system installation or repair. Scott's professionalism, expertise, and friendly demeanor made the entire process a pleasure, and I'm grateful to have found such a reliable and trustworthy company.

I'm missing the personalized care and attention to detail that Dr. Tran and her team provided. The new dentist I've switched to just can't compare to the exceptional service I received at Dr. Tran's office. From the initial warm welcome to the thorough explanations of each procedure, every aspect of my experience was top-notch. The eco-friendly and modern facilities were just the icing on the cake. I appreciated the little touches, such as being able to watch my favorite TV show on the flat screen while getting my teeth cleaned. Dr. Tran's expertise and gentle touch made even the most dreaded procedures, like getting shots, a breeze. If I'm being completely honest, I'm already considering making the commute back to Dr. Tran's office just to get the quality care I've grown accustomed to. My only regret is not appreciating it enough while I was still a patient there.

The atmosphere is always cozy and welcoming, making it a great spot to catch up with friends or get some work done. The staff is friendly and knowledgeable, happy to recommend drinks or games to play. I've tried a variety of their coffee drinks and they're all delicious, made with care and attention to detail. The community events they host are also a great way to meet new people and feel connected to the neighborhood. Overall, I'm so grateful to have this coffee shop in my community and I'm excited to see the new location thrive.

The lack of attention and disorganization was appalling. We watched as other tables received their meals and finished their dining experience while we still waited. The fact that our order was misplaced and hadn't even been started after 25 minutes is unacceptable. The waitress seemed frazzled and unapologetic, which added to our frustration. We left hungry and extremely disappointed, vowing never to return. With so many other excellent sushi options available, it's clear that this establishment needs to revamp its service and management to retain customers. Until then, I strongly advise others to dine elsewhere.

As I reflect on my disastrous experience at this establishment, I am still fuming about the utter disregard for customer satisfaction. It's astonishing how a restaurant can get so many things wrong, from the subpar food to the abysmal service. The fact that they managed to botch even the simplest of orders, like the bottomless chips and salsa, is a testament to their incompetence. The atmosphere of the restaurant was also lacking, with a attempts to create a festive Mexican vibe falling flat. The decor was clichéd and unoriginal, with sombreros and piñatas scattered about in a half-hearted attempt to create a lively ambiance. But with the surly staff and mediocre food, it was impossible to shake off the feeling of disappointment and frustration. What's even more disturbing is the blatant disregard for customer feedback. When I politely brought my concerns to the waitress's attention, I was met with eye-rolling, sighs, and a general attitude of indifference. It's clear that the staff is not trained to handle even the most basic of customer complaints, and instead resort to being rude and dismissive. The food, as I mentioned earlier, was nothing special. The quesadilla, which I had hoped would be a redeeming factor, was oversized but lacked flavor and texture. The "mexican" food was a lazy attempt at recreating authentic dishes, with too much reliance on pre-packaged mixes and sauces. The margarita, which I had ordered with a double shot, was an insult to the very concept of a margarita. It was weak, bland, and tasted more like margarita mix than a carefully crafted cocktail. As I left the restaurant, I couldn't help but feel like I had been robbed of my time and money. The experience was a perfect storm of bad food, bad service, and a bad attitude. I would not recommend this place to my worst enemy, and I would caution anyone considering visiting to think twice. The two stars I gave this restaurant are generous, and I would not hesitate to give it a well-deserved one-star review if I could. In conclusion, my experience at this restaurant was a disaster from start to finish. The food was subpar, the service was abysmal, and the atmosphere was lacking. The staff's attitude and behavior were unacceptable, and it's clear that they are not interested in providing even the most basic level of customer satisfaction. If you value your time and money, stay far, far away from this dump. There are plenty of other restaurants out there that actually care about their customers and serve decent food. This place is a waste of time and money, and I would not recommend it to anyone.

The mole sauce was rich and flavorful, a highlight of my visit. Despite the occasional lack of attentiveness, I appreciate their chicken tamales and traditional Mexican sides. With some improvement in service, this place could become a favorite for those seeking authentic, homestyle dishes like their tamales and rice and beans.

The splash pad is well-maintained and provides a great spot for kids to cool off during the warmer months. It's also conveniently located near a few shops, making it easy for parents to keep an eye on their little ones while still being able to browse nearby stores. The surrounding area is also pretty well-shaded, which is a bonus for hot summer days. My stepdaughter has always had a blast playing there, and I appreciate that it's a free activity, which is hard to come by these days. Overall, while the shopping experience at this location leaves much to be desired, the splash pad is a definite highlight and a great resource for families in the area. Despite my overall dissatisfaction with the mall, I will likely continue to visit the splash pad with my kids, and for that, I'm willing to overlook some of the other drawbacks.

It's disheartening to see a favorite spot decline. The lack of attention to detail, such as melted cheese, is inexcusable. Hopefully, they'll address these issues and return to their former quality, but until then, I'll be taking my business elsewhere, seeking a better Mexican food experience.

Unfortunately, the uniqueness of the fajitas didn't translate to a positive dining experience for us. The combination of the dry, baked chicken and the overcooked, bitter pepper and onion mixture was a letdown. We were expecting the typical sizzling, flavorful dish that we've come to associate with fajitas, but what we got was a lackluster, unappetizing meal. The excellent sides, such as the guacamole, pico, cheese, and lettuce, couldn't make up for the disappointing main course. As a result, I've decided that Paco's is no longer a restaurant I'll be visiting. It's a shame, because I had high hopes for this place, but after multiple attempts, I just can't seem to find a reason to return. Perhaps they'll revamp their menu or cooking techniques, but for now, I'll be taking my business (and my appetite) elsewhere.
by the stunning vistas and unique attractions, making the trip well worth the time and effort to witness nature's breathtaking beauty up close.

As I weigh the pros and cons of living at Uptown Gardens, I have to consider my overall experience and whether the benefits outweigh the drawbacks. On one hand, the management team has been exceptional, always responsive and helpful with any issues that have arisen. The proximity to Uptown Charlotte is a major plus, with plenty of restaurants, bars, and entertainment options within walking distance. My apartment itself is spacious and quiet, which has been a welcome respite from the hustle and bustle of city living. However, the lack of amenities is a significant drawback. The small gym and pool are often crowded, and it would be nice to have more options for recreation and relaxation. The safety concerns are also a worry, particularly with the abandoned lot nearby and the always-open gates. While I haven't had any personal issues, it's unsettling to see unfamiliar people wandering around the area at night. The train noise is another major issue. While I've grown accustomed to it over time, it's still a disruption, especially when the horns blast for extended periods. I wish I had been informed about this before signing my lease, as it might have been a deal-breaker for me. The constant construction has also been a frustration, with equipment and noise disrupting my daily life. Despite these issues, I have to acknowledge that Uptown Gardens has been a decent place to call home. The management team's attentiveness and the apartment's spaciousness have made up for some of the shortcomings. If you're considering moving to Uptown Gardens, I would recommend weighing the pros and cons carefully and doing your research. It's not the perfect complex, but it might be a good fit for you if you prioritize location and a quiet, spacious living space. Just be aware of the potential drawbacks, and don't hesitate to ask questions before signing a lease.

Overall, it's an average dining experience, nothing spectacular but fills the hunger. The ambiance is nice, but it can't compensate for the limited options and potentially stale food. If you're in the area and craving Chinese food on a tight budget, this place might suffice. However, if you're willing to spend a bit more, I'd recommend exploring other options like Buffet Asia for a more satisfying meal with a wider variety of fresh dishes.

The lack of professionalism and fairness was appalling. My mother's win was clearly legitimate, yet the employees failed to acknowledge it. The bingo supervisor's rude attitude only added to our frustration. Overall, our Mother's Day celebration was ruined by the poor management and dishonest practices at this establishment. We will not be returning and will be taking our business to Lone Butte or Fort McDowell, where bingo is run with integrity.

Despite my mixed experiences, I decided to give them another try at their new location. Unfortunately, the inconsistencies persisted. The atmosphere of the new place is nicer, but the service remains hit-or-miss. On my latest visit, our server seemed overwhelmed, taking a long time to take our orders and forgetting one of our appetizers. However, the food was still decent, and I enjoyed my chili relleno. My husband, on the other hand, was not impressed with his dish again. The prices have not changed, and I still feel that they are slightly overpriced for the quality and portion size. The fact that they charge extra for chips and salsa is also a bit of a turn-off. Overall, I appreciate the effort they put into their cooking, but the unreliable service and pricing issues prevent me from fully enjoying my experiences here. Perhaps with more consistent service and a revision of their pricing strategy, I would consider bumping up my rating. Until then, I will remain a somewhat satisfied but mostly disappointed customer.

I'm definitely looking forward to checking that out. The overall atmosphere was electric, and I loved the variety of music they played. Our group had an amazing time dancing and singing along to the songs. The staff were attentive and ensured our glasses were always full. Although the bottle service was a bit steep for my taste, it didn't deter from the overall experience. I've already recommended Blue Martini to my friends, and we're planning to go back soon. The fact that they have themed nights, like the Halloween party we attended, makes it a great spot to try something new and exciting.

Overall, our experience was pleasant, but I was slightly underwhelmed by the buffet options. The quality and flavor of my husband's dishes, on the other hand, were impressive. Perhaps the buffet is not the best representation of the restaurant's capabilities. I would be willing to give them another try, ordering off the menu next time to fully appreciate their culinary skills. For now, I remain somewhat neutral, knowing that similar establishments, like Amarind's, have set a high standard for Thai cuisine in the city. Service was friendly and attentive, adding to the positive atmosphere.
Foi uma grande decepção, pois esperávamos muito mais confort e qualidade pelo preço pago, mesmo sendo baixo, a experiência não valeu a pena.
Disappointing visit overall, expected more from a popular restaurant, especially with their salad options, and better customer service to resolve issues promptly.

The lack of variety in their menu is quite disappointing, and the prices they charge are not justified by the quality or speed of service. For a pizza place to thrive, especially in a competitive market, they need to offer more options or excel in their specialty. Unfortunately, this establishment falls short on both counts. The long wait times, combined with the limited menu and high prices, make it unlikely that we will return for a third visit. Overall, our experiences have been underwhelming, and we would not recommend this place to others.

was a bit slow and seemed disorganized, which was surprising given the small number of customers at the time. However, the friendly atmosphere and exceptional quality of the food made up for it. The exotic crepe was a highlight, with the combination of fresh fruit and coconut sorbet being absolutely divine. The fresh fruit tart I took to go was also a winner, with a perfect balance of sweet and tangy. Overall, I'm glad I got to experience this charming creperie with my cousins, and we're all already planning our next visit. Despite the minor service hiccup, I would highly recommend this place to anyone with a sweet tooth.

The quality of the food is impressive, especially considering it's a food court establishment. The Greek Salad with Chicken was refreshing and flavorful, with a generous portion of grilled chicken. The ingredients were fresh and the dressing was tangy, making for a satisfying meal. I appreciate that they offer half orders, which is perfect for a lighter bite or for those who want to try a smaller portion. The prices are also reasonable, making it a great value for the quality and quantity of food received. Overall, I would highly recommend this location for a quick and delicious meal while shopping at the mall.

The atmosphere is cozy and inviting, with a warm decor that makes you feel like you're in a family member's kitchen. The service is top-notch, with friendly and attentive staff who ensure that your cup is always full and your plate is never empty. The prices are indeed reasonable, with generous portions that will keep you fueled for the rest of the day. Overall, I'm so glad I stumbled upon The Original Sunrise Cafe, and I highly recommend it to anyone looking for a delicious, homemade-style breakfast in Vegas. It's a hidden gem that's definitely worth seeking out.

As we sat around the traditional Ethiopian table, sharing food and conversation, I felt a sense of community and warmth that is often lacking in modern dining experiences. The staff at Abay seemed to genuinely care about our enjoyment, taking the time to explain the different dishes and making sure we had everything we needed. The combination platter was a great way to sample a variety of flavors and textures, and the portion size was generous to say the least. I was impressed by the complexity of the spices and seasonings used in each dish, and the fact that each bite was a surprise - sometimes spicy, sometimes savory, but always delicious. The atmosphere of the restaurant was cozy and intimate, with soft music playing in the background and the aroma of exotic spices wafting through the air. The fact that it's BYOB is a definite plus, as it allows diners to bring their own wine and enjoy it with their meal without breaking the bank. The corkage fee was incredibly reasonable, and our bottle of wine paired perfectly with the rich and flavorful food. Overall, I would highly recommend Abay to anyone looking to try something new and exciting. The unique dining experience, combined with the delicious food and friendly staff, make it a must-visit destination for foodies and adventurous eaters alike. Whether you're a seasoned fan of Ethiopian cuisine or just looking to try something new, Abay is sure to impress.

The lack of attention to detail and subpar cleaning was astonishing, especially considering the hefty price tag. For $150, I expected a pristine vehicle, but what I got was a half-hearted attempt at cleaning. The fact that I had to re-clean my car myself is a clear indication of their incompetence. Needless to say, I will be taking my business elsewhere and advising others to do the same.

The venue itself was well-designed, with multiple levels and areas to explore, including a large pool and several bars. The crowd was lively and energetic, and the music was pumping all night long. However, the main draw for us was Ellie Goulding, and it was disappointing that she didn't perform as advertised. Instead, she made a guest appearance as a DJ, which wasn't what we were expecting. Despite this, we still managed to have a great time, dancing and enjoying the atmosphere. The staff were friendly and attentive, but the prices of the drinks were outrageous. Overall, it was a fun night out in Vegas, but not quite what we were promised. If you're looking for a lively outdoor party scene, this might be the place for you, but be aware of the potential for misleading advertising and expensive drinks.

As we left Roland's, my mother and I couldn't help but feel a bit underwhelmed by the whole experience. The sign had promised so much, touting their famous Lobster Rolls and Bloody Mary's, but in reality, it felt like they fell short. The lobster itself was certainly fresh and flavorful, but the presentation and portion size left something to be desired. And the Bloody Mary, which I had been looking forward to, was overpowered by the horseradish, making it undrinkable for me. The atmosphere of the place also didn't help, as it was freezing inside and we had to keep our winter coats on throughout our meal. It was a shame, really, because we had been excited to try Roland's and had heard good things about it. But based on our experience, I'm not sure we'll be back anytime soon. Maybe they were just having an off day, but for the price, I expect a lot more. We ended up leaving and continuing our shopping trip, still a bit peckish and disappointed by the lackluster snack. Needless to say, our high hopes for Roland's were dashed, and we'll have to look elsewhere for a satisfying bite to eat on our next trip to the strip.

The food itself was delicious, with unique flavor combinations that showcased the chef's skill. However, the exceptional cuisine was overshadowed by the hostile atmosphere created by the staff. A little kindness and courtesy would go a long way in making this establishment a standout in Edinburgh's dining scene, rather than a memorable disappointment due to poor service. With some refinement in customer service, this place could truly thrive.

Despite the unfriendly demeanor of the staff, I must admit that the store has a unique charm to it. The selection of Native American crafts and supplies is unparalleled, and I've found some truly one-of-a-kind items here. However, the lack of representation from other tribes is still a major drawback for me. As a Native American myself, I'd love to see more diversity in the products and artwork on display. The fact that everything seems to be Navajo-dominated can be overwhelming and exclusionary. Nevertheless, if you're looking for an authentic Native American shopping experience, this store is still worth a visit. Just be prepared for some attitude from the staff and customers, and don't expect to be catered to. It's a bit of a rough-around-the-edges kind of place, but the goods are genuine and the atmosphere is undeniably Native. With some improvements to customer service and representation, this store could truly thrive and become a staple of the Native American community. Until then, I'll continue to shop here, but with tempered expectations.

The bed was comfortable and amenities were satisfactory. Overall, despite initial issues, the stay was pleasant and staff were apologetic. With some improvements to their key card system and new staff training, this place has great potential. I would recommend it for budget-friendly travelers, just be patient and prepared for any minor hiccups.

The atmosphere of the shop is also worth mentioning, as it provides a cozy and inviting space for customers to relax and enjoy their beverages. The seating area is comfortable and well-designed, with ample seating options for both small and large groups. The staff is friendly and attentive, always willing to offer recommendations or answer questions about their menu items. I appreciate the fact that they take the time to prepare each drink to order, rather than relying on pre-made mixes or automated machines. This attention to detail and commitment to quality is what sets Coffee Bean and Tea Leaf apart from other coffee shops in the area. Overall, I'm glad they decided to open another location in the district, and I look forward to becoming a regular customer. With its unique tea options and high-quality coffee, this shop is sure to become a favorite among coffee and tea lovers alike.

Overall, it was an average experience. The staff were friendly and helpful, but the hotel itself felt a bit dated. We didn't have any major complaints, but it didn't exceed our expectations either. For the price, it was a good value, and the location was convenient. We might consider staying here again in the future, but we'd also be open to exploring other options.

Overall, our experience at the Palace Tower was a mixed bag. While we appreciated the upgrade to a nicer room, the initial issues with our accommodation were a major turnoff. The lack of free Wi-Fi and outdated tech amenities made it feel like we were staying in a budget hotel, not a luxury resort. The tense atmosphere created by the manager yelling at the bartender was also unsettling. However, we did enjoy the buffet, Payard crepe and sweets, and the pool and gym facilities were top-notch. It's clear that this casino prioritizes profits over guest satisfaction, which is a shame. If you're looking for a more welcoming and accommodating experience, we would recommend considering alternative options like the Bellagio or Planet Hollywood. Despite the few highlights, our stay was largely disappointing and we wouldn't rush to return. The deceptive practices, like the paid buffet line skip, only added to our frustration.

As a long-time fan of the Short Leash food truck, I was disappointed to find that the restaurant didn't quite live up to my expectations. The lack of attention from our waitress was a major issue, and it seemed like we were forgotten about after our food was delivered. The fact that we had to eat without silverware was not only inconvenient, but it also made the experience feel rushed and unrefined. The food itself was also a letdown, with my hot dog lacking the toppings that I've come to love from the truck. The salad was bland and uninspiring, and the fact that it wasn't dressed properly was a missed opportunity to add some much-needed flavor. Despite these issues, I do want to give Short Leash the benefit of the doubt. As I mentioned, it was First Friday, and the place was likely bustling with customers. Maybe they were just having an off night, and I'm willing to give them another chance to prove themselves. The prices, especially for drinks, were very reasonable, and I appreciate that they're offering affordable options for customers. However, if I'm being honest, I was expecting a lot more from a restaurant that has built such a loyal following from its food truck. I hope that Short Leash will take my feedback to heart and work on improving their service and food quality, because I truly want to see them succeed. For now, I'll stick with the food truck, but I'll be keeping an eye on the restaurant to see if they can turn things around.

Overall, our experience at Meat & Potato was a mixed bag. While the unique, old-style ambiance was intriguing, the crowded seating and noise level detracted from our dining experience. The food, although above average, did not live up to our expectations, especially considering the prices. The mussel appetizer was fresh and flavorful, but the 36 oz ribeye, while cooked to perfection, lacked a wow factor. The steak fries were crispy and well-seasoned, but not particularly memorable. Our waiter, despite the challenges posed by the crowded conditions, was friendly and made an effort to provide good service. However, the delays between courses and the difficulty in getting his attention were notable. Perhaps a weekday visit or a seat at the bar would be a better way to experience Meat & Potato, as the lively atmosphere and extensive drink selection seem well-suited to a more casual, social outing. As a romantic dinner destination, however, it falls short due to the noise and cramped seating. With some adjustments to the seating configuration and service, Meat & Potato could reach its full potential and become a top-notch dining establishment.

The service was friendly and efficient, despite the morning rush. The staff seemed well-organized and managed to keep up with the demanding pace. I appreciated the fact that they had a separate counter for to-go orders, which helped to speed up the process. However, the atmosphere of the restaurant itself was not particularly inviting for a sit-down meal, which might be why I opted for take-out in the first place. The decor was modern and sleek, but it lacked a warm and cozy ambiance that I typically look for in a breakfast spot. Overall, I would recommend this place for their steel cut oatmeal, but perhaps not for a leisurely breakfast experience. The prices are a bit steep, but if you're looking for a healthy and filling start to your day in Vegas, it might be worth the splurge. I'd consider returning to try some of their other menu items, but for now, the oatmeal remains the highlight of my visit.

I was thoroughly impressed with the efficiency and customer service I received. The price was also very reasonable, especially considering the quick turnaround time. I would highly recommend Nextech to anyone in need of phone repairs. The shop was clean and organized, and Cody's expertise was evident in the way he handled my device. Overall, my experience was top-notch, and I appreciate the exceptional service I received. I will definitely be returning to Nextech for any future repair needs, and I will be recommending them to friends and family. Five stars isn't enough!

Overall, my experience at this location has been disappointing. The lack of professionalism and respect for customers is appalling. Despite the few friendly workers, the majority seem to be more interested in having their own party than providing good service. The loud music and horseplay create an uncomfortable atmosphere, making it difficult to focus or relax. I'll stick to the location near Walmart, where the staff is courteous and the environment is more welcoming. Unfortunately, this location's behavior has left a bad taste, and I wouldn't recommend it to others. One star is even generous.

Overall, I would recommend this restaurant to anyone looking for a trendy spot to grab dinner before a night out. The service was also top-notch, with friendly and attentive waitstaff who made sure our glasses were always full. Although the prices may be a bit steep for some, the unique atmosphere and flavorful dishes make it worth the extra cost. I'm already looking forward to my next visit, and I'm excited to try more of their spicy options. The bar overlooking the kitchen seems like it would be a great spot to sit and watch the chefs at work, and I think it would add an extra layer of entertainment to the dining experience.

As I continued to browse the shop, I was impressed by the vast array of items on display. From vintage baseball cards to game-worn jerseys, and even rare sports equipment, the selection was truly impressive. The two guys working at the shop were more than happy to share stories and anecdotes about the various items, which added to the overall experience. My husband, being the avid Cubs fan that he is, was particularly thrilled to chat with them about the team's history and some of the notable players. One of the things that struck me about the shop was the attention to detail and the care with which the items were displayed. Each piece was carefully framed, mounted, or showcased, and the overall presentation was very professional. I was also pleased to see that the shop had a wide range of items to suit different budgets and interests. While some of the more rare and unique pieces were certainly pricey, there were also more affordable options available, such as the unsigned photo I purchased. Despite the crowds and the busy atmosphere, the shop felt welcoming and inviting. The staff were friendly and knowledgeable, and they seemed genuinely passionate about sports and memorabilia. I appreciated the fact that they were willing to chat and share their expertise, rather than simply trying to make a sale. Overall, I would definitely recommend this shop to anyone who is interested in sports memorabilia or simply looking for a unique and interesting place to browse. In terms of suggestions for improvement, I think the shop could benefit from a bit more space and a more streamlined layout. As I mentioned earlier, it can get quite crowded and busy, especially during signings and other events. Additionally, it might be helpful to have a bit more signage or clear pricing information, as some of the items were not clearly labeled. However, these are minor quibbles, and overall I was very pleased with my experience at the shop. If you're a sports fan or just looking for something fun to do, I would definitely recommend checking it out.

I may be the only person to think this place isn't so great. I'm here if friends make me go, it's right in the heart of Noda on the corner of 36th St. and every time I go, I feel like I want to knock at least one person out. Every time I'm here, it's so crowded, and then you have to deal with a big, bad security guy that takes his position way over the line. On one occasion, I came here with my deaf friends on their evening out, and I'll never forget the looks from the "crowd" of people there - extremely rude. The atmosphere is just too generic for my taste, and the crowd doesn't help. If you enjoy a crowded space with an absentminded crowd, then this might be the place for you, but it's definitely not my cup of tea.

The staff is friendly and knowledgeable, making it a great experience for both kids and adults. The interactive displays are engaging and fun, with something new to discover each visit, making the yearly pass a great value.
Prices are reasonable, portions are generous, and the overall experience is wonderful, making it a must-visit for delicious Thai food.

As I continued to explore the suite, I was impressed by the attention to detail and the luxurious amenities that were provided. The custom-made pool table was a great touch, and the wet bar area, although not yet completed, showed promise of being a fantastic spot to entertain guests. The living room was equipped with everything I needed to relax and unwind, from the large flat-screen TV to the Wii game console and Bose sound system. The bedroom was truly the pièce de résistance, with its dark and sexy decor, crystal lamps, and massive leather headboard. The king-size bed was incredibly comfortable, and I appreciated the fact that there was another large flat-screen TV opposite the bed, perfect for watching movies or sports. The master bath was truly opulent, with its marble floors, massive walk-in shower, and 4-person jacuzzi tub. I even appreciated the small touch of having a phone in the bathroom, just in case I needed to make a call while, ahem, taking care of business. One of the things that really stood out to me about the Celebrity Suites was the service. From the moment I arrived, the staff at the Hard Rock were friendly, attentive, and eager to ensure that my stay was nothing short of exceptional. Whether I needed extra towels, a drink from the bar, or recommendations for restaurants and shows, the staff were always happy to help. Overall, I would highly recommend the Celebrity Suites at the Hard Rock to anyone looking to splurge and experience the ultimate in luxury and decadence in Las Vegas. With its stunning decor, luxurious amenities, and exceptional service, the Hard Rock has truly outdone itself with these new suites. Whether you're celebrating a special occasion or just want to treat yourself to a night of pampering, the Celebrity Suites are the perfect choice. So why settle for an ordinary hotel room when you can live like a rock star? Book your stay at the Hard Rock and experience the ultimate in Vegas luxury.

Overall, it's an average dining experience, but the generous portions and friendly owner make up for some of the shortcomings, making it a decent option for a quick and filling meal, especially if you're a fan of their signature orange chicken dish served fresh.

The atmosphere was cozy and intimate, perfect for a night out with friends. The prices were reasonable considering the high quality of the food and service. Overall, we had a fantastic experience and would highly recommend this restaurant to anyone looking for a delicious meal and exceptional service. With its great food, lovely atmosphere, and outstanding staff, it's sure to become a favorite destination for special occasions and casual nights out alike, making it a must-visit.

The staff at both the Rum Runner Lounge and the Badger Cafe are incredibly friendly and welcoming. They always seem to remember us, even when we haven't been in for a while, and they're quick to recommend new menu items or drinks. The food at the Badger Cafe is top-notch, with a great selection of burgers, sandwiches, and salads. I'm particularly fond of their breakfast menu, which is served all day. The portion sizes are generous, and the prices are very reasonable. Overall, I highly recommend the Rum Runner Lounge and the Badger Cafe to anyone looking for a relaxed, low-key spot to grab a bite or hang out with friends.

As the show dragged on, I found myself checking my watch multiple times, willing the minutes to pass faster. The performances, although technically impressive, lacked a certain je ne sais quoi that would have kept me engaged. The crowd around me seemed just as unenthusiastic, with many people fidgeting in their seats or whispering to each other. I was expecting a spectacle that would leave me in awe, but instead, I felt like I was watching a series of disconnected acts that failed to coalesce into a cohesive whole. The pool, which I had assumed would be a unique and exciting element, ended up being more of a gimmick than a integral part of the show. The water-based performances were few and far between, and when they did occur, they felt like a rehashing of things I'd seen before. My wife, who had been looking forward to the show all day, was equally underwhelmed, and we both left feeling disappointed and ripped off. For the exorbitant price we paid, I expected a truly unforgettable experience, but what we got was a lackluster display of circus acts that failed to deliver on its promise of wonder and enchantment. Needless to say, I would not recommend CIRQUE to anyone, and would instead steer them towards more entertaining and value-for-money options like ABSINTHE.

Flavors and atmosphere transported me back home. Authentic Taiwanese cuisine, a rare gem, made my morning unforgettable, with each bite a delightful reminder of the island's rich culinary heritage, a must-visit for anyone seeking genuine Taiwanese breakfast experience.

Overall, the experience was subpar and not worth the money. The food was hit or miss, with some items being enjoyable while others were overpowered by strong flavors. The service was lacking, with our server seemingly disappearing after taking our order. This lack of attention and care made the entire experience feel unwelcoming. With numerous other options available in Las Vegas, it's unlikely we'll return to this establishment. The free entrée voucher was a nice gesture, but it wasn't enough to make up for the disappointing service and inconsistent food quality.
