I was particularly impressed by the little touches, like the Aveda toiletries and complimentary robes, which showed that the resort was dedicated to providing a luxurious experience. If I were to suggest any improvements, it would be to perhaps add more dining options or activities on site, but overall, I was thoroughly satisfied with my stay. I would highly recommend Firesky Resort & Spa to anyone looking for a relaxing getaway, and I look forward to returning in the future to experience even more of what this wonderful resort has to offer.

The atmosphere is cozy and inviting, making it perfect for a quick bite or meeting with friends. Overall, I highly recommend this restaurant for its excellent cuisine, generous servings, and top-notch service. Whether you're a fan of Greek food or just looking to try something new, this place is sure to please. Give it a try and you won't be disappointed, just be prepared for a potential wait during peak hours.

I'm thoroughly impressed by the vast selection of international snacks at Lee Lee's. The moment I step into the store, I'm transported to a global market, with the sights, smells, and tastes of different cultures surrounding me. The store's organization by culinary location makes it easy to navigate and discover new treats. I've tried the Nestle Prestigio chocolate wafers, and they're a game-changer - the combination of coconut and chocolate is addictive. The Pucca Chocolate is another favorite, with its unique pretzel and milk chocolate filling. And for any chocolate lover, the Lotte Ghana Chocolate is a must-try. With its rich, smooth flavor, it's no wonder it's a popular choice. Overall, Lee Lee's is a treasure trove of international snacks, and I highly recommend it to anyone looking to try something new and exciting. Whether you're craving Asian, Latin American, or Indian treats, Lee Lee's has got you covered.

Hopefully, that will make a difference, and I can finally enjoy a hot meal here. The staff is friendly, and the atmosphere is cozy, so I'm willing to give them another chance to get it right and provide the experience I know they're capable of.

Overall, our experience was underwhelming. The food lacked variety and the flavors were overly reliant on sweet sauces. While the staff was polite, the service was minimal. For a fast-food chain, Panda Express failed to impress, and we'll likely stick to other options like Chipotle for a more satisfying meal.

I also appreciate the location of Excalibur, it's situated at the southern end of the Strip, making it easy to get to and from other hotels and attractions. The monorail station is conveniently located nearby, and there are plenty of taxi and ride-sharing options available. We've never had a problem getting around, and the staff at Excalibur are always helpful in arranging transportation or providing directions. Another benefit of staying at Excalibur is the variety of entertainment options available. The hotel has its own casino, of course, but it's also home to several restaurants, bars, and shows. We've seen a few of the productions, including the Tournament of Kings dinner show, which is a lot of fun. And, as I mentioned earlier, there are plenty of other dining options within walking distance, including the famous Lindo Michoacan Mexican restaurant and the Shake Shack. One thing to note is that Excalibur can get pretty busy, especially on weekends and during peak travel seasons. The casino and common areas can get crowded, and the lines for check-in and check-out can be long. However, we've never had a problem with noise or disruptions in our room, and the staff do a good job of managing the crowds. Overall, I think Excalibur is a great option for anyone looking for a affordable, no-frills place to stay on the Strip. It may not be the fanciest or most luxurious hotel, but it's clean, comfortable, and convenient. And, as I said, it's hard to beat the price. We'll definitely be back, and I'd recommend Excalibur to anyone looking for a good value in Las Vegas.

In retrospect, the initial sales pitch did feel somewhat aggressive, but the quality of the products and the expertise of the staff won me over. The slow-mo video analysis was incredibly insightful, and it really helped me understand my running mechanics. The shoes I purchased have been a game-changer for my workouts, and the insoles have provided excellent support and comfort. Although the prices were steeper than I anticipated, I'm willing to pay a premium for products that truly deliver. I would recommend RoadRunner to fellow runners, but with the caveat to be prepared for a potential hard sell. Overall, my experience was positive, and I'm enjoying my new gear. With a bit more transparency in their pricing, I would have gladly given them a full five stars.

The entire experience was a disaster from start to finish, and it's clear that the staff at this establishment are in dire need of some serious customer service training. The fact that our waiter felt entitled to yell at us not once, but twice, is absolutely appalling and completely unacceptable. It's not like we were being difficult or asking for special treatment - we just wanted to be treated with some basic respect and courtesy. The food, as I mentioned earlier, was subpar and not worth the money we paid. The fact that some items were cold and barely edible is a serious concern, and it's clear that the kitchen is not paying attention to the quality of the dishes they're serving. The only redeeming factor was the dessert selection, but even that wasn't enough to make up for the terrible service and mediocre food. What really takes the cake, though, is the waiter's behavior when it came time to pay the bill. Watching us like a hawk to see how much we would tip, and then yelling at my friend when he didn't leave enough, is just disgusting. It's not like we owed him anything - the service was bad, and we shouldn't have been expected to reward him for it. Overall, I would strongly advise against eating at this restaurant, especially if you're a student looking to take advantage of their advertised discount. There are far better options in Montreal, and you'd be wise to avoid this place at all costs.

Overall, I was thoroughly impressed with this hidden gem. The combination of delicious food, generous drink portions, and exceptional service makes it an ideal spot for groups and solo visitors alike. Whether you're a student at UNLV or just looking for a relaxed dining experience, this place is definitely worth checking out. With its convenient location and late hours, it's perfect for a night out with friends or a quick bite after a long day. I would highly recommend this spot to anyone looking for a welcoming and satisfying dining experience in the area.

As I reflect on our exceptional dining experience, I am reminded of the attention to detail that permeated every aspect of the meal. From the impeccable service to the exquisite cuisine, each element worked in harmony to create a truly unforgettable evening. The wait staff's knowledge of the menu and their willingness to answer questions and make recommendations was impressive, and their enthusiasm for the dishes was infectious. The pacing of the meal was also noteworthy, with each course arriving at a leisurely pace that allowed us to fully appreciate the flavors and textures of each dish. The portion sizes were generous, but not overwhelming, and the presentation of each plate was visually stunning. The use of fresh, seasonal ingredients was evident in every bite, and the chef's creativity and skill in combining flavors and techniques was inspiring. One of the most impressive aspects of the meal was the way in which the restaurant balanced traditional cuisine with innovative twists and surprises. The turtle soup, for example, was a classic dish that was elevated by the use of fresh, high-quality ingredients and a delicate touch. The gumbo du jour, on the other hand, was a bold and adventurous choice that paid off in a big way, with the alligator sausage adding a unique and exciting flavor dimension to the dish. The main courses were equally impressive, with the rack of wild boar standing out as a particular highlight. The combination of the tender, flavorful meat with the sweet and spicy accompaniments was absolute perfection, and the mashed potatoes were a revelation - creamy, fluffy, and full of depth and richness. The lump crab cake was another standout, with a generous portion of succulent crab meat that was perfectly seasoned and cooked. As we finished our meal and prepared to leave, I couldn't help but feel a sense of gratitude and appreciation for the exceptional experience we had just enjoyed. The restaurant had truly outdone itself, and I felt lucky to have had the opportunity to dine there. As I mentioned earlier, I wish there were more than 5 stars to give, as this restaurant has set a new standard for excellence in my book. If you're looking for a truly exceptional dining experience, look no further - this restaurant is sure to impress even the most discerning palates.

The dishes lacked flavor and presentation was unappealing. For a restaurant with so many options, the execution fell short. Perhaps focusing on a smaller, well-crafted menu would elevate the dining experience. As it stands, the restaurant's attempts at variety come across as disjointed and uninspired, leaving patrons underwhelmed and disappointed. A bit more attention to detail could make a significant difference.

I demand a full refund and an explanation for their fraudulent actions. Their customer service is unhelpful and unresponsive. I would not recommend this company to anyone, and I advise others to be cautious when dealing with them. It's clear they prioritize making a quick buck over providing honest service. Avoid them at all costs to prevent similar financial headaches and stress.
Unfortunately, the rest of the menu falls short, lacking balance and freshness, making it a disappointing experience overall, despite the excellent chips and salsa.

As we finished our drinks and prepared to leave, I couldn't help but feel underwhelmed by the overall experience. The atmosphere, which I had expected to be lively and vibrant, felt instead hollow and lacking in energy. The bartender's attitude, while not outright rude, seemed dismissive and unapologetic, which didn't help to alleviate my growing dissatisfaction. Despite the unique decor and intriguing menu, the subpar service and mistakes with our order left a sour taste in my mouth. It's a shame, really, as I had been looking forward to trying 5Church and was excited to see what they had to offer. Unfortunately, our visit fell short of expectations, and I'm not sure if I'll be returning anytime soon. With so many other great options in the area, it's going to take more than a trendy vibe and creative cocktails to keep customers coming back. Unless they can step up their service game and attention to detail, I fear that 5Church may indeed follow in the footsteps of its predecessors and struggle to establish a loyal following.

Overall, our experience was marred by the inattentive service, which overshadowed the generally good food. Despite the delicious ravioli and tender pork belly, the long wait times and neglect by our server left a sour taste. With some improvement in service, this establishment could reach its full potential. As it stands, I'd cautiously recommend it, but with the caveat to perhaps visit with a larger group to ensure more attentive care. Hopefully, our experience was an isolated incident.

The whole experience felt like a factory line, where patients are just a means to an end. I left feeling frustrated, uninformed, and like I'd wasted my money. The clinic's focus on efficiency and profit is clearly prioritized over patient care and satisfaction. As someone who was expecting expert advice and personalized attention, I was severely let down. The fact that I was referred to the in-house aesthetician for further guidance, at an additional cost, only added to my disappointment. It's unacceptable that a dermatologist wouldn't take the time to address basic concerns about skin care and potential health issues. I would not recommend this clinic to anyone seeking genuine and comprehensive dermatological care. The high ratings and reputation of this clinic are truly puzzling, and I hope that others will take my experience into consideration before making an appointment.

Extremely disappointed and frustrated with the experience. The inconvenience caused was significant, and the lack of reliability is alarming. A business that can't uphold its own hours is untrustworthy. I wasted my time and gas, only to be left with nothing. Needless to say, I will not be returning and would advise others to beware of their false operating hours.

I'm still trying to process how a buffet that's supposed to be one of the top-rated in Las Vegas could be such a letdown. The atmosphere was lively, I'll give them that. The decor was modern and sleek, and the staff were friendly and attentive. But when it comes to the food, which is the main event at a buffet, Wicked Spoon fell woefully short. I mean, who serves bone marrow with crouton-like bread? It's just lazy. And don't even get me started on the octopus salad. I've had better luck with random food combinations at a middle school cafeteria. The Korean grilled shortribs were the sole redeeming dish of the night, but even that was just a basic, no-frills preparation. I've had better shortribs at a Korean BBQ joint in a strip mall. The rest of the dishes were just a mess. Overcooked, underseasoned, and uninspired. I swear, I've had better luck with buffet food at a Holiday Inn. And the prices! $45 per person with tax? You've got to be kidding me. I've eaten at some of the best restaurants in the city for less than that. I'm starting to think that the Yelpers who rave about Wicked Spoon are either easily impressed or have never actually been to a good buffet. I mean, I've been to Bacchanal at Caesar's, and that's a real buffet. The selection is vast, the quality is top-notch, and the prices are comparable. Wicked Spoon can't hold a candle to it. So, if you're looking for a mediocre buffet experience with a hefty price tag, then Wicked Spoon is the place for you. But if you want a truly exceptional dining experience, keep looking. Trust me, you won't be missing out on anything by skipping Wicked Spoon. As I left the buffet, I couldn't help but feel a sense of disappointment and frustration. I had been looking forward to trying Wicked Spoon all day, and it failed to deliver in every way. Maybe, just maybe, I caught them on a bad night. But I doubt it. With so many other great dining options in Las Vegas, I won't be giving Wicked Spoon another chance to disappoint me.
Completely unacceptable experience, ruined our evening with its incompetence and utter disregard for customer satisfaction and basic requests.

The exceptional service and attention to detail were evident throughout the evening, with the staff knowledgeable and happy to guide us through the extensive menu. Each dish was expertly prepared and presented, with flavors and textures that exceeded our expectations. The atmosphere was sophisticated and elegant, making it the perfect setting for a special occasion or business dinner. Overall, our experience was truly unforgettable, and we left feeling indulged and impressed. The combination of outstanding cuisine, impeccable service, and luxurious ambiance makes this restaurant a must-visit destination for anyone seeking a world-class dining experience.

Unacceptable service and cleanliness standards. Clearly, the management is not taking necessary steps to address these issues, making for a disappointing experience. I will not be returning to this location and would not recommend it to anyone. Serious changes are needed to improve customer satisfaction.
Very disappointing experience, would not recommend to anyone, especially for special occasions when timely delivery matters the most, and reliability is expected.

The service was also subpar, with our server seemingly overwhelmed by our large group. Orders were mixed up and it took a while to get our food. For a restaurant of its caliber, I expected more. The Grand Lux Cafe usually delivers, but this visit was a letdown. Maybe it was an off night, but I hope they step up their game, especially with the high prices they charge. Until then, I'll think twice before returning, especially with a group.

As I continued to explore the Arizona Science Center, I was impressed by the variety of interactive exhibits that catered to different age groups and interests. The staff were friendly and knowledgeable, always eager to answer questions and provide insights into the various displays. The center's ability to balance education with entertainment is truly commendable, making it an ideal destination for families, school groups, and even solo visitors like myself. One of the aspects that struck me was the attention to detail in each exhibit. For instance, the Pirates Exhibit not only showcased the artifacts but also provided a step-by-step explanation of the conservation process, which I found fascinating. Similarly, the Van Gogh exhibit, although unconventional, offered a unique perspective on the artist's work and life. The quotes projected alongside his paintings added a deeper layer of understanding to his art, highlighting the turmoil and passion that drove his creativity. The planetarium show was another highlight of my visit. The presenter's enthusiasm was infectious, and the interactive trivia session before the show was a great way to get the audience engaged. The show itself was breathtaking, with stunning visuals and informative commentary that left me wanting to learn more about the night sky. The Arizona Science Center's commitment to making complex scientific concepts accessible to everyone is truly admirable. What I appreciate most about the Arizona Science Center is its ability to evolve and innovate. With new exhibits and events being added regularly, there's always something new to look forward to. The after-hours event sponsored by Yelp was a great example of this, offering a relaxed and intimate setting to explore the center's offerings. The crowd was smaller, and the atmosphere was more laid-back, allowing me to take my time and fully absorb the exhibits without the usual hustle and bustle. As I left the Arizona Science Center, I couldn't help but feel grateful for the experience. It's a testament to the power of interactive learning and the importance of making science and art accessible to everyone. Whether you're a science buff, an art enthusiast, or simply looking for a fun and educational experience, the Arizona Science Center is a must-visit destination in Phoenix. With its unique exhibits, engaging presentations, and commitment to innovation, it's no wonder that it continues to impress visitors of all ages. I'm already looking forward to my next visit, eager to see what new wonders and discoveries the center has in store.

The amenities were basic, but the staff was friendly. However, the overall atmosphere was overwhelming due to the smoke and noise, making it difficult to fully enjoy my stay despite the affordable price and pleasant pool area.

We were pleased with the generous portion sizes and the quality of the ingredients used. The breading on the chicken was crispy and not too heavy, and the melted mozzarella cheese added a rich and creamy element to the dish. Overall, our experience at Lorenzo's was a positive one, and we would definitely recommend it to others looking for a satisfying and delicious Italian meal. The prices are reasonable, and the atmosphere is welcoming and inviting, making it a great choice for a night out with family or friends. We'll be back to try more of their menu items.

Ich denke, dass das Restaurant ansonsten einen guten Eindruck macht, aber die Preise sollten vielleicht noch einmal überdacht werden. Die Bedienung war aufmerksam und freundlich, was den Besuch angenehm gemacht hat. Wenn man Wert auf gute Qualität legt und nicht so sehr auf die Menge achtet, ist dieses Restaurant definitiv einen Besuch wert. Der libanesische Syrah des Château Heritage ist ein Highlight und passt hervorragend zu den angebotenen Gerichten. Insgesamt würde ich dieses Restaurant weiterempfehlen, jedoch mit der Maßgabe, dass man sich über die Preise im Klaren sein sollte.

As I sat there, I couldn't help but feel grateful for the initial emptiness, which allowed me to fully take in the atmosphere and appreciate the craftsmanship of the bakers. The pistachio croissant was truly exceptional, with a perfect balance of flaky texture and rich, nutty flavor. It's clear that the team at this bakery is dedicated to their craft, and it shows in every detail, from the presentation to the taste. As the morning wore on and the crowd grew, the energy in the room became more lively and welcoming. I struck up a conversation with a few of the regulars, who raved about the bakery's consistency and quality. It's clear that this place has built a loyal following, and for good reason. The selection of pastries and breads is impressive, and everything I tried was delicious. I have to admit, I was a bit disappointed that I didn't get to share my purchases with my housemates as planned. The plain croissants, chocolate bread, and chorizo/mozzarella bread were all devoured on the car ride back to Brooklyn, and I didn't even make it out of Canada before polishing off the last of the treats. It was worth it, though - every bite was a reminder of the wonderful experience I had at this bakery, and I'm already planning my next trip back to Montreal so I can visit again.

As I reflected on my experience, I realized that the potential for this pizzeria is there, but it needs some refinement. The use of canned mushrooms was a letdown, and I hope they consider switching to fresh ingredients in the future. The sparse cheese and underwhelming melt were also areas for improvement. However, the crust's crispiness and the sauce's flavor were redeeming qualities. Given the price point, I expect a higher level of quality and attention to detail. I'm willing to give them the benefit of the doubt, considering they've just opened, and I'm looking forward to trying them again in a few weeks. Perhaps with some time to iron out the kinks, they'll be able to elevate their offerings and provide a more satisfying experience for customers. I'll be keeping an eye on their progress and hoping for a more impressive showing on my next visit. With a few tweaks, this could become a go-to spot for pizza in the neighborhood.

Overall, a pleasant dining experience with some notable dishes. The combination of flavors and textures was enjoyable, making me want to try more of their offerings. The atmosphere was also cozy, adding to the overall satisfaction of my visit, leaving a positive impression.

Food arrived quickly, but server seemed distracted, forgot one order, and didn't check on us often, making the experience even more disappointing and unworthy of a return visit anytime soon unfortunately.
Friendly staff and great food make it a must-visit for a delicious and comfortable dining experience every time.

The quality and taste were average, nothing special. For the price, I expected a premium product, but these mini-muffins fell short. Compared to other bakeries, the value is severely lacking. Overall, I would not recommend this bakery due to their outrageous pricing and tiny portions, making it a disappointing experience.

As I continued to enjoy my meal, I couldn't help but notice the generous portions that came with The Box Combo. The chicken strips were plentiful, and the fries, although not the most spectacular, were cooked to a perfect crisp. The Texas toast, as I mentioned earlier, was a highlight, and I found myself wishing I had ordered a few extra slices on the side. The cole slaw, while not the most creamy or flavorful I've had, provided a nice refreshing contrast to the richness of the chicken and fries. The Cane's Sauce, which I was initially skeptical about, ended up being a pleasant surprise. It had a tangy, slightly sweet flavor that complemented the chicken nicely, and I found myself dipping my strips in it repeatedly. The sweet tea, as I mentioned earlier, was just sweet enough, and I appreciated the fact that it wasn't overpoweringly sugary. One thing that impressed me about Raising Cane's was the evident care and attention that went into preparing my meal. Despite being a fast food joint, the staff seemed to take pride in their work, and the food was clearly made to order. The friendly service only added to the positive experience, and I appreciated the warm smile and welcoming demeanor of the staff member who handed me my order. Overall, while Raising Cane's may not be the healthiest option, it's definitely a great choice for a quick, satisfying meal that's a step above the usual fast food fare. I would recommend it to anyone looking for a tasty, no-frills meal, and I'm looking forward to trying some of their other combos on my next visit. With its friendly staff, generous portions, and tasty food, Raising Cane's has won me over as a fan, and I'm excited to see what other delicious meals they have in store.

The atmosphere is lively and the staff is friendly. Overall, it's a wonderful spot to relax and enjoy a delicious meal with family or friends, and we're already looking forward to our next visit to try more of their tasty dishes and drinks.

Despite the charming atmosphere and appealing baked goods display, our overall experience at Urban Beans was disappointing. The lack of attention to detail, such as forgetting the whipped cream and serving lukewarm beverages, was surprising. The breakfast sandwiches, although generously sized, lacked flavor and texture, with untreated English muffins being a notable letdown. The delay in serving the sandwiches, which arrived after we had finished our drinks, added to the frustration. Given the moderate crowd, we expected more efficiency and care in the preparation and presentation of our order. While we appreciate the dog-friendly policy and the potential for a better experience with espresso and baked goods, our visit fell short of expectations. With some refinement in service, food quality, and cleanliness, Urban Beans could live up to its promising atmosphere and become a top choice for local breakfast and coffee enthusiasts. For now, however, we will explore other options.

I was extremely disappointed and frustrated with the experience, especially since I had confirmed the availability and price with my customer beforehand. The inefficiency of their ticket system and lack of actual stock on the floor is astounding. It's clear that Office Max is not equipped to handle electronics sales, and I would not recommend them to anyone looking for technology products. The significant price difference I found at Fry's Electronics only added to my disappointment, making me wonder how Office Max expects to compete in the electronics market. Overall, my experience was a waste of time and I will be taking my electronics business elsewhere.

The service was top-notch, with our server being attentive and knowledgeable about the menu. They made some great recommendations and ensured that our glasses were always full. The atmosphere was lively and fun, with a great mix of music and decor that added to the overall ambiance. We were impressed by the attention to detail and the care that the staff took to ensure that every aspect of our dining experience was enjoyable. Overall, we were thoroughly impressed with our visit to the Tip Top and would highly recommend it to anyone looking for a great meal and a fun night out in Madison. With its unique menu offerings, extensive drink selection, and excellent service, the Tip Top is definitely a standout in the Madison dining scene. We can't wait to go back and try more of their delicious dishes!
Great service and delicious food, definitely a hidden gem, can't wait to bring my girlfriend and try more of their menu items.

As I sat in the audience, I couldn't help but feel a rush of excitement as the Blue Man Group took the stage. The energy was palpable, and it was clear that the performers were just as enthusiastic as the crowd. The show was a masterclass in creativity, with the group using everything from PVC pipes to LED lights to create an immersive experience. The "balls" segment, which I mentioned earlier, was a particular highlight - it was amazing to see how the group used these giant, bouncy orbs to create a sense of chaos and unpredictability. One of the things that struck me about the show was the way the Blue Man Group interacted with the audience. Despite not speaking a word, they were able to connect with the crowd on a deep level, drawing people in and making them feel like they were part of the performance. The twinkie session, which I mentioned earlier, was a great example of this - it was hilarious to see the group use these innocent-looking snacks to create a sense of mischief and mayhem. Of course, no review of the Blue Man Group would be complete without mentioning the finale, which was truly spectacular. The combination of fast music, flashing lights, and (of course) toilet paper created a sense of sensory overload that was exhilarating and exhausting at the same time. It was the perfect way to cap off an already incredible show, and it left me feeling energized and eager for more. As I left the theater, I was grateful for the opportunity to meet the performers and take some photos. It was clear that they were passionate about what they did, and that they were dedicated to creating a unique and unforgettable experience for their audience. The live band, who played a crucial role in the show, were also on hand to chat and take photos - they were friendly and down-to-earth, and it was great to be able to show my appreciation for their hard work. Overall, I would highly recommend the Blue Man Group to anyone looking for a fun and entertaining night out. The show is suitable for all ages, and it's a great way to experience something truly unique and creative. So if you get the chance to see them, don't hesitate - go for it, and get ready for an unforgettable experience!
Prices are reasonable, and the service is usually friendly, making it a decent option for casual dining or takeout, but nothing particularly stands out beyond their signature wings.

As I delved deeper into the world of La Gourmandine, I discovered that their attention to detail and commitment to using high-quality ingredients truly set them apart from other bakeries. The abricotine, with its delicate balance of flavors and textures, was a masterclass in French patisserie. The flaky, buttery croissant provided a perfect foundation for the rich pastry cream and sweet apricot jam, creating a delightful harmony of flavors that left me craving more. The pain au chocolat, which my friend ordered, was equally impressive, with a generous amount of soft, velvety chocolate filling that complemented the crispy, golden-brown pastry perfectly. I was also impressed by the variety of options available, from classic croissants and danishes to more unique offerings like the abricotine. The presentation of each pastry was also noteworthy, with beautifully crafted designs and a clear attention to detail that made each item almost too pretty to eat. Despite the initial wait in line, the service was friendly and efficient, with the staff happily answering questions and making recommendations. My suggestion to move the seating area outside still stands, as it would not only improve the flow of traffic inside the store but also provide a charming and inviting space for customers to enjoy their pastries. Overall, La Gourmandine is a must-visit destination for anyone looking for authentic, delicious French pastries in Pittsburgh, and I have no doubt that I will be returning again and again to sample more of their creations. With its exceptional quality, charming atmosphere, and dedication to traditional French baking techniques, La Gourmandine is a true gem in the heart of the city.

The burrito lacked the vibrant flavors I'm accustomed to. For the price, I expected more. Perhaps I'm spoiled by my weekly flea market treats, but I believe airports can offer better dining experiences. This meal was a letdown, and I wouldn't recommend it to fellow travelers seeking authentic Mexican cuisine.

to the Summerlin dining scene. The staff were friendly and attentive, but as I mentioned, the plethora of options and explanations for each pizza style and cooking method made the ordering process feel a bit overwhelming. Perhaps simplifying the menu or providing a clearer guide for newcomers would help streamline the experience. Despite the minor missteps, the quality of the ingredients and the creativity of the pizza offerings show promise. With a bit of refinement, particularly in their wine service and menu presentation, this pizzeria could easily become a top destination for pizza enthusiasts in the area. For now, it's a solid choice for those looking to try something new, and I'm interested to see how they continue to evolve and improve. Overall, a good start, and I'm excited to return and taste their progress.
Definitely will be back to sample their menu and enjoy more of their craft beers in a welcoming atmosphere always.

As we waited for our food, we took a glance around the restaurant and noticed the cozy atmosphere, complete with vintage decorations and a warm color scheme. The staff was friendly and attentive, checking in on us frequently to refill our drinks and ensure everything was to our liking. When our food arrived, we were impressed by the generous portion sizes and the presentation of our dishes. The BLT I ordered was cooked to perfection, with crispy bacon, fresh lettuce, and juicy tomato on toasted bread. My friend's club sandwich was equally impressive, with layers of turkey, bacon, lettuce, and tomato stacked high on three slices of bread. The seasoned waffle fries were a nice touch, adding a satisfying crunch to our meals. We both agreed that the food was delicious and exceeded our expectations. The prices were also very reasonable, making it an excellent value for the quality and quantity of food we received. The bar special was an added bonus, and we took advantage of the $1.50 bottles of Bud Light Platinum to quench our thirst. Overall, our experience at Henry's was fantastic, and we're already looking forward to our next visit. The combination of great food, friendly service, and excellent value makes it a must-visit destination for anyone in the area. We're excited to try more of their menu items and explore the bar scene further. With its unassuming exterior and outstanding interior, Henry's is a hidden gem that's sure to become a favorite among locals and visitors alike.

As I continued to explore the buffet, I noticed that the service was attentive and friendly, with staff regularly refilling drinks and clearing tables. However, I did find it a bit odd that the crepe station was so heavily promoted, yet the chef was clearly overwhelmed with the demand. Perhaps having two or more chefs preparing crepes would help to reduce the wait time and improve the overall experience. Despite the crepe station being a bit of a letdown, I was pleasantly surprised by the quality of the other dishes on offer. The mushrooms, as I mentioned earlier, were tasty, although a bit too saucy for my liking. I also enjoyed the variety of cheeses and breads available, which were perfect for snacking on while exploring the rest of the buffet. One thing that did strike me as a bit odd was the lack of crab legs, which several other reviewers had mentioned as a highlight of the buffet. I'm not sure if they were just out of stock or if they're not a regular feature, but it was a bit disappointing not to see them. On the other hand, the creme brulee was absolutely incredible, and I would highly recommend saving room for it. The combination of the creamy custard base and the perfectly caramelized sugar on top was absolute perfection. And the fact that the pastry chef had hidden away a few fruit tarts for special request was a lovely touch - it's always nice to feel like you're getting a little something extra. The atmosphere of the buffet was also a major highlight, with the live birds flying around and the charming French-inspired decor making it feel like a real treat. I loved the option to sit "inside" or "outside", and the fact that the buffet was bustling but not too crowded made it feel like a really special experience. If I were to offer any suggestions for improvement, it would be to consider adding more bathroom facilities - the single toilet was a bit of a bottleneck, and the line was quite long at times. It would also be nice to have a bit more clarity on what's included in the buffet price, as we were under the impression that mimosa was included, but it apparently wasn't. Overall, while the buffet wasn't perfect, I did enjoy it more than my previous experience at Rio, and I would definitely consider returning in the future. Perhaps with a few tweaks to the crepe station and the bathroom situation, this buffet could really reach its full potential and become a must-visit destination for foodies in the area. As it stands, it's still a solid choice for a special occasion or a fun day out with friends, and I would recommend it to anyone looking for a unique and delicious dining experience.

The subpar service and food quality have finally driven us away. Despite its convenience, the constant mistakes and poor food preparation are unbearable. We're willing to trade a shorter drive for a better experience, hoping the next location will redeem the brand's reputation and serve fresher, more accurate orders with a side of good customer service.

Overall, the experience was average, with some hits and misses. The nostalgic factor is strong, but healthy it's not. If you're craving a guilty pleasure, this might satisfy. However, don't expect consistency in portion sizes. For the price, it's a decent option, but don't go in with high expectations for nutritional value or generous servings. It's a classic fast food joint with all the trimmings, including plenty of butter.

As I sat down to enjoy my meal, I couldn't help but appreciate the serene atmosphere and the fact that the food was indeed fresh and delicious. The use of local organic ingredients was evident in the flavors and textures of the dishes, and I appreciated the effort to support the local community. However, the prices did seem a bit steep, especially considering that the seating was exclusively outdoors. The country-store inside was a lovely touch, with its eclectic selection of handmade pastas, canned goods, and other specialty items. It was clear that the owners were passionate about promoting sustainable and artisanal practices. Despite the minor drawbacks, I would still recommend this spot to those looking for a unique and peaceful dining experience. The tree-lined drive and picturesque surroundings made for a lovely setting, and the ability to take a stroll with the baby or leave them in the stroller while socializing was a definite plus for young families. Overall, it's a great option for those seeking a healthy, farm-to-table meal in a relaxed and natural setting.

The fact that they tried to fix it after I complained is not enough to redeem their poor service. A good car wash and detailing should not require a customer to double-check their work. The initial lack of attention to detail and thoroughness is unacceptable, especially for the price paid. I expect a certain level of quality when paying $20 for a cleaning service. Unfortunately, this place fell short of my expectations. The experience left a bad taste in my mouth, and I would not recommend this place to anyone. Until they improve their quality control and attention to detail, I'll be taking my business elsewhere. One star is even generous, considering the subpar service I received.

Overall, I would recommend this place to those seeking traditional Japanese cuisine, but with managed expectations. The service was attentive and friendly, which added to the pleasant atmosphere. However, the prices might deter some customers from returning frequently. In comparison to other Japanese restaurants in the area, this one falls somewhere in the middle – not outstanding, but reliable. With a few tweaks to their menu, such as refining their fried dishes, they could potentially elevate their reputation. As it stands, it's a solid choice for a casual dinner, but not necessarily a destination restaurant.
is a bit steep for a casual morning coffee experience.

Overall, my experience was frustrating and unfulfilling. Despite the helpful customer service, the pressure to make a purchase and limited stock options made for a disappointing visit. I hope to find something worthy of the store credit in the future, but for now, I'm left with a negative impression. Unfortunately, this experience has deterred me from making future purchases, which is a shame given the initial excitement of receiving a gift from this store.

The atmosphere of the restaurant was cozy and inviting, with a modern decor that added to the overall charm. The service was also top-notch, with friendly and attentive staff who ensured that our glasses were always full. What truly impressed me, however, was the quality of the ingredients and the care with which each dish was prepared. The flavors were bold and well-balanced, and you could tell that the chefs were passionate about their craft. Overall, I would highly recommend this place to anyone looking for a delicious and authentic Italian dining experience. The prices were also very reasonable, making it a great value for the quality of food and service received.

I am extremely disappointed and frustrated with the way this situation was handled. The fact that they refused to take responsibility for their mistake and instead blamed me for returning my own clothes is unacceptable. The lack of accountability and poor customer service is shocking, especially considering the high price they charge for their services. I had expected a higher level of quality and attention to detail, but it seems that they are more interested in making a profit than in providing a reliable and trustworthy service. The experience has left a sour taste in my mouth, and I would not recommend this business to anyone. The fact that they are willing to deny any wrongdoing and shift the blame to the customer is a clear indication of their priorities. I hope that others will learn from my experience and think twice before using their services. With so many other laundry options available, it's clear that this business is not worth the hassle and expense. Save yourself the trouble and take your business elsewhere. The convenience of their service is not worth the risk of losing your belongings or dealing with their uncooperative customer service team.

The lack of staffing is unacceptable, especially considering the consistent long lines. It's clear that the staff are doing their best, but they're being set up for failure. The limited parking and overcrowding only add to the frustration. I've tried to be patient and sympathetic, but it's getting to the point where I'd rather go out of my way to avoid this location. With so many other options available, it's surprising that this Post Office hasn't made any changes to improve their service. Until then, I'll be taking my business elsewhere.

Overall, our experience was disappointing, and the poor service overshadowed the affordability of the meal. The steak was overcooked, and the eggs were lukewarm, which further added to our frustration. Although the unique tabasco A1 sauce was a pleasant surprise, it wasn't enough to redeem the subpar food and service. For a 24-hour establishment, we expected more attention to detail and better coordination among the staff. Unfortunately, our visit fell short of expectations, and we would think twice before returning, despite the convenience of their hours and affordable prices. Perhaps they can improve with time and better training.

The breathtaking views of the city and surrounding mountains make every step worthwhile, with unique red rock formations and scenic overlooks to explore, leaving you feeling accomplished and eager to return.

The overall atmosphere of Blue Hound was lively and inviting, perfect for our group gathering. We were impressed by the extensive selection of appetizers, which offered something for everyone. From classic favorites to more unique options, each dish was expertly prepared and presented. Although our waiter seemed slightly put off by our appetizer-only order, the service remained attentive and courteous. The validated parking was a wonderful touch, adding to the overall value and convenience of our experience. We left feeling satisfied and already looking forward to our next visit, eager to explore more of the menu and enjoy the patio area.
Terribly expensive drinks and mediocre food make for a disappointing experience overall unfortunately always.

The service was friendly, but a bit slow. Our server seemed overwhelmed, but still managed to maintain a pleasant demeanor. Overall, it was a decent experience, but the happy hour limitations were a letdown. The Hangar 1 mandarin orange tini was a highlight, and I'd return for that alone. Perhaps a revisit on a less busy day would yield a more impressive experience, allowing me to fully appreciate their offerings.

We were expecting a more modern and luxurious stay, but unfortunately, the room's decor and size fell short of our expectations. The kitchen, although equipped with the essentials, was cramped and made cooking a challenge. The indoor pool was a nice touch, but it was often crowded and noisy. The fact that the resort is not located on the strip was also a drawback, as we had to rely on shuttles or taxis to get to the main attractions. Despite the friendly front desk staff and concierge, our overall experience was marred by the frustrating timeshare presentation and the resort's limitations. If you're looking for a hassle-free and modern stay, you might want to consider other options. However, if you're on a tight budget and don't mind the outdated decor and off-strip location, this resort might still be a decent choice. Just be prepared for the high-pressure sales pitch and plan your itinerary accordingly. Overall, our stay was average at best, and we would likely not return due to the timeshare presentation and the resort's overall lack of polish.

We thoroughly enjoyed our meals and the atmosphere was lively and inviting. The service was top-notch, with attentive waiters who ensured our glasses were always full. Although the prices were a bit steep, the quality and presentation of the dishes made it well worth the extra cost, leaving us with a wonderful dining experience.

As we finished our meal and prepared to leave, I couldn't help but feel a sense of disappointment. The atmosphere, although unique and visually appealing, didn't quite live up to my expectations. The food, while edible, was not impressive, and the prices seemed steep for the quality and quantity we received. I had been looking forward to trying this place for weeks, and the letdown was palpable. Despite the subpar food, our waitress was friendly and attentive, making sure our drinks were always full and checking in on us regularly. However, even her excellent service couldn't make up for the shortcomings of the meal. As we left, I couldn't help but wonder if we had just caught them on a bad night or if this was the norm. I've been to plenty of restaurants that have exceeded my expectations, and unfortunately, this one fell short. The Conquest Sandwich, while tasty, wasn't anything special, and the mushroom burger was a mess. The fries, although crispy and flavorful, couldn't redeem the soggy, falling-apart burger. It's a shame, really, because I had high hopes for this place. Perhaps, as I mentioned earlier, I'll give it another try when I'm 21 and can experience the lounge area. Maybe the atmosphere and drinks will be enough to win me over. But for now, I wouldn't recommend this place to anyone looking for a satisfying, reasonably priced meal. There are plenty of other restaurants in the area that offer better food and value. In retrospect, I think my expectations were inflated by the glowing reviews and photos. It's a good reminder to take online reviews with a grain of salt and not to get too caught up in the hype. Still, I'm always on the lookout for new restaurants to try, and I'm willing to give places a second chance. Maybe someday I'll return and have a better experience. Until then, I'll stick to other eateries that have proven themselves to be consistently delicious and worth the price.

Overall, despite a few minor hiccups with our entrees, the exceptional service and delightful appetizers made our dining experience truly memorable. The complimentary dessert was a lovely touch, and we appreciated the staff's attention to detail. While the kitchen may have been slightly off due to the busy Labor Day weekend, the server's prompt response to our concerns and willingness to make things right was impressive. We would definitely return to this restaurant and recommend it to others, hoping that on a less busy night, the entrees will live up to the high standards set by the appetizers and service.

The lack of cohesion and poorly executed transitions between acts made it feel like a disjointed mess. The attempts at humor and audience interaction fell flat, and the overall atmosphere was more cringeworthy than entertaining. I was expecting a high-energy, captivating show, but what I got was a dull, unimpressive experience. The talent of the individual performers was undeniable, but it was wasted on a lackluster production. I would not recommend this show to anyone, especially at the full price. Even at the discounted rate I paid, I felt ripped off. Unless they seriously revamp the show and address the numerous issues, I would advise others to skip it and explore the many other entertainment options Vegas has to offer. Overall, a disappointing and unmemorable experience.

The service was also quite friendly and attentive, with our server checking in on us regularly to refill our drinks and clear our plates. One thing that did stand out to me was the freshness of the ingredients, particularly the juices and the bacon, which were clearly made with high-quality components. However, as I mentioned earlier, the bagel and lox dish was a bit of a letdown in terms of presentation and value. Despite this, I would still recommend this spot to anyone looking for a convenient and delicious breakfast option while staying at the Saguaro. The atmosphere is certainly a major draw, and the staff's warm hospitality makes for a pleasant dining experience. If you're not too fussy about having a gourmet meal and just want something tasty and easy, then this place is a great choice. Overall, it's a solid option for a casual breakfast, and I would consider returning if I were in the area again.

The atmosphere is welcoming and relaxed, making it perfect for a casual night out with family or friends. The menu offers a great variety of options, and the prices are very reasonable. I've tried several items, and everything has been delicious and freshly prepared. The $6 burger deal is a steal, and the fish tacos are a must-try. Overall, I'm impressed with the quality of food and service, and I'll definitely be back to try more of their menu items. Highly recommended for a low-key, enjoyable dining experience.

The flavors and presentation are consistently impressive. Friendly staff and a cozy atmosphere make each visit enjoyable. I highly recommend Jun's for anyone seeking delicious, authentic Korean cuisine at an affordable price. Their commitment to quality and customer satisfaction is evident in every aspect of the dining experience, leaving me eager to return and try more of their offerings.

Overall, our recent dining experience at Mix was underwhelming, to say the least. The dishes lacked the finesse and attention to detail that we've come to expect from an Alain Ducasse establishment. The atmosphere, while once sleek and modern, now feels dated and over-the-top. Despite the knowledgeable and friendly wait staff, the subpar cuisine and exorbitant prices make it difficult for us to recommend Mix to others. Perhaps with a revamp of the menu and a refresh of the decor, Mix can regain its former glory, but until then, we'll be taking our business elsewhere. The locals seem to have caught on, as the restaurant was surprisingly empty on a weekend evening.

As a sushi aficionado, I was expecting a more authentic and flavorful experience, but unfortunately, Sushi Roku fell short. The lackluster sushi and overpriced special Toro were major letdowns. While my Chilean sea bass was cooked to perfection, the sauce was a misfire, and the pineapple flavor overpowered the truffle miso glaze. The mishap with my date's steak was disappointing, but I appreciate the prompt attention from the host and staff, who quickly rectified the issue. Despite the culinary shortcomings, the service and decor at Sushi Roku were top-notch. Our waiter was attentive and knowledgeable, and the views of the strip were stunning. However, as I always say, good service and ambiance can only take you so far if the food doesn't deliver. If you're a sushi enthusiast like myself, you may want to explore other options. On the other hand, if you're in the mood for something more approachable and don't mind sacrificing some authenticity, Sushi Roku's rolls might be a safer bet. Ultimately, my experience was a mixed bag, and while I appreciate the efforts of the staff, I wouldn't rush back to Sushi Roku for their sushi. Perhaps with some tweaks to their menu and a focus on using fresher, higher-quality ingredients, they could elevate their game and become a contender in the competitive world of sushi. Until then, I'll be taking my sushi cravings elsewhere.
which makes it extremely convenient for a quick and satisfying meal anytime, highly recommend this local hidden gem always.

Insgesamt ist Arlt also eine gute Alternative zu den großen Elektronikmärkten, wenn man in Karlsruhe nach Computerteilen oder Zubehör sucht. Die Preise sind wie erwähnt günstiger und das Angebot ist umfangreich. Leider lässt der Service durch die langen Wartezeiten und den offensichtlichen Personalmangel zu wünschen übrig. Wenn man jedoch genau weiß, was man will und bereit ist, ein wenig zu warten oder die Ware im Voraus zu bestellen, kann man bei Arlt gute Geschäfte machen. Die Möglichkeit, die Ware im Internet zu bestellen und dann im Laden abzuholen, ist praktisch und die 3%-Ersparnis ist ein nettes Bonus. Es wäre jedoch schön, wenn Arlt das Personalproblem in den Griff bekäme, um den Einkaufsprozess noch angenehmer zu gestalten. Bis dahin bleibt Arlt eine gute Option für Computerkram in Karlsruhe, aber mit einigen Einschränkungen. Mit mehr Personal und verbessertem Service würde Arlt sicherlich zu einem noch besseren Anbieter werden und die fünf Sterne von mir erhalten. Bis dahin bleibt es bei vier Sternen, weil der Preis und das Angebot einfach zu gut sind, um nicht positiv hervorzuheben.

Overall, my experience at Bouchon was a mixed bag. While the food was undeniably delicious, the slow service really put a damper on the evening. I understand that handling a large group can be challenging, but it seemed like the staff was unprepared and disorganized. Despite the wait, the hot roasted pistachios and pain epi with butter were a lovely touch, and my salad and entree were both tasty and satisfying. It's clear that the kitchen is capable of producing high-quality dishes, but the front-of-house needs to step up their game. If you're a fan of raw oysters, it seems like Bouchon is the place to be, but for vegetarians, the options are limited. With some improvements to their service, I would consider returning to Bouchon, but for now, I would caution large groups to be prepared for a wait.

The atmosphere was cozy and intimate, with a rustic charm that added to the dining experience. Our server was attentive and knowledgeable, happy to answer questions about the menu and make recommendations. Overall, a fantastic evening with delicious food and excellent service, highly recommended for a night out.

The atmosphere of the Grapevine is also noteworthy, with a cozy and intimate setting that makes you feel like you're among friends. The decor is tasteful and understated, allowing the focus to remain on the wine and conversation. Whether you're a seasoned oenophile or just starting to explore the world of wine, the Grapevine is an ideal spot to learn and discover new favorites. The staff's passion for wine is infectious, and they're always happy to offer recommendations or share stories about the different varietals and vineyards they feature. I've attended a few of their "Guest Bartender" charity events, and they're always a blast. The energy is lively, and it's great to see the community come together to support a good cause. The Grapevine's commitment to philanthropy is truly admirable, and it's clear that they're dedicated to making a positive impact in the area. Overall, I highly recommend the Grapevine to anyone looking for a unique and enjoyable wine experience. With its exceptional selection, knowledgeable staff, and community-focused spirit, it's a must-visit destination for wine lovers in the Baxter area. So grab a glass, pull up a stool, and get ready to indulge in the wonders of wine at the Grapevine!

In addition to the issues we experienced, the overall cleanliness of the room was also a concern. There were dust bunnies under the furniture and a general feeling of neglect. The new paint and pictures that had been added seemed like a superficial attempt to revamp the space, rather than a genuine effort to improve the quality of the accommodations. The lack of attention to detail was further evident in the bathroom, where the spa tub, although a nice feature, was not properly cleaned. We found hair and soap scum from previous guests, which made us question the thoroughness of the housekeeping staff. The fact that the housekeeping lady had burst into our room without knocking earlier in our stay also made us wonder about the respect for guests' privacy. Given the numerous problems we encountered, it's surprising that the manager, Dave, didn't seem more concerned about our experience. His dismissive attitude and lack of apology only added to our frustration. As we reflected on our stay, it became clear that the hotel's focus on rebranding and cosmetic updates had not translated to meaningful improvements in the quality of the rooms or the service provided. Overall, our disappointing experience in room 1641 has left a lasting impression, and we would not recommend "The D" to others based on our stay. While the view from the room was pleasant, it was not enough to outweigh the numerous issues we encountered. Until the hotel addresses these problems and demonstrates a genuine commitment to providing a better experience for its guests, we would advise others to look elsewhere for their accommodations.

Perhaps the atmosphere will translate better during daylight hours, and the food and drink offerings will shine in a different light. The Papago orange blossom on tap was a highlight, and I appreciate the friendly staff's efforts to make us feel welcome. However, the extensive renovations and eclectic decor, while visually striking, feel like a mishmash of concepts rather than a cohesive vision. With some refinement and focus, this establishment could truly thrive and become a standout destination, rather than a confusing amalgam of styles and themes. I look forward to my next visit to see if they can find their footing.

...especially when you're expecting a hearty, satisfying meal. The lack of filling was really noticeable, and it felt like we were just eating a lot of bread with a hint of steak and cheese. The flavors were decent, but it wasn't enough to make up for the small portion size. My friend was surprised and disappointed by the change, as he had always enjoyed the philly steak Texas Style in the past. The atmosphere of the restaurant was lively and inviting, with plenty of TVs showing sports and a modern decor that added to the ambiance. However, the food was a letdown, and I hope that next time I visit, they will step up their game and provide a more generous serving. With a little improvement in the kitchen, this place could be a great spot to grab a bite, but for now, I'm not convinced.

The quality of the sushi is impressive, with fresh and delicious options to choose from. The atmosphere is cozy and inviting, making it a great spot for a night out. Overall, I highly recommend this place for anyone looking for a great all-you-can-eat sushi deal in Phoenix. The price is unbeatable and the service is excellent, making it a must-visit for sushi lovers.
Unbelievable customer service, completely ignored and disrespected as a customer, will not be returning to this location, extremely disappointing experience.

The service was absolutely appalling and the staff was extremely rude. We were treated like criminals, and it was clear they only cared about making a quick buck. The whole ordeal was humiliating and left a bad taste in our mouths. I would not recommend this place to my worst enemy, the promoters and staff are scams and thieves. Avoid at all costs.

Overall, I'm extremely satisfied with this buffet and have been going there for a while now. The variety of options is impressive, and the quality of the food is consistently good. I've tried many of the dishes, and they all taste authentic and delicious. The price point of $6.99 is unbeatable, making it an excellent option for families or large groups. The atmosphere is also pleasant, with a clean and spacious dining area. I appreciate the self-serve drink station, which eliminates the need to wait for refills. Whether you're in the mood for Chinese staples or something more unique, this buffet has something for everyone. I highly recommend giving it a try – you won't be disappointed! It's definitely my go-to spot for Chinese food.

Unfortunately, our experience with Thai Basil was a letdown. Despite the promising ratings and convenient location, the food failed to impress. The lack of heat in the dishes, particularly the Thai Basil Plate and Pad Thai, was surprising given our explicit request for "hot" spice level. As someone who frequently enjoys Thai cuisine, it was disappointing to find the flavors so subdued. The Pad Thai, in particular, was a disappointment, lacking the rich and complex flavors we've come to expect from this classic dish. The fresh rolls, while having a good flavor, were also a bit of a mystery due to the unidentifiable crunchy ingredient. It would have been nice to have more options for protein, such as tofu or shrimp, to add some variety to the dish. Overall, while the Thai Basil Plate showed some promise, it wasn't enough to redeem the rest of the meal. Given the numerous excellent Thai restaurants in the Phoenix area that we've had the pleasure of trying, it's unlikely we'll be returning to Thai Basil. Perhaps they were just having an off day, but based on our experience, we wouldn't recommend it to fellow Thai food enthusiasts.

Overall, it was a great value and delicious meal. The atmosphere was lively and nostalgic, making for a pleasant dining experience. I would definitely return to try more of their specials and support their eco-friendly efforts in repurposing the old building. Service and food were both impressive.

The Italian Ice itself was refreshing on a hot day, but it lacked a distinct flavor profile that would set it apart from other similar establishments. The portion size was decent for the price, but the overall experience was just average. We didn't try any of their other offerings, such as the gelato or snacks, so maybe those are more impressive. However, based on our experience with the Italian Ice, we wouldn't go out of our way to recommend Joe's or make a special trip to return. Perhaps the crowds we've seen are due to the affordable prices or the novelty of the spot, but for us, it was just an unremarkable visit.

I've been to this place multiple times, and the lack of staff is a persistent issue. It's not just the wait times that are frustrating, but also the fact that they seem to be understaffed during peak hours. I've seen them juggling multiple customers at once, trying to handle phone calls, and dealing with walk-ins, all while maintaining a semblance of order. It's impressive, in a way, but also concerning. How can they expect to provide quality service when they're stretched so thin? The fact that I had to wait 15-20 minutes on hold just to get an update on my glasses is unacceptable. And when I finally did get to speak to someone, they seemed put off by my inquiry. It was as if I was bothering them, rather than being a paying customer. The lack of communication and follow-through is a major issue here. If they can't even be bothered to call me when my glasses are ready, how can I trust them to get my prescription right? The incident with the polarized coating on my sunglasses was the final straw. Not only did they damage my lenses, but they also seemed unconcerned about it. The lady who did the adjustment couldn't even see the problem, despite it being glaringly obvious. It took the manager to intervene and acknowledge the issue. And even then, it took them an inordinate amount of time to repair the lenses. I ended up getting a replacement pair online, which arrived in a fraction of the time it took them to fix my original pair. The only redeeming quality of this place is the free adjustments. It's a nice perk, but it's not enough to outweigh the numerous drawbacks. If you value your time and want to avoid the frustration of dealing with an understaffed and disorganized optometrist, I would recommend taking your business (and your prescription) elsewhere. In conclusion, while this place may be decent for eye exams and pricing, their customer service and follow-through are severely lacking. Unless they address the staffing issue and improve their communication, I would not recommend this place to anyone. It's just not worth the hassle and frustration. Get your exam, get your prescription, and take your business online or to a more reputable optometrist. Your time and sanity will thank you.

The unique selection and welcoming staff make it a must-visit. We appreciate the punch card rewards and look forward to trying more items. The store's quirky atmosphere and variety of sweets make it an excellent destination for special occasions and everyday treats, keeping us coming back for their distinctive goodies.

The experience was quite disappointing, especially considering the price point. It's unacceptable to serve an incomplete dish, especially one that's a direct copy of another restaurant's signature item. The fact that they didn't inform me of the missing ingredients beforehand or offer a discount is a clear indication of a lack of attention to detail and customer care. The offer of a cookie as compensation was also underwhelming, especially when compared to the $7.99 price tag of the salad. Overall, my experience was a letdown, and I would not recommend this place to anyone looking for a reliable and satisfying dining experience. With better options like Cowboy Ciao available, it's unlikely that I'll be returning to this establishment anytime soon. The Stetson salad at Cowboy Ciao is a game-changer, and I highly recommend giving it a try instead.

I'm extremely disappointed in the overall experience at this BBQ place. The fact that they can't even get the basics right, such as a decent sauce and tender meat, is shocking. The smokiness was overpowering and it felt like they were trying to hide the lack of flavor with a heavy-handed approach to smoking. The sides, as I mentioned, were mediocre at best and the absence of cornbread on the menu is a cardinal sin for any BBQ joint. The Hawaiian rolls were a pathetic substitute and lacked any real texture or taste. If you're looking for a genuine BBQ experience, keep looking. This place is a pale imitation of the real thing. The comparison to great BBQ places like those found in Texas or Dinosaur BBQ is almost laughable. Those places know how to do BBQ right, with rich, complex flavors and tender, fall-off-the-bone meat. In contrast, this place is a sad, sorry excuse for a BBQ restaurant. Save your money and your stomach, and avoid this place at all costs. One star is even too generous for this dump.

But if you're looking for a quality dining experience, keep looking. The lack of attention to detail and subpar food is not worth the savings. With so many exceptional restaurants in Las Vegas, it's surprising this place stays in business. Unless they revamp their menu and train their staff, I would not recommend wasting your time or money here. There are far better options available in the city.
Poor customer experience overall, will take my business elsewhere due to low quality food and unclean facilities.

As I sat there sipping my martini, I couldn't help but feel that Crave was trying to be something it's not. The ambiance was upscale, with modern decor and a trendy vibe, but the food and prices just didn't match. The edamame was cooked to perfection, but it was nothing out of the ordinary. The sushi rolls were fresh, but the flavors were not particularly unique or exciting. The jumbo shrimp was probably the highlight of the meal, but even that was not enough to justify the hefty price tag. I understand that being located in a new and trendy area like Downtown Summerlin comes with a price, but I believe that Crave is taking advantage of its location to charge exorbitant prices. The menu is not particularly innovative or gourmet, and the portion sizes are not generous enough to warrant the high prices. As I mentioned earlier, I could get similar or even better quality food at other establishments like Ra or Sushi Roku without breaking the bank. The service, however, was top-notch, and our server was attentive and friendly. The chef even came out to chat with us, which was a nice touch. But despite the great service, I just couldn't shake off the feeling that I was being overcharged for mediocre food. Perhaps Crave will revisit its pricing strategy and menu offerings to better reflect the quality and value of its dishes. Until then, I'm afraid I won't be returning anytime soon. With so many other great dining options in the area, I just don't see the value in paying premium prices for average food. Crave, you have a lot of potential, but you need to step up your game if you want to compete with the big players in the culinary scene.

The atmosphere, although not entirely electric, still maintained a certain allure, likely due to the venue's sleek design and impeccable upkeep. The transition from day to night seemed seamless, with the outdoor pool section and open-air Vegas strip view providing a unique backdrop for a nightclub experience. However, the crowd dynamics were somewhat off-putting, with a noticeable imbalance between the number of women and men, and a general lack of enthusiasm that is typically characteristic of a vibrant nightclub scene. Despite the somewhat underwhelming experience, I appreciate the opportunity to have checked out the nightclub, especially considering its novelty. It will be interesting to see how the venue evolves over time, as it settles into its niche within the Las Vegas nightlife landscape. Perhaps with a more established crowd and a refined approach to programming, it will become a staple of the scene, offering a compelling alternative to more seasoned establishments like The Bank, where we ultimately ended up. For now, I'm content to have had a sneak peek at this new addition to the Vegas nightlife roster, and I look forward to reassessing it during our next annual trip, when it will have had time to find its footing and potentially become a more integral part of the city's vibrant party scene. Until then, it remains a promising, if not yet fully realized, destination for those seeking a fresh take on the traditional nightclub experience.

The decor was modern and sleek, with plenty of natural light pouring in through the large windows. The outdoor seating area was also inviting, although I didn't get a chance to sit there. Our server was friendly and attentive, which was a plus. Despite the subpar food, the overall ambiance was enjoyable and made the experience slightly more bearable. Perhaps with a different dish or a revisit on a different day, my opinion might change. For now, I'd recommend this place for its atmosphere and service, but not necessarily for its brunch offerings.
Overall, it was a positive experience, and we would return to try their dine-in service, hoping the vegetable freshness improves, to fully appreciate their culinary offerings and cozy atmosphere.

The combination of flavors and textures is absolute perfection. The cheesesteak adds a nice savory element, while the ricotta cheese sauce brings a creamy richness. The onions, green peppers, and mushrooms add a fresh and earthy note to each bite. I'm not even kidding when I say this is the best pizza I've had in a long time. The service was also top-notch, with friendly staff and quick delivery. If you're a pizza lover like me, do yourself a favor and order this unique masterpiece - you won't regret it! It's a game-changer.

Overall, my experience at this place was average, and I wouldn't go out of my way to recommend it. The Chicken Philly sandwich was definitely a highlight, but the issue with my husband's order and the high prices were significant drawbacks. It's disappointing when you're looking forward to a hot, fresh meal and have to send it back because it's cold. The fact that they were able to remake it correctly is a plus, but it's not enough to outweigh the other issues. If they could work on their pricing and consistency with food temperature, I might consider giving them another try. As it stands, I would say that this place is just an okay option if you're in the mall and don't have other choices. There are likely better options available that offer similar or better quality food at more reasonable prices.

The variety of options was impressive, and the chefs were still willing to accommodate our orders even at such a late hour. The service was also top-notch, with friendly and attentive staff who ensured our glasses were always full and our plates were never empty. What really sets Hikari apart, though, is the value - for the price, you'd be hard-pressed to find a better all-you-can-eat sushi deal anywhere else. I've already recommended Hikari to all my friends and family, and I'm confident that it will become a staple for anyone looking for high-quality sushi in Vegas. Whether you're a sushi connoisseur or just looking for a unique dining experience, Hikari is definitely worth checking out. I'm already counting down the days until my next visit to Vegas, and Hikari will be at the top of my list.

The overall atmosphere of the restaurant was also lacking, with dim lighting that made it difficult to read the menu and a noisy ambiance that made conversation strained. The booth we were seated in was cramped and uncomfortable, with torn upholstery and a wobbly table. It's clear that the restaurant is in need of some serious renovations and updates. The food, as I mentioned, was a major letdown. The overcooked lamb was a travesty, and the lack of accompaniments such as rice or vegetables made the dish feel bare and overpriced. The inferno challenge, which my husband attempted, was also a disappointment. The fact that they charged us extra for a small dish of plain yogurt to help alleviate the spiciness was just salt in the wound. The service, as I mentioned earlier, was abysmal. Our waiters seemed completely uninterested in our table, and we were left to fend for ourselves for most of the meal. The fact that we had to get up and retrieve our own check and to-go boxes was just the final insult. Overall, our experience at this restaurant was a disaster from start to finish, and we will not be returning.

Overall, my experience at this location was underwhelming, especially given the upscale area it's situated in. The contrast to the other locations I frequent was stark, and I found myself wondering why this one hadn't received the same attention to detail and maintenance. As a regular user of the facilities, I expect a certain level of quality and cleanliness, which this location unfortunately failed to deliver. Unless significant renovations are made, I'll likely stick to my usual haunts, despite the convenience of this location's proximity to my workplace. Improvement is definitely needed here.

I was particularly impressed by the variety of options available, and my mom was thrilled to see some traditional dishes that she hadn't had in years. The har gow and siu mai were standout favorites, and the char siu bao was tender and flavorful. The prices were also very reasonable, especially considering the high quality of the food. I've been to other dim sum places where the dishes were overpriced and lacking in flavor, but this place truly delivers. The atmosphere was lively and bustling, with a warm and inviting decor that made us feel like we were in a authentic Chinese restaurant. Overall, I would highly recommend this place to anyone looking for a delicious and authentic dim sum experience. Don't let the negative reviews deter you - give it a try and see for yourself why it's a hidden gem.

The whole experience was frustrating and disorganized. With a lack of options and poor service, it's surprising they're still in business. The atmosphere was also underwhelming, with not enough TVs to accommodate sports fans. After waiting for what felt like an eternity, our food finally arrived, but the quality was subpar. For a brewery, you'd expect a decent selection of beers, but that wasn't the case here. Overall, our visit was a huge letdown, and we won't be returning. Two and a half hours of our time was wasted on poor service and mediocre food.

The lack of organization and attentiveness from the staff was staggering, and it seemed like they were all working independently without any cohesive system in place. Our server, who finally took our orders, seemed overwhelmed and took a while to return with our food. The chili cheese fries I ordered were a major letdown, and the "volcano" chili was a misnomer - it was bland and had an odd sweetness to it, which I can only assume was from the BBQ sauce. The portion size was also smaller than expected, especially considering the price. My friend's beer experience was also a disappointment, and the fact that they didn't have a working tap system was concerning. Overall, the combination of poor service, subpar food, and lack of attention to detail made for a thoroughly unenjoyable experience. I would not recommend this place to anyone, unless they're looking for a disappointing and overpriced meal.
