With so many other great options available, it's hard to see why anyone would choose to return to this establishment. Needless to say, my friend and I will be taking our business (and our appetites) elsewhere.

Despite the wait, the Parmesan truffle fries and Ronin burger were standout dishes, showcasing the kitchen's potential. However, the inconsistent cooking of my burger, being too pink for a medium-well order, was a letdown. This mistake has happened to me before at this location, which raises concerns about quality control. Furthermore, the forgetfulness of my husband's tea order added to the frustration. The ambiance of the restaurant is certainly a strong point, but it's not enough to make up for the subpar service and kitchen mishaps. With some improvements in these areas, this restaurant could truly excel.

The service is also top-notch, friendly staff and a cozy atmosphere make it a perfect spot for dates or gatherings, we always leave feeling satisfied and already planning our next visit, definitely a favorite restaurant of ours, can't wait to try more of their creative dishes!

As I explored the store, I was impressed by the wide selection of international products, from exotic spices to artisanal cheeses. The store's commitment to showcasing local and sustainable products is truly commendable. I was also delighted to find a variety of ready-to-eat options, including a salad bar and a hot food counter, which made for a quick and delicious lunch. The store's atmosphere was lively and welcoming, with upbeat music playing in the background and the aroma of freshly baked bread wafting through the air. I appreciated the fact that the store had a dedicated section for dietary restrictions, making it easy for customers with special needs to find suitable options. One thing that sets this world market apart from others is its community-oriented approach. The store hosts various events and workshops, from cooking classes to wine tastings, which fosters a sense of connection among customers and staff. Overall, my first visit to this particular world market was a resounding success, and I'm eager to return and continue exploring the many wonders it has to offer. With its unique blend of global cuisine, eclectic products, and welcoming atmosphere, this store is sure to become a staple in my weekly shopping routine.

Extremely unhelpful and unprofessional experience. The lack of electronic fingerprinting capabilities is surprising, given the name "Live Scan Las Vegas". The long processing time and poor customer service make it not worth the hassle. Burton's studio is a much better option, with friendly staff and efficient services. Save yourself the frustration and avoid this place altogether, opting for a more reliable and courteous alternative instead.

The lack of authenticity and overreliance on spices is truly disappointing. As someone who has a deep appreciation for Mexican cuisine, it's disheartening to see a restaurant like Mad Mex perpetuating a watered-down, unbalanced representation of Tex-Mex. The fact that the wings, typically an American pub staple, were the highlight of the meal speaks volumes about the kitchen's priorities. The Carnitas, which had potential, was ultimately overpowered by an excessive amount of spice, leaving me wondering if the chef has ever actually tasted the nuances of traditional Mexican cooking. With so many excellent Mexican and Tex-Mex restaurants out there, it's puzzling that Mad Mex continues to attract customers. Perhaps, as I mentioned earlier, the dim lighting and liberal drink pours are enough to distract from the subpar food, but for those seeking a genuine culinary experience, there are far better options available. Overall, my experience at Mad Mex was a letdown, and I would not recommend it to anyone seeking authentic, well-crafted Mexican or Tex-Mex cuisine.

Prices were reasonable, and the cozy atmosphere added to our enjoyment. We would definitely return to try more of their creative dishes and appreciate the bring-your-own wine policy, making for a lovely evening out in the Rue Duluth neighborhood. Highly recommended for a delicious meal.

As I continued my stay, I was disappointed to find that the resort's lack of amenities and subpar services were not the only issues. The rooms, although touted as luxurious, were in dire need of renovation. The furniture was outdated, the carpets were stained, and the air conditioning unit was loud and inefficient. The kitchen, which was supposed to be a major selling point, was a letdown. The appliances were old and difficult to use, and the lack of basic cooking utensils and supplies made it difficult to prepare even the simplest of meals. The resort's location, which I had initially thought would be a plus, turned out to be a major drawback. The $30 cab ride to The Strip was a significant expense, and the shuttle service, which was supposed to be a convenient alternative, was unreliable and restrictive. The fact that it only ran from 10 am to midnight and did not allow bags or luggage made it virtually useless for anyone attending conventions or events. The Wi-Fi situation was also a major inconvenience. Having to pay for Wi-Fi in the rooms was bad enough, but the fact that it was only free in the lobby made it difficult to get any work done or stay connected with family and friends. And don't even get me started on the lack of a restaurant on the premises. Having to venture out to find food or buy groceries was a hassle, especially considering the resort's isolated location. But the final straw was the cockroaches. I had never seen so many in my life, and they were everywhere - in the rooms, around the pool, and even in the lobby. It was disgusting and made me question the resort's cleanliness and maintenance. The fact that pest control was not included in the yearly dues was appalling, and it made me wonder what else the resort was skimping on. As I checked out and left the resort, I couldn't help but feel relieved to be leaving such a disappointing and overpriced experience behind. The resort's lack of amenities, subpar services, and numerous issues made it a place I would never recommend to anyone. In fact, I would advise people to steer clear of it altogether. With so many other great options in Las Vegas, there's no reason to settle for a mediocre resort like this one. Save your money and your sanity, and choose a different resort for your next vacation. Trust me, you won't regret it. In conclusion, my experience at this resort was a disaster from start to finish. The lack of amenities, the poor location, and the numerous issues with the rooms and services made it a place I would never want to visit again. As an RCI member, I expect a certain level of quality and service, and this resort fell far short of those expectations. I hope that in the future, the resort will take steps to address these issues and provide a better experience for its guests. But until then, I would not recommend it to anyone.

I'm extremely disappointed in the decline of Bally's, a hotel I've always held in high regard. The issues we encountered during our recent stay were not only frustrating but also unacceptable. Firstly, the people movers being down again was a huge inconvenience, especially considering our mobility issues. After a long day of walking around the convention, we rely on these to get around the hotel. The upgrade to our usual suite was a nice gesture, but finding dirty diapers by the window was absolutely appalling. The $30 dining credit offered as compensation was a mere token and didn't come close to making up for the disgust and discomfort we felt. On a more positive note, the roulette dealer was exceptional and provided top-notch service. The valet driver, Regina, was also outstanding and remembered our names after a year, which was a lovely personal touch. However, my main gripe remains the people movers. I understand that they may be turned off near the entrance to encourage people to sit at machines, but this is a poor excuse for a hotel that claims to cater to its guests' needs. I implore the management to take our complaints seriously and take immediate action to address these issues. Until then, I'm afraid Bally's will continue to lose its loyal customers.

The BARBIE slider was cooked to perfection, with a generous patty, crispy bacon, and melted cheese all coming together in harmony. The portion was massive, and I appreciated the generous serving. Despite the disappointment with the fries, the overall experience was exceptional. The staff was friendly and apologetic about the fry situation, which showed they care about their customers. I'm already planning my next visit to try more of their menu items, including those elusive peanut oil fries. With its unique flavors and generous portions, this truck has won me over, and I'm excited to see what the future holds for this Vegas gem.

for an unforgettable dining experience. The teppanyaki grill added a fun twist to our evening. Margarita's recommendations were spot on, and Tim's culinary skills impressed us. The filet mignon and lobster tail were cooked to perfection. We left feeling satisfied and already looking forward to our next visit. Benihana exceeded our expectations, and we highly recommend it to anyone seeking a unique and delicious meal.

I'm extremely disappointed in the way they handled my payment. The overall experience was enjoyable, with a great selection of music and a lively atmosphere, but the billing issue has left a sour taste. The multiple rooms and outdoor area were definite perks, and the bartender's generosity was appreciated. However, the alleged theft has overshadowed the positives. I hope the establishment takes steps to address this issue and prevent it from happening to others. Until then, I would advise patrons to closely monitor their transactions. A fun night out should not be marred by dishonest business practices.

The lack of transparency and inconsistent information is not only frustrating but also a waste of time. I've had to reschedule multiple times due to their limited hours and unavailability of staff. The fact that they don't have a nurse on site regularly is unacceptable, especially for a clinic that offers shots and other medical services. The inconvenience and poor communication make it clear that this clinic is not patient-centered. With so many other options available, I would strongly advise against visiting this clinic. Their inflexible schedule and subpar service make them a last resort, at best.

The atmosphere was lovely, with elegant decor and a nice view, but the poor service really overshadowed our experience. It's a shame, because I was really looking forward to trying their French cuisine. Instead, we left feeling frustrated and undervalued as customers. The fact that our waitress became defensive and argumentative when we pointed out the mistake was completely unacceptable. As a customer, you expect to be treated with respect and courtesy, especially in a high-end establishment like this. Unfortunately, our visit fell far short of expectations, and I would caution others to be aware of the potential for poor service when visiting this restaurant. Overall, a disappointing experience that I won't soon forget.

I've been to Big Wong several times, and each visit has been a delightful experience. The service is always friendly and prompt, with the staff eager to recommend their favorite dishes. The atmosphere is casual and no-frills, which suits the affordable prices and generous portions. The crispy shrimp wontons are a must-try, with a perfect balance of crunch and flavor. The salt and pepper wings are also a highlight, with a spicy kick that will leave you wanting more. The chicken curry is rich and creamy, with tender chunks of chicken that fall apart easily. With such a vast menu at an unbeatable price point, Big Wong is an excellent choice for a quick and satisfying meal. Whether you're in the mood for something classic or adventurous, Big Wong has something for everyone. Be sure to call ahead for take-out, and enjoy your delicious and affordable meal on-the-go.

The overall experience was disappointing and the food quality was subpar. I expected more from this establishment, but unfortunately, it failed to meet my expectations, leaving a bad taste and unpleasant after-effects. Needless to say, I won't be returning anytime soon.

The atmosphere was lively and upscale, with a pleasant decor that added to the overall dining experience. Our server was attentive and friendly, ensuring that our drinks were always filled and clearing our plates promptly. The variety of options was impressive, and we appreciated the creativity that went into crafting each dish. The small portions allowed us to try a little bit of everything, and we were surprised by how much we enjoyed some of the unique flavor combinations. Overall, we were thoroughly impressed with the quality and value of the buffet, and we can't wait to come back and try more of their innovative dishes. The price was very reasonable, especially considering the high quality of the food and the generous selection.

Despite the waitress's behavior, we managed to enjoy our meal and each other's company. The portions were generous, and the prices were reasonable, making it a good value for the quality of food we received. However, the experience was somewhat marred by the waitress's consistent attitude and lack of warmth. It's understandable to have an off day, but if this is a regular occurrence, it may be worth the restaurant's attention to improve their overall customer service. The atmosphere of the restaurant was pleasant, with a traditional Chinese decor and a clean, well-maintained dining area. The Lazy Susan at our table was a nice touch, even if we didn't end up sharing our food as much as we had hoped. Overall, while the food was good and the prices were fair, the service left a bit to be desired. If you're looking for a reliable Chinese food option and don't mind a potentially gruff server, this might be a good choice. But if you're prioritizing excellent customer service, you might want to look elsewhere. With a bit more attention to training their staff, this restaurant could easily become a top choice for Chinese food in the area.

Overall, Roman Candle is a fantastic spot for casual dining, and I appreciate the efforts to incorporate local flavors and ingredients. The atmosphere is cozy and inviting, making it perfect for a night out with friends or a family dinner. With its unique pizza offerings and excellent supporting menu items, Roman Candle has become a staple in my dining routine, and I highly recommend it to anyone in the area looking for a delicious meal.

I also appreciate the convenience of being able to filter by size, style, and brand when shopping online, which makes it much easier to find what I'm looking for. In contrast, browsing through the racks at this store can be overwhelming, especially when everything is jumbled together. I've found that even when I do stumble upon a brand or style I like, the sizing can be inconsistent, which adds to the frustration. Another issue I've encountered is the quality of the items. While the prices may be low, I've noticed that some of the clothes can be quite worn or faded, even if they're still in decent condition. As a parent, I want to make sure my baby's clothes are not only cute but also comfortable and durable. Unfortunately, I haven't always been impressed with the quality of the items I've found at this store. Overall, while I understand the appeal of thrift shopping and the potential to find hidden gems, I just haven't had the best experience at this particular store. The disorganization, limited selection of brands I like, and inconsistent quality have all contributed to my decision to shop elsewhere. For me, the convenience and reliability of online shopping outweigh the potential savings of thrift shopping, at least when it comes to baby clothes.

Extremely disappointed and frustrated with the service and attention to detail. The mistake was not only inconvenient but also a dietary concern. Will not be returning to this location anytime soon, expecting better quality control and customer satisfaction from a reputable establishment like this. Totally unacceptable experience overall.

I must say that my experience with Ikea has been a mixed bag. On one hand, I was pleased with the service I received from Mark, the salesperson who helped me find the perfect bedroom furniture. He was knowledgeable, friendly, and made sure I had everything I needed. However, the problems I encountered after leaving the store were frustrating and disappointing. The missing hardware for the slats was a significant issue, and the lack of follow-up from Kim was unacceptable. I was shocked that the call center in Maryland was unable to assist me in a timely manner, and the options they presented were not feasible for me. Having to drive 234 miles back to the store or wait a week for the missing items to be shipped was not a reasonable solution. It was only when I contacted the corporate office and spoke with Felicia that I received the kind of service I expected from Ikea. She listened to my concerns, empathized with my situation, and offered to help resolve the issue promptly. I appreciate her efforts, and I hope that the parts will arrive within the promised timeframe. If they do, I will reconsider my review and rating. However, if the issue is not resolved satisfactorily, I will stand by my original assessment.

The prices were also very reasonable, making it an excellent value for the quality and quantity of food. I've already recommended this place to friends and family, and I'm excited to return and try more of their menu items. The staff were attentive and knowledgeable, happy to answer questions and make suggestions. Overall, my impulsive stop turned into a fantastic dining experience that I won't soon forget. I'm looking forward to enjoying more of their delicious po'boys and beignets when I return to New Orleans next month. It's definitely a must-visit destination for any food lover.

The pastie was delicious and filling, a great start to the day. Despite the small space, the service was friendly and efficient. I was distracted by the drumset and the mysterious Myles Teddywedger, whose apparent passing added a somber note to my visit. Overall, I'd recommend this quirky spot for a tasty breakfast treat, but be prepared for a cramped and eclectic experience.

The lack of attention to detail and care in the preparation of our meals was truly disappointing. As a local, I expect more from a renowned restaurant like Spago. The atmosphere, which was once lively and inviting, now feels like a tired, overpriced tourist trap. Our server seemed put off by our presence, and the overall service was slow and inattentive. In contrast, Wolfgang Puck at Crystals offers a far superior dining experience, with fresh, expertly prepared dishes and a warm, welcoming staff. The 20% discount for locals is just the icing on the cake. Unless Spago makes significant changes, I would not recommend it to anyone, local or tourist alike. There are far better options available, and I will be taking my business elsewhere from now on.

As I continue to reflect on our experience living in this complex, I am reminded of the countless times we've had to deal with the incompetence of the staff and management. The lack of accountability and transparency is staggering. It's like they're not even trying to provide a decent living environment for their tenants. The constant excuses and blame-shifting are exhausting. When we first moved in, we were promised a certain level of service and amenities, but it's clear that those promises were nothing more than empty words. The condition of the grounds and common areas is a perfect reflection of the management's priorities. The dog waste, cigarette butts, and trash are not only an eyesore, but they also create a health hazard. The fact that they can't even be bothered to clean up after themselves is appalling. And don't even get me started on the pool. The excuse that tenants spilling beer is causing the pool to turn green is laughable. It's clear that they're not properly maintaining the pool, and it's a shame that we're paying for a amenity that we can't even use. The scorpion and bug problem is also a major concern. As a parent, it's terrifying to think that my infant daughter could be at risk of being stung or bitten. The fact that the office staff laughed at my concerns is despicable. It's not funny, it's not trivial, and it's not something that should be taken lightly. The fact that they give me grief when I ask for the bug guy to come spray our apartment is just another example of their incompetence. The financial issues we've experienced are also a major red flag. Being overcharged $450 is a significant amount of money, and the fact that the office staff couldn't help me resolve the issue is unacceptable.

The atmosphere is lively and inviting, making it perfect for a casual evening out with friends. While the blue wasabi is a unique touch, it's not a game-changer. Overall, the experience was pleasant, but not exceptional. The consistently good food and nice ambiance make it a reliable choice for happy hour or dinner. However, don't expect to be blown away by anything extraordinary. It's a solid, middle-of-the-road sushi spot that gets the job done, but doesn't particularly stand out from the crowd. I'd recommend it for a low-key night out.

Overall, our experience at Cocomo Joes was a letdown. The ambiance, although attempting to be tropical and fun, felt cheap and uninviting. The dim lighting, while possibly intended to be cozy, made it difficult to navigate the menu and enjoy our meal. The subpar food and high prices were a major disappointment, and the lack of attention from our waitress, despite her friendly demeanor, added to our frustration. With so many other great dining options in the area, it's unlikely that we'll give Cocomo Joes another chance. The decision to leave and forego additional drinks was an easy one, and we won't be recommending this spot to friends or family.
Prices are reasonable, service is friendly, and the overall experience is exceptional, making it a must-visit spot for both locals and visitors like myself from Sierra Vista.

The overall experience was a huge disappointment, and I couldn't wait to leave. The atmosphere was also lacking, with a dull and uninviting decor that seemed to match the subpar food quality. The service, as I mentioned earlier, was clueless, and it seemed like the staff was just going through the motions. I was expecting a high-end buffet experience, especially given the Caesar's reputation, but what I got was a lackluster and unappetizing spread. The "Buffet of Buffets" tour was a great idea, but this particular stop was a major letdown. If you're planning on doing the tour, I would highly recommend skipping Lago and opting for one of the other buffets, like the ones at Harrah's or the Rio, which I've heard are much better. Overall, my experience at Lago was a resounding thumbs down, and I would not recommend it to anyone. Save your money and your taste buds, and avoid this buffet at all costs.

The service was also lacking, with our server seeming overwhelmed and inattentive. It took multiple requests to get simple things like refills on drinks. The atmosphere, which was once cozy and inviting, now felt dirty and neglected. The presence of flies buzzing around our table added to the overall sense of discomfort. Despite the partial refund, the experience was still a huge disappointment. It's clear that the establishment has undergone significant changes, and not for the better. We won't be returning anytime soon, which is a shame given our past positive experiences.
Quality has decreased, portions are smaller, and prices have increased significantly, making it less desirable than it once was, losing its unique charm and character over the years.

His professionalism and expertise are unmatched, and the end result exceeded my expectations. The artificial turf looks fantastic, and I've already noticed a significant reduction in my water bill. I'm thoroughly satisfied with the service and quality provided by Z Best Turf, and I highly recommend them to anyone considering turf installation.

As I reflect on my visit, I'm reminded that first impressions can be deceiving, and I'm willing to give this wine bar the benefit of the doubt. Perhaps it was an off night, or maybe I just caught the staff on a bad day. The hostess, despite being overwhelmed with multiple roles, was friendly and welcoming, which is a definite plus. However, the lack of attention to our table was noticeable, and the fact that my friends had to pour their own wine was a bit of a faux pas. The wine selection, although not extensively explored by me, seemed to please my friends, and the Desert Blood was an interesting choice. I'm curious to know more about their wine list and how it pairs with their menu offerings. Speaking of which, I didn't get a chance to try any of their food, but I've heard mixed reviews about their small plates and snacks. The atmosphere, as I mentioned, was a bit of a letdown. The eclectic mix of decor didn't quite come together as I had hoped, and the overall vibe felt disjointed. Nevertheless, the squishy leather loveseats were comfortable, and the Indian lanterns added a touch of warmth to the space. With a bit more attention to detail and a clearer vision for the ambiance, this wine bar could potentially become a cozy spot to relax and enjoy a glass of wine. I'm looking forward to my next visit, when I'll be able to provide a more comprehensive review and hopefully, a more positive experience.

The energetic atmosphere and lively music made it easy to let loose and have a blast. Although the smell of sweat became overpowering at times, it was a small price to pay for the exhilarating experience. The staff were friendly and helpful, ensuring everyone's safety while trampolining. I appreciated the unique concept of Lockdown and the fact that it offered a refreshing change from the usual nightlife scene in Las Vegas. Overall, I would definitely return to Lockdown and continue to recommend it to others looking for a fun and active night out in the city.

Overpriced drinks and mediocre food made the visit even more disappointing, solidifying my decision to never return to this establishment, Groupon or not, due to its overall poor quality and unpleasant atmosphere.

I've tried a variety of their beers, but my go-to is usually the Märzen, which pairs perfectly with the spicy tapas. The staff's knowledge of the beers is impressive, and they're always happy to offer recommendations or samples. One thing that sets Gordon Biersch apart from other bars is the consistency of their service, regardless of how busy they are. The prices are reasonable, especially considering the generous portions of tapas. Overall, Gordon Biersch has become my favorite spot to grab a drink and some small plates with friends or on a date. Whether you're a beer connoisseur or just looking for a relaxed atmosphere, Gordon Biersch is definitely worth checking out. With its unique combination of great beer, delicious tapas, and friendly service, it's no wonder I keep coming back for more. The experience is always enjoyable and leaves me looking forward to my next visit.

I was extremely disappointed in the way Donald handled the situation, showing no concern for the customer's satisfaction. As a paying customer, I expect a certain level of quality and service, which was clearly lacking in this experience. The fact that he blamed the poor condition of the pizza on the mushroom topping was unconvincing and unprofessional. The lack of apology or offer to make it right was appalling. Needless to say, I will never be ordering from this establishment again and would advise others to think twice before doing so. The contrast to Domino's excellent pizza and service was striking.

I was really looking forward to trying this place, especially with all the hype surrounding it, but unfortunately, it fell flat for me. The atmosphere was lively and modern, but that's where the positives ended. As I mentioned earlier, the food was a letdown, and I couldn't help but compare it to other burger joints that offer better quality and value. The SinCity burger, which was supposed to be their flagship item, was a disappointment, and the sweet potato smashfries were a missed opportunity. I think what bothered me the most was the lack of balance in the flavors. Everything was either too salty or too dry, and the addition of rosemary and garlic didn't seem to make a difference. The fried pickles, which I was excited to try, were overpowering and not enjoyable. It's clear that this place has a loyal following, but I just don't get it. Maybe I'm just not sophisticated enough to appreciate their unique take on burgers and fries, but for the prices they're charging, I expect a lot more. In comparison to other burger places, this one just doesn't hold up. The prices are higher, and the quality is lower. I'd much rather go to a place like In-N-Out, where I know I'm getting a fresh, high-quality burger at a reasonable price. Or, if I'm feeling fancy, I'd rather go to a place like Red Robin, where the atmosphere is fun and the food is consistently good. Overall, I'd say that this place is overhyped and overpriced, and I wouldn't recommend it to anyone looking for a great burger experience. Unless, of course, you're a fan of extremely salty food, in which case, you might enjoy it. But for me, I'll be taking my business (and my appetite) elsewhere.

As the night went on, things only got worse. The manager's attempt to help our server was appreciated, but it was too little, too late. The damage was done, and our party was already frustrated and disappointed. We had been looking forward to this celebratory dinner for weeks, and it was supposed to be a special occasion. Instead, it turned into a disaster that none of us would ever forget. The fact that our server blamed his difficulties on his dyslexia was not only unprofessional, but it also made us feel like we were the problem, not him. It was like he was saying, "You guys are just too much for me to handle, and it's not my fault that I'm not doing my job well." That kind of attitude is not what you expect from a server, especially at a restaurant that used to be known for its excellent service. The food, as I mentioned earlier, was also a major letdown. The tri-tip was inedible, the chicken parmesan pasta was a disappointment, and the talapia and shrimp dish was missing its sauce. The beef ribs were fatty and rubbery, and the potatoes were cold and came without toppings. It was like the kitchen was not even trying to get things right. What's even more disappointing is that CJ used to be one of our favorite restaurants. We had been there many times before, and the food and service had always been top-notch. But this experience was a complete disaster, and it's clear that the restaurant has gone downhill. The host was devastated that he couldn't provide us with the great meal and experience that he had intended, and we were all disappointed that our special occasion had been ruined. In conclusion, I would not recommend CJ to anyone, especially not to large parties. The service is subpar, the food is mediocre at best, and the overall experience is just not worth it. There are many other great restaurants out there that can provide a much better experience, and I would encourage everyone to take their business elsewhere. CJ, you need to get your act together and start providing the kind of service and food that you used to be known for. Until then, we will be taking our business (and our large parties) elsewhere. To the manager and owner of CJ, I would suggest that you take a hard look at your restaurant and make some serious changes. Start by providing your servers with the training and support they need to handle large parties. Make sure that your kitchen is stocked with enough menus and that your chefs are prepared to handle a large number of orders. And most importantly, make sure that your customers are treated with the respect and care that they deserve. Until you can provide a consistently good experience, you will continue to lose customers and reputation.

As I reflected on my experience, I couldn't help but feel frustrated and disappointed. The issues with my order, from the lack of extra crispy chicken to the missing side of sweet corn, were frustrating enough. But the extra charge on my debit card, despite using a Visa logo, was the icing on the cake. It seemed like a clear mistake on the part of the restaurant, and the fact that they didn't catch it until I called to dispute the charge was alarming. The visit back to the store to retrieve my missing corn was somewhat redeemed by the counter girl's apology, but it would have been nice if they had offered some kind of compensation for the hassle. A free dessert or a discount on my next visit would have gone a long way in making up for the mistakes. Instead, I was left feeling like I was just another customer who had been inconvenienced by their errors. The final straw was realizing that my order was also missing butter and honey. At that point, I had given up on the idea of enjoying my meal. The food itself was okay, but it was nothing special. The crispy and regular chicken tasted similar, and the whole experience had been so marred by mistakes that I couldn't even enjoy the food. Overall, my experience was a disaster from start to finish. The mistakes, the extra charge, and the lack of customer service all combined to make for a frustrating and disappointing experience. I had hoped that things would have improved since my last visit six months ago, but sadly, that was not the case. As I said, I'll probably try again in another 6-12 months, but for now, I'm taking my business (and my appetite) elsewhere.

As we finally left the restaurant, I couldn't help but feel disappointed and frustrated with the entire experience. The fact that the waitress seemed to prioritize the other table, presumably because of the person's status, was not only unprofessional but also added insult to injury. It's understandable that servers may have favorite tables or regulars, but it's essential to provide equal attention and service to all customers, regardless of their social standing. The lack of attention to detail in our order, from the missing meat in the salad to the undercooked pizza, was also a major letdown. It's not like we were asking for anything out of the ordinary; just a simple pizza dinner with some basic toppings. The fact that the kitchen couldn't even get that right was alarming. The only redeeming quality of our meal was the garlic bread, which was crispy and flavorful, but that was not enough to save the evening. What really took the cake, though, was the wait for the check and the payment process. Thirteen minutes to receive the check, followed by another 15-20 minutes to pay, was absolutely ridiculous. With two young kids in tow, this wait felt like an eternity, and it was clear that the waitress was not managing her tables efficiently. As we left the restaurant, I couldn't help but think that Nello's has seen better days and that it's time for us to find a new go-to pizza spot. With so many other options available, it's unlikely that we'll be returning to Nello's anytime soon.

We left feeling satisfied and already looking forward to our next visit. The endless shrimp promotion is definitely a great value, and the variety of options kept my husband happy. Jana's attentive service and friendly demeanor made a big difference in our overall experience. Although my steak was slightly tough, the flavors were spot on, and the snow crab more than made up for it. With its cozy atmosphere and reliable food quality, this location has won us over, and we're excited to become regulars. Great job, and we'll be back soon!
Highly recommended for special occasions or a lovely evening out with exceptional food and atmosphere always guaranteed here.

The flavors and portion sizes are consistently great. Their menu offers a wide variety of options, catering to different tastes. Whether we're in the mood for something classic or adventurous, New York Chinese always delivers. The staff is friendly and courteous, making the experience even more enjoyable. Overall, it's our go-to spot for delicious Chinese food that never disappoints.

The ambiance was modern and chic, with a rooftop pool offering stunning city views. We enjoyed a romantic dinner at the hotel restaurant, savoring delicious dishes and exceptional service. Overall, our stay was unforgettable, and we highly recommend this hotel to couples celebrating special occasions. With its excellent location, luxurious amenities, and warm hospitality, it's an ideal choice for a memorable getaway in downtown Phoenix.

Overall, I'm impressed with the consistency and quality of their offerings. The pastrami sub was piled high with tender, flavorful meat, and the steak sub was a pleasant surprise with its shaved steak. The delivery time was remarkably quick, and the fact that the food arrived hot is a testament to their efficient process. I appreciate the fair prices and the clear delivery policies. The artisanal bread is a nice touch, setting them apart from chain establishments like Subway. With two successful orders under my belt, I'm confident in recommending this place to others looking for a reliable and satisfying dining experience.
Overall, the experience was decent, but the buffet's limited options and unimpressive mac and cheese detracted from the meal's overall value and Southern comfort food authenticity.

I'm extremely disappointed in the changes and feel that the new concept has lost the charm and comfort of the original Sweet Tomatoes. The variety of soups and salads that I grew to love are now limited and overpriced. The wonton chicken salad was a staple for me and its removal is a huge loss. I urge the management to reconsider their decision and bring back the old menu, or at least offer some of the classic dishes that loyal customers like myself have come to expect from Sweet Tomatoes. Bring back the old Sweet Tomatoes!

The lack of attention to detail and care in their food preparation is staggering. It's clear that the staff are not invested in providing a good customer experience, and the management seems to be turning a blind eye to the consistent poor service. I've seen other customers walk out frustrated, and I've even had colleagues vow never to return after a single disappointing visit. The fact that they can't even get takeout orders right is a testament to their ineptitude. For a restaurant that's supposedly busy, they seem to be doing a fantastic job of driving away potential customers. Unless they seriously revamp their service and food quality, I wouldn't recommend this place to my worst enemy. Save your taste buds and your sanity, and take your business (and your appetite) elsewhere. Trust me, you won't be missing out on anything.

The lack of communication and inefficiency was staggering. We were not provided with updates or apologies, leaving us frustrated and unsure of what to expect. The overall experience was disappointing and fell short of my previous encounters with the airline. I hope they can rectify these issues to prevent similar incidents in the future and restore my confidence in their services.

The food itself was decent, but not exceptional enough to justify the high prices. My Filet Mignon, although cooked to the wrong temperature, was still tender and flavorful. However, the sides and appetizers we ordered were nothing special and lacked a wow factor. The service was attentive, but our waiter's explanation for the undercooked steak came across as more of an excuse than an apology. Overall, I left feeling underwhelmed and overcharged. For a celebrity-endorsed restaurant, I expected a more refined and sophisticated atmosphere, but instead, it felt like a noisy, overpriced eatery trying too hard to be trendy. Unless they revamp their approach to cooking and ambiance, I wouldn't recommend this steak house to others. There are far better options available that offer a more authentic upscale dining experience.
The quality and attention to detail are top-notch, making every visit a delightful experience, and I always leave feeling pampered and satisfied.
overpriced and lacking flavor, with disappointing service to top it off, making it a disappointing experience overall.

I am still fuming as I write this review, recalling the disappointing experience my friends and I had at this salon. The lack of concern and poor customer service we received is unacceptable, especially considering the amount of money we spent. As someone who works in the service industry, I understand the importance of ensuring customer satisfaction and providing quality services. It's not just about completing a task, but also about making the customer feel valued and appreciated. In our case, the salon failed miserably. Not only did they fail to deliver a satisfactory manicure and pedicure service, but they also showed a complete disregard for our concerns when we brought the issue to their attention. The fact that they suggested we should have opted for gel paint instead of regular polish is not only unhelpful but also unprofessional. It's like they were shifting the blame onto us, rather than taking responsibility for their own mistakes. What's even more disturbing is that they didn't even offer to make things right. A simple offer to repaint our nails or provide a discount on our next visit would have gone a long way in showing that they valued our business and cared about our experience. Instead, they chose to do nothing, effectively losing not just one customer, but four. I will make sure to share my disappointing experience with my friends and family, and I would advise others to think twice before visiting this salon. There are plenty of other salons out there that prioritize customer satisfaction and provide quality services, and I would be happy to take my business (and my friends' business) elsewhere.

As we finished our meal and prepared to leave, I couldn't help but feel a sense of relief wash over me. The experience had been a mixed bag, to say the least. While the service had been attentive, if a bit overly enthusiastic, the food had been a letdown. The fondue dippers, Caesar salad, and burger had all failed to impress, and the prices had been steep to boot. Despite the culinary missteps, my wife and I had managed to find some humor in the situation. The decor, which included the aforementioned thirty-foot Guy Fieri picture, had been kitschy and entertaining. The staff uniforms, which appeared to be inspired by a cross between a diner and a sports team, had also added to the lighthearted atmosphere. However, as we reflected on our experience, it was clear that the restaurant's reliance on gimmicks and celebrity endorsements had not been enough to make up for the subpar food. The "Mayor of Flavor Town" burger, which had sounded promising on the menu, had been a messy and underwhelming affair. The fries, which had been the highlight of the meal, had not been enough to redeem the rest of the dish. As we left the restaurant and made our way back to our hotel room, my wife turned to me and said, "Well, that was an experience." I nodded in agreement, and we both burst out laughing. It was clear that our meal had been a memorable one, even if it hadn't been particularly enjoyable. In the end, I would not recommend this restaurant to others. While it may be a fun and quirky spot for fans of Guy Fieri, the food and prices are not worth the visit. With so many other excellent dining options available, it's hard to justify spending $95 on a meal that is, at best, mediocre. Unless you're a die-hard fan of the celebrity chef, it's best to steer clear of this restaurant and opt for something else. As I looked back at the restaurant, I caught one last glimpse of the giant Guy Fieri picture, its eyes seeming to follow me out the door. I couldn't help but chuckle at the absurdity of it all, and I made a mental note to avoid any restaurants with oversized celebrity portraits in the future. Despite the lackluster meal, my wife and I had managed to find some humor and entertainment in the experience, and for that, I suppose we should be grateful.

Overall, the experience is underwhelming and lacks consistency. With so many other dining options available, it's disappointing to see this establishment not living up to its potential. Unless they revamp their menu and improve their service, I would advise others to explore alternative restaurants that offer better quality and value. Sadly, this place falls short of expectations and fails to impress.

The steak was overcooked and lacked flavor, while the mashed potatoes were lukewarm. My husband's pasta was also a letdown, with an unimpressive sauce. Given the long wait and subpar food, we left feeling disappointed and still a bit hungry. The experience was a stark contrast to our usual dining expectations, and we would not recommend this restaurant to others. Perhaps it's time for Southpoint to reevaluate its culinary offerings to better serve its guests.

Unfortunately, the subpar food quality and unwelcoming service made for a disappointing experience. The pinkish-colored chicken was a major red flag, and the unmelted cheese was a letdown. Overall, my visit was a letdown, and I won't be back to give them another chance.

The combination of good food, comfortable accommodations, and exciting activities made for a memorable night. Although the casino's smokiness was a drawback, the hotel's modern and relaxing atmosphere more than made up for it. Our room's spectacular view was the perfect way to unwind after a fun-filled evening. The fine dining restaurant at Orange Tree exceeded our expectations, with each dish we shared being expertly prepared and presented. The crab, lamb chop, and bacon-wrapped scallop were standouts, and the service was top-notch. Overall, our experience at the resort was a resounding success, and we would highly recommend it to others looking for a unique and enjoyable getaway. The scavenger hunt on Ollie the Trolley was just the icing on the cake, adding an extra layer of excitement to an already fantastic night. We left feeling pleased and already looking forward to our next visit.

We were shocked and appalled by the doctor's behavior, and our baby was clearly traumatized by the experience. As a parent, it's devastating to see your child treated with such disregard and roughness. The fact that Doctor McAllister resorted to physical restraint on a fragile 11-month-old is unacceptable and raises serious concerns about his suitability to work with children. We strongly advise parents to exercise caution and consider alternative healthcare providers for their little ones. Our trust has been severely broken, and we hope that by sharing our experience, we can prevent similar incidents from happening to other families.

The nightlife was vibrant and the staff were friendly, although sometimes slow to respond. Overall, it's a fantastic spot for those seeking a lively atmosphere and a range of dining options. However, the hotel's reliance on cheap materials and ongoing technical issues are concerning. With some refinement and attention to detail, this hotel could truly thrive. For now, it's an excellent choice for young travelers seeking a fun, party-centric experience, but perhaps not ideal for those prioritizing luxury or longevity. The hotel's potential is undeniable, making it a great spot to visit sooner rather than later.

The atmosphere of the restaurant was also noteworthy, with a cozy and intimate setting that made us feel like we were in a small Spanish village. The service was attentive and knowledgeable, with our server happily answering our questions about the different dishes and making recommendations. The prices were very reasonable, especially considering the high quality of the food and the generous portion sizes. Overall, we were all extremely impressed with our experience and would highly recommend this restaurant to anyone looking for delicious and authentic Spanish cuisine. We're already looking forward to our next visit and trying even more of the dishes on the menu. With its great food, welcoming atmosphere, and excellent service, this restaurant is definitely a hidden gem that's worth discovering.

The rooms, which were once modern and sleek, now show significant signs of wear and tear. The carpet was stained, the furniture was outdated, and the bathroom could use a renovation. It's clear that the hotel has not kept up with the times, and it's disappointing to see such a decline. The overall atmosphere of the hotel felt dull and uninviting, a far cry from the vibrant and exciting experience I had 10 years ago. With so many other great options on the strip, it's hard to justify returning to a hotel that has fallen so far behind.

The atmosphere was lively and upscale, with a knowledgeable staff that added to the exceptional experience, making it a must-visit for any cocktail enthusiast looking for unique and expertly crafted drinks in a welcoming setting.

Overall, it's an average experience, with the high prices and smaller portions being a drawback, but the friendly staff and convenient location keep me coming back from time to time for a quick coffee.

The overall experience was top-notch, with the unique atmosphere and exceptional service making it a memorable celebration for my father's birthday. The burlesque dancers added a touch of elegance and sophistication, creating a lively yet refined ambiance. Quinn's attentiveness and expertise ensured that our dining experience was seamless and enjoyable. The complimentary birthday cupcake shots were a lovely gesture, and the food was outstanding, with the foie gras butter being a highlight. We were all impressed by the quality and presentation of the dishes, and we can't wait to return to SHe on our next visit to try more of their creative offerings.

I think it's essential to set realistic expectations, especially for those who, like us, are traveling from another part of town. The atmosphere was lively and fun, which added to the overall experience. Our server was attentive and knowledgeable, making great recommendations. However, the prices were a bit steep for what we received. Perhaps if we had ordered more of their signature or unique dishes, we would have felt more impressed. As it stands, I would recommend this place to those in the immediate area or to anyone looking for a solid, albeit not spectacular, brunch option. Just don't feel obligated to go out of your way, unless you're already in the neighborhood or craving something specific they offer. Overall, a pleasant experience, but not a game-changer.

I've had the pleasure of referring numerous friends and colleagues to John, and the feedback is always overwhelmingly positive. His expertise and personalized approach have saved me a significant amount of money over the years, and I appreciate the time he takes to explain complex financial concepts in a way that's easy to understand. The entire team at Coffey & Rader is professional, friendly, and genuinely invested in their clients' well-being. I feel grateful to have John and his team handling my financial affairs, and I highly recommend them to anyone seeking trustworthy and skilled financial management. Their exceptional service and dedication have earned my loyalty and trust.

...over the years. Unfortunately, the quality of the dishes no longer justifies the high prices. Despite the beautiful courtyard setting, our overall experience was disappointing. The slow service and lackluster food made for a mediocre night out. While the key lime tart and Four Seasons salad were enjoyable, they weren't enough to redeem the restaurant's overall decline. Unless they revamp their menu and improve service, I'd hesitate to recommend AZ88 to others seeking a great dining experience.

"The food was tasty and portions were generous, but Amy's exceptional service truly made our special day unforgettable. Her attention to detail and warm demeanor added a personal touch, making us feel valued and appreciated. We'll definitely be back and requesting Amy as our server again, highly recommend this place for any occasion."

The lack of attention to detail and subpar food quality were a disappointing combination. Our server seemed friendly, but the service was slow and inattentive at times. We had to ask multiple times for refills on our drinks, and it took a while to get the check. The overall atmosphere was lacking, with dim lighting and a general sense of neglect. It's clear that the restaurant is not prioritizing the customer experience. Given the numerous issues with the food and service, it's no wonder the parking lot was empty on a Saturday night. The fact that they're advertising brunch at 10:00 p.m. is a laughable mistake, suggesting a lack of organization and attention to detail. With so many other excellent dining options available, it's hard to see why anyone would choose to eat here. Unless they undergo significant changes to their menu, service, and overall approach, it's unlikely this restaurant will be able to attract and retain customers. As it stands, I would not recommend wasting your time or money on a visit. There are far better places to enjoy a delicious and authentic Mexican meal.

The overall atmosphere of the casino has taken a turn for the worse, and it's no longer the enjoyable experience it once was. I was really looking forward to my stay, but the smoke and decline in food quality made it a letdown. Even the security guard acknowledged the issue with the smoke, which makes me wonder why management hasn't taken steps to address it. The coffee shop, which was once a highlight of my visits, now serves subpar food with lackluster service. It's disappointing to see a place I once loved fall so far. I'll be taking my business elsewhere in Las Vegas, and I hope Orleans takes customer feedback seriously to make necessary improvements.

The exceptional customer service I received from Mariellen and Rafael has won me over. I appreciate their dedication to helping customers save money. The store's inventory and discounts are also a major plus. From now on, I'll be making the extra trip to this Whole Foods location, as the staff's friendly and helpful attitude makes it well worth it. I'm excited to continue shopping here and exploring their products.

The overall experience was a mixed bag, with some highlights but also some notable letdowns. The brisket was a redeeming factor, and the abundance of seafood in my dish was appreciated. However, the inconsistent preparation of the mac N cheese was a major disappointment. For a dish that's supposed to be creamy and cheesy throughout, having a dry and flavorless bottom was a letdown. The warm greeting and clean atmosphere weren't enough to make up for the culinary missteps. With some tweaks to their recipes and attention to detail, this place could reach its full potential, but as it stands, we're unlikely to return.

Very disappointing experience overall. The barista seemed completely unbothered by our complaints. With such poor customer service, it's unlikely we'll return. The lack of attention to detail and apathy towards customers is alarming, especially considering my friend's consistent negative experiences. Definitely taking our business elsewhere.

As I was leaving the store, I couldn't help but feel disappointed and frustrated with the experience I had just had. I mean, I'm a fan of the MAC brand and I've always had great experiences at other MAC stores and counters, but this one was just awful. The lack of customer service and the rude behavior of the staff was really surprising to me, especially considering that it's located in a high-end shopping area like the Forum Shops in Caesars Palace. I've worked in retail for a while now, and I know how important it is to provide good customer service, regardless of what the customer looks like or how much they're planning to spend. It's not about judging people based on their appearance, it's about treating everyone with respect and making them feel welcome in the store. And that's exactly what was missing from my experience at this MAC store. I was also surprised that the staff seemed so uninterested in helping me, even when I was standing at the counter waiting to make a purchase. I mean, I had already picked out the products I wanted to buy, and all I needed was for someone to ring me up and answer a few questions I had. But instead, I was left standing there for a while, waiting for someone to acknowledge me and help me with my purchase. And then, when the girl with the tattoos finally did come over to ring me up, she was barely even looking at me, let alone making an effort to be friendly or helpful. It was like she was annoyed that I was even there, and that she had to bother with ringing up my purchase. I was shocked, because I've never experienced anything like that before at a MAC store. My dad was also really put off by the whole experience, and he was about to say something to the staff about how rude they were being. But I just wanted to get out of there as quickly as possible, so I paid for my products and we left. I was really looking forward to visiting the MAC store and exploring all the different products they had, but the bad customer service really ruined the experience for me. I would definitely not recommend this MAC store to anyone, and I would advise people to avoid it if they can. There are plenty of other MAC stores and counters where the staff is friendly and helpful, and where you can get a much better shopping experience. I'm just disappointed that this store didn't live up to the standards that I've come to expect from MAC. It's also worth noting that the location of the store, in the Forum Shops in Caesars Palace, is usually a place where you would expect to see a high level of customer service, given the luxury brands that are located there. But unfortunately, the MAC store fell far short of that standard. I hope that in the future, they will take steps to improve their customer service and provide a better experience for their customers. In the end, I left the store feeling disappointed and frustrated, and I wouldn't go back there again even if they paid me. The bad customer service and rude behavior of the staff was just too much, and it really ruined what could have been a fun and enjoyable shopping experience. I hope that MAC will take my feedback seriously and take steps to improve the customer service at this store, because until then, I would not recommend it to anyone.

Overall, our dining experience was a major letdown, and we left feeling disappointed and overcharged. The combination of subpar food, poor service, and lackluster atmosphere made it clear that this restaurant is not living up to its potential. The fact that they received a three-star review from Frommer's Scotland is puzzling, and we can't help but wonder if the reviewer had a completely different experience. The noise level in the restaurant was another issue, with the loud chatter and clinking of glasses making it difficult to carry on a conversation. The white tablecloths and fancy decor seemed out of place in such a chaotic environment. It's clear that the restaurant is trying to appeal to a crowd that is more interested in socializing and drinking than in enjoying a good meal. Despite the chef's ability to cook the duck to the right temperature, the lack of flavor and seasoning was a major oversight. The fact that we had to add salt to the dish is a basic mistake that should not be happening in a restaurant of this caliber. The pork and vegetables were also underwhelming, and the dessert options were limited and unimpressive. The cheese plate, in particular, was a joke, with only two lackluster cheeses to choose from. In conclusion, our experience at this restaurant was a disappointment, and we would not recommend it to others. With so many other excellent dining options available, it's hard to see why anyone would choose to eat here. Unless the restaurant makes some significant changes to its menu, service, and atmosphere, we can't see it living up to its potential.

I've had better experiences finding what I need during these times. The shelves are fully stocked, and the crowds are smaller. Overall, I'm satisfied with this discount store, considering the trade-offs for lower prices. It's a great option for those on a budget, and I'll continue to shop here for my essential items, keeping my expectations in check.

The staff is friendly and accommodating, making sure we have everything we need. The atmosphere is warm and inviting, allowing our students to relax and refuel before their classes. We appreciate the consistent quality and look forward to many more wonderful lunches at Las Glorias.

Overall, my experience working at this mall has been decent, but as a shopper, I can see why some people might be put off by the outdated feel and lackluster customer service in some stores. However, the convenience of having a wide range of outlet stores in one place, along with the nearby options at Town Square, makes it a worthwhile destination for those looking to snag some deals. The indoor aspect of the mall is definitely a plus during the scorching summer months, but the disjointed layout, with some stores only accessible from the outside, can be a bit frustrating. Despite its flaws, I still find myself recommending this mall to friends and family, especially those visiting from out of town who are looking for a one-stop shopping experience. That being said, if I'm being completely honest, I do prefer the North Outlet, which seems to have a more modern and streamlined feel to it. Perhaps with some further renovations and updates, this mall can regain some of its former glory and become a top destination for shoppers once again. For now, it's a solid, if unremarkable, option for those looking to score some discounts on their favorite brands.

The scaled-back production lacked the grandeur and excitement that initially drew me to Zumanity. The remaining acts, although still talented, felt disconnected and lacking in cohesion. The hostess's forced humor fell flat, making the experience feel stale and unoriginal. My friends' lukewarm reaction was a testament to the show's diminished impact. Overall, I regret recommending it, and I wouldn't suggest it to others unless significant changes are made to revitalize the performance. Sadly, Zumanity's magic has faded, leaving behind a shadow of its former self. It's a disappointing decline for a once-thrilling show.

This outdated practice left a sour taste, overshadowing the decent culinary experience. The prices for sides were also steep, making the overall meal overpriced. As a result, I would not recommend this establishment to fellow Korean food enthusiasts, despite their satisfactory dishes, due to this unreasonable and cultural inconsistency.

I was thoroughly entertained by the acrobatic feats, martial arts, and puppetry. The special effects and stage design were impressive, making the experience even more captivating. Overall, KA was an exhilarating and unforgettable show that exceeded my expectations, leaving me eager to explore more of Cirque du Soleil's productions, starting with "O" as my next adventure.

The Shish Cafe is excellent! Being a typical small town Wisconsin girl, I'm pretty wary of "new things". I don't think I've been to a Mediterranean restaurant in my life. I was totally unprepared for the deliciousness of shawarma, and the hummus, and the iggie!! Honestly, I can't wait to go back. Also, I assume it's the dude that runs the place that is especially friendly and showed me the shaker with the yummy spice on the table and he said it was "his spice". okay! it's good! My only complaint is that really, the entrees are all priced like $4 too much to warrant going here as much as I'd like. Despite this, I highly recommend The Shish Cafe for its unique flavors and welcoming atmosphere. The portion sizes are generous, and the quality of the ingredients is evident. I'm already planning my next visit to try more of their dishes.

The lack of accountability and poor communication from the staff really left a sour taste in our mouths. It's not like we were trying to scam a free side of ranch, we just wanted to be informed about the extra charge. A simple "our ranch dressing is $1 extra" would have sufficed. Instead, we were met with a dismissive attitude and a clear lack of concern for customer satisfaction. The fact that the manager didn't even bother to apologize or offer any kind of resolution was appalling. As a result, we left feeling frustrated and disappointed. The food, while decent, was not enough to make up for the subpar service. The crabcake sliders I had were tasty, but not exceptional. Overall, the experience was a letdown, and I would not recommend this place to anyone who values good service. Unless they seriously revamp their staff training and customer service policies, I would advise others to take their business elsewhere. With so many other great restaurants to choose from, it's just not worth the hassle and poor treatment. Needless to say, we won't be returning anytime soon.

The ambiance is cozy and relaxed, making it an ideal spot to unwind and socialize. The staff is friendly and attentive, ensuring that your glasses are always full. Although the prices may be steep, the unique cocktails are worth trying at least once. If you're looking for a break from the hustle and bustle of the casino floor, this lounge is a great option. Just be prepared to spend a bit of money and don't expect to get rowdy, as the atmosphere is more laid-back and sophisticated. Overall, it's a nice spot to recharge before heading back to the action.

I appreciate the unique twist they bring to their dishes, and the service has always been friendly and attentive. The remodel has definitely improved the ambiance, making it a more inviting space to relax and enjoy a meal. However, I still think they could benefit from refreshing their menu to keep things exciting for regular customers like myself. Perhaps some seasonal specials or limited-time offerings could help keep the menu feeling fresh. Despite the prices, I'll likely continue to visit, especially during happy hour when the value is better. The birthday club coupon was a nice perk, and I'm looking forward to seeing what other promotions they might offer in the future. Overall, it's a solid choice for those looking to try something a bit different, and I'm hopeful they'll continue to evolve and improve.

I would definitely recommend this hotel to those on a budget who don't plan on spending too much time in the hotel itself. The strip view from our room on the 11th floor was stunning, especially at night when the entire strip was lit up. However, as a vegetarian, I was thoroughly disappointed with the buffet options and would not recommend it to fellow vegetarians. The $20 price tag was also a bit steep for the quality of food provided. On the other hand, the $14 resort fee was reasonable considering it covered unlimited access to the pool, tower, and WiFi. The hotel's location on the end of the strip was actually a plus for us, as it provided a quieter and more relaxed atmosphere. If you're looking for a no-frills, affordable place to stay with a great view, this hotel might be a good option. Just be sure to explore other dining options off-site. Overall, our stay was pleasant and we got a good value for the price we paid.

The atmosphere was always welcoming and the staff were friendly and knowledgeable about their coffee. I appreciated the consistency of their brews and the fact that they sourced high-quality beans. The loss of Caribou has left a void in the neighborhood, and Peet's just doesn't compare. I've tried to adjust, but it's not the same. The unique character and charm of Caribou are deeply missed, and I often find myself reminiscing about the good times I had there. I hope that someday, a similar coffee shop will fill the gap, but until then, I'll just have to keep looking for a new favorite spot.

We've become regulars and can't wait to try more dishes. The ambiance is cozy and inviting, making it perfect for dates or family dinners. Overall, a fantastic dining experience that keeps us coming back for more, with Pam's exceptional service being the icing on the cake, making every visit truly special.

Overall, the atmosphere is lively and fun, especially on Fridays with live music. The outdoor seating area is perfect for a relaxing evening with friends. Although the setup could be improved, the quality of the Sangria and cheese plate makes up for it. With a few tweaks to their service model, the Olive Mill could become a top destination for happy hour enthusiasts. For now, it remains a great spot to unwind and enjoy good company, making it an excellent choice for entertaining out-of-town visitors.

It's disappointing to see a once-beloved brand like Metro, which I've been loyal to since the 90's, fall short of expectations. The lack of transparency about being out of ice cream and the subsequent failure to offer a suitable solution or apology is unacceptable. As a customer, it's reasonable to expect a certain level of quality and service, especially when it comes to something as simple as a milkshake. The fact that the waiter didn't even offer to comp the item or provide a substitute is a clear indication of a larger problem with the location's management and customer service. I've given this location multiple chances to improve, but it's clear that they're more concerned with getting bodies in the door than providing a quality experience. Unfortunately, I'll be taking my business (and my family's) elsewhere. It's a shame, really, as I was excited to have a Metro location closer to home. Now, I'll just have to find a new go-to spot that prioritizes customer satisfaction and quality control.

As I reflected on our stay, I realized that this hotel is perfect for those who are looking for a no-frills, budget-friendly option. It's not going to blow you away with its amenities or luxurious decor, but it gets the job done. The location, while not ideal, is manageable with a cab ride. We ended up taking a cab to the nearby attractions, and as I mentioned earlier, it cost us around $10-15, depending on the destination. It's essential to factor in these extra costs when considering the overall value of your stay. The breakfast buffet, although limited, was a decent spread, and the $10.49 price tag wasn't too bad. The staff, as I mentioned earlier, were friendly and accommodating, which made our stay more enjoyable. If I were to suggest improvements, I would recommend that they look into upgrading their shower heads and ensuring that the tubs drain properly. These small issues can make a significant difference in the overall guest experience. In conclusion, if you're looking for a cheap place to stay and don't mind a few quirks, this hotel might be the way to go. Just be aware of the potential extra costs, such as cab rides, and weigh them against the savings you'll get from the low room rate. With a bit of planning and managing of expectations, you can have a decent stay at this hotel. Overall, it's not a bad option for those on a tight budget, and I would consider staying here again if I needed a cheap place to crash.

As we dined, the atmosphere was lively and energetic, with the fluorescent accent lights adding a touch of vibrancy to the space. The music was upbeat and reminiscent of a nightclub, which fit perfectly with the club-like twist of the steakhouse. Our server, despite being busy with multiple tables, was attentive and knowledgeable about the menu, making excellent recommendations and ensuring that our glasses were always full. The 40 oz. ribeye for two was undoubtedly the highlight of our meal, and we were impressed by the generous portion size and the exceptional quality of the meat. The au jus was rich and flavorful, and we found ourselves dipping our steak into it repeatedly throughout the meal. The accompanying sides were also well-prepared, with the asparagus spears and mac and cheese shell being particular standouts. While the garbage salad was a bit of a letdown, we appreciated the creativity and effort that went into creating such a unique dish. The baked potato, topped with truffles and butter, was a nice touch, and the spinach creamed was decent, if not particularly memorable. The roasted vegetables, however, were a disappointment, lacking flavor and texture. Despite the limited menu options for non-steak lovers, we found that the quality of the dishes made up for the lack of variety. The seafood options, although limited, sounded appealing, and we would have liked to try some of the other dishes on offer. The drinks menu, on the other hand, was extensive and impressive, with a wide range of cocktails and wine options to choose from. Overall, our experience at this steakhouse was enjoyable and memorable, with the 40 oz. ribeye for two being the undeniable star of the show. While the atmosphere may not be to everyone's taste, it's clear that the restaurant is catering to a specific crowd, and the option to get passes to the clubs at Palms after dinner is a nice touch. We would definitely recommend making reservations, especially on weekends or during peak hours, to ensure a smooth and enjoyable dining experience.

Despite my mediocre experience, I can see why my boyfriend is so enthusiastic about this restaurant. The atmosphere was lively and modern, with a trendy vibe that appealed to a wide range of customers. The service was also top-notch, with friendly and attentive staff who ensured that our needs were met throughout the meal. Perhaps I just ordered the wrong dish, as my boyfriend's repeated visits suggest that there are some real gems on the menu. I've heard great things about their unique burger offerings, such as the Kalbi Burger and the Pad Thai Burger, which combine traditional burger ingredients with bold Asian flavors. Next time, I might opt for one of these more adventurous options to see if they live up to the hype. For now, I'm willing to give this place the benefit of the doubt and try it again, especially since my boyfriend is always raving about it. With a bit more exploration of the menu, I'm hopeful that I'll discover what makes this restaurant so special to him. Until then, it remains a solid, if unremarkable, dining option in my book.

I've been to several vape shops in the area, but this one stands out from the rest. The staff is always eager to help and answer any questions I may have, whether it's about a new device or a specific e-liquid flavor. They have a wide selection of products, and they're always willing to offer recommendations based on my preferences. The store itself is clean and well-organized, making it easy to navigate and find what I'm looking for. I also appreciate that they're active in the vaping community, often hosting events and promotions that bring customers together. Overall, I'm impressed with the level of service and expertise provided by this vape shop, and I would highly recommend it to anyone looking for a great vaping experience. The owners and staff are truly passionate about what they do, and it shows in the way they run their business.
Unfortunately, the lackluster experience was consistent across visits, leaving much to be desired in terms of taste and overall quality sadly.

Overall, our experience was underwhelming and not worth the high cost. The lack of attention to detail and slow service made for a frustrating dinner. Despite the promising recommendation, we left feeling disappointed and unlikely to return. With so many other great options available, it's hard to justify giving this place another chance. Unless they revamp their menu and improve their service, we'd advise others to explore alternative dining options.

As I reflect on my experience at Sweet O, I think my main issue was that it didn't quite live up to my expectations. The atmosphere was pleasant, with a cozy and intimate setting that made it easy to converse with my friends. The staff was friendly and attentive, with our waitress being particularly accommodating and patient. However, the food and drinks, while not bad by any means, didn't blow me away. The German Riesling flight was a highlight, and I appreciated the generous discount on the price. But the cheese plate, which I was looking forward to, was a letdown. The blue cheese and brie mixture was overpowering and unpleasant, and the bread was too hard and unyielding. The panini I had was fine, but it didn't showcase the pesto in the best way possible. My friends seemed to enjoy their desserts, particularly the raspberry cheesecake, which they raved about. But for me, the experience was just okay. I didn't feel like I was missing out on anything by not trying the chocolate, but it's possible that the desserts are where Sweet O truly shines. One thing that struck me was how empty the restaurant was, even on a weekend evening. Given its location on the west side, I would have expected it to be busier. Perhaps it's still building up a loyal customer base, or maybe it's just not well-known enough yet. Whatever the reason, it made for a quiet and relaxed atmosphere, which was nice but also a bit eerie at times. Ultimately, I wouldn't discourage anyone from trying Sweet O, especially if they're in the area. But for me, it's not worth the 30-minute drive from Tempe. There are plenty of other restaurants in the valley that offer similar or better experiences, and I wouldn't go out of my way to come back to Sweet O. Maybe with some tweaks to the menu and a bit more attention to detail, it could become a standout destination. But for now, it's just an okay option in a crowded culinary landscape.

The atmosphere is cozy and inviting, making it a great spot to catch up with friends or family. Prices are reasonable, especially with the coupons. Overall, it's a reliable breakfast spot that consistently delivers a satisfying meal without any frills, and I appreciate the friendly service and convenient location that keeps me coming back.

The whole experience was just extremely disappointing, especially since we were willing to give them another chance after the initial mishap. It's understandable that new restaurants may have some kinks to work out, but serving raw chicken is a serious food safety issue that can't be taken lightly. The fact that the manager was "busy" and couldn't be bothered to come out and apologize in person was also quite unprofessional. The car hop who came out to assist us seemed genuinely concerned, but the lack of urgency and follow-through from the management was appalling. We were relieved that they eventually refunded our order, but the damage was already done. The combination of poor service, food safety issues, and unprofessional management has ensured that we will never be returning to this establishment.
