It's a shame, really, because the concept of the restaurant had promise, but it seems like they have a long way to go before they can provide a safe and satisfactory dining experience for their customers. Needless to say, we would not recommend this place to anyone until they can get their act together.
They prey on unsuspecting customers with false promises, hidden fees, and subpar service, leaving you frustrated and financially drained, regretting the decision to use their services.

As I reflected on my experience, I couldn't help but wonder if the barista's inexperience was a contributing factor to the subpar drink. The fact that he was alone and seemed overwhelmed by a simple transaction didn't exactly fill me with confidence. I've had my fair share of bad coffee, but this one was particularly disappointing given the promising atmosphere and aesthetics of the cafe. The artwork on the walls and the modern decor suggested a establishment that took pride in its offerings, but unfortunately, the coffee didn't live up to the visuals. I'm willing to give them the benefit of the doubt and consider that it might have been an off day, but until they can consistently deliver a decent cup of coffee, I'll be taking my business (and my refined palate) elsewhere. Perhaps with some additional training and support for their staff, they can elevate their coffee game and become a worthy competitor to the likes of Starbucks. Until then, I'll remain skeptical and hesitant to return.

As we left the restaurant, we couldn't help but feel disappointed and frustrated with the overall experience. The food, although not bad, was not impressive enough to make up for the poor service we received. The owner's attitude and behavior were completely unacceptable, and it's clear that she needs to work on her customer service skills. It's unfortunate, because with a little more attention to detail and a more welcoming atmosphere, this restaurant could have potential. The fact that the owner was so unwilling to accommodate our request to pay by card, even when we offered to increase the amount to over $5, was baffling. It's not like we were trying to take advantage of her or the restaurant, but rather, we were trying to pay for the meal we had just enjoyed. The way she spoke to us, with a tone of bitterness and anger, was completely uncalled for and made us feel uncomfortable and unwelcome. Overall, our experience at this restaurant was a letdown, and we would not recommend it to anyone. The food was average, the service was terrible, and the ambiance, although quaint, was not enough to make up for the other shortcomings. With so many other great restaurants in the area, it's easy to see why this one is not more popular. Unless the owner takes steps to improve the service and overall experience, we can't see this restaurant thriving. Needless to say, we will not be returning, and we would advise others to think twice before using their Groupon or visiting this restaurant.

The overall atmosphere of the place seemed to be lacking, with a rather empty and quiet dining area, which didn't help to make my experience any more enjoyable. I was really looking forward to a hearty breakfast to start my day in Vegas, but unfortunately, this place fell short of my expectations. The food, although edible, was not impressive, and the service was subpar. For a $25 breakfast, I expect to be treated with a bit more care and attention, especially when it comes to something as simple as providing condiments for my toast. The fact that my server only showed interest in my stay when it was time to pay made it feel like they were only looking out for their own interests, rather than genuinely caring about my experience. Needless to say, I would not recommend this place to anyone, and I'm glad I could warn that group of potential customers as I was leaving.

Unfortunately, the positives couldn't make up for the disappointing cuisine. For a high-end steakhouse, the quality of the dishes fell short. The beautiful ambiance and decent service were overshadowed by the subpar food. Overall, it was an overpriced and underwhelming experience that didn't live up to expectations of a authentic New York-style steakhouse.

and the service, although informative, felt somewhat pretentious. The atmosphere was also not inviting, making my overall experience disappointing. Perhaps it's a place for regulars, but for a newcomer, it was overwhelming and unwelcoming, which is a shame because I had high hopes for their unique sandwich offerings.

The lack of attention to detail and cleanliness is appalling, and it's clear that the management is not taking the necessary steps to address these issues. The fact that a used condom was found in one of the rooms is absolutely disgusting and raises serious concerns about the hotel's housekeeping standards. The staff's indifference to our complaints and their inability to provide basic services such as shuttle arrangements is unacceptable. The overpriced restaurant and seedy bar/lounge only add to the overall feeling of disappointment and frustration. Given the hotel's prime location, it's shocking that they're not taking advantage of it to provide a better experience for their guests. Instead, they seem to be relying on their location to attract customers, rather than actually putting in the effort to provide good service and amenities. Overall, I would not recommend this hotel to anyone and would advise others to look elsewhere for a cleaner, more reliable, and more customer-friendly experience.

As I reflect on my most recent visit, I am still appalled by the sheer disregard for customer satisfaction and basic hygiene. The fact that the bar staff, Ryan, felt comfortable sharing his dissatisfaction with the establishment's management and encouraging customers to take their business elsewhere speaks volumes about the lack of accountability and leadership. It's unacceptable that customers are being advised to leave and go to a different restaurant, Paradise Bakery, by the staff themselves. The kitchen's lack of cleanliness is a major concern, and I was horrified to witness the cook's blatant disregard for food safety protocols. The fact that he was handling food with his bare hands after wiping his nose and coughing is a serious health risk. The smell of old, rotting beer at the bar and the non-functioning drain on the beer tap only add to the overall sense of neglect and poor maintenance. Unfortunately, the food itself was the final disappointment. After waiting for an inordinate amount of time, I was served a tasteless, unappetizing meal that lacked any redeeming qualities. Given my previous experiences at this establishment, I had hoped that things would improve, but it's clear that the problems run deep. With so many other options available, I will not be returning to this restaurant again. The combination of poor timing, uncleanliness, and subpar food has solidified my decision to take my business elsewhere. Airport food or not, there's no excuse for such a lackluster experience.

The entire experience at ACME was not only disappointing but also disturbing. The bartender's attitude and the bouncer's inconsistent enforcement of the "females only" policy upstairs were major turn-offs. The fact that they would make such a derogatory comment about having to "act like you have a vagina" to access the upstairs area was completely unacceptable. The atmosphere was also quite seedy, with the aforementioned patron dancing on the bar. Overall, our visit to ACME was a disaster, and we would not recommend it to anyone. In contrast, our subsequent visit to Saddleranch was a breath of fresh air, with a fun and welcoming atmosphere that made up for the horrible experience we had at ACME.
However, the exceptional quality and generous portions made it worthwhile, and the outstanding service further justified the cost, making for a memorable dining experience overall.

It's unacceptable and frustrating to see such a lack of coordination and expertise. The inconsistent diagnoses caused unnecessary stress and anxiety for my family. We expected a higher level of care, especially from a hospital with friendly nurses and a clean environment. Unfortunately, the doctors' incompetence overshadowed the hospital's positive aspects, making our experience disappointing and worrisome.
reasonably priced, cozy atmosphere, and generous portions make it a perfect destination for a satisfying and delightful meal experience.
Will not be returning due to the extremely rude and inattentive staff members always.

Overall, it was a great stay despite a few quirks. The room's amenities and comfy bed made up for the extra fees. I'd recommend it to others, but be aware of the pricey vending machines and navigating the casino to get to your room. Still, $40 a night is a steal for the quality provided.
The service is friendly and attentive, making it a great spot for families and casual dining, with a cozy atmosphere that keeps us coming back for more.
The staff were friendly and accommodating, making our anniversary celebration even more special with their thoughtful gestures and excellent service.

The overall shopping experience is frustrating and disappointing. Employees seem uninterested and unhelpful, adding to the chaos. Despite its convenient location, I'd rather drive farther to a cleaner, better-managed store with decent customer service, which is unfortunate given my proximity to this one. One star is even too generous for this subpar Walmart.

As I reflected on our dining experience, I couldn't help but think about the numerous other restaurants I've been to in the area that offer far superior food and service at a fraction of the cost. The fact that this establishment can get away with serving subpar dishes at exorbitant prices is a testament to the power of its location and the view of Mark's Square. It's clear that they're relying on the allure of the plaza to bring in customers, rather than focusing on providing a quality dining experience. The pear and gorgonzola salad was another disappointment. The pears were underripe and lacked any discernible flavor, while the gorgonzola was bland and uninspired. The combination of the two was lackluster, and the presentation was unimpressive. For a salad that cost over $15, I expected a lot more in terms of flavor, texture, and presentation. Our server, who was not the same person I interacted with at the register, was friendly and attentive, but even she couldn't make up for the shortcomings of the food. She seemed to be doing her best to provide good service, but the kitchen's failures were too great to overcome. As we finished our meal and prepared to leave, I couldn't help but feel a sense of regret and disappointment. We had wasted a significant amount of money on a meal that was, at best, mediocre. The view of Mark's Square, which had initially drawn us in, was not enough to redeem the establishment's numerous failures. In contrast, Traittoria Reggiano, which I mentioned earlier, is a hidden gem that offers exceptional food and service at a fraction of the cost. The flavors are bold and authentic, the portions are generous, and the prices are reasonable. It's a small, family-owned restaurant that truly cares about providing a quality dining experience, rather than relying on its location to bring in customers. If you're looking for a great meal in the area, I would strongly advise against this establishment and instead recommend Traittoria Reggiano or even chains like BRIO or Maggiano's. While they may not have the same view, they offer far superior food and service at a more reasonable price. Save your money and your taste buds, and avoid this overpriced and underwhelming dining experience. In conclusion, my two-star review is generous, considering the numerous disappointments we experienced during our meal. The view of Mark's Square is not enough to redeem the establishment's subpar food, poor service, and exorbitant prices. Until they focus on providing a quality dining experience, rather than relying on their location, I would not recommend this restaurant to anyone.

We thoroughly enjoyed our evening and would definitely return. The atmosphere was lively, yet intimate, making it perfect for a night out with friends or a romantic dinner. Overall, a great experience that exceeded our expectations, with top-notch cuisine and exceptional service in a beautiful setting. Highly recommended for special occasions or a fancy night out.

As the night went on, we found ourselves getting more and more comfortable in the downstairs portion of the club. The music was pumping, and the girls were definitely putting on a show. We had a few favorites that we ended up requesting multiple times, and they seemed to enjoy our company just as much as we enjoyed theirs. One of them even took a liking to my brother, the bachelor, and gave him a few extra-special dances to commemorate the occasion. Despite the downsides I mentioned earlier, we still managed to have an amazing time. The atmosphere was electric, and the staff (with the exception of the bald dude at the entrance) were friendly and accommodating. Our waitress was particularly great, making sure we always had drinks in hand and even throwing in a few extras here and there. As the night wore on, we started to get a little more rowdy, but the security staff were always on hand to keep things under control. They were firm but fair, and we appreciated their presence. We even had a few laughs with them, and they seemed to be enjoying the party just as much as we were. One thing that's worth noting is that the club has a pretty strict no-photography policy, which we appreciated. It's nice to be able to let loose and not have to worry about ending up on someone's Facebook page the next morning. They also have a coat check, which was convenient since we had a few jackets and bags with us. Overall, I'd say that the downstairs portion of OG is definitely worth checking out if you're in the area. Just be aware of the potential downsides, and make sure to keep an eye on your belongings. With the right mindset and a bit of caution, you can have a wild and unforgettable time. And who knows, you might even find yourself staying for 4.5 hours like we did. In retrospect, I think we made the right decision in choosing OG over some of the other strip clubs in the area. The atmosphere was more laid-back, and the girls were definitely more friendly and approachable. We even ended up meeting a few of the other patrons, and we all had a great time together. As we left the club and made our way back to the strip, we were all buzzing from the excitement of the night. We had a few last-minute drinks at a nearby bar, and then stumbled back to our hotel room, exhausted but exhilarated. It was definitely a night to remember, and we're all still talking about it to this day. If you're looking for a wild and unforgettable experience in Vegas, I'd definitely recommend checking out the downstairs portion of OG. Just don't forget to bring your wallet, and be prepared for a night that you'll never forget.

The poor service was disappointing, especially considering the number of vacant tables. It's clear that the restaurant needs to invest in more staff to keep up with demand and provide a better experience for loyal customers like us.
Prices are reasonable and portions are generous, making it a great value for the quality and taste, I highly recommend it to anyone craving delicious ramen in the area.

I was thoroughly unimpressed by the dishes I ordered, and the prices did not justify the lack of flavor. For a restaurant that prides itself on being unique and creative, I expected a lot more depth and complexity in their dishes. Unfortunately, everything I tried tasted like a watered-down version of authentic Asian cuisine. The fact that the owner claims it's not an Asian fusion place, yet the decor and menu suggest otherwise, only adds to the confusion. As a paying customer, I don't care about the label - I care about the food being delicious and worth my money. Sadly, Clever Koi fell short in that regard. Unless they revamp their menu and focus on developing bold, authentic flavors, I wouldn't recommend this place to anyone looking for a satisfying dining experience. Perhaps with some tweaks and improvements, Clever Koi can live up to its name and deliver a truly clever and delicious culinary experience.

Overall, my experiences at this pub have been consistently pleasant, if not exactly memorable. The beer selection is decent, with a few local options that are always a welcome sight. The atmosphere, as I mentioned, is cozy and laid-back, making it a great spot to catch up with friends or watch a game. While it may not be the most polished or upscale establishment, it has a certain charm that keeps me coming back. The fact that the staff is friendly and recognizes regulars is a big plus, and the people-watching is always entertaining. If you're looking for a no-frills, down-to-earth spot to grab a pint and some decent bar food, this pub is definitely worth a visit. Just don't expect to be blown away by the cuisine or ambiance – it's a solid, dependable option that gets the job done.

Overall, I was underwhelmed by the food and service at this establishment. The portions were small and the prices seemed steep for the quality received. The lack of heat in their spice level 3 dish was also a letdown, as I was expecting a bit of a kick. The highlight of my meal was the soup that came with the lunch special, but it wasn't enough to redeem the rest of the experience. With slower-than-expected lunch service, I wouldn't recommend this place to those with limited time. While I'm still on the hunt for a great Thai spot in town, this one unfortunately won't be making the cut. Perhaps they'll revamp their menu or service, but for now, I'll be taking my business elsewhere.

As I reflected on my experience, I couldn't help but feel that the Wynn's brunch buffet, while certainly a cut above the average buffet, didn't quite live up to the luxury standard I've come to expect from the Wynn brand. The atmosphere was elegant, with beautifully appointed decor and a spacious dining area, but the food, while good, didn't particularly impress me. The variety, as I mentioned earlier, was a bit puzzling, with a strong emphasis on Asian and Indian cuisine that, while tasty, didn't quite fit my traditional brunch expectations. That being said, the service was top-notch, with our server being friendly, attentive, and accommodating. The fact that they automatically added the mimosa option to our bill without us having to ask was a nice touch, and the server's enthusiasm and knowledge of the menu were impressive. The omelet station, as I mentioned earlier, was a highlight, with the chef expertly crafting made-to-order omelets with a wide range of fillings. If I were to offer suggestions for improvement, I would recommend expanding the selection of traditional brunch items, such as eggs benedict, quiche, and breakfast meats, and perhaps scaling back on the Asian and Indian options. I would also love to see some more premium ingredients, such as lobster or filet mignon, added to the buffet to give it a more luxurious feel. Overall, while the Wynn's brunch buffet was a solid, if unremarkable, experience, I wouldn't necessarily go out of my way to recommend it to others. That being said, if you're a fan of Asian and Indian cuisine, or if you're looking for a unique brunch experience, you may find the Wynn's buffet to be a good fit. And who knows, you may even discover some new favorite dishes. For me, though, I'll have to keep searching for that perfect brunch buffet that truly wows me.

We've tried a variety of other dishes as well, and everything has been outstanding. The edamame and agedashi tofu make for great appetizers, and the ramen bowls are a hearty, flavorful option for a chilly evening. The presentation of each dish is also noteworthy, with garnishes and sauces adding a pop of color to the plates. What really sets Sens apart, though, is the consistency - every visit has been just as enjoyable as the last, with friendly servers and a lively atmosphere that's perfect for a night out with friends or a date. Whether you're a foodie or just looking for a new spot to try, Sens is definitely worth a visit. With its unique dishes and exceptional service, it's no wonder we've become borderline addicted - and we can't wait to go back!

The coffee is consistently good, but the slow wifi can be frustrating. Despite the crowds, the staff remains friendly and accommodating. Overall, it's a convenient spot for late-night coffee, but be prepared for a wait and spotty internet connectivity, making it less ideal for intense studying sessions.

As I reflect on my two consecutive nights at Olives, I am still impressed by the consistency of the dishes and the exceptional service. The staff were attentive and knowledgeable, happily answering our questions about the menu and making spot-on recommendations. On our second visit, we decided to try some new dishes, including the pan-seared scallops and the grilled lamb chops, both of which were cooked to perfection. The scallops were seared to a beautiful golden brown and served with a flavorful lemon-caper sauce, while the lamb chops were tender and juicy, paired with a rich and creamy mint sauce. One thing that struck me about Olives is the attention to detail in every aspect of the dining experience. From the beautifully presented dishes to the elegant table settings, every element is carefully considered to create a sophisticated and refined atmosphere. The outdoor seating area, with its stunning view of the Bellagio fountain, is a must-try, even on a chilly evening. The sound of the water and the music accompanying the fountain show added a touch of magic to our meal, making it a truly unforgettable experience. Overall, I would highly recommend Olives to anyone looking for a top-notch dining experience in Las Vegas. With its exceptional food, impeccable service, and stunning ambiance, it is a restaurant that is sure to impress even the most discerning palates.

The staff were friendly and attentive, regularly refilling drinks and clearing plates. Despite the limited options, the dishes that were available were freshly prepared and flavorful. I particularly enjoyed the naan bread and the chicken tikka masala. However, the dessert selection was lacking, with only a few choices available. Overall, while Spice Cafe shows promise, it needs to expand its buffet offerings to compete with other Indian restaurants in the area. I'm willing to give them another chance to see if they can improve and provide a more diverse dining experience.

The level of customer service we received was appalling, and it's clear that this company prioritizes making a quick profit over taking care of their passengers. The fact that they don't accept cash is already a major inconvenience, but the way they handled the situation with my co-worker's lost wallet was absolutely unacceptable. The dispatcher's lack of effort to assist us and the driver's unconvincing denial of having the wallet only added to our frustration. We were left with no choice but to take matters into our own hands and report the incident to the authorities. I would strongly advise against using this cab company, as they seem to have no regard for their customers' well-being or property. The hassle and stress we experienced were completely avoidable, and I hope that others can learn from our terrible experience.

The service was attentive and friendly, our server checked in on us just the right amount. The atmosphere was cozy and inviting, perfect for a low-key evening out. The food portions were generous and the prices were reasonable. I was impressed by the quality of the ingredients and the presentation of the dishes. The Trifecta was a highlight, with each component complementing the others beautifully. Overall, I'm glad we stumbled upon this hidden gem and I'm already looking forward to my next visit to try more of their menu offerings.

As we finally started to receive our dishes, we were impressed by the presentation and the aroma of the food. The dry chili chicken, which I mentioned earlier, was a highlight of the meal - crispy, spicy, and full of flavor. The Kung Pao chicken was also delicious, with a nice balance of savory and spicy notes. However, the long wait had taken a toll on our appetite, and we couldn't fully enjoy the food as we would have liked. Despite the chaos in the kitchen, the service staff were friendly and attentive, trying their best to keep us updated on the status of our food. The manager's apology and offer to comp our meal were a nice touch, and we appreciated the effort to make things right. As we finished our meal and prepared to leave, we couldn't help but feel that Lao Sze Chuan has potential, but they need to work on their kitchen workflow and communication to provide a better dining experience. With some tweaks to their service and kitchen management, I would definitely consider returning to Lao Sze Chuan to try more of their dishes. The food is delicious, and the atmosphere is cozy and inviting. Perhaps it's best to visit on a less busy night, or to call ahead to ask about wait times. For now, I would recommend Lao Sze Chuan to fans of spicy Sze Chuan cuisine, but with the caveat to be patient and prepared for potential delays.

As I reflected on my stay, I couldn't help but feel that the Wynn's focus on nickel-and-diming their guests overshadowed the luxurious amenities and accommodations they have to offer. The room, as I mentioned, was stunning, with a comfortable king-sized bed and a beautifully appointed living area. The gym, too, was a highlight, with its top-of-the-line equipment and thoughtful amenities like free headphones and water bottles. However, these positives were consistently offset by the resort's puzzling attempts to squeeze extra revenue out of their guests. The issues with the Le Reve tickets and the buffet credit were just the beginning. Throughout our stay, we encountered numerous other small but frustrating examples of the Wynn's penny-pinching approach. For example, the in-room Wi-Fi was slow and unreliable, and the resort charged an exorbitant fee for parking. These may seem like minor complaints, but they added up to create a sense of annoyance and disappointment that lingered throughout our stay. What's more, the Wynn's customer service team seemed woefully unprepared to address these issues. When I spoke with the reservations agent and the managers, I was met with a combination of defensiveness and indifference. It was clear that they were more interested in following the resort's policies and procedures than in providing genuine assistance and resolving our problems. Ultimately, my experience at the Wynn was a disappointment, and it's unlikely that I'll be returning anytime soon. While the room and gym were certainly highlights, the resort's focus on maximizing revenue and minimizing expenses created a sense of frustration and disillusionment that I wouldn't wish on anyone. If you're looking for a truly luxurious and hassle-free experience, I would strongly encourage you to consider other options. The Wynn may have a reputation for excellence, but in my opinion, it falls far short of the mark.

The experience was extremely disappointing, and the lack of concern from the staff was appalling. It's clear that they're more interested in handing out coupons to lure in customers than actually providing a decent meal. The fact that the place was empty when I picked up my order should have been a red flag, as it suggests that the food may have been sitting out for a while. The boiled chicken was tough and fatty, and the overcooked rice was dry and flavorless. For the same price, you can get a high-quality meal at a reputable restaurant like PF Changs. It's shocking that this place has managed to stay in business, and I would strongly advise others to avoid it at all costs. Save your money and your taste buds, and take your business elsewhere.

The service is always friendly and attentive, making our dining experience even more enjoyable. We've never had a bad meal here, and the prices are very reasonable. The atmosphere is casual and welcoming, perfect for a quick lunch or dinner with family and friends, making it a great spot to satisfy our Mexican food cravings.

The convenience was much appreciated. We ended up visiting twice during our trip, and both times the staff were friendly and accommodating. The variety of donuts was impressive, and the fact that they catered to vegan diets was a huge plus. Overall, I'm so glad we stumbled upon this hidden gem, and I highly recommend it to anyone with a sweet tooth, especially those with dietary restrictions. It's definitely a must-visit when in Vegas.

The wall-mounted sofa bed was uncomfortable and lacked proper bedding. Overall, my stay was disappointing, and I wouldn't recommend this Hyatt location to others. For the price, I expected better service and amenities. Unfortunately, this experience fell short of my expectations, making it a less desirable choice for future travels.

that offer a more relaxed atmosphere and similar quality of food and drinks. I've tried to give this place multiple chances, but the inconvenience always outweighs the positives. Unless they expand or improve their seating and waiting area, I'll have to take my business elsewhere. The hassle just isn't worth it, no matter how great their beer selection is.

We were thoroughly impressed with our experience and would definitely recommend this spot to friends and family. The "holy shitake" pizza was a highlight, with the garlic sauce and herb crust complementing the earthy flavor of the mushrooms perfectly. The portion size was generous, and we left feeling satisfied but not overly stuffed. The casual atmosphere made it an ideal spot for a low-key dinner or gathering with friends. The fact that they cater to alternative diets is a big plus, and the variety of options on the menu ensures that there's something for everyone. We're looking forward to trying more of their menu items, especially the gluten-free pizzas and other unique pizza bases. With its friendly staff, clean facilities, and delicious food, this pizza place has won us over and we'll be back for more. Overall, a great addition to the neighborhood.

Unfortunately, my latest experience at Kanda in Laval was the final straw. The sushi was no longer the delicious, fresh dish I had grown to love. Instead, it was lackluster and uninspiring, with some pieces even tasting stale. The presentation, which was once beautifully done, now seemed sloppy and rushed. For a place that was once a staple for our group outings, it's sad to see the quality decline so significantly. The combination of poor service and subpar food is a recipe for disaster, and I fear that Kanda will continue to lose customers if they don't make some serious changes. As much as I hate to say it, I'll be taking my business (and my love of sushi) elsewhere from now on. It's time to find a new go-to spot that can deliver on both quality and service.

I'm extremely disappointed in the way my situation was handled by both the Downtown Grand and Choice Hotels corporate. The lack of effort to provide a meaningful resolution is staggering. A form letter apology from Choice Hotels corporate is not only insulting, but it also shows a complete disregard for customer satisfaction. I had expected more from a reputable hotel chain like Choice Hotels. The offer from Sarah, the business manager at the Downtown Grand, to reschedule my stay for another time, although appreciated, is not a viable solution for me. As I mentioned earlier, I won't be able to make it to Vegas by July 2015, which makes the offer essentially worthless. I was really hoping for a full refund or at least a partial refund, which would have been a fair compromise. The fact that the Downtown Grand is keeping my $400+ and not providing any meaningful compensation is not only unfair but also short-sighted. As I mentioned, my friends and I usually spend a significant amount of money at the hotel's pizza restaurant and were considering staying at the hotel this time. However, due to the way my situation was handled, we have decided to take our business elsewhere. The Downtown Grand's loss of our business will likely exceed a couple of thousand dollars per year, which is a significant amount for any hotel. In conclusion, my experience with the Downtown Grand has been extremely disappointing, and I would not recommend this hotel to anyone. The hotel's inability to provide a fair resolution to my situation and the lack of effort from Choice Hotels corporate to address my concerns have left a sour taste in my mouth. Unless the hotel changes its policies and starts prioritizing customer satisfaction, I fear that they will continue to lose business from loyal customers like myself.

However, if you're seeking a more vibrant atmosphere or a place to enjoy a quiet evening, you might want to consider other options. The music is loud, and the overall ambiance can be overwhelming, especially on weekends when the bar is packed. I've noticed that the crowd can get quite rowdy, which might not be ideal for everyone. On the other hand, if you're looking for a no-frills, budget-friendly spot to grab a drink with friends, Bar Salsa might fit the bill. Just be prepared for the crowds and noise. It's also worth noting that the bar's small size can make it feel claustrophobic, especially when it's busy. Despite its limitations, Bar Salsa seems to have a loyal following, and I can see why it appeals to some people. Ultimately, whether or not you'll enjoy Bar Salsa depends on your personal preferences and what you're looking for in a nightlife experience. If you're in the area and want to try something new, it might be worth stopping by, but I wouldn't go out of my way to visit. With its cheap drinks and lively atmosphere, Bar Salsa is a decent option for a night out, but it's not a standout destination in my book.

In addition to the excellent food, I also appreciate the cozy and intimate atmosphere of Thai House. The decor is traditional and inviting, with warm colors and Thai-inspired artwork adorning the walls. The small space can get crowded, especially on weekends, but it only adds to the energetic and lively vibe of the restaurant. The owners and staff are always friendly and welcoming, making you feel like you're part of the family. One thing that sets Thai House apart from other Thai restaurants is their attention to detail and commitment to using high-quality ingredients. You can tell that they're using fresh herbs and spices, and the dishes are carefully prepared to ensure that each bite is bursting with flavor. The portion sizes are also generous, making it a great value for the price. Overall, I highly recommend Thai House to anyone looking for delicious and authentic Thai cuisine. While the service may not be perfect, the food and atmosphere more than make up for it. And at these prices, it's a steal. Whether you're a seasoned foodie or just looking for a new place to try, Thai House is definitely worth a visit. I've been coming back for years, and I'm sure you will too once you taste their incredible Panang curry and other dishes. With its perfect balance of flavor, price, and atmosphere, Thai House is sure to remain one of my go-to spots for Thai food.

The quality of the meat and sides was impressive, and the service was friendly. Despite the price, I enjoyed my visit and would recommend it to others. Perhaps with a few more options or larger portions, Joes could justify the cost and give Kinfolks a run for its money. Overall, a solid choice for BBQ lovers.

I was thoroughly disappointed with the lunch service, especially considering my fantastic dinner experience. The long wait times and subpar food quality were a stark contrast to the prompt and delicious meal I had during happy hour. It's clear that the restaurant struggles to maintain consistency across different meal services. The fact that there was only one waiter and one chef/cook on duty during lunch hours may have contributed to the delays, but it's no excuse for the poor food quality. The over-salting of the duck confit bun was inexcusable, and the lack of authenticity in their house iced tea was a minor but notable disappointment. Despite the horrible lunch experience, I still believe that the restaurant has potential, given my previous dinner experience. However, I would caution against visiting during lunch hours until they address their service and food quality issues. Perhaps they could consider increasing staff during peak hours or reworking their recipes to ensure consistency. Until then, I would recommend sticking to dinner service, where they seem to excel. It's a shame that my cousin's last meal in Madison had to be such a letdown, but I hope that the restaurant will take feedback like mine to heart and make necessary improvements.

The lack of concern and inadequate response from the manager was appalling. A simple dessert offer did not compensate for the potential health risk I faced. I expected a more sincere apology, a complimentary meal, or even an offer to replace the contaminated soup. Instead, I was left feeling disrespected and unvalued as a customer. This experience has led me to question the restaurant's quality control and cleanliness standards. I will not be returning to Zupas and would advise others to exercise caution when dining there, carefully inspecting their food before consumption.

but would consider it if in the area. The high points were the decor and dessert, while the low points were the overcooked steak and underwhelming appetizers. With a larger group, the service was somewhat strained, but our server did their best. Overall, an average experience that didn't exceed expectations, leaving me feeling neutral about recommending it to others. Perhaps a smaller group or different menu choices would yield a better outcome.

The ambiance was elegant and sophisticated, with dim lighting and comfortable seating. Our waiter was attentive and knowledgeable, making excellent recommendations throughout the evening. The portions were generous, to say the least, and the prices were reasonable considering the high quality of the food and service. Overall, our experience at "The D" was exceptional, and we can't wait to return and try more of their delicious dishes. The combination of outstanding cuisine, impeccable service, and cozy atmosphere makes this restaurant a must-visit for anyone looking for a top-notch dining experience. We're already planning our next visit.
The atmosphere is cozy and inviting, with friendly staff making up for the long wait times, making this place a must-visit for foodies and brunch enthusiasts alike, every single time.

I'm extremely disappointed in the overall experience at this establishment. The combination of rude staff, inconsistent service, and blatant disregard for customer satisfaction is appalling. It's clear that the management prioritizes profits over people, as the staff seems to be more interested in turning tables than providing a pleasant dining experience. The fact that I was denied service and forced to leave because of a ridiculous policy is unacceptable. The happy hour and all-you-can-eat deals may be enticing, but the hassle and frustration that come with them are not worth it. I've tried to give this place multiple chances, but the consistent poor service has finally driven me away. I would not recommend this restaurant to anyone, and I will be taking my business (and my appetite) elsewhere. The Vegas roll may be delicious, but it's not enough to redeem the awful service and mistreatment of customers.

The staff was friendly and knowledgeable, making the experience stress-free for both me and my pets. The significant cost savings and convenience of the walk-in clinic make it an excellent option for pet owners. I highly recommend this place for all your pet vaccination needs, and I will definitely be returning for future vaccinations.
nothing special but good portions and prices, making it a solid option for a casual, no-frills meal in the area, with standard Chinese fare and no surprises.

The atmosphere of the restaurant was lively and vibrant, with a fun and eclectic decor that immediately transported us to the Caribbean. The music was upbeat and added to the energetic vibe of the place. Tony and Beth, the bartenders, were not only knowledgeable about the menu and drinks, but also warm and welcoming, making us feel like we were part of the family. We loved hearing about Tony's recent move from Portland and sharing our own experiences of spending summers in Oregon. As we sipped our drinks and savored our appetizers, we couldn't help but feel like we were in for a real treat. The Scallops and Plantain and Avocado Spring Rolls were just the beginning of an incredible culinary journey. The combination of flavors and textures was amazing, and we found ourselves wanting more. The pumpkin and sweet potato soup was a surprise hit, and I ended up devouring most of it. My husband's Kingston Rum Punch was potent, but delicious, and paired perfectly with the Rum Glazed Prawns and Roti Flatbread. The Prawns were cooked to perfection, with a sweet and sticky glaze that complemented the tender roti flatbread. And the Pina Colada? Absolutely divine. It was clear that the bartender had put love and care into crafting each drink, using only the freshest ingredients and creative combinations. Even the bread pudding, which wasn't my favorite, was still enjoyable and a nice way to round off the meal. What really impressed us, though, was the exceptional service. Tony and Beth were attentive, friendly, and made sure we had everything we needed throughout our meal. They were happy to answer our questions, make recommendations, and even shared some fun stories and anecdotes. The Rum Bar at Breadfruit is more than just a restaurant - it's an experience. And we can't wait to come back, bring our friends, and indulge in more of their delicious Caribbean cuisine and craft cocktails. If you're looking for a fun and lively spot with amazing food and drinks, look no further than Breadfruit. We'll definitely be back!

However, I must admit that Grape Street has a certain charm to it, and the ambiance is quite pleasant. The dim lighting and wooden decor do give it a cozy feel, reminiscent of a traditional wine cellar. The service, as I mentioned earlier, was prompt and efficient, with friendly staff who attended to our needs without being overly intrusive. Despite the improvements in my second visit, I still can't help but feel that the food is not quite up to par. The prices are also a bit steep for the quality of cuisine they offer. Overall, while Grape Street is a decent option for a casual meal, it falls short of being a truly exceptional dining experience. If you're in the area and looking for a reliable Italian meal, I would still recommend Parma over Grape Street. That being said, Grape Street might be worth a try if you're looking for a unique atmosphere and are willing to compromise on the food.

Overall, my dining experience was a letdown. The combination of the muddy tilapia, sweet sauce, and chemically-tasting avocados made for a dish that was both unappetizing and confusing. I appreciated the management's kindness in honoring our gift certificate, but the food itself was a major disappointment. With so many great fish taco options in the Valley, it's clear that this restaurant needs to go back to the drawing board and rethink their recipe. Unfortunately, I wouldn't recommend their fish tacos to anyone, and I'm still trying to figure out what inspired such a strange and unpalatable flavor combination.

Overall, our experience was a letdown, especially considering the high prices. With so many other excellent steakhouses in the area, it's unlikely we'll give this one another chance. The inconsistency in food quality and unimpressive dishes, like the rib steak and dessert, outweighed the pleasant ambiance and service, making it a disappointing evening for our large group.

The staff was friendly and the atmosphere was casual, making it a great spot for a quick lunch. The burger was cooked to perfection and the fries were crispy. I loved the nostalgia of drinking a Shasta soda from a can. Overall, I'm so glad I tried this place and I'll definitely be back for another delicious and affordable meal. The value for the price is unbeatable, and I've already recommended it to my coworkers.

I've never had a bad experience here, and the consistency is impressive. Friendly staff and great food make it a staple in our household, we always leave feeling satisfied and already looking forward to our next visit, it's a truly exceptional fast food establishment.

Overall, the experience was disappointing and overpriced. For a high-end steakhouse, I expected much better quality and attention to detail. The ambiance was nice, but it couldn't make up for the subpar food and service. Unfortunately, Craftsteak did not live up to its reputation, and I would not recommend it to others. With so many other excellent steak options in Vegas, there's no need to settle for a lackluster meal like the one we had at Craftsteak.

The lack of customer service and attention to detail is appalling. It's clear that the morning staff is not properly trained or managed. The constant mistakes and rude behavior have driven me away for good. I've taken my business elsewhere and will make sure to share my horrific experiences with friends, family, and online platforms. The location desperately needs a overhaul of their staff and customer service policies to improve their reputation and retain customers. Until then, I strongly advise others to avoid this location at all costs.

I have to say, my experience at this establishment was a mixed bag, to put it mildly. The room, as I mentioned, was fantastic - the modern decor, the gorgeous glass accents, and that incredible patio all combined to create a truly exceptional ambiance. But, unfortunately, the rest of my visit didn't quite live up to the same standards. The food, while not bad by any means, was just so..... average. I mean, who serves water chestnuts wrapped in bacon with a side of straight-up honey? It's just not impressive. And don't even get me started on the service - our server seemed more interested in flirting with the other staff members than actually attending to our needs. But, I will give them credit where credit is due: those martinis were expertly crafted, even if they were a bit on the full side. All in all, I'd say my visit averaged out to about 3 stars, which is a shame, because with a bit more attention to detail and some better training for the staff, this place could really be something special.

As the show progressed, we found ourselves giggling at the over-the-top antics and cheesy one-liners. The crowd around us was fully immersed, cheering and clapping along to Rick's every word. But my friend and I were having a different experience, analyzing every trick and illusion, trying to figure out the method behind the magic. It was almost like a fun challenge, seeing if we could debunk his claims before he even finished speaking. Despite the initial skepticism, I have to admit that Rick's energy is infectious, and by the end of the show, even we were caught up in the excitement. The VIP tickets, which included a meet-and-greet and photo opportunity, were a nice touch, although, as I mentioned earlier, the photo itself is still a bit cringeworthy. All in all, if you're looking for a lighthearted, entertaining evening that's fun for the whole family, Rick's show might be worth checking out – just don't expect to be blown away by groundbreaking magic or profound philosophy.

As I sat down at my table, I couldn't help but feel like a VIP, with the attentive staff catering to my every need. The menu is extensive, with a wide range of options to suit every taste and craving. I opted for the sushi, and let me tell you, it was some of the freshest and most delicious I've ever had. The presentation was also top-notch, with each dish carefully crafted to be almost too beautiful to eat. Almost. The atmosphere is electric, with a constant buzz of excitement and energy emanating from the crowd. Whether you're looking for a romantic evening out or a night on the town with friends, Tao has something for everyone. And don't even get me started on the people-watching - it's like a never-ending parade of interesting and fashionable individuals. Overall, I would highly recommend Tao to anyone looking for a unique and unforgettable dining experience in Las Vegas. Just be prepared for the hefty price tag, but trust me, it's worth every penny. With its impeccable service, stunning atmosphere, and mouth-watering cuisine, Tao is a must-visit destination for anyone looking to live it up in Sin City.

The atmosphere is modern and sleek, with a vibrant energy that complements the bold flavors of the dishes. Our server was knowledgeable and attentive, happy to answer questions about the menu and make recommendations. The prices were reasonable, especially considering the high quality of the ingredients and the care that clearly goes into preparing each dish. Overall, I'm so glad I stumbled upon this hidden gem and I'll definitely be back to try more of the innovative Spanish-inspired cuisine. With its unique flavor profile, excellent service, and extensive tequila selection, this restaurant is a must-visit for anyone looking to shake up their dining routine in Phoenix.

Overall, I'm glad we stumbled upon this hidden gem, thanks to the Yelp reviews. The atmosphere was cozy and inviting, making it a perfect spot to catch up with my friend. The prices were reasonable, and the portion sizes were just right. I would definitely recommend this place to others and look forward to trying more of their menu items in the future, especially if they have that balsamic dressing available for sale.

The combination of flavors and textures was absolute perfection. The spicy kick from the tuna paired beautifully with the sweetness of the salmon, all tied together by the tangy garlic ponzu. It was a truly unforgettable dish that left me wanting more. Despite the unusual music choice, our dining experience was exceptional, and we can't wait to return to Sumo and try more of their creative sushi rolls.

The service was also subpar, with our server seeming uninterested in our table. The overall atmosphere was lacking, making the experience even more disappointing. For the prices they were charging, I expected much better quality and service. Unfortunately, this place did not meet my expectations in any way, and I would not recommend it to anyone. The fact that we opted to buy groceries instead of finishing our meals speaks volumes about the poor quality of the food and drinks.

I was really looking forward to a fun night out with my friends, but the experience at Marquee was a major letdown. The crowd was not what I expected, and the constant pressure to buy a table and drinks was overwhelming. It felt like the bouncers were more interested in making a sale than in ensuring that we had a good time. The fact that they kept trying to seat us with older men or guys who seemed out of place was just weird and uncomfortable. We decided to leave early, which is unheard of for me in Vegas, and I wouldn't recommend Marquee to anyone who's looking for a genuine party experience. The stairs were also a major turn-off, and I can see why some people might feel uncomfortable or even unsafe walking up them alone. Overall, I think Marquee is a club that's more focused on its luxurious decor and making a profit than on providing a fun and welcoming atmosphere for its patrons. Unless they make some changes, I wouldn't waste my time or money on this club again.

As I look back, Macayo's was more than just a restaurant to me - it was a staple of my childhood, a place where family gatherings and celebrations were commonplace. The familiarity of their menu and the warmth of their staff, despite the gaudy uniforms, evoke a sense of nostalgia that's hard to shake off. While the food may not be authentic Mexican cuisine, it's a unique blend of flavors that has become synonymous with Vegas-style Mexican food. The TCT remains a guilty pleasure, and I often find myself driving out of my way to satisfy the occasional craving. Macayo's may not be the most sophisticated dining experience, but its nostalgic charm and comforting dishes have earned it a special place in my heart, and I'm sure, in the hearts of many other Vegas natives. It's a testament to the power of food to evoke emotions and create lasting memories.

Overall, I was pleasantly surprised by the quality of the haircut, especially given the affordable price. The lady who cut my hair seemed experienced and confident in her work, which made me feel at ease. The fade was even and well-defined, and she took just the right amount of hair off the top. I appreciated that she didn't try to make small talk or upsell me on any additional services, she just got the job done quickly and efficiently. Despite the initial confusion when I first arrived, I would still recommend this place to others who need a quick and simple military-style haircut. Just be aware that you might not get much communication about wait times or what to expect, so it's best to plan accordingly. If I were to come back, I would definitely ask for the same stylist, as she did a great job and seemed to know what she was doing. With a little improvement in customer communication, this place could easily earn a full 5 stars from me. For now, I'm happy with the value and quality I received, and I would come back if I need another quick trim in the future.

The ambiance was chaotic and overwhelming. I was expecting a cozy pizza spot, but instead, it felt like a noisy nightclub. The prices were outrageous, especially considering the unusual pizza options. I left feeling disappointed and frustrated, definitely not planning to return. The server's attitude was the final nail in the coffin, making me wonder how a place like this stays in business. Needless to say, I won't be recommending this overhyped, overpriced spot to anyone.

The service was also top-notch, with friendly staff and quick turnaround. Overall, I'm glad we took a chance on Rock-n-Roll fingers, and I highly recommend it to anyone craving delicious, high-quality chicken strips. We'll definitely be back for more of their mouthwatering food.

The atmosphere was cozy and inviting, perfect for a snowy evening. Our server was friendly and attentive, ensuring our glasses were always full. The pub's decor added to the authentic Irish experience, with dark wood and lively music. Although the portions could be larger, the quality of the food made up for it. Overall, I'd definitely recommend this pub to anyone looking for a delicious pint and tasty pub fare. We'll be back, and I'm already looking forward to trying more of their menu offerings.

Overall, it's a nostalgic spot that hasn't kept up with the times. The atmosphere feels outdated, and the service, although friendly, is slow and inattentive to table maintenance. While the sweet tea is a highlight, the reheated food and lackluster dining experience make it unlikely I'll return or recommend it to others anytime soon.

I was really looking forward to exploring every nook and cranny, but unfortunately, the overpowering scents cut my visit short. The store's potential is immense, with its unique and carefully selected items, but the fragrance issue is a major deterrent. I would highly recommend this store to anyone who can tolerate strong smells, but for those with sensitivities, it's best to proceed with caution. Perhaps the owners could consider alternative fragrance options or scent-free days to accommodate customers with allergies or asthma, allowing them to fully appreciate the store's incredible inventory and curated selection.

I was thoroughly impressed with the overall experience and can't wait to go back. The combination of delicious food, extensive beer options, and welcoming atmosphere makes it a standout destination. Whether you're a beer connoisseur or just looking for a casual spot to grab a bite, this place has something for everyone. The happy hour specials and free tastings are a great bonus, and the staff's passion for beer is evident in their knowledgeable and enthusiastic service. Overall, it's a must-visit for anyone in the area, and I'm already planning my next trip back to try more of their amazing sandwiches and beers.

Overall, my experience at Jack in the Box was underwhelming. The food was mediocre and the service was subpar. While I appreciate the variety of options on the menu, it felt like they were trying to do too much and not excelling at any one thing. The lack of enthusiasm from the staff was also a turn-off. For a fast food joint, you'd think they'd prioritize efficiency and friendliness, but that wasn't the case here. Unless they revamp their service and focus on perfecting a few key items, I just don't see myself returning. There are better fast food options out there, and I'll be sticking to those. Maybe other locations are better, but this one didn't win me over.

Clearly, the establishment is severely understaffed, leading to poor service and food safety issues. The fact that my uncovered food was left waiting to be delivered is alarming. This experience was a complete disappointment, and I would not recommend this place to anyone. The lack of organization and attention to detail is unacceptable, making my decision to never return an easy one.

The problem with Topman, in my opinion, is that it's trying too hard to be trendy and fashionable, but ultimately falls flat. The clothes are not particularly well-made, and the designs are often unoriginal and lacking in creativity. I've seen the same styles and patterns repeated in various forms throughout the store, which makes it feel like they're just churning out generic, mass-market clothing without much thought or effort. My friends seem to like the store, but I think that's because they're drawn in by the trendy branding and the promise of being fashionable. However, when you actually look at the clothes and consider the prices, it's hard to justify spending so much money on something that's not particularly special or unique. Overall, I think Topman is a bit of a disappointment, and I would recommend shopping elsewhere for better value and quality. Unless they revamp their designs and pricing, I'll stick to shopping with my friends, but only if they're buying.

The seafood pan roast is a must-try, packed with succulent shrimp, scallops, and mussels. Service is always friendly and attentive, despite the chaos during peak hours. Be prepared for a wait, but trust me, it's worth it for this hidden gem's mouth-watering dishes and unique atmosphere that will keep you coming back for more.

The atmosphere at Harold's is undeniably laid-back and welcoming, making it an excellent spot to unwind with friends or catch a game. The live band adds a lively touch, playing a mix of classic rock and country tunes that gets the crowd singing along. While the bar menu may not be fancy, it's hearty and satisfying, with plenty of options to pair with your favorite beer. I've tried their burgers and wings, and both were cooked to perfection. The staff is also friendly and attentive, always happy to refill your drink or offer recommendations. One thing to note is that the patio can get a bit smoky, as mentioned earlier, but it's a small trade-off for the overall experience. Overall, Harold's is a great spot for those looking for a casual, no-frills good time, and I'll definitely be back to enjoy another sunset and some live music.

We will definitely return, highly recommending Arrivederci to friends and family for its exceptional cuisine and warm atmosphere, making it a perfect spot for special occasions and everyday dining alike, with great prices too.

As I walked around the store, I noticed that the shelves were well-stocked and the aisles were clean, which is more than I can say for some of the other retail stores I've visited recently. The furniture pick-up area was also well-organized, and my friend was able to quickly and easily collect her purchases. I was impressed by the efficiency of the process, and the staff member who assisted her was friendly and helpful. One thing that did strike me as a bit odd was the layout of the store. It seemed like some of the departments were tucked away in corners or down long aisles, which made it a bit difficult to navigate. However, this wasn't a major issue, and I was able to find everything I needed without too much trouble. Overall, my experience at this Walmart was pleasant and uneventful, which is exactly what I'm looking for in a shopping trip. I wouldn't hesitate to return if I needed to, and I appreciate the convenience of having a McDonald's and self-checkout lanes on site. While I understand that Walmart may not be everyone's favorite retailer, I think it's unfair to judge the store or its customers based on preconceived notions or stereotypes. This location, at least, seemed like a friendly and welcoming place to shop.

The service was friendly and attentive, making our overall experience pleasant. Prices were reasonable, considering the convenience of being located within Bass Pro. While the food wasn't exceptional, it was satisfying enough to fuel our shopping trip. If I were to return, I'd be curious to explore their dinner options and see if they offer anything more impressive. Overall, it's a decent choice if you're looking for a bite to eat while visiting Bass Pro.

The service was attentive and friendly, which somewhat made up for the disappointing food. However, the quality of the breakfast dishes was a major letdown. For a cafe with such high ratings, I expected more flavorful and well-prepared meals. Unfortunately, my experience was subpar, and I wouldn't recommend their breakfast options to others. Perhaps they excel in other areas, but for now, I'll have to give them an average rating, solely thanks to the pleasant staff who tried to make my visit more enjoyable despite the lackluster food. Overall, a mediocre experience.

Overall, my experience was underwhelming and overpriced. The chicken sandwich, although cooked well, lacked any distinct flavor profile. The onion rings were crispy but unremarkable. For the cost, I expected a more satisfying meal. The friendly service was a redeeming quality, but not enough to justify the premium pricing. Unless they revamp their menu or pricing strategy, I'll be taking my lunch business elsewhere. There are simply too many other options that offer better value and flavor, making it unlikely for me to return to this establishment in the near future.
Staff seemed completely unbothered, no apology or explanation offered, making the whole experience even more frustrating and disappointing.

As we waited for our food, I couldn't help but notice the stark contrast between the website's promises and the actual dining experience. The "striking murals" of Farhad Elahi were nowhere to be found in our section of the restaurant, and the "plush seating" was replaced with standard, unremarkable tables and chairs. The ambiance, or lack thereof, was only the beginning of our disappointing evening. The food, which we had been looking forward to all day, was a major letdown. The mulagatani soup, as I mentioned earlier, was flavorless and uninspiring, and the other dishes we ordered were not much better. The Pakistani-style dishes, which I had been excited to try, were boring and lacking in both flavor and heat. The service, unfortunately, was not much better. Our server seemed overwhelmed and inattentive, and it took an inordinate amount of time to get our food and drinks. Considering it was Valentine's Day, I had expected a more romantic and attentive experience, but sadly, that was not the case. As we finished our meal and prepared to leave, I couldn't help but feel disappointed and frustrated with the entire experience. The high prices and pretentious atmosphere only added to my dissatisfaction, and I left feeling like I had been duped by the restaurant's misleading website and promises of a "hipster hangout." Overall, I would not recommend this restaurant to anyone looking for a romantic or authentic dining experience, and I will not be returning anytime soon.

As I reflect on my experience at OTB, I'm still trying to process how a place that showed such promise on my 21st birthday could fall so short on a subsequent visit. The special martini they crafted for me was a lovely touch, and I had high hopes that the $5 burger deal would be a great way to spend a casual evening with friends. Unfortunately, the subpar service, questionable food quality, and unprofessional behavior of the kitchen staff left a sour taste in my mouth. The fact that our server seemed overwhelmed and unable to attend to our needs was frustrating, but I tried to be understanding given the unique setup of the restaurant. However, when I took a bite of my burger and was met with a charred, grayish-brown patty, I knew something was seriously amiss. The combination of toppings, which sounded intriguing on the menu, was overshadowed by the unpleasant texture and flavor of the overcooked meat. What really took the cake, though, was the smell of marijuana wafting from the kitchen. It's unacceptable for any establishment to allow employees to engage in such behavior on the job, let alone in a kitchen where food is being prepared. The fact that this smell was able to permeate the entire back area and make its way to our table is a clear indication of a lack of supervision and regard for customer comfort. The aftermath of our meal was even more disturbing, as several members of our party experienced stomach pains and discomfort after consuming the burgers. While I can only speculate about the cause, it's certainly possible that the restaurant is trying to move old or spoiled product by offering it at a discounted price. This is a serious concern, and one that I hope the management will take seriously. In the end, my curiosity about OTB's unique burger offerings has been thoroughly extinguished. While I appreciate the creativity of their menu, it's not enough to outweigh the numerous issues we encountered during our visit. Until the restaurant addresses its problems with service, food quality, and kitchen professionalism, I would advise others to steer clear. There are plenty of other establishments in the area that offer delicious, safely prepared food in a comfortable and respectful environment. OTB, unfortunately, is not one of them.

"The service was also subpar, our server seemed overwhelmed. For a Christmas buffet, the quality and variety were lacking. Given the high prices, we expected much more. Overall, a disappointing experience, especially considering the long wait times and limited seating. Definitely not worth the hassle or cost, especially for a special occasion like Christmas."

I'm extremely disappointed in the decline of service quality at this Gruelich's location. The constant push for unnecessary repairs has become overwhelming, and it's clear that their priority is no longer the customer's satisfaction, but rather their own profit. The fact that they didn't even bother to check their computer records before recommending the transmission flush is not only unprofessional, but also a clear indication of their dishonest intentions. As a loyal customer for over 15 years, it's disheartening to see such a drastic change in their business practices. I've always appreciated the convenience of having a trustworthy mechanic nearby, but unfortunately, I can no longer recommend this location to anyone. The lack of transparency and integrity has led me to take my business elsewhere, and I hope that others will do the same. It's time for Gruelich's to re-evaluate their priorities and focus on providing honest, quality service to their customers. Until then, I'll be taking my cars (and my business) to a more reputable mechanic.

I was thoroughly impressed with the overall experience at Rick's shop. The staff were friendly and knowledgeable, and the tour was well-organized and informative. Meeting Rick himself was the highlight of the visit, and he was more than happy to take photos and sign autographs. What struck me was how down-to-earth and genuine he was, taking the time to chat with each person and make them feel welcome. The shop itself was also impressive, with a wide range of interesting items on display. Compared to the other shops I visited, Rick's stood out for its warm and welcoming atmosphere. I would highly recommend a visit to anyone who is a fan of the show or just looking for a unique experience. The fact that Rick and other stars of the show are often onsite makes it a must-visit destination. Overall, I would give Rick's shop a well-deserved 5 stars, and I look forward to visiting again in the future.

The ambiance was cozy and intimate, perfect for a night out with someone special. The tapas dishes were creatively prepared and presented, with generous portions that allowed us to try a variety of flavors. While not every dish blew me away, the overall experience was enjoyable and the prices were reasonable. I appreciated the wait staff's knowledge and enthusiasm for the wine list, which added to the evening's charm. Overall, I would recommend Pullman to anyone looking for a relaxed, wine-focused dining experience with a touch of elegance. It's a great spot to unwind and savor good food and wine.

As I finally emerged from the labyrinthine entrance, I couldn't help but feel a sense of accomplishment, as if I had just completed an obstacle course. The fact that I had to navigate through a maze of temporary corridors and stairways just to reach the main concourse was not only frustrating but also exhausting. And to make matters worse, the signage throughout the station was inadequate, to say the least. I saw several people, including tourists and commuters alike, looking around confused, trying to make sense of the convoluted layout. I decided to take a deep breath and approach one of the station staff to ask for directions to platform 1. The poor soul looked just as frazzled as I did, and I could sense her frustration as she tried to explain the complex route to me. It was clear that even the staff were struggling to navigate the temporary layout. I felt a pang of sympathy for her, having to deal with irate commuters like myself all day. As I finally made my way to platform 1, I couldn't help but notice the state of the station. The building works had left the area looking like a construction site, with scaffolding and temporary walls blocking off large sections of the concourse. The noise level was deafening, with drills and hammers ringing out throughout the station. It was clear that the renovation was a much-needed one, but the execution was leaving much to be desired. I took a seat on the platform and waited for my train, observing the other commuters around me. Some were typing away on their laptops, while others were scrolling through their phones, trying to distract themselves from the chaos around them. I struck up a conversation with a fellow commuter, and we commiserated about the state of the station. It was clear that we were not alone in our frustration. As the train arrived and we boarded, I felt a sense of relief wash over me. I was finally leaving the chaos of Waverley Train station behind, at least for a little while. But as I looked out the window and watched the station recede into the distance, I couldn't help but feel a sense of dread. I knew that I would have to navigate that labyrinthine entrance again on my return journey, and I wasn't looking forward to it. In conclusion, my experience at Waverley Train station was a frustrating and exhausting one. The temporary layout, combined with the inadequate signage and confusing directions, made for a stressful and overwhelming experience. While I understand that the renovation is necessary, I implore the station management to take steps to improve the navigation and signage throughout the station. Perhaps a more comprehensive map or clearer directions would help to alleviate some of the frustration. Until then, I'll just have to grit my teeth and prepare for the challenge that is Waverley Train station. As I settled into my seat and the train pulled out of the station, I couldn't help but wonder what other commuters had experienced at Waverley Train station. Had they too struggled to navigate the temporary layout? Had they also felt the frustration and exhaustion that I had? I decided to take to social media to share my experience and see if others had similar stories to tell. And as I scrolled through the comments and messages, I realized that I was not alone. Many others had shared my frustration, and some had even worse stories to tell. It was clear that Waverley Train station was a source of stress and anxiety for many commuters, and it was time for something to be done about it.

Prices were reasonable, service was friendly, but not overly attentive. The burger truly stood out, juicy and flavorful, making it a highlight of the meal. Overall, a solid choice, but not exceptional enough to warrant frequent visits, hence the moderate priority for return trips.

to grab a quick bite or fill up on gas, as the overall experience was pleasant and convenient, making it a great stop for travelers and locals alike, with its well-maintained facilities and ample options.

As I sat there, disappointed and frustrated, I couldn't help but think that this place had fallen short of my expectations. The atmosphere, which had initially impressed me, now felt like a facade, a distraction from the subpar food and service. The huge assortment of options, which had seemed like a strength, now seemed like a weakness, a sign that the kitchen was spread too thin and unable to deliver on quality. I've been to several other pastry places that have gotten it right, where the pastries are kept warm in the oven and served hot, fresh, and delicious. Those places may not have as many options, but what they do offer is made with care and attention to detail. It's clear that quality control is a priority, and it shows in every bite. In contrast, this place seemed to be prioritizing quantity over quality, and it showed in the cold, soggy mess that was served to us. The staff's lack of concern and half-hearted offer to heat it up only added to our disappointment. We left feeling let down and unlikely to return, which is a shame, because with a bit more attention to quality control, this place could be truly great.

The value for the price was definitely a highlight of our experience. The soup and salad were standard, but the entree was cooked well and presented nicely. The dessert was also a pleasant surprise, with a decent selection to choose from. Our server, as I mentioned, was friendly and attentive, but the delay in receiving our food was noticeable. Despite the initial disappointment with the singing waiters, the overall atmosphere was lively and enjoyable. The decor was quaint and added to the charm of the restaurant. However, the food and entertainment didn't quite live up to our expectations. Overall, it was an average dining experience, but the set meal deal made it a decent value. If you're looking for a affordable and casual meal on the strip, this might be a good option, but don't go in with high hopes for exceptional food or entertainment.

We left feeling underwhelmed and not impressed by the quality of food. The service was friendly, but that wasn't enough to make up for the lackluster dishes. Given the numerous exceptional restaurants in Las Vegas, it's hard to recommend this place when there are better options available. Overall, our comped meal was a nice gesture, but not enough to win us over as paying customers in the future.

The service was also subpar, with our server seeming overwhelmed and inattentive. It took a while to get our orders taken and even longer to get the check. For the price, I expected a lot more quality and attention to detail. Unfortunately, this place failed to deliver on both counts. The atmosphere was nice, but that's not enough to make up for the lackluster food and service. Overall, I would not recommend this place to anyone, especially for the price they're charging. There are far better options available for Sunday brunch.

Unprofessional and uninformative experience overall, putting my son's skin health at risk. We will be taking our business elsewhere to ensure proper care and attention to detail. Very disappointed in the lack of transparency and poor communication from the PA.

As a parent, it was disappointing to see the amount of smoking allowed in the casino area, and the smell of smoke often wafted into the non-smoking areas, including the elevators and hallways. I understand that casinos and smoking often go hand-in-hand, but it would be nice to see Aria take steps to better contain the smoke or provide more non-smoking areas. Despite this, our stay at Aria was overall very enjoyable. The staff was friendly and helpful, and the hotel's modern amenities and technology were impressive. The room was clean and comfortable, and the kids loved the high-tech controls and the large TV. The location was also convenient, with many restaurants and shops within walking distance. One of the highlights of our stay was the buffet at Aria. While we didn't have a chance to try many of the other restaurants, the buffet was excellent, with a wide variety of options and high-quality food. The kids especially loved the dessert section, which featured a wide range of sweet treats. In addition to the buffet, we also enjoyed the hotel's pool area, which was clean and well-maintained. The kids had a blast swimming and playing in the water, and the adults appreciated the comfortable lounge chairs and umbrellas. Overall, I would recommend Aria to anyone looking for a modern and convenient hotel in the heart of Las Vegas. While the smoking in the casino was a drawback, the hotel's many amenities and excellent service made up for it. With a few tweaks to their smoking policy, I would have no hesitation in giving Aria a full 5-star rating. It's worth noting that Aria is a large hotel, and it can take some time to get from one place to another. However, the hotel provides a convenient tram service to help guests get around, and the staff is always happy to provide directions or assistance. In conclusion, our stay at Aria was a great experience, and I would definitely consider staying here again in the future. The hotel's modern amenities, convenient location, and excellent service make it a great choice for anyone looking for a comfortable and enjoyable stay in Las Vegas.

The lack of attention to detail and subpar cuisine was shocking, especially given the chef's reputation. For a restaurant of this caliber, the mistakes were inexcusable. The atmosphere, although elegant, couldn't compensate for the poor food and service. It's clear that the Las Vegas location is resting on the coattails of its NYC counterpart.
